params.enroll: The department shall adopt regulations establishing a procedure for a qualified individual to enroll in or withdraw from the program. No enrollment procedure or application was published in the sources I found.

rules.summary: Alaska's new Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Administration, gives an enrolled person a post office box to use as a substitute mailing address and forwards their mail, and state and municipal agencies must accept that address. A victim of a crime involving sexual assault, domestic violence, or stalking can enroll if a court has issued a protective order for them or they meet other standards the department sets. The department must still adopt regulations setting out how to enroll.
rules.quote: (2) designate a post office box as a substitute mailing address for an 02 individual enrolled in the program; 03 (3) forward the mail of an individual enrolled in the program from the 04 post office box designated under (2) of this subsection to the individual's residential 05 street address, post office box, school address, or work address as specified on the 06 individual's application for enrollment in the program; 07 (4) maintain the confidentiality of the address of an individual enrolled 08 in the program; and 09 (5) adopt regulations establishing a procedure for a qualified individual 10 under (c) of this section to enroll in or withdraw from the program. 11 (c) The following individuals may enroll in the program: 12 (1) a victim of a crime involving domestic violence, stalking, or sexual 13 assault if 14 (A) a court has issued a protective order on behalf of the 15 victim; or 16 (B) the victim meets other standards set by the department;
rules.pinpoint: AS 44.21.022(b)(2) to (c)(1), enacted by sec. 75 of Chapter 9 SLA 26 (HB 239), effective July 1, 2026 under sec. 94; agencies must accept the address under AS 44.21.022(e)
rules.source_title: Enrolled HB 239 (Chapter 9 SLA 26), sec. 75 enacting AS 44.21.022, Address confidentiality program (Alaska Legislature bill text)

rules.summary: By statute, a compensation application and personally identifying information about the applicant are confidential records that the Violent Crimes Compensation Board may not release.
rules.quote: An application for compensation and personally identifying information relating to an applicant for compensation are confidential records and may not be released by the board.
rules.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

rules.summary: Alabama law gives a sexual assault survivor the right not to be charged for a medical forensic exam. The provider may bill the survivor's health insurer.
rules.quote: Not to be prevented from, or charged for, receiving a medical forensic examination.
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-121 (Justia)

rules.summary: The same statute lets a health care provider bill a health insurer for the forensic exam.
rules.quote: For the purposes of this subdivision, a health care provider may bill a health insurer for providing a medical forensic examination.
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-121 (Justia)

rules.summary: The Commission's rule says a hospital, clinic, or SANE facility should not bill the survivor for the exam.
rules.quote: A hospital, medical clinic, or SANE facility should not bill the victim of sexual violence for the sexual assault examination.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-11-.01

params.payer: Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission (Sexual Assault Examination Payment Program), after any collateral source such as insurance

rules.summary: State law lets the Commission pay for forensic exams that collect evidence after sexual abuse crimes, and for treatment to prevent sexually transmitted infections.
rules.quote: Provide for the cost of forensic medical examinations for the purpose of gathering evidence and treatment for preventing sexually transmitted infections in sexual abuse crimes and offenses.
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-5 (Justia)

params.payer: Insurance or other collateral source first, then the Commission's Sexual Assault Examination Payment Program

rules.summary: Insurance or another collateral source has to be used first, then the provider submits the exam to the Commission's Sexual Assault Examination Payment Program.
rules.quote: Any collateral source available for the payment of a sexual assault examination must be utilized prior to submitting a sexual assault examination to the Commission's Sexual Assault Examination Payment Program.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-11-.01

params.payer: Exam program covers only the initial forensic exam and STI prevention; injury treatment, other medication and hospital admissions go through a regular compensation claim

rules.summary: The exam payment program does not pay for injury treatment, medication other than STI treatment and prevention, or hospital admissions. Those costs may still be covered through a regular compensation claim, and every survivor should be given an application.
rules.quote: Expenses that are ineligible pursuant to the Commission’s Sexual Assault Examination Payment Program may be eligible for crime victims’ compensation benefits.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-11-.01

params.payer: Commission's Sexual Assault Examination Payment Program, including 'Jane Doe' exams for adults (not children)

rules.summary: The exam program pays for 'Jane Doe' sexual assault exams on adults. It does not pay for 'Jane Doe' exams on children, and for a minor the facility must confirm a report to DHR or law enforcement.
rules.quote: The Commission will provide reimbursement for “Jane Doe” sexual assault examinations performed on adult victims.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-11-.01

rules.summary: The most the Commission will pay in total for a victim's or claimant's economic loss is $15,000.
rules.quote: (1) Compensation payable to a victim or claimant sustaining economic loss due to injury or death may not exceed a total of fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000.00).
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

rules.summary: Therapy is capped at $6,250 or 50 sessions.
rules.quote: Reimbursement for therapy expenses shall not exceed $6,250, or 50 sessions.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

rules.summary: When the victim is a minor, the person who files the claim is limited to 15 individual therapy sessions, unless the victim has died.
rules.quote: When the victim is a minor, the claimant shall be limited to 15 individual therapy sessions, unless the victim is deceased.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

rules.summary: For crimes on or after July 9, 2020, lost wages are paid at up to $400 a week for up to 26 weeks.
rules.quote: For incidents of criminally injurious conduct occurring on or after July 9, 2020, lost wages are limited to $400.00 per week for a maximum of 26 weeks.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

rules.summary: A sexual assault victim can get up to two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's note. Employer verification is still required.
rules.quote: A victim of sexual assault may be granted compensation for maximum of two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's excuse.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

rules.summary: Moving and temporary relocation together are capped at $1,000.
rules.quote: Moving and temporary relocation expenses may not exceed a combined total of $1,000.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

rules.summary: Travel expenses are capped at $3,000.
rules.quote: The maximum award for travel expenses is $3,000.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.scope: travel for medical and psychological treatment needed because of the crime

rules.summary: Travel for medical and psychological treatment needed because of the crime can be covered.
rules.quote: Travel may be allowed for medical and psychological treatment that is needed as a result of the victimization.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

rules.summary: Allowable expenses include needed medical care and rehabilitation.
rules.quote: Charges incurred for needed products, services, and accommodations, including, but not limited to, medical care, rehabilitation
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-3 (Justia)

rules.summary: Medical bills the survivor already paid out of pocket can be fully reimbursed up to $15,000.
rules.quote: When the claimant has already paid out-of-pocket for medical treatment and services, the claimant may be fully reimbursed for all eligible expenses not to exceed $15,000.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.scope: unpaid bills only; bills already paid out of pocket can be paid back up to $15,000

rules.summary: Medical bills that are still unpaid (not psychiatric care, counseling, or dental) may be paid at a reduced rate of 30% of eligible charges, up to $6,000. Medical bills you already paid yourself may be paid back in full, up to $15,000.
rules.quote: Outstanding charges for medical treatment, excluding psychiatric care, counseling, and dental treatment, may be compensated at a reduced rate of thirty percent (30%) of eligible charges up to a maximum amount of six thousand dollars ($6,000). When the claimant has already paid out-of-pocket for medical treatment and services, the claimant may be fully reimbursed for all eligible expenses not to exceed $15,000.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.scope: a 28-day course of HIV prevention medicine, if you are at risk of HIV exposure

rules.summary: If a survivor is at risk of HIV exposure, the Commission may pay for a 28-day course of HIV prophylaxis, including directly to the survivor.
rules.quote: If it is determined that a victim of sexual violence is at risk for exposure to HIV, the Commission may provide payment for a 28-day drug regimen of HIV prophylaxis to a SANE facility, hospital, medical clinic, pharmacy, or victim of sexual violence.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-11-.01

rules.summary: If the survivor has health insurance, the pharmacy, hospital, or clinic filling the prescription must first seek payment from the insurance.
rules.quote: If a victim of sexual violence has health insurance, the pharmacy, hospital, or medical clinic filling the prescription for HIV prophylaxis must first seek payment of the expense from the health insurance provider.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-11-.01

params.scope: windows and locks for a home you own, or rent and must pay to repair

rules.summary: Listed under the property rule as an allowed item: windows and locks for a home the victim owns, or rents when the victim must pay for repairs.
rules.quote: Security enhancement. Windows and locks for real property owned by the claimant/victim; and windows and locks for rental property leased by the claimant/victim when the claimant/victim is financially responsible for repair(s) to the leased property.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

rules.summary: Damaged prescription eyeglasses are covered up to $350, with a receipt or estimate.
rules.quote: The maximum award for damaged prescription eyeglasses is $350.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.item: personal property reimbursement or replacement

rules.summary: The Commission does not reimburse or replace property, so a lost or damaged phone or other personal item is not covered. The only items listed under this rule are security windows and locks and damaged prescription eyeglasses.
rules.quote: The Commission does not provide property reimbursement or replacement.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.item: stolen property, property damage, checks, cash

rules.summary: Stolen property, property damage, checks, and cash are not covered.
rules.quote: Stolen property, property damage, checks or cash will not be covered by the Commission.
rules.source_title: ACVCC: Compensation

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: Pain and suffering is not compensated.
rules.quote: The Commission does not provide compensation for pain and suffering.
rules.source_title: ACVCC: Compensation

rules.summary: Legal fees are not paid, except fees to set up a legal guardian for the victim.
rules.quote: All legal fees shall be excluded from payment except legal fees incurred to establish a legal guardian for the victim
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.extension: or later if the Commission finds good cause

rules.summary: The claim must be filed within one year of the injury, unless the Commission finds good cause for filing late.
rules.quote: A claim has been filed with the commission later than one year after the injury or death upon which the claim is based, unless the commission finds there was good cause for the failure to file within that time.
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-12 (Justia)

params.exception: or later if the Commission finds good cause

rules.summary: The crime has to be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, unless the Commission finds good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: The criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer later than 72 hours after its occurrence, unless the commission finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-12 (Justia)

rules.summary: Good cause for late reporting includes the claimant being a minor or having an infirmity or incapacity.
rules.quote: Good cause includes, but is not limited to the minority, infirmity or incapacity of the claimant.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.02

rules.summary: The Commission does not pay expenses already paid by insurance or another collateral source.
rules.quote: (6) Requested expenses shall not be eligible for compensation in the event that they have been paid by a collateral source
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.02

rules.summary: An award can be reduced or denied to the extent the loss is recouped from collateral sources.
rules.quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant may be diminished or denied to the extent that the economic loss is recouped from collateral sources
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-12 (Justia)

rules.summary: An award can be reduced or denied to the extent the Commission finds the victim responsible for the injury.
rules.quote: or to the extent that the degree of responsibility for the cause of the injury or death is attributable to the victim as determined by the commission.
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-12 (Justia)

rules.summary: An award can be denied, withdrawn, or reduced if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement.
rules.quote: The commission, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies, may deny, withdraw, or reduce an award of compensation.
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-12 (Justia)

rules.summary: An emergency award paid ahead of the final decision is capped at $1,000 and is subtracted from the final award.
rules.quote: The amount of such emergency award shall not exceed one thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.05

rules.summary: The Commission's sexual assault brochure says it can help with ongoing medical and counseling costs and other assault-related expenses.
rules.quote: The Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission can assist you with ongoing medical and counseling expenses and other expenses related to the assault.
rules.source_title: ACVCC brochure: Sexual Assault Victimization

rules.summary: An award can be made whether or not anyone is prosecuted or convicted.
rules.quote: an award may be made whether or not any person is prosecuted or convicted.
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-13 (Justia)

params.rule: Crimes in Alabama that cause serious personal injury or death can qualify; the victim does not have to live in Alabama.

rules.summary: A crime in Alabama, or an attempt, that causes serious injury or death can qualify, wherever the victim lives.
rules.quote: An act occurring or attempted within the geographical boundaries of this state which results in serious personal injury or death to a victim for which punishment by fine, imprisonment, or death may be imposed.
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-3 (Justia)

params.rule: Alabama residents victimized in another US state, if they kept a permanent Alabama residence and meet one of the statute's listed conditions.

rules.summary: Citizens of Alabama hurt by a crime in another US state can qualify if they had a permanent home in Alabama and meet one of the listed conditions (for example, a job in Alabama or full-time student out of state).
rules.quote: provided however, the citizen at the time such act was committed had a permanent place of residence within the geographical boundaries of this state
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-3 (Justia)

params.rule: US citizen, legally present person, or alien eligible for public benefits; proof required with the application.

rules.summary: Benefits go only to US citizens, people legally present in the US, or aliens eligible for public benefits.
rules.quote: A person must be a U.S. citizen, a person who is legally present in the U.S., or an alien eligible for public benefits in order to receive compensation benefits.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.02

params.target: Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission P.O. Box 231267 Montgomery, Alabama 36123-1267

rules.summary: Mail the completed application to the Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission, P.O. Box 231267, Montgomery, Alabama 36123-1267.
rules.quote: The completed application can be returned by: FAX: (334)290-4455 Email: info@acvcc.alabama.gov Mail: Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission P.O. Box 231267 Montgomery, Alabama 36123-1267
rules.pinpoint: Compensation page, How Do I File A Claim?
rules.source_title: ACVCC: Compensation

rules.summary: Email the completed application to info@acvcc.alabama.gov.
rules.quote: Please download the completed application and email it to info@acvcc.alabama.gov or fax it to 334-290-4455.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, submission box
rules.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

rules.summary: Fax the completed application to 334-290-4455.
rules.quote: Please download the completed application and email it to info@acvcc.alabama.gov or fax it to 334-290-4455.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, submission box
rules.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

params.note: Signed application; a fax or electronic signature is accepted.

rules.summary: The application must be signed; a fax or electronic signature is accepted, but the Commission may ask for an original notarized signature.
rules.quote: The claimant must submit an application that has been signed by either facsimile signature or electronic signature.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.02

params.note: Proof of U.S. citizenship, legal presence, or eligible-alien status; ACVCC lists accepted documents at acvcc.alabama.gov/victims/who-is-eligible/legal-presence/.

rules.summary: Include proof of U.S. citizenship or that you are an alien eligible for public benefits.
rules.quote: You must submit proof of US citizenship or that you are an alien eligible for public benefits.
rules.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

params.note: Only if one is available.

rules.summary: Include a copy of the police report if one is available.
rules.quote: Complete this section and, if one is available, provide a copy of the Police Report.
rules.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

params.note: Bills or receipts directly related to each type of compensation requested.

rules.summary: For each type of compensation you request, include the related bills or receipts.
rules.quote: Provide any corresponding and directly related bills/receipts.
rules.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

params.note: Signed and dated health information release (Patient Authorization page of the application), only if medical expenses are requested.

rules.summary: If you are asking for medical expenses, the victim or a representative must sign and date the health information authorization in the application.
rules.quote: Either the patient (victim) or their representative must sign and date this authorization if consideration of medical expenses is being requested.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Patient Authorization for Use and Disclosure of Protected Health Information
rules.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

params.note: Written good cause, only if filing more than one year after the incident.

rules.summary: If you file more than one year after the incident, explain the good cause in writing.
rules.quote: The claim must be filed within one (1) year of the incident, or good cause must be submitted in writing.
rules.source_title: ACVCC: Application Form page

params.note: Written good cause, only if the crime was not reported to law enforcement within 72 hours.

rules.summary: If the crime was not reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, explain the good cause in writing.
rules.quote: The crime must be reported to the proper law enforcement agency within 72 hours of the incident, or good cause must be submitted in writing.
rules.source_title: ACVCC: Application Form page

params.note: Proof of authority to act for the victim, only if the claimant is someone other than the victim.

rules.summary: If someone other than the victim signs as claimant, include documentation that they are legally authorized to act for the victim.
rules.quote: The claimant (if other than victim) must be the person legally authorized to act on the behalf of the victim. Documentation of this authority must be provided.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, signature note
rules.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

params.note: Proof of guardianship or conservatorship, only if the victim is 19 or older and incapacitated.

rules.summary: If the victim is 19 or older but incapacitated, include proof of guardianship or conservatorship.
rules.quote: If the victim is 19 or older, but is incapacitated, you will have to provide proof of guardianship/conservatorship over the victim.
rules.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

params.note: Written documentation from the employer or a W-2.

rules.summary: For lost wages, include written documentation from your employer or a W-2.
rules.quote: Lost wages shall be verified by obtaining written documentation from the employer or by submission of a W-2 tax document.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.note: IRS tax transcript, only if self-employed.

rules.summary: For lost wages, if you are self-employed, include a tax transcript from the IRS.
rules.quote: A tax transcript from the IRS is required if the person seeking reimbursement of his/her lost wages is self-employed.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.note: Doctor's excuse, only for sexual assault lost wages beyond two weeks.

rules.summary: A sexual assault victim can claim up to two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's excuse; beyond two weeks, include a doctor's excuse.
rules.quote: A victim of sexual assault may be granted compensation for maximum of two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's excuse. A doctor's excuse must be provided for lost wages in excess of two weeks to be considered for reimbursement.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.note: Letter from the clinician certifying necessary therapy due to the victimization.

rules.summary: For counseling, the Commission needs a letter from the clinician certifying that therapy is necessary because of the victimization.
rules.quote: ACVCC must receive a letter from the clinician certifying that the victim is engaged in necessary therapy due to his/her victimization.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

params.note: Quarterly updates from the clinician.

rules.summary: For ongoing counseling, the clinician must send quarterly updates certifying the treatment is still necessary.
rules.quote: Quarterly updates from the clinician certifying that the treatment is necessary and the result of victimization must be submitted in order for payment to be considered.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

params.note: Itemized bill for treatment sessions from the clinician.

rules.summary: For counseling, the clinician must provide an itemized bill for the treatment sessions.
rules.quote: The clinician must provide an itemized bill for treatment sessions.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

params.note: Written estimates and/or receipts for moving expenses.

rules.summary: For moving expenses, include written estimates or receipts.
rules.quote: Written estimates and/or receipts are required for payment of moving expenses.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.note: Hotel bill, credit card receipt, or other verifiable document for temporary relocation.

rules.summary: For temporary relocation, include a copy of the hotel bill, credit card receipt, or another verifiable document.
rules.quote: A copy of the hotel bill, credit card receipt, or other verifiable document is required for verification.
rules.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

rules.summary: The Commission may not disclose the names and addresses of victims or claimants who applied for compensation, or the facts of the crime against them.
rules.quote: The commission may not disclose the names and addresses of victims or claimants who have applied for compensation pursuant to this article or the facts or circumstances of the criminally injurious conduct perpetrated against them.
rules.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-4 (Justia)

params.condition: if you get it within 96 hours of the assault

rules.summary: Survivors are exempt from paying for a sexual assault medical-legal exam received within 96 hours of the attack. The 96-hour limit can be waived for a minor or when the board finds good cause.
rules.quote: (A) All victims shall be exempted from the payment of expenses incurred as a result of receiving a medical-legal examination if the victim receives the medical-legal examination within ninety-six (96) hours of the attack. (B) However, the time limitation of ninety-six (96) hours may be waived if the victim is a minor or if the Crime Victims Reparations Board finds that good cause exists for the failure to provide the medical-legal examination within the required time.
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 12-12-403 (2025), Sexual assault examinations and treatment, payment

params.payer: Arkansas Crime Victims Reparations Board

rules.summary: After the board pays, the exam provider may not send any remaining balance to the survivor.
rules.quote: The licensed healthcare provider shall not submit any remaining balance after reimbursement by the board to the victim.
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 12-12-403 (2025), Sexual assault examinations and treatment, payment

params.payer: Arkansas Crime Victims Reparations Board (Sexual Assault Reimbursement Program)

rules.summary: The exam provider bills the Crime Victims Reparations Board directly, through the Sexual Assault Reimbursement Program, using a sexual assault reimbursement form.
rules.quote: A licensed healthcare provider that performs a medical-legal examination shall submit a sexual assault reimbursement form, an itemized statement that meets the requirements of 45 C. F. R. § 164.512(d), as it existed on January 2, 2001, directly to the board for payment.
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 12-12-403 (2025), Sexual assault examinations and treatment, payment

rules.summary: A survivor does not have to report to police or cooperate with law enforcement to get a forensic exam or have its charges reimbursed.
rules.quote: This subsection does not require a victim of sexual assault to participate in the criminal justice system or to cooperate with law enforcement in order to be provided with a forensic medical exam or reimbursement for charges incurred on account of a forensic medical exam, or both.
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 12-12-403 (2025), Sexual assault examinations and treatment, payment

rules.summary: Not having to report for the exam does not stop a report of suspected child abuse or neglect that the state's child abuse law allows or requires.
rules.quote: Subdivision (b)(2)(A) of this section does not preclude a report of suspected abuse or neglect as permitted or required by the Child Maltreatment Act, § 12-18-101 et seq.
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 12-12-403 (2025), Sexual assault examinations and treatment, payment

rules.summary: Exam bills are denied or reduced to the extent the cost can be recovered from a collateral source, which the rules define to include insurance, Medicaid, and Medicare.
rules.quote: Medical-legal examination bills will be denied or diminished to the extent that the expenses can be recuperated from a collateral source.
rules.source_title: Code of Arkansas Rules, 16 CAR Part 60, Crime Victims Reparations Board Rules (Bureau of Legislative Research, 03/22/2026)

params.payer: Arkansas Crime Victims Reparations Board, paid directly to the medical provider

rules.summary: The board may pay a medical provider directly for a sexual assault testing kit even if the survivor never files an application, and those costs include testing for sexually transmitted diseases.
rules.quote: The board may directly reimburse a medical care provider for costs associated with a sexual assault testing kit, even in the absence of a victim's application. (3) Such costs, which include those associated with testing for sexually transmitted diseases, may be reimbursed regardless of which fund or cost center is used to make the reimbursement.
rules.source_title: Code of Arkansas Rules, 16 CAR Part 60, Crime Victims Reparations Board Rules (Bureau of Legislative Research, 03/22/2026)

params.payer: Sexual Assault Reimbursement Program (Crime Victims Reparations Board)

rules.summary: The DPS About page says the Sexual Assault Reimbursement Program pays for evidence collection after a sexual assault, including ambulance services and medical or legal exams, so the survivor does not bear the expense.
rules.quote: the Sexual Assault Reimbursement Program allows evidence to be collected after a sexual assault has been committed without the victim bearing the burden of the expense, and it pays for ambulance services and medical or legal examinations.
rules.source_title: Arkansas DPS, About CVRB page

rules.summary: The most the program pays for one victim, across all claimants, is $10,000.
rules.quote: Reparations payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of that victim may not exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000).
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-716 (2025), Limitation on reparations

params.exception: or up to $25,000 if an injury leaves you fully disabled for life

rules.summary: For catastrophic injuries that cause total and permanent disability, the maximum rises to $25,000.
rules.quote: However, for those victims whose injuries are catastrophic and result in a total and permanent disability, the maximum reparations amount shall not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000).
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-716 (2025), Limitation on reparations

rules.summary: Mental health counseling not covered by insurance is paid up to $2,500 or six months, whichever comes first, if a treatment plan is sent within 30 days. The board's rules let it waive this maximum for a documented special need.
rules.quote: the Crime Victims Reparations Board will pay a maximum of two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) or provide for six (6) months, whichever occurs first, provided the treatment plan is submitted within thirty (30) days of:
rules.source_title: Code of Arkansas Rules, 16 CAR Part 60, Crime Victims Reparations Board Rules (Bureau of Legislative Research, 03/22/2026)

rules.summary: For medical bills not covered by insurance, the board pays up to 65% of the bills, with total reimbursement capped at $10,000.
rules.quote: the Crime Victims Reparations Board will award up to sixty-five percent (65%) of medical bills, not to exceed a total reimbursement of ten thousand dollars ($10,000).
rules.source_title: Code of Arkansas Rules, 16 CAR Part 60, Crime Victims Reparations Board Rules (Bureau of Legislative Research, 03/22/2026)

params.scope: medical bills when a catastrophic injury causes total and permanent disability

rules.summary: For catastrophic injuries that cause total and permanent disability, medical bills can be paid up to $25,000 in total.
rules.quote: However, for those victims whose injuries are catastrophic and result in a total and permanent disability, the total reimbursement shall not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000).
rules.source_title: Code of Arkansas Rules, 16 CAR Part 60, Crime Victims Reparations Board Rules (Bureau of Legislative Research, 03/22/2026)

rules.summary: Funeral expenses are capped at $7,500.
rules.quote: Compensation for funeral expenses of deceased victims may not exceed seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500).
rules.source_title: Code of Arkansas Rules, 16 CAR Part 60, Crime Victims Reparations Board Rules (Bureau of Legislative Research, 03/22/2026)

rules.summary: An advance (emergency) award is available when compensation is probable and undue hardship would result; it is capped at $500 and deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: The amount of such advance (emergency) award shall not exceed five hundred dollars ($500).
rules.source_title: Code of Arkansas Rules, 16 CAR Part 60, Crime Victims Reparations Board Rules (Bureau of Legislative Research, 03/22/2026)

params.extension: or later if the board finds good cause

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 5 years after the injury, unless the board finds good cause for filing late.
rules.quote: Unless the claim has been filed with the Crime Victims Reparations Board within five (5) years after the injury or death upon which the claim is based, except: (A) When the board finds good cause for the failure to file a timely claim
rules.pinpoint: A.C.A. 16-90-712(a)(1)(A), as amended by Act 666 of 2025
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-712 (2025), Conditions for reparations

rules.summary: If the victim is a minor, the claim may be filed within 5 years after the victim turns 18.
rules.quote: If the victim is a minor, the claim is filed within five (5) years after the date the victim reaches eighteen (18) years of age
rules.pinpoint: A.C.A. 16-90-712(a)(1)(B), as amended by Act 666 of 2025
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-712 (2025), Conditions for reparations

params.exception: or later if the board finds good cause

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to the proper authorities within 72 hours, unless the board finds good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: Unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to the proper authorities within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence, or the board finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-712 (2025), Conditions for reparations

rules.summary: Under the board's rules, good cause for a late police report includes the victim's physical incapacity, mental incompetence, or age. It also includes an injury that could not reasonably be discovered. Other reasons can count too.
rules.quote: Good cause shall include, but not be limited to, the: (A) Physical incapacity of a victim; (B) Mental incompetence of a victim; (C) Age of the victim; and (D) Injury was not reasonably discoverable.
rules.source_title: Code of Arkansas Rules, 16 CAR Part 60, Crime Victims Reparations Board Rules (Bureau of Legislative Research, 03/22/2026)

params.scope: minors, per the DPS criteria page

rules.summary: The program's criteria page says minors are excluded from the 72-hour report rule. The board's rules count the victim's age as one kind of good cause for a late report.
rules.quote: reported to authorities within 72 hours (minors excluded)
rules.pinpoint: DPS Criteria to Receive Compensation page
rules.source_title: Arkansas DPS, CVRB Criteria to Receive Compensation page

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: If the board finds the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement, it may deny, withdraw, or reduce the award. This does not apply to a minor victim of a sex offense or a victim of human trafficking.
rules.quote: Except as provided in subdivision (c)(2) of this section, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies, the board may deny, withdraw, or reduce an award of reparations. (2) This subsection does not apply if the claimant or victim is a victim of human trafficking or a minor victim of a sex offense, as defined in § 12-12-903.
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-712 (2025), Conditions for reparations

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by any amount recovered from collateral sources such as insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, workers' compensation, or the offender.
rules.quote: Reparations otherwise payable to a claimant shall be diminished to the extent: (1) That the economic loss is recouped from collateral sources
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-712 (2025), Conditions for reparations

rules.summary: An award can be reduced by the share of responsibility for the injury the board attributes to the victim.
rules.quote: Of the degree of responsibility for the cause of the injury or death attributable to the victim, as determined by the board.
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-712 (2025), Conditions for reparations

rules.summary: Personal injury includes bodily harm, pregnancy, or mental anguish caused by a violent criminal act, which covers injury from a sexual assault committed in Arkansas.
rules.quote: “Personal injury” means actual bodily harm, including pregnancy or mental anguish which is the direct result of a violent criminal act
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-703 (2025), Definitions

rules.summary: Victims of sexual assault are named in the statute: an immediate family member of a sexual assault victim also counts as a victim.
rules.quote: Is an immediate family member of a deceased victim, a victim of sexual assault, or a child victim
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-703 (2025), Definitions

params.rule: Crimes committed in Arkansas regardless of residency; Arkansas residents injured in a state with no program they are eligible for.

rules.summary: Covers anyone injured by a crime in Arkansas, plus Arkansas residents hurt in a state with no compensation program they qualify for.
rules.quote: “Victim” means a person who suffers personal injury or death as a result of criminally injurious conduct committed either within the State of Arkansas or against any Arkansas resident who suffers personal injury as the result of criminally injurious conduct which occurs in states presently not having crime victims reparations programs for which the victim is eligible
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-703 (2025), Definitions

rules.summary: Medical care is an allowable expense.
rules.quote: “Allowable expense” means charges incurred for needed products, services, and accommodations, including, but not limited to: (i) Medical care;
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-703 (2025), Definitions

rules.summary: Mental health expenses caused by the crime are compensable.
rules.quote: Mental health expenses incurred as a result of the criminally injurious conduct of another.
rules.source_title: Code of Arkansas Rules, 16 CAR Part 60, Crime Victims Reparations Board Rules (Bureau of Legislative Research, 03/22/2026)

rules.summary: Lost income (work loss) is part of compensable economic loss. The board's rules and the application require proof that the victim was employed.
rules.quote: “Work loss” means loss of income from work the victim or claimant would have performed if the victim had not been injured or died
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-703 (2025), Definitions

params.scope: new locks and windows after a sexual assault in your own home

rules.summary: The application lists buying and installing locks and windows after a sexual assault in the victim's home as an expense that may be eligible.
rules.quote: Purchase and installation of locks and windows following a sexual assault or act of domestic abuse occurring within the victim's primary residence.
rules.pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Section H
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

params.scope: travel and lodging for criminal justice proceedings about the crime

rules.summary: The application lists travel and lodging for a criminal justice proceeding related to the crime as an expense that may be eligible.
rules.quote: Travel and lodging resulting from a criminal justice proceeding related to the victimization.
rules.pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Section H
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

params.scope: replacement services, such as child care or convalescent care

rules.summary: The application lets a victim request replacement service loss, such as child care or convalescent care.
rules.quote: Replacement Service Loss (child care, convalescent care, etc.)
rules.pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Section C
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

rules.summary: The application asks for medical expenses including hospital and doctor charges, counseling, ambulance fees, and prescription medication costs.
rules.quote: List all medical expenses incurred as a result of crime related injuries, including hospital and doctor charges, counseling expenses, ambulance fees, and prescription medication costs.
rules.pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Section C
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

rules.summary: Dental care is one of the treatment types a victim can request on the application.
rules.quote: Dental Care
rules.pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Section C
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

params.item: property crimes; pain and suffering

rules.summary: The program says it does not cover property crimes or pain and suffering. No source lists replacing stolen or damaged personal property as covered.
rules.quote: This program does not cover property crimes nor pain and suffering.
rules.source_title: Arkansas DPS, Crime Victims Reparations Board home page

params.item: noneconomic detriment (pain, suffering, inconvenience, physical impairment, nonpecuniary damage)

rules.summary: Compensable economic loss does not include noneconomic detriment such as pain, suffering, or inconvenience.
rules.quote: “Economic loss” means monetary detriment consisting of allowable expense and work loss, but shall not include noneconomic detriment
rules.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-703 (2025), Definitions

rules.summary: In its crime scene cleanup section, the application says cleaning is different from replacing property, and property replacement is prohibited.
rules.quote: Property replacement is prohibited.
rules.pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Section G
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

rules.summary: The program offers an online application, which its Documents and Forms page marks as the preferred way to apply.
rules.quote: We offer an ONLINE APPLICATION process for Victim Compensation! Access the Online Application
rules.pinpoint: CVRB home page, Crime Victim Compensation Application
rules.source_title: Arkansas DPS, Crime Victims Reparations Board home page

params.target: 322 South Main Street, Suite 615 Little Rock, AR 72201
params.note: The page says to submit the application to the reparations office and lists this as the office address; it does not say mail in so many words. The 2023 paper application and the Arkansas.gov portal page list 1 State Police Plaza Drive, Little Rock, AR 72209 instead. Call 501-682-1020 to confirm the address before mailing.

rules.summary: A paper application can be sent to the Crime Victims Reparations office, listed on the DPS site at 322 South Main Street, Suite 615, Little Rock, AR 72201.
rules.quote: Victims may apply for compensation by submitting an application to the Arkansas Crime Victim's Reparations office. Applications are available from the Arkansas Crime Victim's Reparations office or from one of Arkansas's 28 elected prosecutors. These programs are funded by fees collected from criminal offenders and a federal grant through the Victims of Crime Act, administered by the U.S. Department of Justice. Contact CVRB 322 South Main Street, Suite 615 Little Rock, AR 72201
rules.pinpoint: About CVRB page, applying and Contact CVRB
rules.source_title: Arkansas DPS, About CVRB page

params.note: Copy of the law enforcement incident report. 16 CAR 60-206(b)(2) also accepts other official documentation from the agency the crime was reported to.

rules.summary: Attach a copy of the law enforcement agency's incident report to the application.
rules.quote: NOTE: You must attach a copy of the law-enforcement agency's incident report to this application.
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

params.note: Itemized medical, dental, and counseling bills or other statements verifying expenses; the claim is not processed without them.

rules.summary: When asking for medical or counseling costs, attach copies of all itemized medical and counseling bills or other statements verifying the expenses.
rules.quote: NOTE: In addition to completing this section, you must attach copies of all itemized medical bills, mental health counseling bills, or other statements verifying expenses.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Section C, Request for Medical Treatment/Mental-Health Counseling
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

params.note: Most recent pay stub; self-employed applicants send tax returns from the last three years.

rules.summary: For lost wages, attach your most recent pay stub, or if self-employed, your tax returns from the last three years.
rules.quote: Attach a copy of your most recent pay stub from your employer. If you are self-employed, you must furnish copies of your tax returns from the last three (3) years so lost wages can be most accurately determined.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Section D, Request for Lost Wages
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

params.note: Name and address of the physician who can verify the disability period, or a copy of a recent disability statement.

rules.summary: For lost wages, give the name and address of the physician who can verify your time off, or attach a recent disability statement.
rules.quote: You must also provide the complete name and address of the physician who can verify your disability period, or you may attach a copy of a recent disability statement.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Section D, Request for Lost Wages
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

params.note: Funeral bill and death certificate, only when requesting funeral or burial expenses for a deceased victim.

rules.summary: For funeral or burial expenses, include a copy of the funeral bill and the death certificate.
rules.quote: NOTE: You must submit a copy of the funeral bill and the death certificate with this application.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Section E, Request for Funeral/Burial Expenses
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

params.note: Loss of support only: the deceased victim's last three years of tax returns, Social Security benefit verification, and proof of guardianship for a minor dependent.

rules.summary: For loss of support after a victim's death, include the victim's last three years of tax returns, Social Security benefit verification, and proof of guardianship for a minor dependent.
rules.quote: NOTE: You must attach copies of the deceased victim's last three (3) years' tax returns. You must also provide verification regarding the denial or receipt of any benefits from the Social Security Administration. You must be the legal guardian of a minor dependent to request loss of support on their behalf and must provide verification of guardianship.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Section F, Request for Loss of Support
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

params.note: Crime scene cleanup only, which the application limits to survivors or dependents of homicide victims.

rules.summary: For crime scene cleanup, attach receipts or other supporting documentation.
rules.quote: Receipts or supporting documentation must be attached to this application.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Section G, Request for Assistance with Crime Scene Clean Up
rules.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

params.agency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration, Office of Driver Services
params.enroll: Presents a valid order of protection issued under the Domestic Abuse Act of 1991, § 9-15-101 et seq. (2) Completes this ACP affidavit; and (3) Agrees to the terms of participation in the ACP.
params.note: Driver's license and ID card only, not a general substitute address for government records or mail. Eligibility is limited to victims of domestic violence and their dependents; sexual abuse counts only when caused by a family or household member or a dating partner (A.C.A. 27-16-811(a)(1)(C)), and the affidavit also lists a valid order of protection.

rules.summary: Arkansas's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the DFA Office of Driver Services, is free and puts a post office box on the driver's license or ID card instead of the home address. It is only for victims of domestic violence and their dependents, and the person must also present a valid order of protection under the Domestic Abuse Act and an affidavit. Sexual abuse counts as domestic violence only when it is by a family or household member or a dating partner.
rules.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program is a free program administered by the Office of Driver Services. Participants in tis program will be issued a driver’s license or identification card that displays a post office box in lieu of a residential address.
rules.pinpoint: DFA Address Confidentiality Program page, Program Description
rules.source_title: Arkansas DFA Office of Driver Services, Address Confidentiality Program page

rules.summary: Medical treatment documents a claimant submits with a reparations application are confidential by statute, and so are law enforcement investigative reports if another law makes them confidential. The statute does not make the whole claim file or the applicant's identity confidential.
rules.quote: When submitted to the Crime Victims Reparations Board as part of an application, the following information shall be confidential: (1) Documents submitted by a claimant which relate to medical treatment; and (2) Law enforcement investigative reports, if confidential under any other law.
rules.source_title: Arkansas DPS, CVRB Statutes compilation PDF (current through 2023 Regular Session)

params.payer: County where the offense occurred

rules.summary: The county where the offense happened pays medical or forensic exam costs to collect evidence of the sexual offenses the statute lists, or of a dangerous crime against children.
rules.quote: Any medical or forensic interview or examination expenses arising out of the need to secure evidence that a person has been the victim of a dangerous crime against children as defined in section 13-705 or a sexual offense pursuant to section 13-1404, 13-1405, 13-1406 or 13-3212 shall be paid by the county in which the offense occurred
rules.source_title: A.R.S. 13-1414 (expenses of investigation; forensic exams paid by county)

params.condition: if the county must pay for it

rules.summary: A hospital or provider may not send the patient a balance bill for a county-paid forensic exam. The statute does not say whether the patient's insurance may be billed.
rules.quote: A health care institution or health care provider may not issue, either directly or through its billing company, any additional balance bill to a patient relating to a medical or forensic interview or examination for which the county is required to pay pursuant to section 13-1414.
rules.source_title: A.R.S. 36-420.02 (no extra charges or balance bills for forensic exams)

params.condition: if the county must pay for it

rules.summary: A health care institution may not charge the patient intake, consultation, facility, or other fees as part of a county-paid forensic exam.
rules.quote: A health care institution may not charge an intake, consultation, facility or other fee to a patient as part of a medical or forensic interview or examination for which the county is required to pay pursuant to section 13-1414.
rules.source_title: A.R.S. 36-420.02 (no extra charges or balance bills for forensic exams)

rules.summary: The maximum award is $25,000 per claim for all economic loss from one incident; each eligible person files a separate claim.
rules.quote: Twenty-five thousand dollars for all economic loss submitted under a claim as a result of an incident of criminally injurious conduct;
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Mental health counseling and care is capped at $5,000 per victim or derivative victim.
rules.quote: For mental health counseling and care expenses, $5,000 per victim or derivative victim;
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Work loss is limited each calendar week to the pay for 40 hours at the current minimum wage.
rules.quote: are limited to an amount per calendar week equal to 40 hours at the current minimum wage
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Transportation costs are capped at $2,000 per victim or derivative victim, paid as reimbursement of actual costs.
rules.quote: For transportation costs, $2,000 per victim or derivative victim paid as reimbursement of actual transportation expenses.
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $2,000 for professional cleanup, of which up to $500 may go to cleanup not done by a professional service.
rules.quote: For crime scene cleanup expenses, $2,000 for cleanup provided by a professional service, of which $500 may be for crime scene cleanup not provided by a professional service
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Funeral expenses are capped at $10,000.
rules.quote: For funeral expenses, $10,000;
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Reasonable and customary medical expenses from the victim's injury or condition are covered.
rules.quote: Reasonable and customary medical expenses due to the victim's physical injury, medical condition, mental health condition, or death.
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Mental health counseling and care for the victim's or derivative victim's mental distress from the crime is covered, from a licensed or authorized provider.
rules.quote: Reasonable and customary mental health counseling and care expenses due to a victim's or derivative victim's mental distress resulting from the criminally injurious conduct
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Work loss is covered when the crime's physical injury, mental distress, or medical condition reduces the victim's ability to work.
rules.quote: A victim whose ability to work is reduced due to physical injury, mental distress, or medical condition resulting from the criminally injurious conduct;
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

params.scope: trips to medical care, counseling, or court

rules.summary: Transportation to medical care, to mental health counseling, and to criminal court proceedings, clemency or parole hearings, or an execution related to the crime is covered.
rules.quote: Obtaining medical care as defined in subsection (C)(1), b. Obtaining mental health counseling and care as defined in subsection (C)(4), c. A victim or derivative victim attending a criminal court proceeding, clemency hearing, parole hearing, or execution directly related to the incident of criminally injurious conduct
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

params.scope: trips to a forensic exam or interview

rules.summary: Transportation to get a medical forensic exam or forensic interview is covered.
rules.quote: The victim obtaining a medical forensic examination or participating in a medical forensic interview
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is covered for sexual assault, homicide, and aggravated assault.
rules.quote: Reasonable and customary crime scene cleanup expenses due to a victim's homicide, aggravated assault, or sexual assault
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup includes repairing or replacing exterior doors, locks, or windows damaged by the crime at a residence.
rules.quote: Repairing or replacing exterior doors, locks, or windows damaged as a direct result of criminally injurious conduct occurring within a residence or the surrounding curtilage.
rules.pinpoint: A.A.C. R10-4-101(8)(b); covered for sexual assault under R10-4-108(C)(5)
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

params.scope: trips to respond to a substantiated threat to the victim's safety

rules.summary: Transportation costs for responding to a substantiated threat to the victim's safety or well-being are covered, within the transportation cap.
rules.quote: Responding to a substantiated threat to the safety or well-being of the victim or a derivative victim
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Medical expense includes repairing a victim's prosthetic device, eyeglasses or corrective lenses, or dental device.
rules.quote: Repair of damage to a victim's prosthetic device, eyeglasses or other corrective lenses, or a dental device
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

params.item: Property loss or repair

rules.summary: The brochure says property loss or repair is not covered, nor are attorney fees or pain and suffering. The current rules still pay to repair a victim's eyeglasses, prosthetic or dental device (as medical) and damaged exterior doors, locks or windows at a residence (as crime scene cleanup).
rules.quote: The Program cannot consider claims for: • Attorney Fees • Property Loss or Repair • Pain and Suffering
rules.source_title: ACJC Victim Compensation brochure (English)

rules.summary: Attorney's fees are not paid.
rules.quote: The Board shall not make a compensation award to pay attorney's fees incurred by a victim or claimant.
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: The claim must be submitted within two years after the crime is discovered.
rules.quote: A claim, as described in R10-4-107, was submitted to the operational unit within two years after discovery of the criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: The Board must give more time to file if it finds good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: The Board shall extend the time limits under subsections (A)(4) and (A)(7) if the Board determines there is good cause for a delay.
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

params.exception: counted from when the crime was discovered

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours after it is discovered.
rules.quote: The criminally injurious conduct was reported to an appropriate law enforcement authority within 72 hours after its discovery;
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

params.exception: or later if the Board finds good cause

rules.summary: The Board must extend both the reporting time limit and the filing deadline when there is good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: The Board shall extend the time limits under subsections (A)(4) and (A)(7) if the Board determines there is good cause for a delay.
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: The Board must deny an award if it finds the victim or claimant did not fully cooperate with law enforcement, unless a substantial medical, mental health, or safety risk was the reason. To decide, the Board looks at things like whether the victim or claimant failed to help the prosecution or failed to appear as a witness for it.
rules.quote: The Board shall deny a compensation award to a claimant if: 1. The Board determines that the victim or claimant did not cooperate fully with the appropriate law enforcement agency and the failure to cooperate fully was not due to a substantial medical, mental health, or safety risk. The Board shall use the following criteria to determine whether failure to cooperate fully with law enforcement warrants that a claim be denied: a. The victim or claimant failed to assist in the prosecution of a person who engaged in the criminally injurious conduct or failed to appear as a witness for the prosecution;
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: The award is denied or reduced when the loss was or can be recovered from insurance, a government benefit, or another collateral source.
rules.quote: The Board shall deny or reduce a compensation award to a claimant if: 1. The victim or claimant has recouped or is eligible to recoup the economic loss from an obtainable and accessible collateral source, including benefits from a federal or federally financed program;
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: An award may be denied or reduced in proportion to how much the Board finds the victim responsible for the incident.
rules.quote: The Board shall deny or reduce a compensation award under subsection (F)(3) in proportion to the degree to which the Board determines the victim is responsible for the incident of criminally injurious conduct that is the subject of the claim.
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: A county program may grant one emergency award of up to $1,000 for serious hardship; it is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: An operational unit that makes an emergency compensation award shall ensure that the emergency compensation award does not exceed $1,000.
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

rules.summary: Any state or federal crime that poses a substantial threat of injury, mental distress, or death qualifies, whether or not the offender is caught, charged, or convicted.
rules.quote: Constitutes a crime as defined by state or federal law regardless of whether the perpetrator of the conduct is apprehended, charged, or convicted;
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

params.rule: Crimes in Arizona qualify for anyone; Arizona residents hurt outside Arizona qualify only where no accessible compensation program exists.

rules.summary: The crime must have happened in Arizona, or outside Arizona to an Arizona resident in a place without an accessible compensation program.
rules.quote: Occurred in Arizona; or b. Occurred outside of Arizona in an area without an accessible crime compensation program and affected a resident;
rules.source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1
