params.enroll: Applicants do not enroll or apply directly with the Arizona Address Confidentiality Program. Any person interested in applying to the program must meet in person with a registered Application Assistant.

rules.summary: Arizona's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Secretary of State, gives victims of sexual offenses, domestic violence, and stalking a substitute address and confidential mail forwarding. It is meant to help keep them from being found through public records by the person they are trying to stay safe from.
rules.quote: The Arizona Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) is a program that helps victims of domestic violence, sexual offenses, and/or stalking from being located by the person they are seeking safety from through public records. The program provides a substitute address and confidential mail forwarding services to individuals and families across Arizona.
rules.pinpoint: Arizona SOS About ACP page, opening paragraph; statutory basis A.R.S. 41-161 to 41-169
rules.source_title: Arizona Secretary of State: About ACP (Address Confidentiality Program)

rules.summary: The costs of a sexual assault medical evidentiary exam may not be charged to the survivor, directly or indirectly.
rules.quote: Costs incurred by a qualified health care professional, hospital, clinic, sexual assault forensic examination team, or other emergency medical facility for a medical evidentiary examination of a victim of a sexual assault, as described in the protocol developed pursuant to Section 13823.5, when the examination is performed pursuant to Sections 13823.5 and 13823.7, shall not be charged directly or indirectly to the victim of the assault.
rules.source_title: Cal. Penal Code 13823.95 (sexual assault medical evidentiary exam costs), via Justia 2025 California Code

params.payer: The local law enforcement agency in whose jurisdiction the offense was committed (treated as a local cost)

rules.summary: The exam is a local cost, billed to and paid within 60 days by the local law enforcement agency where the offense happened.
rules.quote: The cost of a medical evidentiary examination performed by a qualified health care professional, hospital, or other emergency medical facility for a victim of a sexual assault shall be treated as a local cost and charged to and reimbursed within 60 days by the local law enforcement agency in whose jurisdiction the alleged offense was committed.
rules.source_title: Cal. Penal Code 13823.95 (sexual assault medical evidentiary exam costs), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: CalVCB can pay a victim at most $70,000 in total.
rules.quote: The most CalVCB can reimburse a victim for is $70,000.
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, What Is Covered, Limits: Dollar limits
rules.source_title: CalVCB: What Is Covered

rules.summary: A victim can be reimbursed up to $10,000 for outpatient mental health counseling; the board may approve more in dire or exceptional circumstances.
rules.quote: The following persons may be reimbursed for the expense of their outpatient mental health counseling in an amount not to exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000): (i) A victim.
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13957 (scope of compensation, caps), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: Peer counseling from a rape crisis center is paid at no more than $15 per hour, and only for in-person counseling for up to 10 weeks plus one series of support group sessions.
rules.quote: Payments for peer counseling services provided by a rape crisis center may not exceed fifteen dollars ($15) for each hour of services provided. Those services shall be limited to in-person counseling for a period not to exceed 10 weeks plus one series of facilitated support group counseling sessions.
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13957.7 (bill deadline, peer counseling rate), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: CalVCB's current Benefit Reference Guide lists mental health treatment for a direct victim as up to 60 sessions and $10,000.
rules.quote: Up to 60 sessions and $10,000 as detailed below
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB Benefit Reference Guide (Rev. 05/2025), Mental Health Treatment
rules.source_title: CalVCB Benefit Reference Guide (Rev. 05/2025)

rules.summary: Relocation can be paid up to $3,418 when law enforcement finds it necessary for safety or a mental health provider finds it necessary for emotional well-being.
rules.quote: Authorize a cash payment or reimbursement not to exceed three thousand four hundred and eighteen dollars ($3,418) to a victim for expenses incurred in relocating, if the expenses are determined by law enforcement to be necessary for the personal safety of the victim or by a mental health treatment provider to be necessary for the emotional well-being of the victim.
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13957 (scope of compensation, caps), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: If you get relocation money and you know who the offender is, you must agree not to tell that person where you now live and not to let them in your home, or agree to seek a restraining order. You may have to pay the money back if you break this agreement.
rules.quote: When a relocation payment or reimbursement is provided to a victim of sexual assault or domestic violence and the identity of the offender is known to the victim, the victim shall agree not to inform the offender of the location of the victim’s new residence and not to allow the offender on the premises at any time, or shall agree to seek a restraining order against the offender. A victim may be required to repay the relocation payment or reimbursement to the board if the victim violates the terms set forth in this paragraph.
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13957 (scope of compensation, caps), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: Installing or increasing home security is covered up to $1,000.
rules.quote: Reimburse the expense of installing or increasing residential security, not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000).
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13957 (scope of compensation, caps), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: Medical and medical-related expenses from a licensed medical provider are reimbursable, subject to board rate limits.
rules.quote: Subject to the limitations set forth in Section 13957.2, reimburse the amount of medical or medical-related expenses incurred by the victim for services that were provided by a licensed medical provider
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13957 (scope of compensation, caps), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: Lost income caused by the victim's injury can be compensated, subject to the limits in Gov. Code 13957.5.
rules.quote: Subject to the limitations set forth in Section 13957.5, authorize compensation equal to the loss of income or loss of support, or both, that a victim or derivative victim incurs as a direct result of the victim's or derivative victim's injury or the victim's death.
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13957 (scope of compensation, caps), via Justia 2025 California Code

params.scope: round-trip mileage to medical, dental, or mental health appointments

rules.summary: Round-trip mileage to medical, dental, or mental health appointments is reimbursable.
rules.quote: Round trip mileage costs to medical, dental, or mental health appointments
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, What Is Covered, Eligible expenses
rules.source_title: CalVCB: What Is Covered

params.item: Personal property losses, except medically necessary items like eyeglasses and hearing aids

rules.summary: CalVCB does not reimburse personal property losses, except medically necessary items like eyeglasses and hearing aids.
rules.quote: Personal property losses, except for medically necessary items like eyeglasses and hearing aids
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, What Is Covered, Non-eligible expenses
rules.source_title: CalVCB: What Is Covered

params.item: Pain and suffering

rules.summary: CalVCB does not pay compensation for pain and suffering.
rules.quote: Compensation for pain and suffering
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, What Is Covered, Non-eligible expenses
rules.source_title: CalVCB: What Is Covered

params.item: Bills submitted more than three years after the expense was incurred, unless the victim still owes the debt or already paid it for a timely or approved application

rules.summary: A bill generally must be submitted within three years of when the expense was incurred, with exceptions when the victim still owes or already paid it.
rules.quote: No reimbursement may be made for any expense that is submitted more than three years after it is incurred by the victim or derivative victim.
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13957.7 (bill deadline, peer counseling rate), via Justia 2025 California Code

params.extension: or later if you were under 21 or could not reasonably have known of the harm until later

rules.summary: Apply within 7 years of the crime, 7 years after turning 21, or 7 years from when the injury from the crime was or could have been discovered, whichever is later.
rules.quote: An application for compensation shall be filed within seven years of the date of the crime, seven years after the victim attains 21 years of age, or seven years of the time the victim or derivative victim knew or in the exercise of ordinary diligence could have discovered that an injury or death had been sustained as a direct result of crime, whichever is later.
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13953 (filing deadline), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: The board may give you more time to apply for good cause.
rules.quote: The board may for good cause grant an extension of the time period in subdivision (a).
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13953 (filing deadline), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: A sexual assault claim cannot be denied only because no police report was made; medical records, mental health records, or a sexual assault exam can show the crime happened.
rules.quote: An application for a claim based on a sexual assault shall not be denied solely because a police report was not made by the victim. The board shall adopt guidelines that allow it to consider and approve applications for assistance based on a sexual assault relying upon evidence other than a police report to establish that a sexual assault crime has occurred. Factors evidencing that a sexual assault crime has occurred may include, but are not limited to, medical records documenting injuries consistent with allegations of sexual assault, mental health records, or that the victim received a sexual assault examination.
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13956 (denial grounds, police report, cooperation), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: Board rules list other evidence the board may consider. One is a letter from a sexual assault counselor, licensed therapist, or mental health provider saying you are seeking services related to the sexual assault. Another is a court restraining order against the person who assaulted you.
rules.quote: A letter or other written statement from a sexual assault counselor, as defined in Section 1035.2 of the Evidence Code, licensed therapist, or mental health provider, stating that the victim is seeking services related to the allegation of sexual assault. (5) A restraining order from a court against the perpetrator of the sexual assault.
rules.source_title: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2, 649.49 (evidence of a sexual assault qualifying crime), via Cornell LII

rules.summary: Delaying a report of a sexual assault is not, by itself, a failure to cooperate with law enforcement.
rules.quote: Lack of cooperation shall also not be found solely because a victim of sexual assault, domestic violence, or human trafficking delayed reporting the qualifying crime.
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13956 (denial grounds, police report, cooperation), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: CalVCB pays last, only for expenses not reimbursed by insurance or any other source.
rules.quote: CalVCB is a payor of last resort. This means CalVCB pays only for expenses that aren't reimbursed by any other source.
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, What Is Covered, Payor of last resort
rules.source_title: CalVCB: What Is Covered

rules.summary: An application may be denied in whole or in part based on the applicant's involvement in the events leading to the crime.
rules.quote: An application may be denied, in whole or in part, if the board finds that denial is appropriate because of the nature of the victim's or other applicant's involvement in the events leading to the crime
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13956 (denial grounds, police report, cooperation), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: An emergency award is available to someone who is eligible for compensation if the board decides it is needed to avoid or ease substantial hardship from waiting for a final decision on the application.
rules.quote: An emergency award shall be available to a person eligible for compensation pursuant to this chapter if the board determines that such an award is necessary to avoid or mitigate substantial hardship that may result from delaying compensation until complete and final consideration of an application.
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13952.5 (emergency awards), via Justia 2025 California Code

rules.summary: Rape, sexual assault, and sexual battery are listed among the crimes CalVCB covers.
rules.quote: Rape Robbery Sexual assault Stalking Sexual battery
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, Who Is Eligible, Crimes covered
rules.source_title: CalVCB: Who Is Eligible

rules.summary: For listed sex crimes, including rape under Penal Code 261, emotional injury alone can qualify.
rules.quote: Emotional injury, where the crime was a violation of any of the following provisions: (A) Section 236.1, 261, former Section 262, 271, 273a, 273d, 285, 286, 287, 288, former Section 288a, Section 288.5, 289, or 653.2
rules.source_title: Cal. Gov. Code 13955 (eligibility), via Justia 2025 California Code

params.rule: California residents (wherever the crime happened) and non-residents victimized in California

rules.summary: Victims must have been California residents at the time of the crime, or non-residents victimized in California.
rules.quote: A California resident at the time of the crime, or A non-resident victimized in California.
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB, Who Is Eligible, Eligibility criteria
rules.source_title: CalVCB: Who Is Eligible

rules.quote:
or
deliver to your local Victim Witness Assistance Center

rules.summary: Apply online by creating a CalVCB Online account and starting a new application in English or Spanish.
rules.quote: To apply online: Create a CalVCB Online account or login Start a new application (in English or Spanish)
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB How To Get Compensated, Steps to apply, Step 2

params.note: Copies of crime-related bills, or a list of them, attached to the application.

rules.summary: Attach copies of crime-related bills, or a list of them, to the application.
rules.quote: Please attach copies, or a list, of any crime-related bills.
rules.source_title: CalVCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Form VCGCB-VCP-005 (Rev. 10/2017)

params.note: Copies of insurance documentation; Section 9 also asks for insurance details because CalVCB is the payer of last resort.

rules.summary: Attach copies of supporting documents, including crime-related bills and insurance papers. Keep the originals.
rules.quote: Attach copies of any documentation that supports your application for crime victim compensation, including copies of crimerelated bills, insurance, or anything relating to the crime. Save original documents for your records.
rules.source_title: CalVCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Form VCGCB-VCP-005 (Rev. 10/2017)

params.note: Include a copy if one exists; CalVCB says it speeds processing. Not reporting is not by itself grounds for denial in a sexual assault claim.

rules.summary: CalVCB says including copies of crime reports, bills, and receipts gets a claim processed faster.
rules.quote: To get a claim processed faster, applicants should: Complete every section of the application Include copies of crime reports, bills, receipts, and other related documents
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB How To Get Compensated, How we review your application
rules.source_title: CalVCB: How To Get Compensated

params.note: Copies of receipts for crime-related costs.

rules.summary: Include copies of receipts for crime-related costs with the application.
rules.quote: Include copies of crime reports, bills, receipts, and other related documents
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB How To Get Compensated, How we review your application
rules.source_title: CalVCB: How To Get Compensated

params.note: For income loss: a tax return, pay stub, or employer statement.

rules.summary: For income loss, CalVCB asks for proof of income such as a tax return, pay stub, or employer statement.
rules.quote: Proof of income (tax return, pay stub, or statement from an employer).
rules.pinpoint: Benefit Reference Guide (Rev. 05/2025), Income Loss, Examples of What We Need
rules.source_title: CalVCB Benefit Reference Guide (Rev. 05/2025)

params.note: For income loss: a disability statement from a medical or mental health provider.

rules.summary: For income loss, CalVCB asks for a disability statement from a medical or mental health provider.
rules.quote: A disability statement from a medical or mental health provider.
rules.pinpoint: Benefit Reference Guide (Rev. 05/2025), Income Loss, Examples of What We Need
rules.source_title: CalVCB Benefit Reference Guide (Rev. 05/2025)

params.note: For medical and dental expenses: the crime report or medical or dental records showing the services were needed.

rules.quote: Proof from the crime report or medical/dental records that medical/dental services are required.
rules.pinpoint: Benefit Reference Guide (Rev. 05/2025), Medical and Dental Expenses, Examples of What We Need
rules.source_title: CalVCB Benefit Reference Guide (Rev. 05/2025)

params.note: For mental health treatment: itemized receipts, plus a Mental Health Billing Intake form from the provider with the first bill.

rules.quote:
Itemized receipts for mental health treatment received. Providers may also bill CalVCB directly.

rules.summary: CalVCB says applications can take 90 days to process.
rules.quote: Applications can take 90 days to process.
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB How To Get Compensated, Step 3
rules.source_title: CalVCB: How To Get Compensated

params.note: Emergency awards only

rules.summary: Qualifying emergency awards are generally paid within 30 calendar days of receiving the application.
rules.quote: Qualifying emergency awards are generally paid within 30 calendar days of receipt of the application.
rules.pinpoint: Form VCGCB-VCP-005 (Rev. 10/2017), Section 4, Emergency Award Request
rules.source_title: CalVCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Form VCGCB-VCP-005 (Rev. 10/2017)

params.enroll: An application shall be completed in person at a community-based victims' assistance program or a community-based assistance program that serves victims of elder or dependent adult abuse pursuant to the Elder Abuse and Dependent Adult Civil Protection Act (Chapter 11 (commencing with Section 15600) of Part 3 of Division 9 of the Welfare and Institutions Code). The application process shall include a requirement that the applicant meet with a victims' assistance counselor and receive orientation information about the program.

rules.summary: Safe at Home, run by the California Secretary of State, gives survivors of sexual assault and other listed crimes a substitute mailing address that state, county, and city agencies accept in place of a home address.
rules.quote: Safe at Home offers a substitute mailing address to receive first class, certified, and registered mail for victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, child abduction, and elder or dependent adult abuse.
rules.pinpoint: Secretary of State, Safe at Home page, 'What is the Safe at Home program?'
rules.source_title: California Secretary of State: Safe at Home

rules.summary: CalVCB says the information in a claim, including medical information, is strictly confidential and is shared only with the applicant's written permission or when the law requires it.
rules.quote: The information you share with CalVCB is strictly confidential.
rules.pinpoint: CalVCB Confidentiality page, 'Your claim is confidential'
rules.source_title: CalVCB: Confidentiality

params.scope: the evidence part of a forensic exam

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor does not pay for the evidence-collection forensic medical exam, even if they do not want to take part in the criminal justice process or cooperate with law enforcement. The DCJ SAVE page reads this as the evidence-collection portion of the exam; other exam-related medical costs go through SAVE or Victim Compensation, not this rule.
rules.quote: A victim of a sexual offense shall not bear the cost of a forensic medical examination that includes the collection of evidence that is used for the purpose of evidence collection even if the victim does not want to participate in the criminal justice system or otherwise cooperate with the law enforcement agency, prosecuting officer, or other government official.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 18-3-407.5 (Victim evidence, forensic medical examination costs), via Justia

params.payer: Colorado Division of Criminal Justice (Department of Public Safety)

rules.summary: When the survivor does not take part in the criminal justice process, the Colorado Division of Criminal Justice pays for the evidence-collection part of the exam.
rules.quote: The division of criminal justice in the department of public safety shall pay the cost of the examination.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 18-3-407.5 (Victim evidence, forensic medical examination costs), via Justia

params.payer: Law enforcement agency with jurisdiction over the assault

rules.summary: When the survivor reports to police, the law enforcement agency with jurisdiction pays the direct costs of forensic evidence collection.
rules.quote: A law enforcement agency with jurisdiction over a sexual assault must pay for any direct cost associated with the collection of forensic evidence from a victim who reports the assault to the law enforcement agency.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 18-3-407.5 (Victim evidence, forensic medical examination costs), via Justia

params.payer: Sexual Assault Victim Emergency Payment (SAVE) program, Colorado Division of Criminal Justice

rules.summary: The state's SAVE program must pay medical costs that come with getting the forensic exam. These include emergency room, lab, medicine, and doctor fees. It pays as long as it has the money.
rules.quote: The program must cover medical fees and costs associated with obtaining the medical forensic examination, including but not limited to emergency department fees and costs, laboratory fees, prescription medication, and physician's fees, as long as funds are available.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 18-3-407.7 (Sexual assault victim emergency payment program), via Justia

params.payer: SAVE program, for medical and anonymous reporting victims only

rules.summary: The DCJ SAVE page states a per-incident cap of $4,000 for FY 2026, covering the exam and related medical costs, for survivors who make a medical or anonymous report. The cap can change with available funds. Colorado's FY 2026 ended in June, and the page as retrieved in October still showed this figure, so the cap for the current year should be confirmed with DCJ.
rules.quote: For FY (fiscal year) 2026, the current per incident cap payable by the SAVE program is $4,000.
rules.source_title: Colorado DCJ OVP: Sexual Assault Victim Emergency Payment Program (SAVE)

params.payer: SAVE program pays deductibles and co-pays for medical or anonymous reports

rules.summary: For medical or anonymous reports, SAVE pays the survivor's insurance deductibles and co-pays.
rules.quote: If the victim makes an anonymous or medical report, the SAVE program will pay for insurance deductibles and co-pays.
rules.pinpoint: DCJ SAVE program page, How Are Medical Forensic Exams Paid For
rules.source_title: Colorado DCJ OVP: Sexual Assault Victim Emergency Payment Program (SAVE)

params.payer: The survivor's insurance, if the survivor asks; the patient owes any balance after SAVE pays up to its cap

rules.summary: If the survivor has insurance and asks for it to be billed, the hospital bills that insurance for related costs. After SAVE has paid the hospital for eligible costs, up to its cap, the patient must pay any balance left.
rules.quote: If the victim has insurance and requests that their insurance is billed, the hospital bills the survivor's insurance for related costs. If the victim makes an anonymous or medical report, the SAVE program will pay for insurance deductibles and co-pays. After the SAVE program has paid the hospital for eligible medical expenses (up to the cap), the patient is responsible for paying any outstanding balances.
rules.pinpoint: DCJ SAVE program page, How Are Medical Forensic Exams Paid For
rules.source_title: Colorado DCJ OVP: Sexual Assault Victim Emergency Payment Program (SAVE)

rules.summary: Total compensation is capped at $30,000 per victim (losses above that are not compensable).
rules.quote: Aggregate damages to the victim or to the dependents of a victim exceeding thirty thousand dollars
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

rules.summary: Reasonable medical and hospital costs, and medically necessary devices such as eyeglasses or hearing aids, are covered.
rules.quote: Reasonable medical and hospital expenses and expenses incurred for dentures, eyeglasses, hearing aids, or other prosthetic or medically necessary devices;
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

rules.summary: Lost earnings are covered.
rules.quote: Loss of earnings;
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

rules.summary: Mental health counseling is covered.
rules.quote: Mental health counseling;
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

params.scope: trips for medical care, counseling, a funeral, or burial

rules.summary: Reasonable travel costs for medical care, mental health counseling, a funeral, or burial are covered.
rules.quote: Reasonable travel expenses for a victim related to funeral, burial, medical care, or mental health counseling;
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

params.scope: moving costs needed for your safety

rules.summary: Reasonable relocation costs needed for the victim's safety are covered.
rules.quote: Reasonable relocation expenses for a victim to relocate as necessary to ensure the victim's safety.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

rules.summary: Dependent care services are covered.
rules.quote: Dependent care services; and
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

rules.summary: Changes to the victim's home needed for safety are covered.
rules.quote: Any modification to the victim's residence that is necessary to ensure victim safety;
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

rules.summary: Rekeying a car or other lock for the victim's safety is covered.
rules.quote: The rekeying of a motor vehicle or other lock that is necessary to ensure the victim's safety;
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

rules.summary: Funeral and burial costs are covered.
rules.quote: Funeral and burial expenses;
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

params.item: pain and suffering; property damage other than the items listed in 24-4.1-109(1.5)(a) (residential repair or replacement, insurance deductibles, residence safety changes, rekeying, certain towing or impound fees, and medically necessary devices)

rules.summary: Pain and suffering is not paid. Property damage is paid only for the items the law lists: fixing or replacing a home's damaged doors, windows, locks, or other security devices; the deductible on a home or car insurance policy; safety changes to the home; rekeying a car or other lock for safety; towing or impound of a car that police say is where the crime happened; and medically necessary devices, like eyeglasses, that were damaged or stolen. Other belongings, such as a phone, are not covered.
rules.quote: Pain and suffering or property damage expenses other than those specified in subsection (1.5)(a) of this section;
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

params.item: motor vehicle expenses other than an insurance deductible or safety rekeying

rules.summary: Motor vehicle costs are not covered beyond an insurance deductible and safety rekeying.
rules.quote: Motor vehicle expenses other than those specified in subsections (1.5)(a)(I)(B) and (1.5)(a)(III) of this section.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-109 (Losses compensable), via Justia

rules.summary: Law enforcement must be notified, but documentation that a forensic exam was done by a licensed or registered nurse or medical provider satisfies this requirement. The board may also waive it in the interest of justice.
rules.quote: The requirement to notify the appropriate law enforcement officials required by this subsection (1)(b) is satisfied if, as the result of the compensable crime that the application is being submitted for, the victim or applicant provides documentation that a forensic examination was conducted by a licensed or registered nurse or medical provider.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-108 (Approving compensation), via Justia

params.scope: property damage claims

rules.summary: For a property damage claim, police must have been told about the crime within 72 hours, unless the board finds good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: The appropriate law enforcement officials were notified of the perpetration of the crime causing property damage within seventy-two hours after its perpetration, unless the board finds good cause exists for the failure of notification;
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-108 (Approving compensation), via Justia

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: To be approved, you must also have cooperated reasonably with law enforcement in catching and prosecuting the assailant. The board can find good cause for not cooperating.
rules.quote: The applicant has cooperated reasonably with law enforcement officials in the apprehension and prosecution of the assailant, or the board has found good cause exists for the failure to cooperate
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-108 (Approving compensation), via Justia

rules.summary: Property damage claims must be filed within 6 months of the damage, unless the board allows more time for good cause.
rules.quote: The application for approval of compensation for property damage under this part 1 is filed with the board within six months of the date of property damage or within such further extension of time as the board, for good cause shown, allows.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-108 (Approving compensation), via Justia

rules.summary: Compensation pays only after insurance, public benefits, offender payments, and other sources; the board may deduct those payments from an award.
rules.quote: The fund is the payer of last resort.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-110 (Recovery from collateral source), via Justia

rules.summary: An award requires that the injury was not substantially caused by the victim's own wrongful act or substantial provocation; the same section also lets the board reduce an award in the interest of justice.
rules.quote: The death of or injury to the victim was not substantially attributable to the victim's wrongful act or substantial provocation of the victim's assailant; and
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-108 (Approving compensation), via Justia

rules.summary: A local board may approve an emergency payment before the final decision if waiting would cause undue hardship; the amount follows each board's policy and is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: The board may order an emergency approval to the applicant pending a final decision in the claim if it appears to the board, prior to taking action upon the claim, that undue hardship will result to the applicant if immediate payment is not made.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-112 (Emergency approvals), via Justia

rules.summary: Sexual assault is a listed crime, and the compensation definitions make listed crimes compensable.
rules.quote: (n) (I) Sexual assault, in violation of section 18-3-402, C. R. S.;
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-302 (Definitions, list of crimes), via Justia

params.rule: Crimes committed in Colorado (any victim); Colorado residents victimized out of state only where no reasonably accessible program exists there

rules.summary: Anyone hurt by a compensable crime committed in Colorado can apply; Colorado residents hurt elsewhere can apply only if that state or country has no reasonably accessible program they qualify for.
rules.quote: “Victim” also means a person who is a resident of this state and who is a victim of a crime that occurred outside of this state, where the crime would be a compensable crime had it occurred in this state and where the state or country in which the crime occurred does not have a reasonably accessible crime victim compensation program for which the person would be eligible.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-102 (Definitions), via Justia

params.note: Colorado has no central mailing address. Send the application to the Victim Compensation Administrator in the judicial district where the crime occurred; district addresses are listed on the DCJ Crime Victim Compensation page (CO-S1).

rules.summary: Download and fill out the state application and send it to the victim compensation administrator for the judicial district where the crime occurred.
rules.quote: You can also download and fill out this Victim Compensation Application (PDF) and send it to the appropriate administrator.
rules.pinpoint: DCJ How to File a Claim page, How to File a Claim section
rules.source_title: Colorado DCJ: How to File a Claim for Victim Compensation

params.note: Completed application with every question answered (N/A where not applicable), signed by the victim or claimant.

rules.summary: Answer every question on the application, writing N/A where a question does not apply.
rules.quote: Please complete every question. Write N/A if the question is not applicable.
rules.source_title: Colorado Victim Compensation Application (state form, dated 2016)

params.note: Copies of itemized crime-related bills (medical, counseling, funeral, property) with the application; send later bills as they arrive.

rules.summary: Include copies of itemized bills with the application and forward more crime-related bills as they come in.
rules.quote: INCLUDE COPIES OF ITEMIZED BILLS WITH THIS APPLICATION. PLEASE FORWARD ADDITIONAL CRIME RELATED BILLS AS YOU RECEIVE THEM.
rules.source_title: Colorado Victim Compensation Application (state form, dated 2016)

params.note: The current DCJ page also says to submit itemized bills with the application; districts may ask for more.

rules.summary: Submit the application together with itemized bills directly related to the crime, in the district where the crime occurred.
rules.quote: Submit the application and itemized bills directly related to the crime in the district where the crime occurred.
rules.pinpoint: DCJ How to File a Claim page, How to File a Claim section
rules.source_title: Colorado DCJ: How to File a Claim for Victim Compensation

params.note: Attach receipts along with bills; the application can be filed before any bills arrive.

rules.summary: Attach all bills and receipts; you can apply even if no bills have arrived yet.
rules.quote: Please attach all bills and receipts. You may apply even if you have not received any bills as of this date.
rules.source_title: Colorado Victim Compensation Application (state form, dated 2016)

params.note: Section 5 asks for insurance and other payer details (company, policy number, phone) for anyone claiming medical bills; it is information on the form rather than a separate document.

rules.summary: Anyone claiming medical bills must fill in insurance and other payment sources on the application.
rules.quote: All applicants seeking compensation for medical bills must complete the following information on insurance and other sources available to pay medical bills.
rules.source_title: Colorado Victim Compensation Application (state form, dated 2016)

params.note: Only if there is a civil lawsuit: written evidence of the settlement amount and terms.

rules.summary: If there is a civil action, the board must be told and given written evidence of any settlement.
rules.quote: The Crime Victim Compensation Board must be notified of any civil action and be provided with written evidence of the amount and terms of settlement.
rules.source_title: Colorado Victim Compensation Application (state form, dated 2016)

params.note: Generally 30 to 45 days to be notified of the decision; varies by district.

rules.summary: Processing time differs by district, but notice of the decision generally takes 30-45 days.
rules.quote: The processing time is different for each district, however, it generally takes 30-45 days to be notified of the program's decision.
rules.pinpoint: DCJ How to File a Claim page, How to File a Claim section
rules.source_title: Colorado DCJ: How to File a Claim for Victim Compensation

params.agency: Colorado Department of Personnel & Administration, Division of Central Services
params.enroll: To begin the enrollment process, meet with a certified Application Assistant. Visit the Application Center Locations page to view a listing of available Application Assistants. Only AAs can make ACP referrals and submit ACP applications.

rules.summary: Colorado's Address Confidentiality Program gives enrolled survivors of sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, and domestic violence a legal substitute address and mail forwarding, and all state and local government agencies must accept a participant's substitute address.
rules.quote: The Colorado Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) is a statewide program that provides protected healthcare workers and survivors of stalking/harassment, sexual assault, human trafficking, and domestic violence with a legal substitute address and mail forwarding. Under Colorado law, all state and local government agencies must accept a participant’s substitute address.
rules.pinpoint: DCS Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) page, introduction
rules.source_title: Colorado DPA Division of Central Services: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

rules.summary: By statute, any records, claims, or information a district board or district attorney receives, makes, or keeps to process a crime victim compensation claim are confidential.
rules.quote: Any materials received, made, or kept by a board or a district attorney to process a claim on behalf of a crime victim under this article are confidential.
rules.source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-107.5 (Confidentiality of materials), via Justia

rules.summary: No cost of a sexual assault evidence collection exam, including pregnancy and STI testing and preventive treatment under the state protocol, may be charged directly or indirectly to the survivor.
rules.quote: No costs incurred by a health care facility for the examination of a victim of sexual assault, when such examination is performed for the purpose of gathering evidence as prescribed in the protocol, including the costs of testing for pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases and the costs of prophylactic treatment as provided in the protocol, and no costs incurred for a medical forensic assessment interview conducted by a health care facility or provider or by an examiner working in conjunction with a multidisciplinary team established pursuant to section 17a-106a or with a child advocacy center, shall be charged directly or indirectly to such victim.
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 368a, including sec. 19a-112a (sexual assault evidence collection costs)

params.payer: Forensic Sex Evidence Exams account, Connecticut Judicial Department

rules.summary: Exam costs are charged to the Forensic Sex Evidence Exams account in the Judicial Department.
rules.quote: Any such costs shall be charged to the Forensic Sex Evidence Exams account in the Judicial Department.
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 368a, including sec. 19a-112a (sexual assault evidence collection costs)

rules.summary: Toxicology screening done under the protocol may not be charged to the survivor; the state Division of Scientific Services pays.
rules.quote: No costs incurred by a health care facility for any toxicology screening of a victim of sexual assault, when such screening is performed as prescribed in the protocol, shall be charged directly or indirectly to such victim. Any such costs shall be charged to the Division of Scientific Services within the Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection.
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 368a, including sec. 19a-112a (sexual assault evidence collection costs)

params.applies_to: personal_injury

rules.summary: Compensation for a personal injury is capped at $15,000.
rules.quote: Compensation for personal injury shall be in an amount not to exceed fifteen thousand dollars
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

params.applies_to: emotional_harm_only

rules.summary: When the only injury is emotional harm (a mental or emotional impairment caused by a threat of physical injury or death), compensation for medical care, mental health care and security measures is capped at $5,000. Claims involving actual bodily harm fall under the higher personal injury cap above instead.
rules.quote: in cases of emotional harm only, compensation for medical and mental health care and security measures shall be in an amount not to exceed five thousand dollars
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup and security system expenses share one maximum benefit of $1,000 (not $1,000 each).
rules.quote: CRIME SCENE CLEANUP AND SECURITY SYSTEM EXPENSES (maximum benefit $1,000)
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

rules.summary: Replacing clothes and bedding held as evidence falls under the same single up-to-$1,000 benefit as crime scene cleanup and security systems, not a separate $1,000.
rules.quote: Up to $1,000 for crime scene cleanup, security systems, or replacement of clothes and bedding held as evidence
rules.pinpoint: JDP-VS-10 brochure, Examples of Eligible Expenses
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup shares the single $1,000 maximum benefit with security system expenses.
rules.quote: CRIME SCENE CLEANUP AND SECURITY SYSTEM EXPENSES (maximum benefit $1,000)
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

rules.summary: The program can award up to $5,000 more than the limits above to a victim who is a minor when the application is filed and has extra medical or counseling needs.
rules.quote: the Office of Victim Services or a victim compensation commissioner may award additional compensation in an amount not to exceed five thousand dollars above the maximum amounts set forth in said subdivision to a personal injury victim, who is a minor at the time the application for compensation or restitution services is filed, when such victim has additional medical needs or mental health counseling needs
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: The program can also award more than the limits above for good cause, when it finds compelling reasons of fairness.
rules.quote: the Office of Victim Services or a victim compensation commissioner may, for good cause shown and upon a finding of compelling equitable circumstances, award compensation in an amount in excess of the maximum amounts set forth in said subdivision
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: The program may pay expenses actually and reasonably incurred because of the injury, and must cover medical care for a victim with no insurance or whose coverage is used up.
rules.quote: (1) Expenses actually and reasonably incurred as a result of the personal injury or death of the victim, provided coverage for the cost of medical care and treatment of a crime victim who does not have medical insurance or who has exhausted coverage under applicable health insurance policies or Medicaid shall be ordered
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: Mental health therapy prescribed by a licensed medical or mental health professional is a covered benefit, including individual, family and group therapy.
rules.quote: Mental health therapy including individual, family, group, medication management, music therapy, art therapy, horse assisted therapy, psychotherapy, tutoring, personal trainer, gym membership, and summer camp prescribed by a licensed medical or mental health professional
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

rules.summary: Dental fees and dentures are listed as covered medical expenses.
rules.quote: Hospital, doctor, cosmetic, and dental fees; co-pays and other medical related expenses, such as physical therapy, ambulance, prescription expenses, medical equipment, eyeglasses, dentures, and supplies
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

rules.summary: Prescription expenses are listed as covered medical expenses.
rules.quote: Hospital, doctor, cosmetic, and dental fees; co-pays and other medical related expenses, such as physical therapy, ambulance, prescription expenses, medical equipment, eyeglasses, dentures, and supplies
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

rules.summary: The program may pay for loss of earning power caused by the victim's total or partial incapacity.
rules.quote: (2) loss of earning power as a result of total or partial incapacity of such victim
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

params.scope: trips to court, Psychiatric Security Review Board, and parole board proceedings in physical injury cases

rules.summary: In physical injury cases, travel expenses to attend court, Psychiatric Security Review Board, and Board of Pardons and Paroles proceedings are covered.
rules.quote: For physical injury and homicide cases, lost wages and travel expenses for the victim and/or relatives to attend proceedings at court, the Psychiatric Security Review Board, and the Board of Pardons and Paroles
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

rules.summary: Security systems, lock, door and window repair, and clothes and bedding held as evidence are covered, subject to the program maximum for this benefit.
rules.quote: Costs for replacement or repair of damaged locks, doors, and windows; clothes and bedding held as evidence; biohazard clean-up; and the cost and installation of security systems
rules.pinpoint: JD-VS-47, Crime Scene Clean-up and Security Systems
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

params.scope: replacing clothes and bedding held as evidence

rules.summary: Replacing clothes and bedding held as evidence is a covered benefit, inside the shared crime scene cleanup and security maximum.
rules.quote: Costs for replacement or repair of damaged locks, doors, and windows; clothes and bedding held as evidence; biohazard clean-up; and the cost and installation of security systems
rules.pinpoint: JD-VS-47, Crime Scene Clean-up and Security Systems
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

rules.summary: Biohazard cleanup of a crime scene is a covered benefit, inside the shared crime scene cleanup and security maximum.
rules.quote: Costs for replacement or repair of damaged locks, doors, and windows; clothes and bedding held as evidence; biohazard clean-up; and the cost and installation of security systems
rules.pinpoint: JD-VS-47, Crime Scene Clean-up and Security Systems
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

params.item: property loss and damage (for example a phone or other personal property)

rules.summary: Property loss and damage is not an eligible expense, so a lost or damaged phone or other belongings would not be paid. The narrow exceptions are the shared crime scene cleanup, security and evidence clothing and bedding benefit.
rules.quote: Property loss and damage, pain and suffering, and travel to and from medical appointments are not eligible expenses.
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

params.item: travel to and from medical appointments

rules.summary: Travel to and from medical appointments is not an eligible expense.
rules.quote: Property loss and damage, pain and suffering, and travel to and from medical appointments are not eligible expenses.
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

params.item: crimes against property; pain and suffering

rules.summary: The statute bars compensation for property crime losses and for pain and suffering.
rules.quote: no compensation shall be awarded for losses sustained for crimes against property or for noneconomic detriment such as pain and suffering
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: The application must be made within 3 years after the date of the injury.
rules.quote: the application has been made within three years after the date of the personal injury or death
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

params.extension: waiver for physical, emotional or psychological injury

rules.summary: A person who missed the 3-year deadline because of physical, emotional or psychological injuries caused by the crime may apply for a waiver.
rules.quote: fails to make application for compensation within three years after the date of the personal injury or death as a result of physical, emotional or psychological injuries caused by such personal injury or death may apply for a waiver of such time limitation
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: If you were a minor and, through no fault of your own, did not apply within 3 years, you may ask for a waiver. The Office of Victim Services may grant it if it finds you were not at fault.
rules.quote: any minor, including, but not limited to, a minor who is a victim of conduct by another person that constitutes a violation of section 53a-192a or a criminal violation of 18 USC Chapter 77, who, before, on or after October 1, 2005, fails to make application for compensation within three years after the date of the personal injury or death through no fault of the minor, may apply for a waiver of such time limitation. The Office of Victim Services, upon a finding that such minor is not at fault, may grant such waiver.
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: The Office of Victim Services may also waive the time limit for good cause, if it finds compelling reasons that make this fair.
rules.quote: Notwithstanding the provisions of subdivision (1), (2) or (3) of this subsection, the Office of Victim Services may, for good cause shown and upon a finding of compelling equitable circumstances, waive the time limitations of subdivision (1) of this subsection.
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

params.exam_condition: done within 120 hours of the assault

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to police, but a sexual assault survivor does not lose eligibility for skipping the report if they went to a health care facility within 120 hours of the assault for an evidence collection exam, or met the disclosure or protective order rules of section 54-209(d).
rules.quote: (C) such incident or offense has been reported to the police, except that a victim of a sexual assault shall not be ineligible for the payment of compensation by reason of failing to make a report pursuant to this subparagraph if such victim presented himself or herself to a health care facility within one hundred twenty hours of such sexual assault for examination and collection of evidence of such sexual assault in accordance with the provisions of section 19a-112a , or if such victim complied with subsection (d) of section 54-209 .
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: A police report is still the default, but for sexual assault offenses, disclosing the injury to a listed professional, such as a sexual assault counselor, a nurse or physician, or a mental health professional, can stand in for it if the office reasonably concludes the offense occurred.
rules.quote: (K) a domestic violence counselor or a sexual assault counselor, as defined in section 52-146k
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: A police report is still the default, but reporting the injury in a restraining order or civil protection order application, where the order was granted after a hearing, can stand in for it if the office reasonably concludes the offense occurred.
rules.quote: the personal injury is reported in an application for a restraining order under section 46b-15 or an application for a civil protection order under section 46b-16a or on the record to the court, provided such restraining order or civil protection order was granted in the Superior Court following a hearing
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: The award takes into account money the applicant received or can receive from other sources, such as insurance and workers' compensation; life insurance is not counted.
rules.quote: shall take into consideration any amounts that the applicant has received or is eligible to receive from any other source or sources, including, but not limited to, payments from state and municipal agencies, insurance benefits, and workers' compensation awards
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: If a sexual assault survivor believes a health insurance claim would cause undue harm by spreading treatment information, the office may waive counting health insurance as a collateral source.
rules.quote: In a case involving circumstances under which a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or child abuse, or a claimant in such a case, believes that the dissemination of treatment information associated with a health insurance claim would cause undue harm, the Office of Victim Services may waive the consideration of health insurance as a collateral source.
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: To decide on an award, the office looks at what matters in the case. This includes anything the victim did that helped cause the injury, how much the victim helped the office check the claim, and how much the victim helped police catch and prosecute the offender.
rules.quote: shall consider all circumstances determined to be relevant, including, but not limited to, provocation, consent or any other behavior of the victim which directly or indirectly contributed to such victim's injury or death, the extent of the victim's cooperation in investigating the application and the extent of the victim's cooperation with law enforcement agencies in their efforts to apprehend and prosecute the offender
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: No award is made if the offender would be unjustly enriched, or if the victim broke a state penal law that caused or contributed to the injury.
rules.quote: No compensation shall be awarded if: (1) The offender is unjustly enriched by the award, provided compensation awarded to a victim which would benefit the offender in a minimal or inconsequential manner shall not be considered unjust enrichment; (2) the victim violated a penal law of this state, which violation caused or contributed to such victim's injuries or death.
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: Connecticut's sexual assault offenses are named in the compensation statute as crimes the program can pay for, with alternative proof rules.
rules.quote: In instances where a violation of section 53a-70b of the general statutes, revision of 1958, revised to January 1, 2019, or section 53-21 , 53a-70 , 53a-70a , 53a-70c , 53a-71 , 53a-72a , 53a-72b , 53a-73a
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

params.rule: Crimes in Connecticut are covered regardless of the applicant's residency; Connecticut residents hurt elsewhere may qualify only if that state or country has no program they are eligible for.

rules.summary: A crime that happens in Connecticut is covered no matter where the applicant lives.
rules.quote: Compensation shall be awarded pursuant to sections 54-201 to 54-218 , inclusive, for personal injury or death resulting from a crime which occurs (1) within this state, regardless of the residency of the applicant
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

params.target: Office of Victim Services, 225 Spring Street, 4th Floor, Wethersfield, CT 06109

rules.summary: Mail the signed application to the Office of Victim Services, 225 Spring Street, 4th Floor, Wethersfield, CT 06109.
rules.quote: Please send the completed application to: Office of Victim Services, 225 Spring Street, 4th Floor, Wethersfield, CT 06109; or Fax to: 860-263-2780; or Email to: OVSCompensation@jud.ct.gov
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

rules.summary: The signed application can be faxed to OVS at 860-263-2780.
rules.quote: Please send the completed application to: Office of Victim Services, 225 Spring Street, 4th Floor, Wethersfield, CT 06109; or Fax to: 860-263-2780; or Email to: OVSCompensation@jud.ct.gov
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

rules.summary: The signed application can be emailed to OVSCompensation@jud.ct.gov.
rules.quote: Please send the completed application to: Office of Victim Services, 225 Spring Street, 4th Floor, Wethersfield, CT 06109; or Fax to: 860-263-2780; or Email to: OVSCompensation@jud.ct.gov
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

params.note: Copies of crime-related bills from every provider who treated you, if available.

rules.summary: For medical, mental health, dental, or prescription costs, list every provider who treated you and include copies of the crime-related bills.
rules.quote: Please list the names of all providers who treated you and provide copies of crime-related bills, prescription printouts for co-pay amounts, and insurance benefit statements, if available.
rules.pinpoint: JD-VS-8PI, Section 9, Medical, Mental Health, Dental, and Prescription Expenses
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

params.note: Prescription printouts showing co-pay amounts, if available.

rules.summary: For prescriptions, include printouts showing your co-pay amounts.
rules.quote: Please list the names of all providers who treated you and provide copies of crime-related bills, prescription printouts for co-pay amounts, and insurance benefit statements, if available.
rules.pinpoint: JD-VS-8PI, Section 9, Medical, Mental Health, Dental, and Prescription Expenses
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

params.note: Insurance benefit statements, if available; bills must go to insurance first.

rules.summary: Include insurance benefit statements for crime-related medical bills, if you have them.
rules.quote: Please list the names of all providers who treated you and provide copies of crime-related bills, prescription printouts for co-pay amounts, and insurance benefit statements, if available.
rules.pinpoint: JD-VS-8PI, Section 9, Medical, Mental Health, Dental, and Prescription Expenses
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

params.note: Copies of bills and receipts for cleanup or security costs you paid, if available.

rules.summary: For crime scene cleanup or security system costs you paid, include copies of the bills and receipts.
rules.quote: Please fill out this section if you paid all or part of the expenses and provide copies of bills and receipts, if available.
rules.pinpoint: JD-VS-8PI, Section 9, Crime Scene Cleanup and Security System Expenses
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

params.note: Note from the treating health care provider listing days absent, if you missed more than 1 week of work.

rules.summary: If you missed more than 1 week of work, include a note from your treating health care provider listing the days you were out because of the injuries.
rules.quote: If you missed more than 1 week of work, you must provide a note from the treating health care provider listing the days you were absent from work because of the crime-related injuries.
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

params.note: Receipts for travel to court or board proceedings, such as hotel bills and parking.

rules.summary: For travel to court or parole board proceedings, include receipts such as hotel bills and parking.
rules.quote: Receipts for travel expenses are required (hotel bill, parking).
rules.pinpoint: JD-VS-47, Lost Wages and Travel Expenses to Attend Proceedings, Requirements
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

params.note: Copy of the signed civil protection or restraining order, only if the person you told about the crime was a judge.

rules.summary: If you told a judge about the crime, attach a copy of the signed civil protection order or restraining order.
rules.quote: judge (attach a copy of the signed civil protection order or restraining order)
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

params.note: Documentation that relates the injury and each expense to the crime.

rules.summary: The program requires documentation that ties the injury and each expense to the crime.
rules.quote: Documentation that relates the injury and expense to the crime is required.
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

params.note: Handwritten signature on the application; electronic signatures are not accepted and unsigned applications are returned.

rules.summary: Sign the application by hand; unsigned applications are sent back for signature.
rules.quote: Applications that are not signed will be returned for signature.
rules.source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

params.program_name: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP), Connecticut Safe at Home
params.agency: Office of the Secretary of the State
params.enroll: Participants complete applications through a community-based domestic violence or sexual assault crisis program. These programs are located throughout the state. The application process involves meeting with an application assistant and receiving orientation information about the program. Application Assistants send the completed applications to the ACP office.

rules.summary: Connecticut's Address Confidentiality Program is run by the Secretary of the State. It gives a substitute mailing address to victims of sexual assault, family violence, stalking and some other crimes who want to keep their home address private because of safety concerns.
rules.quote: There shall be an address confidentiality program established in the office of the Secretary of the State to provide a substitute mailing address for any person who wishes to keep such person's residential address confidential because of safety concerns and (1) has been a victim of (A) family violence, (B) injury or risk of injury to a child, (C) kidnapping, (D) sexual assault, (E) stalking
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968a, Address Confidentiality Program (secs. 54-240 to 54-240o)

rules.summary: Information the Office of Victim Services or a compensation commissioner receives that is already confidential under another Connecticut law stays confidential while they hold it. The statute does not make the whole claim file confidential.
rules.quote: Any information received which is confidential in accordance with any provision of the general statutes shall remain confidential while in the custody of the Office of Victim Services or a victim compensation commissioner.
rules.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

rules.summary: The hospital may not bill a sexual assault survivor for the evidence kit (PERK), including the kit itself, its administration, and processing of the kit or any biological specimens. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.
rules.quote: The hospital shall not bill a sexual assault victim for costs associated with a PERK, including the costs of the PERK, its administration, and the processing of the PERK or any biological specimens.
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-561.03, Payment for PERKs

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor has the right to have a PERK (evidence kit) performed at no cost.
rules.quote: a sexual assault victim shall have the right to have: (1) A PERK performed at no cost;
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 23-1908, Sexual assault victims' rights

params.exception: or more if you care for more than 2 children who live with you

rules.summary: The program may not award more than $25,000 per victimization. If the victim is or was the parent, guardian, custodian, or main caregiver of more than 2 children who live or lived with them, the program may award up to $5,000 more for each child living with the claimant, starting with the third child.
rules.quote: The Court shall not award compensation in an amount exceeding $25,000 per victimization; except, that: (1) If the victim is or was the parent, guardian, custodian, or primary caregiver to more than 2 children who reside or resided with the victim, the Court may award additional compensation to the claimant of up to $5,000 for each child who resides with the claimant, beginning with the third child
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-507, Awards of compensation

rules.summary: Mental health counseling is capped at $3,000 for adults and $6,000 for minor children.
rules.quote: Compensation for mental health expenses shall not exceed $ 3,000 for adults and $ 6,000 for minor children.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Lost earnings can be paid for up to 52 weeks after the crime, capped at the lesser of 80% of the victim's net pay or $10,000.
rules.quote: Loss of earnings may be compensated for a total period of up to 52 weeks after the date of the crime, in an amount not to exceed the lesser of 80 % of the victim's net pay or $10,000.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Moving expenses of up to $1,500 may be paid when needed for health or safety, on referral from a prosecutor, police officer, judicial officer, medical or mental health provider, or victim advocate.
rules.quote: Upon referral by a prosecutor, law enforcement officer, judicial officer, medical or mental health services provider, or victims advocate, compensation of up to $1,500 may be awarded for reasonable moving expenses where necessary for health or safety.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Temporary emergency housing is capped at $3,000, for a period of up to 120 days, on referral from a prosecutor, police officer, judicial officer, or victim advocate.
rules.quote: Upon referral by a prosecutor, law enforcement officer, judicial officer, or victims advocate, the cost of temporary emergency food and housing for a period of up to 120 days may be awarded. The maximum award for temporary emergency housing shall be $3,000.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Transportation is capped at $500 for necessary out-of-state travel and $100 for local transportation, with a $600 total per claim. It covers trips to court, to take part in the investigation or prosecution, to get medical care, and to get other services needed because of the crime.
rules.quote: Up to $500 for necessary out of state travel and up to $100 for all local transportation, not to exceed a total of $600 per claim, may be awarded for reasonable transportation expenses incurred by the victim or secondary victim
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Up to $1,000 may be paid to replace doors, windows, locks, or other items needed to secure the victim's home. Guard dogs, other animals, and guns or other weapons are not covered.
rules.quote: Compensation of up to $1,000 may be awarded for the reasonable cost of replacement of doors, windows, locks or other items necessary to secure the victim's home or other place of residence, except that the costs of guard dogs, other animals, guns or other weapons shall not be awarded.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Up to $100 may be paid to replace a living victim's clothing held by police as evidence.
rules.quote: Reasonable compensation up to $100 may be awarded for the replacement value of clothing of a living victim which is held by law enforcement officials for evidentiary purposes.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Up to $1,000 may be paid for reasonable crime scene clean-up costs.
rules.quote: Compensation of up to $1000 may be awarded to claimants for reasonable costs associated with cleaning up the crime scene.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Loss of services, meaning replacement services such as child care or housekeeping the victim can no longer provide because of the injury or death, is paid at no more than the D.C. minimum hourly wage, up to $200 per week and $2,500 per victimization.
rules.quote: Compensation for loss of services shall be limited to the minimum hourly wage for the District of Columbia, and shall not exceed $ 200 per week and $ 2,500 per victimization.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Up to $2,000 may be paid for a rental car while the victim's car is held by police as evidence. The current statute describes this cost as alternate transportation, including a rental car or rideshare.
rules.quote: Compensation of up to $2,000 may be awarded for the reasonable cost of a rental car for the period of time that a victim or secondary victim's automobile is being held by the police as evidence or to collect evidence.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Loss of services (replacement child care, housekeeping, and similar services the victim can no longer provide) is capped at $2,500 per victimization, on top of the $200 weekly limit.
rules.quote: Compensation for loss of services shall be limited to the minimum hourly wage for the District of Columbia, and shall not exceed $ 200 per week and $ 2,500 per victimization.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: Funeral and burial expenses are capped at $10,000. An older court rule gives a lower figure, but the statute controls.
rules.quote: Reasonable funeral and burial expenses, including the reasonable cost of embalming, burial containers, cremation, and the chosen method of interment; provided, that a claimant's economic loss under this sub-subparagraph shall not exceed $10,000
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

rules.summary: Reasonable medical expenses are covered, whether the care was provided in D.C. or elsewhere.
rules.quote: Reasonable medical expenses incurred, whether provided in the District or elsewhere;
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

rules.summary: Costs from a pregnancy resulting from a sexual assault are covered, including an abortion or prenatal care and delivery, but not the cost of raising the child.
rules.quote: Compensation may be awarded for costs incurred for pregnancy resulting from a sexual assault. This includes the cost of an abortion, or prenatal care and delivery, but not the cost of raising a child conceived through sexual assault.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

params.scope: counseling from a licensed provider

rules.summary: Out-patient mental health counseling needed because of the crime is covered when provided by a licensed psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, marriage, family, or child counselor, or a counselor licensed by the Board of Professional Counseling.
rules.quote: Out-patient mental health counseling expenses which became necessary as a direct result of the crime and which are provided by a: (i) Licensed psychiatrist or psychologist; (ii) Licensed social worker; (iii) Licensed marriage, family, or child counselor practicing within the scope of licensure; or (iv) Individual licensed by the Board of Professional Counseling
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

rules.summary: Lost income incurred as a direct or indirect result of the injury is covered.
rules.quote: Loss of income or support incurred as a direct or indirect result of an injury or death;
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

rules.summary: Reasonable moving expenses are covered when needed for health or safety.
rules.quote: Reasonable moving expenses where necessary for health or safety;
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

rules.summary: Dental care is part of covered medical expenses.
rules.quote: Ambulance, hospital, surgical, medical, nursing, dental, optometric, ophthalmologic, chiropractic, podiatric, in-patient mental health, and pregnancy-related care;
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

rules.summary: Pain and suffering are not paid, and neither is the value of property damaged or taken during the crime.
rules.quote: “Economic loss” does not mean: (i) Pain and suffering; (ii) The value of any property damaged or taken during the crime;
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

rules.summary: The program cannot pay attorney's fees for help filing an application. A fee may be awarded only for an appeal.
rules.quote: The Crime Victims Compensation Program cannot pay attorney's fees for assisting a victim with the filing of a compensation application.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP Application page, Information on Attorneys
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

params.extension: If you learned of the program later, you may have 1 year from then if the delay was reasonable.

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within one year after the crime. If you learned of the program later and the delay was reasonable, you have one year from when you learned of it.
rules.quote: The claimant filed a claim under this subchapter within one year after: (A) The crime occurred; (B) Learning of the Program, with an adequate showing that the delay in learning of the Program was reasonable;
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

rules.summary: The program may waive the time limits to apply and to report to police for good cause. Serious health or safety concerns can count.
rules.quote: The time limit requirements of this section may be waived for good cause shown, including compelling health or safety concerns.
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

rules.summary: A new 1-year window opens if a request to change the offender's sentence is filed or decided. The same is true for any other motion after conviction in a case where you were the victim.
rules.quote: (C) The filing or resolution of a first application, or any subsequent application entertained by the court, for a sentence modification as described in § 24-403.03 ; (D) The filing or resolution of a motion to modify a term of imprisonment as described in § 24-403.04 ; or (E) The filing or resolution of any other post-conviction motion in which the claimant was a victim or secondary victim
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

rules.summary: Generally the crime must be reported to law enforcement within 7 days, or within 7 days of when a report could reasonably be made.
rules.quote: The crime was reported to a law enforcement office within 7 days after its occurrence or, if the crime could not be reasonably reported within that time period, within 7 days from the time a report can reasonably be made.
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor can meet the reporting requirement without a police report by getting a temporary or final civil protection order or a forensic medical exam, or by reporting to law enforcement any time before the statute of limitations runs out.
rules.quote: In the case of a sexual assault victim: (A) Obtaining a: (i) Temporary civil protection order or civil protection order from the Court; or (ii) Forensic medical examination; or (B) Reporting the offense to a law enforcement office before expiration of the applicable statute of limitations for that offense
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

rules.summary: If the program finds a victim's ability to report was affected by age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or language barriers, or a health or safety concern, the victim can instead submit a court order, law enforcement records, or records from a medical professional.
rules.quote: if the Program determines that the claimant's ability to report the crime may be impacted due to the claimant's age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or linguistic barriers, or any other health or safety concern that jeopardizes the claimant's well-being
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation
