rules.summary: The award equals the claimant's economic loss minus the amount available from collateral sources.
rules.quote: The Court shall award compensation in an amount equal to the claimant’s economic loss, decreased by the amount available to the claimant from collateral sources.
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-507, Awards of compensation

rules.summary: If the victim is a dependent on someone else's insurance policy, that policy does not count as a collateral source unless the victim chooses to use it.
rules.quote: if a victim or secondary victim is a dependent on a primary insurance holder's insurance policy, the primary insurance holder's insurance policy shall not constitute a collateral source for the purposes of subsection (a) of this section, unless the victim or secondary victim chooses to avail themselves of the benefits or compensation from the primary insurance holder's insurance policy.
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-507, Awards of compensation

rules.summary: An application may be denied in whole or in part because of the nature of the victim's involvement in the events leading to the crime.
rules.quote: An application for assistance may be denied, in whole or in part, if the Court finds: (1) Denial is appropriate due to the nature of the victim’s or secondary victim’s involvement in the events leading to the relevant crime;
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-508, Disqualifications and reductions

rules.summary: An application may be denied in whole or in part if the victim did not reasonably cooperate with law enforcement, unless the cooperation was affected by the factors in 4-506(c) (for example the sexual assault reporting alternatives, or age, condition, trauma, language, or safety concerns).
rules.quote: (A) The victim failed to reasonably cooperate with law enforcement; and (B) The victim's cooperation was not impacted by the factors described in § 4-506(c)
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-508, Disqualifications and reductions

rules.summary: An emergency award of up to $1,000 may be made before the final decision if an award is likely and the claimant would face undue financial or emotional hardship without immediate help. It is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: If it appears likely that a final award will be made and that the claimant will suffer undue financial or emotional hardship if immediate financial assistance is not granted, an emergency award not exceeding $1,000 may be made prior to the final determination.
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-510, Emergency awards

rules.summary: First degree sexual abuse is a covered crime. The same statutory list also covers second, third, and fourth degree sexual abuse, misdemeanor sexual abuse, and child sexual abuse offenses.
rules.quote: First degree sexual abuse, as described in section 201 of the Anti-Sexual Abuse Act of 1994
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

params.rule: Anyone injured in D.C.; D.C. residents injured abroad by terrorism or mass violence, or in a state without a VOCA-eligible compensation program

rules.summary: Anyone injured by a crime in D.C. can apply. D.C. residents injured outside D.C. qualify only for terrorism or mass violence abroad, or when the state where it happened has no federally funded compensation program.
rules.quote: “Victim” means a person who suffers personal injury or death in the District, a person who is a resident of the District and suffers personal injury or death as a result of a terrorist act or act of mass violence committed outside of the United States, or a person who is a resident of the District and who suffers personal injury or death outside the District in a state that does not have a crime victims compensation program
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

rules.summary: Email the completed application and supporting documents to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov.
rules.quote: Please submit completed application by email to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov or by mail or in person to 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001; or see remote sites.
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

rules.summary: Mail the completed application to the CVCP office at 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001.
rules.quote: Please submit completed application by email to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov or by mail or in person to 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001; or see remote sites.
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

rules.summary: Drop off the completed application in person at the CVCP office, 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001, or at a remote site.
rules.quote: Please submit completed application by email to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov or by mail or in person to 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001; or see remote sites.
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

rules.summary: The application page also lists fax as a way to submit: 202-879-4230.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP Application page, ways to submit
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

rules.summary: Apply online through the self-guided interactive interview linked from the D.C. Courts.
rules.quote: OR ONLINE AT Self-Guided Interactive Interview Application https://lawhelpinteractive.org/Interview/Gene rateInterview/8116/engine
rules.pinpoint: CVCP Information Brochure, Where can I get an application?
rules.source_title: CVCP Information Brochure (English)

params.note: If no ID is provided, staff will contact you for another way to confirm identity.

rules.summary: Include a valid photo ID with the application.
rules.quote: DOCUMENTS NEEDED • CVCP Application • Valid Photo ID
rules.source_title: CVCP Information Brochure (English)

params.note: Or a DC civil protection order; the application page says temporary restraining orders are not accepted, while the 2023 form also lists anti-stalking orders and a forensic medical exam as crime documentation.

rules.summary: Include a copy of the DC police report or DC civil protection order, plus any bills or receipts you want reimbursed.
rules.quote: submit it along with a copy of your DC police report or DC civil protection order (the program does not accept temporary restraining orders), any bills or receipts that you would like to have reimbursed by the program.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

params.note: Listed on the application as one accepted form of crime documentation (at least one must be selected).

rules.summary: A forensic medical examination is one of the crime documentation options on the application.
rules.quote: Forensic medical examination
rules.pinpoint: CVCP Application (rev. 4/21/23), p.2, Documentation of Crime
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params.note: Bills or receipts for every expense you want reimbursed.

rules.summary: Send any bills or receipts you want the program to reimburse.
rules.quote: any bills or receipts that you would like to have reimbursed by the program.
rules.source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

params.note: Medical, dental, and mental health bills.

rules.summary: Submit copies of all medical, dental, or mental health bills received so far.
rules.quote: Submit copies of all available bills received to date.
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

rules.summary: Attach all insurance payment statements and denials for treatment costs.
rules.quote: Attach all insurance payment statements and rejections.
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params.note: Authorization and release forms for medical, wage, support, and collateral-source records.

rules.summary: The program will ask you to complete authorization and release forms.
rules.quote: YOU WILL BE REQUIRED TO COMPLETE AUTHORIZATION AND RELEASE FORMS
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params.note: Disability statement from the doctor, only if claiming lost wages.

rules.summary: For lost wages, submit a disability statement from the doctor who can verify how long you could not work.
rules.quote: (Please submit disability statement from the verifying doctor)
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params.note: Only if self-employed: federal income tax returns.

rules.summary: If you are self-employed and claiming lost wages, attach your federal income tax returns for the 12 months before the crime.
rules.quote: If yes, you must attach a copy of your Federal Income Tax Returns for the last 12 months preceding crime.
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params.note: Copy of the lease and a referral form, only if requesting temporary housing or moving expenses.

rules.summary: For temporary housing or moving expenses, submit a copy of the lease and a referral form.
rules.quote: If yes, submit a copy of lease. A referral form must also be submitted.
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params.note: Transportation receipts, only if your car was held as evidence.

rules.summary: If your car was held as evidence, submit copies of your alternate transportation receipts.
rules.quote: Please submit copy of transportation receipts.
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params.note: Birth certificates for children, only when listing secondary victims or dependents.

rules.summary: When listing dependents or secondary victims, submit copies of the children's birth certificates.
rules.quote: Submit copies of birth certificates for children.
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params.note: Confidential Information form, attached at the end of the online interview when applying online.

rules.summary: If you apply online, complete the Confidential Information form and attach it at the end of the online interview.
rules.quote: Please click here to complete a Confidential Information form. Once completed, you can attach it at the end of the online interactive interview that you are completing, such as the Crime Victims Compensation Form.
rules.pinpoint: D.C. Courts Forms Help Online, Crime Victims
rules.source_title: D.C. Courts Forms Help Online, Crime Victims (guided online CVCP application)

params.note: Business days for staff to review the application; this is not the time to a decision.

rules.summary: Allow 5 business days for a CVCP team member to review the application.
rules.quote: Please allow 5 business days for a CVCP team member to review your compensation application.
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params.agency: Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants (OVSJG)
params.enroll: Application assistants are available in several agencies across the District to answer questions, verify eligibility, and accept applications. To learn more about the ACP or submit an application, reach out to an application assistant on the list below.

rules.summary: D.C.'s Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants, gives eligible D.C. residents who fear for their safety and have experienced sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, or human trafficking a legal substitute address that District agencies must accept, plus forwarding of first-class, certified, and registered mail. Applicants must also have moved recently, plan to move soon, or have kept their current address off public records, and apply through an application assistant.
rules.quote: The District’s Address Confidentiality Program (ACP), administered by the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants (OVSJG), provides a legal substitute address for eligible DC residents to maintain the confidentiality of her or his actual address.
rules.pinpoint: OVSJG Address Confidentiality Program page, program description
rules.source_title: Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants, Address Confidentiality Program page

rules.summary: Information, records, and hearing transcripts in compensation claim files are confidential and not open to public inspection. The law lists exceptions.
rules.quote: Information, records, and transcripts of hearings contained in the claims files under the provisions of this chapter are confidential and not open to public inspection
rules.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-511, Confidentiality

rules.summary: A survivor of a sexual offense pays nothing out of pocket for the forensic medical exam and does not have to file an application with the program for it.
rules.quote: The victim of the sexual offense shall not pay any out-of-pocket costs associated with the forensic medical examination and shall not be required to file an application with the Agency.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Hospitals and health care professionals must provide forensic medical exams free of charge to sexual offense victims.
rules.quote: Hospitals and health-care professionals shall provide forensic medical examinations free of charge to the victims of sexual offenses.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.payer: Patient's insurance first (including Medicaid and Medicare), then the Victims' Compensation Fund for any uncovered cost

rules.summary: The provider must first seek payment from the patient's insurance, including Medicaid and Medicare, if available. If there is no insurance, or it does not cover the full cost, the provider may seek payment from the Victims' Compensation Fund.
rules.quote: Any hospital or health-care professional performing a forensic medical examination shall seek reimbursement for the examination from the patient's insurance carrier, including Medicaid and Medicare, if available. If insurance is unavailable, or does not cover the full costs of the forensic medical examination, the service provider may seek reimbursement from the Victims' Compensation Fund.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.payer: Victims' Compensation Fund, for crimes committed in Delaware
params.condition: if the crime was in Delaware

rules.summary: Delaware's victim compensation law applies to victims of crimes committed in Delaware, including people who do not live there. That law includes the free forensic exam rule.
rules.quote: This chapter shall apply to: (1) All persons, including nonresidents of Delaware, who are victims of crimes committed on January 1, 1975, or thereafter within this State
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.exception: or up to $50,000 if you are left fully and permanently disabled

rules.summary: Total compensation is capped at $25,000, or up to $50,000 for victims who are permanently and totally disabled.
rules.quote: Compensation may not be awarded under the chapter to a claimant in a total amount in excess of $25,000; provided, however, that the Agency may award compensation to victims who are permanently and totally disabled in an amount not to exceed $50,000.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Temporary housing is capped at $1,500.
rules.quote: b. Temporary housing not to exceed $1,500.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Moving expenses are capped at $1,000.
rules.quote: c. Moving expenses not to exceed $1,000.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Essential personal safety property is capped at $1,500.
rules.quote: d. Essential personal safety property not to exceed $1,500.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $1,000.
rules.quote: a. Crime scene cleanup not to exceed $1,000.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: If the claimant has a lawyer before the Appeals Board, the Board may award attorney fees of up to $1,000 or 15% of the award, whichever is less, paid on top of the compensation. The lawyer may not charge the claimant anything beyond that award.
rules.quote: Such fees shall not exceed $1,000 or 15% of the amount awarded, whichever sum is less, and shall be in addition to the amount of compensation awarded to the claimant.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Loss of support is capped at $3,000 for a victim who depended on the offender's income and lost it because of the crime (the offender must have had income at the time).
rules.quote: i. Loss of support for victims of violence, not to exceed $3,000, when all of the following are established
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Medical expenses are a covered loss.
rules.quote: n. Medical expenses.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Psychiatric care and mental health counseling are covered losses.
rules.quote: o. Psychiatric care and mental health counseling.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Lost past or future earnings caused by a disability from the injury are covered, including vacation, sick, and compensatory time.
rules.quote: r. Loss of past or future earnings, including reimbursement for vacation, sick, and compensatory time, because of a disability resulting from personal injury.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: The cost to change locks is covered, along with replacing items seized as evidence.
rules.quote: k. The cost to change locks and replace items seized as evidence.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.scope: replacing items seized as evidence

rules.summary: Replacing items seized as evidence is covered; this is separate from the general bar on property loss.
rules.quote: k. The cost to change locks and replace items seized as evidence.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.scope: the deposit plus up to 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed day care provider

rules.summary: Child care is covered, limited to the deposit plus 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed provider.
rules.quote: l. Child care not to exceed the deposit plus 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed day care provider.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Hospital expenses are a covered loss.
rules.quote: q. Hospital expenses.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: The program page lists dental expenses and prescription medication among covered costs.
rules.quote: Compensation is available for payment of medical and dental expenses, mental health counseling, prescription medication, lost wages, funeral/burial support, temporary housing and moving or relocation services, crime related expenses and other costs approved by the Agency.
rules.pinpoint: VCAP page, FAQs: Who can get help?
rules.source_title: Delaware DOJ, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program page and FAQs

rules.summary: The program page lists prescription medication among covered costs.
rules.quote: Compensation is available for payment of medical and dental expenses, mental health counseling, prescription medication, lost wages, funeral/burial support, temporary housing and moving or relocation services, crime related expenses and other costs approved by the Agency.
rules.pinpoint: VCAP page, FAQs: Who can get help?
rules.source_title: Delaware DOJ, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program page and FAQs

rules.summary: Reasonable expenses for attending criminal proceedings as a prosecution witness are covered.
rules.quote: m. Reimbursement for reasonable expenses incurred due to attendance at criminal proceedings as a witness for the prosecution.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.scope: fees for a lawyer who represents you before the Appeals Board

rules.summary: You do not need a lawyer before the Appeals Board, but if you have one, the Board may award an amount for the lawyer's services.
rules.quote: A claimant need not be represented by an attorney before the Appeals Board, but if such person is represented the Appeals Board may award an amount for services rendered.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.item: property damage

rules.summary: Pecuniary loss does not include property damage, so damaged personal property (for example a phone) is generally not paid. The cost to replace items seized as evidence is the exception.
rules.quote: “Pecuniary loss” means any expenses actually and necessarily incurred as a result of personal injury or death resulting from a crime, but does not include property damage.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.item: lost, damaged, or stolen property; pain and suffering

rules.summary: The program will not pay for lost, damaged, or stolen property, or for pain and suffering.
rules.quote: You cannot be paid for lost, damaged, or stolen property, or for pain and suffering.
rules.pinpoint: VCAP page, FAQs: Are there any limits?
rules.source_title: Delaware DOJ, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program page and FAQs

params.extension: unless the program gives you more time

rules.summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the injury, unless the Agency grants an extension or finds the deadline unreasonable in the circumstances.
rules.quote: Where the claim has not been filed within 1 year after the personal injury on which the claim in based, unless an extension is granted by the Agency or the Agency, in its discretion, determines that the circumstances render this requirement unreasonable.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: The program may not turn away a claim from sexual assault or abuse of a child because it was filed late.
rules.quote: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the Agency may not limit acceptance or consideration of any applications arising from sexual assault or abuse of a child which may have otherwise been barred from consideration by a statute of limitations.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: If the crime happened before your eighteenth birthday, the program may pay for mental health counseling. This holds even if you applied late, did not report to police in time, or did not cooperate with police. The crime must be properly documented, and you must apply before your twentieth birthday.
rules.quote: Notwithstanding the provision of paragraph (10) of this section and § 9010(a)(3), (4), and (5) of this title to the contrary, the Agency may make an award for the payment of mental health counseling services under this chapter on a claim made by the victim of a crime that occurred before the victim’s eighteenth birthday so long as the occurrence of the crime is appropriately documented, and the claim is filed before the victim’s twentieth birthday.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: For sexual assault or abuse, that twentieth-birthday limit does not apply.
rules.quote: However, the foregoing limitations in this paragraph (11) regarding the victim’s twentieth birthday do not apply in cases of crimes involving sexual assault or abuse.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, but this is waived if it was reported to protective services or Family Court, the victim has a protection from abuse order, the victim cooperated with law enforcement or an appropriate government agency in a sexual assault case, or the Agency finds the requirement unreasonable.
rules.quote: Where the victim has failed to report the crime to a law-enforcement agency within 72 hours of its occurrence. This requirement is waived in any of the following circumstances: a. The crime has been reported to an appropriate governmental agency, such as child or adult protective services or the Family Court. b. The victim can provide a protection from abuse order. c. The victim has cooperated with law enforcement or an appropriate government agency in cases of crimes involving domestic violence, sexual assault or abuse. d. Where the Agency, in its discretion, determines that the circumstances of the crime or the victim render this requirement unreasonable.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: A claim is denied if the victim refused reasonable cooperation with law enforcement.
rules.quote: Where the victim refused to give reasonable cooperation to state or local law-enforcement agencies in their efforts to apprehend or convict the perpetrator of the crime in question.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.scope: child victims of sexual assault or abuse

rules.summary: If you were a child when the sexual assault or abuse happened, the program cannot deny your claim just because you waited to report or to apply.
rules.quote: In no event may the Agency deny any claim solely because the victim was a child victim of sexual assault or abuse, and the victim either delayed reporting the abuse or assault to authorities or the victim delayed an application for services to mitigate the effects of the impact of sexual assault or abuse.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.waived_for: dire hardship, as determined by the Agency

rules.summary: Claims for less than $25 are not paid, except in cases of dire hardship.
rules.quote: Except in cases of dire hardship, as determined by the Agency, there may not be payment of compensation where the claim is for less than $25.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: The award is the loss minus anything the claimant has received or will receive from other sources, including insurance.
rules.quote: If a claim is approved, the award must be the amount of pecuniary loss minus the amount the claimant has received or will receive as indemnification from any other source, including any applicable insurance.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: If the victim bears a share of responsibility for the injury, the Agency reduces the award by that share.
rules.quote: If the victim bears any share of responsibility that caused injury or death, the Agency shall reduce the amount of compensation in accordance with its assessment of the degree of such responsibility attributable to the victim.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: An emergency award is possible only on a showing of dire necessity, requested in writing with the claim form, and not until a police report or other official law enforcement documentation is obtained.
rules.quote: The Agency will make an emergency award only upon a showing of dire necessity. The claimant, must, in writing, request an emergency award when submitting his claim form and show just cause as to why such an award should be considered. No such award will be made until the police report or other official documentation from the appropriate law enforcement agency is acquired.
rules.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

rules.summary: Covered crimes include offenses with the characteristics of rape, unlawful sexual intercourse, unlawful sexual penetration, or unlawful sexual contact.
rules.quote: Any specific offense set forth in Chapter 5 of this title, if the offense was committed after July 1, 1973, and contains the characteristics of murder, rape, unlawful sexual intercourse, unlawful sexual penetration or unlawful sexual contact
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rules.summary: Personal injury includes mental, emotional, or psychological harm and pregnancy resulting from the crime, not only bodily harm.
rules.quote: “Personal injury” means bodily harm, mental, emotional or psychological harm, or includes pregnancy resulting from the crime.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.rule: Crimes committed in Delaware, regardless of the victim's residency

rules.summary: The program covers everyone, including nonresidents, who is a victim of a crime committed in Delaware.
rules.quote: All persons, including nonresidents of Delaware, who are victims of crimes committed on January 1, 1975, or thereafter within this State
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.rule: Delaware domiciliaries victimized out of state, only where that state lacks an eligible program with equal benefits

rules.summary: A Delaware domiciliary hurt by a crime in another state may apply if the crime would be compensable in Delaware and that state has no eligible program with equal benefits.
rules.quote: A person whose domicile is in Delaware and who is the victim or secondary victim of a crime that occurs in another state, possession, or territory of the United States may make an application for compensation if both of the following are true: a. The crimes would be compensable had they occurred in Delaware. b. The placement of the crime occurred in states, possessions, or territories of the United States not having eligible crime victim compensation programs that provide benefits equal to the benefits provided under this chapter.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.target: 900 N. King Street, 4th Floor Wilmington, DE 19801

rules.summary: Mail the claim form to VCAP at 900 N. King Street, 4th Floor, Wilmington, DE 19801.
rules.quote: You must submit a claim form to get the process started. Your claim can be submitted in the following ways: Mail: 900 N. King Street, 4th Floor Wilmington, DE 19801
rules.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), How do I file a claim?
rules.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

rules.summary: Fax the claim form to VCAP at (302) 577-1326.
rules.quote: Fax: (302) 577-1326 If you would prefer to apply online, please visit: https://ccvcde.org
rules.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), How do I file a claim?
rules.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

rules.summary: Apply online through the VCAP claim portal at https://ccvcde.org.
rules.quote: If you would prefer to apply online, please visit: https://ccvcde.org
rules.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), How do I file a claim?
rules.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

params.note: the program's own claim form, in writing and signed by the claimant

rules.summary: The claim must be filed in writing on VCAP's own claim form and signed by the claimant.
rules.quote: All claims filed with the Agency must be in writing on the Agency's provided claim form and signed by the claimant.
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.note: signed subrogation, authorization, and consent agreements that are part of the official claim form

rules.summary: The official claim form includes subrogation, authorization, and consent agreements that must be part of the filing.
rules.quote: claims must be filed in the office of VCAP on official forms which include subrogation, authorization, and consent agreements.
rules.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

params.note: documentation (bills, receipts) supporting every loss claimed

rules.summary: Every loss must be backed by documentation before VCAP awards compensation.
rules.quote: All losses must be supported by documentation prior to compensation being awarded.
rules.pinpoint: Delaware DOJ VCAP page, FAQs, Are there any limits?
rules.source_title: Delaware DOJ, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program page and FAQs

params.note: any further documentation VCAP requests during its investigation, due within 45 days of the request

rules.summary: If VCAP asks for more documentation while investigating, it must be sent within 45 days of the request.
rules.quote: If VCAP, in its investigation of a claim, requires further documentation from the claimant, such documentation must be submitted to VCAP no later than 45 days of the date of VCAP's request.
rules.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

params.note: documentation of temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture, or moving costs, within 45 days of VCAP's request

rules.summary: Survivors claiming temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture, or moving costs must send documentation within 45 days of VCAP's request.
rules.quote: A victim who seeks compensation for temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture and/or moving expenses must submit documentation within 45 days of VCAP's request therefor, unless an extension is granted by the Agency.
rules.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

params.note: proof of a workers' compensation claim, only if the injury happened while working

rules.summary: If the injury happened on the job, the survivor must file a workers' compensation claim and send proof of it before applying to VCAP.
rules.quote: If the victim seeks compensation for an injury sustained while in the course and scope of employment, the victim must submit a claim for worker's compensation, and provide documentation thereof, before making application to VCAP for compensation.
rules.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

params.note: a written request showing just cause, only if asking for an emergency award

rules.summary: To ask for an emergency award, the claimant must request it in writing with the claim form and show just cause.
rules.quote: The claimant, must, in writing, request an emergency award when submitting his claim form and show just cause as to why such an award should be considered.
rules.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

rules.summary: A decision on a claim can take up to 60 days, and longer in rare cases.
rules.quote: It can take up to 60 days to make a decision on your claim. In rare cases, it can take longer.
rules.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), What can I expect next?
rules.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

params.enroll: A person shall file an application with the Program in a manner prescribed by the Program. (11 Del. C. § 9614) For Address Confidentiality Program information please contact DOJ_ACP@delaware.gov. (Delaware DOJ Criminal Division page)

rules.summary: Delaware's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Justice, gives certified participants a substitute address and forwards their mail. Victims of sexual assault can apply if they have filed for a protection from abuse order or are named as a victim in a criminal or delinquency case, and they state that they fear future violence from the perpetrator.
rules.quote: All of the following persons are eligible to apply to become program participants: (1) A victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, kidnapping, or stalking who has filed for a protection from abuse order or who is or was named as a victim in any criminal or delinquency proceeding
rules.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 96, subch. II, Address Confidentiality Act (sections 9611 to 9619)

rules.summary: Under Delaware's Freedom of Information Act, the investigative files the Victims' Compensation Assistance Program compiles or maintains are not public records.
rules.quote: (14) Investigative files compiled or maintained by the Victims’ Compensation Assistance Program
rules.source_title: 29 Del. C. ch. 100, Freedom of Information Act

params.scope: the initial forensic exam

rules.summary: A medical provider who performs the initial forensic exam may not bill the victim (or a minor victim's parent or guardian), directly or indirectly, for that exam.
rules.quote: (1) A medical provider who performs an initial forensic physical examination may not bill a victim or the victim’s parent or guardian if the victim is a minor directly or indirectly for that examination.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.28 (Payment for victims' initial forensic physical examinations)

params.scope: the initial forensic exam

rules.summary: The state's payment is payment in full for the initial forensic exam, and the victim may not be required to pay any of its cost.
rules.quote: Payment made to the medical provider by the department shall be considered by the provider as payment in full for the initial forensic physical examination associated with the collection of evidence. The victim may not be required to pay, directly or indirectly, the cost of an initial forensic physical examination performed in accordance with this section.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.28 (Payment for victims' initial forensic physical examinations)

params.payer: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Office of the Attorney General), Crime Victims' Services Office

rules.summary: The Attorney General's Crime Victims' Services Office pays for the initial forensic exam after sexual battery or a lewd or lascivious offense, whether or not the victim has insurance, takes part in the criminal case, or cooperates with police.
rules.quote: The Crime Victims’ Services Office of the department shall pay for medical expenses connected with an initial forensic physical examination of a victim of sexual battery as defined in chapter 794 or a lewd or lascivious offense as defined in chapter 800. Such payment shall be made regardless of whether the victim is covered by health or disability insurance and whether the victim participates in the criminal justice system or cooperates with law enforcement.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.28 (Payment for victims' initial forensic physical examinations)

rules.summary: State payment for the initial forensic exam may not exceed $1,000 per violation and covers only the medical expenses connected with that exam.
rules.quote: The payment shall be made only out of moneys allocated to the Crime Victims’ Services Office for the purposes of this section, and the payment may not exceed $1,000 with respect to any violation. The department shall develop and maintain separate protocols for the initial forensic physical examination of adults and children. Payment under this section is limited to medical expenses connected with the initial forensic physical examination
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.28 (Payment for victims' initial forensic physical examinations)

params.exception: unless the injury is catastrophic

rules.summary: Total benefits on one claim cannot exceed $15,000 when the victim is living and not catastrophically injured.
rules.quote: Total benefits paid on a single claim cannot exceed $15,000 when the victim is not deceased, or catastrophically injured
rules.pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2)(c))
rules.source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

rules.summary: Medical and dental treatment is capped at $10,000, paid at a rate of 50%.
rules.quote: Medical/Dental Treatment $10,000 at a rate of 50%
rules.pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2))
rules.source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

rules.summary: Mental health care for an injured adult victim is capped at $5,000, paid at a rate of 50%.
rules.quote: Mental Health Injured Adult Victim $5,000 at a rate of 50%
rules.pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2))
rules.source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

params.scope: injured minors until age 18

rules.summary: Mental health care for an injured minor (until age 18) is capped at $10,000, paid at a rate of 50%.
rules.quote: Mental Health Injured Minor (until age 18) $10,000 at a rate of 50%
rules.pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2))
rules.source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

rules.summary: Wage loss is capped at $15,000, paid at a rate of 50% or the gross average weekly wage (GAWW).
rules.quote: Wage Loss $15,000 at a rate of 50% or GAWW
rules.pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2))
rules.source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

rules.summary: Sexual battery relocation assistance is a one-time payment of up to $1,500 per claim, with a lifetime maximum of $3,000.
rules.quote: The department may award a one-time payment of up to $1,500 on any one claim and a lifetime maximum of $3,000 to a victim of sexual battery, as defined in s. 794.011 , who needs relocation assistance.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.199 (Relocation assistance for victims of sexual battery)

params.item: property loss for elderly persons or disabled adults

rules.summary: Property loss awards are only for elderly persons or disabled adults whose loss seriously lowers their quality of life: up to $500 per claim and $1,000 lifetime.
rules.quote: the department may award a maximum of $500 on any one claim and a lifetime maximum of $1,000 on all claims to elderly persons or disabled adults who suffer a property loss that causes a substantial diminution in their quality of life
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.195 (Awards to elderly persons or disabled adults for property loss)

rules.summary: Mental health care for an adult or minor victim of a forcible felony who was not physically injured is capped at $5,000, paid at a rate of 50%, for care within one year of the crime.
rules.quote: Mental Health Minor Victim Mental Injury (until age 18) Mental Health Adult or Minor Victim of Forcible Felony (non injury) $10,000 at a rate of 50% n/a $5,000 at a rate of 50% one year
rules.pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2))
rules.source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

rules.summary: Medical and dental costs are paid only for care within one year of the crime.
rules.quote: Medical/Dental Treatment $10,000 at a rate of 50% one year
rules.pinpoint: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (Jan. 6, 2022), Medical/Dental Treatment
rules.source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

rules.summary: For an injured adult, mental health care is paid only within one year of the crime.
rules.quote: Mental Health Injured Adult Victim $5,000 at a rate of 50% one year
rules.pinpoint: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (Jan. 6, 2022), Mental Health Injured Adult Victim
rules.source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

rules.summary: Wage loss is paid only for loss within one year of the crime.
rules.quote: Wage Loss $15,000 at a rate of 50% or GAWW Timeframe Within Which Loss Must Be Incurred From Date of Crime (up to) one year
rules.pinpoint: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (Jan. 6, 2022), Wage Loss
rules.source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

params.only_benefit_if: if you are an adult and were not physically hurt

rules.summary: People who suffered a psychological injury as a direct result of a forcible felony may get mental health care if the law enforcement report names them as a victim of the crime. For adults who were not physically hurt, this is the only benefit.
rules.quote: Persons who suffered a psychological or psychiatric injury as a direct result of a forcible felony may receive mental health care, when the law enforcement report identifies the individual as a victim of the crime. This is the only benefit available to adult victims who did not suffer a physical injury or death.
rules.source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

params.scope: pay you lost because physical injuries from the crime kept you from working

rules.summary: Wage loss is paid when the victim could not work because of physical injuries from the crime.
rules.quote: Who missed time from work because they were unable to work as a result of the physical injuries sustained as a result of the crime;
rules.source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

params.scope: trips to medical or dental care

rules.summary: Travel to medical or dental treatment can be reimbursed with an itemized bill from the provider and a reasonable mileage estimate.
rules.quote: Reimbursement for transportation costs to medical/dental treatment appointments requires the submission of an itemized bill by the treating provider and a reasonable estimate of the mileage between the victim/applicant's residence.
rules.source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

params.scope: trips to mental health care

rules.summary: Travel to mental health treatment can be reimbursed with an itemized bill from the provider and a reasonable mileage estimate.
rules.quote: Reimbursement for transportation costs to mental health treatment appointments requires the submission of an itemized bill by the treating provider and a reasonable estimate of the mileage between the victim/applicant's residence.
rules.source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

rules.summary: Medical, dental, and mental health costs the victim paid out of pocket are reimbursed at 100 percent, within the time limits and caps.
rules.quote: Out-of-pocket reimbursement to the victim/applicant for qualified funeral/burial, mental health (includes grief counseling), medical/dental expenses, and crime scene cleanup shall be compensated at 100 percent, when services or treatment was rendered within the timeframes established and up to the maximum benefit amount on the Schedule of Benefits.
rules.source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

rules.summary: For sexual battery relocation help, a certified rape crisis center in Florida must certify your need, state that you are cooperating with law enforcement (if that applies), and include your safety plan. The assault must have happened in your home, or somewhere that makes you reasonably fear for your safety at home.
rules.quote: (c) The victim’s need for assistance must be certified by a certified rape crisis center in this state. (d) The center’s certification must assert that the victim is cooperating with law enforcement officials, if applicable, and must include documentation that the victim has developed a safety plan. (e) The act of sexual battery must be committed in the victim’s place of residence or in a location that would lead the victim to reasonably fear for his or her continued safety in the place of residence.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.199 (Relocation assistance for victims of sexual battery)

params.scope: housing only: short-term shelter, rent, or a lease

rules.summary: Relocation money pays only for housing: short-term shelter, rent, or a lease, which can include a security deposit, application fees, and the first month's payment.
rules.quote: "Relocation assistance" compensation is defined as compensable housing expenses limited to short-term interim shelter, rental agreements, or long-term leases, and may include security deposits, application fees, and/or the first month's contractual payment.
rules.source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2001 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

params.item: real property, cash or negotiable instruments, intangible items, cosmetic damage

rules.summary: Under the property loss program, real property, cash, intangible items, and cosmetic damage are not compensable.
rules.quote: Examples of property that is not compensable includes real property, abandoned property, cash or other negotiable instruments, contraband or other illicit items, exchange agreements, items that amount to a monetary loss, are intangible, or are cosmetic damage causing a devaluation of the property.
rules.source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

params.condition: for a crime on or after October 1, 2019

rules.summary: For crimes on or after October 1, 2019, the claim must be filed within 3 years after the crime.
rules.quote: (b)1. A claim arising from a crime occurring on or after October 1, 2019, must be filed within 3 years after the later of: a. The occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based; b. The death of the victim or intervenor; or c. The death of the victim or intervenor is determined to be the result of the crime.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

params.extension: Waived entirely when the delay came from sexual assault forensic kit testing or DNA profile matching.

rules.summary: For newer crimes, if you filed late because testing a sexual assault kit or matching DNA was delayed, the deadline can be waived. For other good cause, the department may allow up to 5 years after the crime.
rules.quote: 2. Upon a showing that a delay in filing a claim under this paragraph occurred because of a delay in the testing of, or a delay in the DNA profile matching from, a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, a person who is eligible for compensation under subsection (1) may receive a waiver of any claim filing deadline. 3. For good cause based on a reason other than a delay described in subparagraph 2., the department may extend the time for filing a claim under subparagraph 1. for a period not to exceed 5 years after such occurrence.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

rules.summary: For a crime before October 1, 2019, the claim must be filed within 1 year after the crime. If you filed late because testing a sexual assault kit or matching DNA was delayed, the deadline can be waived.
rules.quote: (a)1. A claim arising from a crime occurring before October 1, 2019, must be filed within 1 year after: a. The occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based. b. The death of the victim or intervenor. c. The death of the victim or intervenor is determined to be the result of a crime, and the crime occurred after June 30, 1994. 2. Upon a showing that a delay in filing a claim under this paragraph occurred because of a delay in the testing of, or a delay in the DNA profile matching from, a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, a person who is eligible for compensation under subsection (1) may receive a waiver of any claim filing deadline.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

rules.summary: For an older crime, the department may also allow up to 2 years after the crime for other good cause.
rules.quote: 3. For good cause based on reason other than a delay described in subparagraph 2., the department may extend the time for filing a claim under subparagraph 1. for a period not exceeding 2 years after such occurrence.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

params.extension: Good cause can extend it, and a delay in sexual assault kit testing or DNA profile matching can waive it (same subsection; see researcher_notes).

rules.summary: If you were under 18 at the time of a crime on or after October 1, 2019, you have 3 years after turning 18 to file.
rules.quote: (c) For a claim arising from a crime occurring on or after October 1, 2019, when a victim or intervenor who was under the age of 18 at the time the crime occurred reaches the age of 18, the victim or intervenor has 3 years to file a claim.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

rules.summary: If you were under 18 at the time of a crime before October 1, 2019, you have 1 year after turning 18 to file.
rules.quote: (b) For a claim arising from a crime that occurred before October 1, 2019, when a victim or intervenor who was under the age of 18 at the time the crime occurred reaches the age of 18, the victim or intervenor has 1 year to file a claim
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

rules.summary: If you were a minor when it happened and filed late because testing a sexual assault kit or matching DNA was delayed, the deadline can be waived. For other good cause, the department may add up to 1 more year for an older crime, or up to 2 more years for a newer one.
rules.quote: Upon a showing that a delay in filing a claim occurred because of delay in the testing of, or a delay in the DNA profile matching from, a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, a person who is eligible for compensation under this subsection may receive a waiver of any claim filing deadline. For good cause based on any other reason, the department may extend the time period allowed for filing a claim under paragraph (b) for an additional period not to exceed 1 year or under paragraph (c) for an additional period not to exceed 2 years.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

params.exception: for a crime on or after October 1, 2019, or later with good cause

rules.summary: For crimes on or after October 1, 2019, the crime must be reported to the proper authorities within five days unless the department finds good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: 2. Five days after the occurrence of such crime, if the crime occurred on or after October 1, 2019, unless the department, for good cause shown, finds the delay to have been justified.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)

rules.summary: The report must go to state or federal law enforcement or prosecutors.
rules.quote: "Proper authorities" means state and federal law enforcement officials and prosecuting attorneys.
rules.source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2001 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: The program may deny, reduce, or take back an award if it finds you have not cooperated with the state attorney, law enforcement, and the program.
rules.quote: The department, upon finding that any claimant or award recipient has not duly cooperated with the state attorney, all law enforcement agencies, and the department, may deny, reduce, or withdraw any award, as the case may be.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)

rules.summary: The program pays last, after insurance and every other source.
rules.quote: Payment made in accordance with this section shall be considered payment of last resort that follows all other sources.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)

rules.summary: The program must deny an award if it finds you would not face serious financial hardship without it. It looks at all of your financial resources.
rules.quote: If the department finds that the claimant, if not granted assistance pursuant to this chapter to meet the loss of earnings or support or out-of-pocket loss, will not suffer serious financial hardship as a result of the loss of earnings or support and the out-of-pocket loss incurred as a result of the injury, the department shall deny the award. In determining serious financial hardship, the department shall consider all the financial resources of the claimant.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)

rules.summary: The award can be reduced or denied if the department finds the victim's conduct contributed to the injury.
rules.quote: In determining the amount of an award, the department shall determine whether, because of his or her conduct, the victim of such crime or the intervenor contributed to the infliction of his or her physical injury or psychiatric or psychological injury or to his or her death, and the department shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether, in accordance with such determination.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)

rules.summary: A contribution penalty is 25 percent of payments made directly to the victim; more than 25 percent means denial.
rules.quote: Penalty assessments, if imposed, based on contribution will be applied only to payments made directly to the victim or applicant at the rate of 25 percent of the amount otherwise payable. A penalty assessment of more than 25 percent will result in the denial of benefits.
rules.source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

rules.summary: If the program thinks an award is likely, and you get Social Security benefits or waiting would cause you undue hardship, it may give you an emergency award of up to $1,000. That amount comes out of your final award.
rules.quote: if it appears to the department that such claim is one with respect to which an award probably will be made, and that either the claimant is a recipient of benefits under the federal Social Security Act or undue hardship will result to the claimant if immediate payment is not made, the department may make an emergency award to the claimant, pending a final decision in the case, on the following conditions: (1) The amount of such emergency award may not exceed $1,000; (2) The amount of such emergency award shall be deducted from any final award made to the claimant;
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.12 (Emergency awards)

rules.summary: Covered crimes include any felony or misdemeanor causing physical injury and any forcible felony causing psychological injury.
rules.quote: (a) A felony or misdemeanor offense committed by an adult or a juvenile which results in physical injury or death, a forcible felony committed by an adult or juvenile which directly results in psychiatric or psychological injury
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.03 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Sexual battery is a forcible felony under Florida law.
rules.quote: “Forcible felony” means treason; murder; manslaughter; sexual battery;
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 776.08 (Forcible felony)

params.rule: Crimes committed in Florida are covered; Florida residents harmed out of state are covered only where that jurisdiction lacks an eligible VOCA compensation program.

rules.summary: A Florida resident hurt by a crime in another state is covered only if that state has no eligible crime victim compensation program.
rules.quote: (d) A criminal act committed outside this state against a resident of this state which would have been compensable if it had occurred in this state and which occurred in a jurisdiction that does not have an eligible crime victim compensation program as the term is defined in the federal Victims of Crime Act of 1984.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.03 (Definitions)

params.rule: A resident keeps a primary dwelling in Florida; students and military personnel stationed in Florida count as residents.

rules.summary: For this program a resident is someone whose primary home is in Florida, and students and military personnel stationed in Florida are treated as residents.
rules.quote: "Resident" means one who maintains his or her primary dwelling in Florida. Residency is governed by a person's intent, as evidenced by all surrounding facts and circumstances. Military personnel stationed in Florida and students shall be deemed residents for purposes of this program.
rules.source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2001 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

rules.summary: Mail the completed claim form and documents to the Bureau of Victim Compensation, PL-01, The Capitol, Tallahassee, FL 32399-1050.
rules.quote: Address: PL-01, The Capitol, Tallahassee, FL 32399-1050
rules.pinpoint: Claim Form BVC100 (08/24), page 1 header and Section One, instruction 4
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Claim Form BVC100 (08/24)

rules.summary: Email the completed claim form and documents to VCIntake@MyFloridaLegal.com.
rules.quote: Email: VCIntake@MyFloridaLegal.com
rules.pinpoint: Claim Form BVC100 (08/24), page 1 header and Section One, instruction 4
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Claim Form BVC100 (08/24)

rules.summary: Fax the completed claim form and documents to (850) 414-6197.
rules.pinpoint: Claim Form BVC100 (08/24), page 1 header and Section One, instruction 4
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Claim Form BVC100 (08/24)

params.target: the Tallahassee office of the department

rules.summary: By statute a claim can also be filed in person at the Department of Legal Affairs office in Tallahassee.
rules.quote: Claims may be filed in the Tallahassee office of the department in person or by mail.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

params.note: Completed, signed, and dated claim form (BVC100).

rules.summary: The claim form itself must be completed, signed, and dated.
rules.quote: A completed, signed and dated application.
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Brochure

params.note: A law enforcement report or other accepted proof of crime, such as Law Enforcement Information Reporting Form BVC430.

rules.summary: Include proof that a compensable crime occurred, such as a law enforcement report.
rules.quote: Documentation which proves a compensable crime occurred. Acceptable documentation includes: a law enforcement report, affidavit charging an individual with a crime filed by law enforcement
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Brochure

params.note: Itemized bills on industry standard forms or provider letterhead.

rules.summary: Include proof of crime-related expenses, such as itemized bills.
rules.quote: Proof of crime related expenses, such as itemized bills, if applicable.
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Brochure

params.note: For reimbursement of costs already paid out of pocket.

rules.summary: To be reimbursed for expenses already paid, include itemized bills and receipts with the application.
rules.quote: Reimbursement for out-of-pocket compensable expenses. Provide itemized bills and receipts with your applica on.
rules.pinpoint: Claim Form BVC100 (08/24), Section Two, Emergency Reimbursement
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Claim Form BVC100 (08/24)

params.note: Proof of insurance or other third-party payments, such as an explanation of benefits, if applicable.

rules.summary: Include proof of any third-party payments, such as an insurance explanation of benefits.
rules.quote: Proof of third-party payments such as insurance, restitution, judgments or settlements (e.g., copy of insurance explanation of benefits, settlement agreements, court documents for restitution and judgments), if applicable.
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Brochure

params.note: Copy of insurance card or policy declaration.

rules.summary: Attach a copy of your insurance card or policy declaration.
rules.quote: A ach a copy of your insurance card or policy declara on.
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Claim Form BVC100 (08/24)

params.note: Wage Loss Employment Report (BVC405), for wage loss claims.

rules.summary: For wage loss, attach a Wage Loss Employment Report (BVC405) and a Treatment Disability Statement (BVC409).
rules.quote: A ach a completed Wage Loss Employment Report (BVC405) and Treatment Disability Statement (BVC409).
rules.pinpoint: Claim Form BVC100 (08/24), Section Two, Wage Loss
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Claim Form BVC100 (08/24)

params.note: Treatment Disability Statement (BVC409) signed by a doctor, for wage loss or disability claims.

rules.summary: For wage loss, a doctor fills out a Treatment Disability Statement (BVC409) showing the dates excused from work.
rules.quote: A ach a completed Wage Loss Employment Report (BVC405) and Treatment Disability Statement (BVC409).
rules.pinpoint: Claim Form BVC100 (08/24), Section Two, Wage Loss; Section Twelve
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Claim Form BVC100 (08/24)

params.note: Requested after filing, not required up front.

rules.summary: After a claim is received, the bureau may ask for specific medical and financial information.
rules.quote: When claims are received, victims/applicants may be asked to provide specific medical and financial information.
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Brochure

params.note: Relocation Certification Worksheet (BVC106) certified by a Florida rape crisis or domestic violence center, for relocation claims.

rules.summary: Relocation claims need certification from a Florida rape crisis or domestic violence center.
rules.quote: Relocation benefits require certification documentation from a certified domestic violence or rape crisis center (depending on the claim type selected) in the State of Florida.
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Brochure

params.note: Housing contract or Notification of Residential Agreement (BVC110), for relocation claims.

rules.summary: Relocation claims need a standard housing contract or a Notification of Residential Agreement (BVC110) at the time of application.
rules.quote: A standard housing contract or a No fica on of Residen al Agreement (BVC110) is required at the me of applica on.
rules.pinpoint: Claim Form BVC100 (08/24), Section Four, Relocation Payment Limitations
rules.source_title: Victim Compensation Claim Form BVC100 (08/24)

params.agency: Office of the Attorney General of Florida
params.enroll: Contact the Attorney General's switchboard at (850) 414-3300 and ask to be connected to the Address Confidentiality Program; applications are filed with the Office of the Attorney General and there is no application fee.

rules.summary: Florida's Address Confidentiality Program gives relocated victims of domestic violence a substitute mailing address, and the Attorney General's office accepts their mail and legal papers. To ask about it, call (850) 414-3300 and ask for the program.
rules.quote: the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) provides a substitute mailing address for relocated victims of domestic violence, with this office serving as legal agent for receipt of mail and service of process. If you require information regarding the Address Confidentiality Program, please contact the switchboard at (850) 414-3300. Once you call, please request to be connected to the Address Confidentiality Program, and you will be transferred to the appropriate personnel who can assist you further.
rules.pinpoint: Office of the Attorney General, Address Confidentiality Program page; Fla. Stat. 741.401-741.465
rules.source_title: Office of the Attorney General, Address Confidentiality Program page (Florida Crime Prevention Training Institute site)

rules.summary: Any part of a public record held by an agency that regularly receives information about crime victims, such as the Bureau of Victim Compensation, that reveals a victim's name, phone, address, or assets, or anything that could be used to locate or harass the victim, is exempt from Florida's public records law.
rules.quote: Any portion of a public record which reveals the identity, including the name or personal identification number, home or employment telephone number, home or employment address, or personal assets, of a victim, or any other information that could be used to locate, intimidate, harass, or abuse the victim, which identifies that person as the victim of a crime, and which is a public record that is generated or received by any agency that regularly generates or receives information from or concerning the victims of crime is exempt from s. 119.07 (1) and s. 24(a), Art. I of the State Constitution.
rules.source_title: Fla. Stat. 119.071 (General exemptions from inspection or copying of public records)

rules.summary: A survivor cannot be made to pay, directly or indirectly, for a forensic medical exam; the Georgia Crime Victims Emergency Fund pays, whether or not the survivor reports or cooperates with police.
rules.quote: A victim shall have the right to have a forensic medical examination regardless of whether the victim participates in the criminal justice system or cooperates with law enforcement in pursuing prosecution of the underlying crime. A victim shall not be required to pay, directly or indirectly, for the cost of a forensic medical examination. The cost of a forensic medical examination shall be paid for by the Georgia Crime Victims Emergency Fund, as provided for in Chapter 15 of this title.
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-5-72 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.payer: Georgia Crime Victims Emergency Fund (state), even if the survivor has health insurance

rules.summary: The state fund pays for the forensic medical exam up to $1,000, even if the survivor has health insurance or other coverage.
rules.quote: When a forensic medical examination is conducted, the cost of such forensic medical examination shall be paid for by the fund in an amount not to exceed $1,000.00. The fund shall be responsible for payment of such cost notwithstanding whether the person receiving such forensic medical examination has health insurance or any other source of health care coverage.
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-15 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.applies_to: exam costs above the $1,000 limit

rules.summary: The program says providers may not bill law enforcement or the patient's insurance for exam costs above the $1,000 limit.
rules.quote: If FME expenses are over $1,000.00, can we bill law enforcement or the patient’s insurance for the difference? No. The maximum allowable amount is $1,000.00 for the collection of evidence for a FME.
rules.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

rules.summary: The exam program pays up to $1,000 per victim, per victimization, for sexual assaults in Georgia on or after July 1, 2011.
rules.quote: The sexual assault must have occurred in Georgia on or after July 1, 2011. The program will pay for the cost of a FME up to $1,000 per victim, per victimization.
rules.source_title: CJCC: Forensic Medical Examinations

rules.summary: Whatever the program pays a provider for a forensic medical exam counts as payment in full, so the provider cannot bill the balance to anyone else.
rules.quote: Payment made by the CVCP for an FME must be considered as payment in full.
rules.source_title: Criminal Justice Coordinating Council Administrative Rules (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 144)

params.payer: Georgia Crime Victims Compensation Program, including exams done in another state when the crime happened in Georgia

rules.summary: The program pays for a forensic medical exam done in another state as long as the assault happened in Georgia and the provider meets program criteria.
rules.quote: The Georgia Crime Victims Compensation Program ("CVCP") will pay for FMEs performed in another state as long as the crime occurred in Georgia
rules.source_title: Criminal Justice Coordinating Council Administrative Rules (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 144)

params.payer: Georgia Crime Victims Compensation Program, for sexual assaults in Georgia
params.condition: if the crime was in Georgia

rules.summary: The program pays for the exam only if the sexual assault happened in Georgia on or after July 1, 2011.
rules.quote: The sexual assault must have occurred in Georgia on or after July 1, 2011.
rules.source_title: Criminal Justice Coordinating Council Administrative Rules (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 144)

rules.summary: For crimes on or after July 1, 2002, the total award to a claimant cannot exceed $25,000.
rules.quote: with respect to any claim filed with the board as a result of a crime occurring on or after July 1, 2002, no award made under the provisions of this chapter payable to a claimant sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of a victim shall exceed $25,000.00 in the aggregate
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: Medical expenses are capped at $15,000.
rules.quote: No award under this chapter for the following losses shall exceed the maximum amount authorized: Category Maximum Award Lost wages $ 10,000.00 Funeral expenses 6,000.00 Financial hardship or loss of support 10,000.00 Medical 15,000.00 Counseling 3,000.00 Crime scene sanitization 1,500.00
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: Counseling is capped at $3,000.
rules.quote: No award under this chapter for the following losses shall exceed the maximum amount authorized: Category Maximum Award Lost wages $ 10,000.00 Funeral expenses 6,000.00 Financial hardship or loss of support 10,000.00 Medical 15,000.00 Counseling 3,000.00 Crime scene sanitization 1,500.00
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: Lost wages are capped at $10,000.
rules.quote: No award under this chapter for the following losses shall exceed the maximum amount authorized: Category Maximum Award Lost wages $ 10,000.00 Funeral expenses 6,000.00 Financial hardship or loss of support 10,000.00 Medical 15,000.00 Counseling 3,000.00 Crime scene sanitization 1,500.00
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: Funeral expenses are capped at $6,000.
rules.quote: No award under this chapter for the following losses shall exceed the maximum amount authorized: Category Maximum Award Lost wages $ 10,000.00 Funeral expenses 6,000.00 Financial hardship or loss of support 10,000.00 Medical 15,000.00 Counseling 3,000.00 Crime scene sanitization 1,500.00
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: Crime scene sanitization is capped at $1,500.
rules.quote: No award under this chapter for the following losses shall exceed the maximum amount authorized: Category Maximum Award Lost wages $ 10,000.00 Funeral expenses 6,000.00 Financial hardship or loss of support 10,000.00 Medical 15,000.00 Counseling 3,000.00 Crime scene sanitization 1,500.00
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: Medical and dental bills, including prescriptions and copays, are covered up to $15,000.
rules.quote: Medical and Dental Expenses (including prescriptions and copays) Up to $15,000
rules.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rules.summary: Dental expenses are covered within the $15,000 medical and dental limit.
rules.quote: Medical and Dental Expenses (including prescriptions and copays) Up to $15,000
rules.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rules.summary: Prescriptions and copays are covered within the $15,000 medical and dental limit.
rules.quote: Medical and Dental Expenses (including prescriptions and copays) Up to $15,000
rules.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rules.summary: Mental health counseling is covered up to $3,000; itemized counseling bills must be submitted.
rules.quote: Mental Health Counseling Up to $3,000 Submit copies of any itemized counseling bills related to the victimization.
rules.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

params.scope: counseling by a professional licensed or certified by the state

rules.summary: Counseling is paid only when a professional licensed or certified by the state provides it.
rules.quote: Compensable counseling services are those services rendered by professionals duly licensed or certified by the appropriate state authorities.
rules.source_title: Criminal Justice Coordinating Council Administrative Rules (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 144)

rules.summary: Lost wages are covered only for work missed without pay or with only partial pay.
rules.quote: You can only be reimbursed when you missed work and were not paid, or your wages were only partially covered.
rules.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rules.summary: Crime scene sanitization by a trained company is covered up to $1,500.
rules.quote: Crime Scene Sanitization Up to $1,500 Submit an itemized bill from a company trained in crime scene and biohazard clean-up.
rules.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

params.item: loss of property (for example a phone or other belongings)

rules.summary: No award is made for loss of property, so items like a damaged or taken phone are not reimbursed.
rules.quote: No award of any kind shall be made under this chapter to a victim of a crime for loss of property.
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-7 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.item: attorney's fees for a claim hearing

rules.summary: Compensation funds are not awarded to pay attorney's fees for a claimant who hires a lawyer for a Board hearing.
rules.quote: if a claimant chooses to be represented by an attorney, that claimant shall be responsible for the payment of their attorney's fees. Compensation funds shall not be awarded to pay attorney's fees.
rules.source_title: Criminal Justice Coordinating Council Administrative Rules (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 144)

params.extension: or later if the board extends it for good cause

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within three years of the crime, and the board may extend that for good cause.
rules.quote: A claim shall be filed by a victim not later than three years after the occurrence of the crime upon which such claim is based or not later than three years after the death of the victim; provided, however, that if such victim was a minor at the time of the commission of the crime, he or she shall have until three years after his or her eighteenth birthday to file such claim; and provided, further, that upon good cause shown, the board may extend the time for filing a claim.
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-5 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.extension: The board may extend the time for good cause shown.

rules.summary: A victim who was a minor at the time of the crime has until three years after their eighteenth birthday to file.
rules.quote: if such victim was a minor at the time of the commission of the crime, he or she shall have until three years after his or her eighteenth birthday to file such claim
