rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-5 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: By statute, no award is made if records show the crime was reported more than 72 hours after it happened, unless the board finds good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: In no case may an award be made where the police records, records of an investigating agency, or records created pursuant to a mandatory reporting requirement show that such report was made more than 72 hours after the occurrence of such crime unless the board, for good cause shown, finds the delay to have been justified
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: For sexual assaults after May 12, 2008, the program says no police report is required; it may use documentation from the forensic medical exam instead.
rules.quote: If the sexual assault occurred after May 12, 2008 you are not required to have a police report to apply for the CVCP. The program may use documentation from the forensic medical exam which shows that a sexual assault occurred.
rules.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

rules.summary: The application says the incident must be reported to law enforcement or an investigative agency, which can include medical authorities, DFCS, APS, the courts or the school system; an arrest or prosecution is not required.
rules.quote: While the incident must be reported to law enforcement or an investigative agency (DFCS, APS, the courts, medical authorities, or the school system), arrest and/or prosecution of an offender is not a program or eligibility requirement.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

rules.summary: By statute, an award may be reduced by payments received from the offender or from other private or public sources, such as workers' compensation, but gifts from family members or charitable donations do not count.
rules.quote: Any award made pursuant to this chapter may be reduced by or set off by the amount of any payments received or to be received as a result of the injury, serious mental or emotional trauma: (1) From or on behalf of the person who committed the crime; and (2) From any other private or public source, including an award of workers’ compensation pursuant to the laws of this state, provided that private sources shall not include contributions received from family members or persons or private organizations making charitable donations to a claimant.
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: No award is made until the claimant has used other available resources such as health insurance, employee benefits, workers' compensation and Medicaid/Medicare.
rules.quote: No award will be made until the claimant has exhausted all other public and private resources available to him or her (such as health insurance, employee benefits, worker's compensation, other state government assistance, Medicaid/Medicare).
rules.source_title: Criminal Justice Coordinating Council Administrative Rules (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 144)

rules.summary: The application's instructions say that if you are a victim of sexual assault and are not the main policyholder, you may opt out of giving insurance information for this incident.
rules.quote: If you are not the primary policyholder and are a victim of sexual assault or family violence, you may opt out of providing insurance information for this incident by checking the opt-out box in Section 6 of the application.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

rules.summary: The award may be reduced or the claim rejected if the victim's own conduct contributed to the injury or trauma.
rules.quote: In determining the amount of an award, the director and board shall determine whether because of his or her conduct the victim contributed to the infliction of his or her injury, serious mental or emotional trauma, or financial hardship, and the director and board may reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether in accordance with such determination.
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: The board may deny, reduce or withdraw an award if the claimant has not fully cooperated with law enforcement.
rules.quote: The board, upon finding that any claimant or award recipient has not fully cooperated with all law enforcement agencies, may deny, reduce, or withdraw any award.
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: The program lists sexual offenses among its most common compensable crimes.
rules.quote: Most Common Compensable Crimes Child Molestation Cruelty to Children Child Abuse Human Trafficking Sexual Offenses
rules.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation program page

rules.summary: A person who suffers serious mental or emotional trauma from being threatened with a crime that could cause physical injury is eligible, in addition to people physically injured by a crime.
rules.quote: Suffers a serious mental or emotional trauma as a result of being threatened with a crime which could result in physical injury or death
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-7 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rules.summary: The statutory definition of a covered crime includes violations of Chapter 6 of Title 16 (Georgia's sexual offenses chapter) and aggravated assault with intent to rape.
rules.quote: (v) A violation of Chapter 6 of Title 16; (vi) A violation of Part 2 of Article 3 of Chapter 12 of Title 16; (vii) A violation of Code Section 16-5-70; (viii) Aggravated assault with the intent to rape in violation of Code Section 16-5-21
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-2 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.rule: Victims may be residents or nonresidents of Georgia.

rules.summary: Victims may be Georgia residents or nonresidents.
rules.quote: Victims may be legal residents or nonresidents of this state.
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-7 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.rule: A Georgia resident hurt in another state may qualify if that state has no program, or paid less than Georgia would.

rules.summary: A covered crime includes an act in Georgia, or for a Georgia resident, an act in a state with no compensation program or a state that paid less than Georgia would.
rules.quote: An act which is committed in this state; in a state which does not have a victims’ compensation program, if the claimant is a resident of this state; or in a state which has compensated the claimant in an amount less than the claimant would be entitled to pursuant to this chapter, if the claimant is a resident of this state
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-2 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.target: Criminal Justice Coordinating Council, Crime Victims Compensation Program 104 Marietta Street NW, Suite 400 Atlanta, GA 30303

rules.summary: Mail the complete application packet to the CJCC Crime Victims Compensation Program office in Atlanta.
rules.quote: Mail the complete application packet to Criminal Justice Coordinating Council, Crime Victims Compensation Program 104 Marietta Street NW, Suite 400 Atlanta, GA 30303
rules.pinpoint: GA application instructions (Revised Sept 2026), Instructions item 4
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

rules.summary: A survivor can instead register and apply online through the Victims Comp Portal.
rules.quote: You can also register to apply online, by visiting victimscompportal.cjcc.ga.gov.
rules.pinpoint: GA application instructions (Revised Sept 2026), Instructions item 4
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

params.note: completed application, signed everywhere a signature is requested (part of the Complete Application Packet)

rules.summary: Fill out the whole application and sign every place that asks for a signature.
rules.quote: Please complete the entire application, printing clearly. Sign every place where a signature is requested.
rules.pinpoint: GA application instructions (Revised Sept 2026), Instructions item 1
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

params.note: police or incident report naming the victim or witness with a summary; reports from DFCS, APS, schools, courts or medical authorities are accepted; the application can be filed without it and the program follows up

rules.summary: The packet should include a police or incident report that names the victim or witness and summarizes what happened.
rules.quote: Provide us with a police or incident report that lists the victim or witness name, and a summary of the incident.
rules.pinpoint: GA application instructions (Revised Sept 2026), Instructions item 2
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

params.note: for sexual assault, forensic medical exam documentation can be used in place of a police report

rules.summary: For a sexual assault after May 12, 2008, no police report is needed; the program may use forensic exam documentation instead.
rules.quote: If the sexual assault occurred after May 12, 2008 you are not required to have a police report to apply for the CVCP. The program may use documentation from the forensic medical exam which shows that a sexual assault occurred.
rules.pinpoint: CJCC Victims Compensation FAQ, police report question
rules.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

rules.summary: Itemized bills for the expenses being claimed must be submitted with the application.
rules.quote: Benefits received are based on actual eligible expenses and itemized bills must be submitted with your application for review.
rules.pinpoint: GA application instructions (Revised Sept 2026), Please Note
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

params.note: prescriptions need an itemized summary and an itemized bill from the prescribing doctor

rules.summary: Prescription claims need an itemized summary and an itemized bill from the prescribing doctor.
rules.quote: Prescriptions must include an itemized summary and an itemized bill from the prescribing doctor.
rules.pinpoint: CJCC What Our Programs Cover, Medical and Dental Expenses

params.note: Psychological Service Report / treatment plan or counseling verification form, needed after the first visit

rules.summary: After the first counseling visit, the program pays only once a complete Psychological Service Report, treatment plan, or counseling verification form is submitted.
rules.quote: After the first visit, compensation will not be provided for counseling services without the submission of a complete Psychological Service Report ("PSR")/ treatment plan or counseling verification form.
rules.source_title: Criminal Justice Coordinating Council Administrative Rules (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 144)

params.note: lost wages claims: proof of income before the crime (pay stubs, payroll history, W-2, tax transcript)

rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

params.note: death certificate, only for funeral benefits

rules.summary: Funeral benefit claims must include a death certificate.
rules.quote: A death certificate must be submitted with your application for funeral benefits.
rules.pinpoint: GA application instructions (Revised Sept 2026), Benefits Covered footnote
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

rules.summary: Once a claim is awarded, payment can take up to eight weeks to arrive from the GBI.
rules.quote: Once a claim is awarded, please allow up to eight weeks for a payment to be mailed/sent from the Georgia Bureau of Investigation (GBI).

rules.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

params.enroll: Individuals must complete the application form, complete with a sworn statement.

rules.summary: Georgia's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, helps survivors of sexual assault and others whose safety may be at risk if their home address is made public.
rules.quote: The Georgia Safe at Home Program is an address confidentiality program that helps survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, stalking, or other eligible individuals whose safety may be compromised by public disclosure of their residential address.
rules.source_title: Georgia Secretary of State: Safe At Home

rules.summary: When the compensation board requests records from police, prosecutors, courts, or other agencies to decide a claim, it must keep those records confidential.
rules.quote: provided, however, that the board shall preserve the confidentiality of any such records received
rules.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-4 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.applies_to: what police are to do

rules.summary: The Attorney General's sexual assault response program page says a primary police role is to make sure victims are offered and given free forensic exams, whether or not they report to police. This is a program role statement, not a statute, and it does not say who pays or whether insurance can be billed.
rules.quote: The primary roles of the police are to ensure that victims are offered and provided free forensic examinations regardless if a police report is made
rules.pinpoint: Dept. of the Attorney General, HSART Program page, "Who We Are and What We Do"
rules.source_title: Department of the Attorney General: Hawaii Sexual Assault Response and Training (HSART) Program

params.exception: or more when covered medical costs are over $10,000

rules.summary: The maximum award is $10,000; if compensable medical expenses exceed $10,000, the award can go up to $20,000 or the actual medical expenses, whichever is lower.
rules.quote: No compensation shall be awarded under this chapter in an amount in excess of $10,000; provided that, if a case involves compensable medical expenses in excess of $10,000, no compensation shall be awarded in excess of $20,000 or the actual amount of compensable medical expenses, whichever is lower.
rules.source_title: HRS 351-62 Limitations upon award of compensation

params.extension: or later only if you show good cause

rules.summary: The application must be filed within eighteen months after the date of injury; the commission may accept a later application for good cause.
rules.quote: No order for the payment of compensation shall be made under this chapter unless the application has been made within eighteen months after the date of injury, death, or property damage; provided that upon a showing of good cause, the commission may consider applications filed beyond this time period.
rules.source_title: HRS 351-62 Limitations upon award of compensation

params.extension: good cause, which the commission's rules limit to a mental, physical or legal impairment; ignorance of the law, incarceration or negligence do not count

rules.summary: Under the commission's rules, good cause for filing after 18 months or reporting to police late means the applicant could not do it because of a mental, physical or legal impairment; not knowing the law, incarceration, or negligent failure to learn the facts is not good cause.
rules.quote: "Good cause" means a determination that the applicant was unable to file an application within 18 months after the date of the incident or report the incident to the police without undue delay due to a mental, physical or legal impairment. Good cause may not be established by ignorance of the law, incarceration, or negligent failure to ascertain the facts giving rise to a claim
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params.exception: unless an arrest was made

rules.summary: No prosecution or conviction is needed, but an arrest must have been made or the crime must have been reported to police without undue delay.
rules.quote: An order may be made under this section whether or not any person is prosecuted for or convicted of a crime arising out of an act or omission described in subsection (a) if an arrest has been made or the act or omission has been reported to the police without undue delay.
rules.source_title: HRS 351-31 Eligibility for compensation

params.exception: or later only if you show good cause

rules.summary: The commission's rules define undue delay in reporting to police as 72 hours, and the commission may consider a later police report if there is good cause.
rules.quote: "Undue delay" means 72 hours, provided that upon a showing of good cause, the commission may consider a police
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: The commission deducts money received or to be received from other sources, such as the offender or public or private funds, that is tied to the injury.
rules.quote: In determining the amount of compensation to be awarded under this chapter, the commission shall deduct amounts or benefits received or to be received from any source, whether from the offender or from any person on behalf of the offender, or from public or private funds
rules.source_title: HRS 351-63 Recovery from collateral source

rules.summary: The program calls itself the payor of last resort and pays after all other sources are used up.
rules.quote: is a “payor of last resort” and may pay compensation after all other sources have been exhausted.
rules.source_title: CVCC: Crime-Related Expenses

rules.summary: The commission considers whether the victim shares responsibility for the crime and reduces the award in proportion.
rules.quote: the commission shall consider the behavior of the victim, and whether, because of provocation or otherwise, the victim bears any share of responsibility for the crime that caused the victim's injury or death and the commission shall reduce the amount of compensation in proportion to the amount of responsibility for the crime which caused the victim's injury or death
rules.source_title: HRS 351-31 Eligibility for compensation

rules.summary: In sexual assault cases, an award may not be reduced or denied because of how the victim was dressed, where the victim was, the time of the assault, alcohol or drug use, or a previous sexual relationship with the offender.
rules.quote: Factors that shall not be considered in reducing or denying an award include, but are not limited to: (1) Cases involving sexual assault: (A) The manner in which the victim was dressed at the time of the assault; (B) Where the victim was prior to the sexual assault; (C) The time of the sexual assault; (D) Whether the victim was or may have been under the influence of alcohol or drugs; (E) Whether the victim had a previous sexual relationship with the offender;
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Sexual assault in the first through fourth degree are covered crimes.
rules.quote: Sexual assault in the first degree (section 707-730); (13) Sexual assault in the second degree (section 707-731); (14) Sexual assault in the third degree (section 707-732); (15) Sexual assault in the fourth degree (section 707-733);
rules.source_title: HRS 351-32 Violent crimes

rules.summary: Sex trafficking is a covered crime.
rules.quote: Sex trafficking (section 712-1202)
rules.source_title: HRS 351-32 Violent crimes

params.rule: Any private citizen hurt by a crime within Hawaii's criminal jurisdiction; Hawaii residents hurt in another state by a listed crime; Hawaii residents hurt by terrorism outside the United States.

rules.summary: Under the statute, people hurt by a covered crime within Hawaii's criminal jurisdiction can apply. The statute also names Hawaii residents hurt by a covered crime in another state.
rules.quote: In the event any private citizen is injured or killed by any act or omission of any other person coming within the criminal jurisdiction of the State after June 6, 1967, or any state resident is injured or killed by any act or omission of any other person after July 1, 1989, in another state, which act or omission is within the description of the crimes enumerated in section 351-32
rules.source_title: HRS 351-31 Eligibility for compensation

rules.summary: Medical expenses directly related to the crime are covered, including hospitalization.
rules.quote: Medical expenses are those expenses directly related to the incident that may include: (1) Hospitalization;
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Prescription drugs are a covered medical expense.
rules.quote: (5) Prescription drugs;
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Prescription eyeglasses, contact lenses, dentures and prosthetics are a covered medical expense if they were damaged in the crime.
rules.quote: (6) Prescription eyeglasses, contact lens, dentures, and prosthetics if damaged in the crime;
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Mental health expenses are listed as a covered crime-related expense.
rules.quote: Medical and mental health expenses
rules.source_title: CVCC: Crime-Related Expenses

rules.summary: Dental expenses are listed as covered.
rules.quote: Dental expenses
rules.source_title: CVCC: Crime-Related Expenses

rules.summary: The commission may pay for the victim's loss of earning power from total or partial incapacity.
rules.quote: Loss to the victim of earning power as a result of total or partial incapacity;
rules.source_title: HRS 351-33 Award of compensation

rules.summary: The commission may pay for the victim's pain and suffering; the program calls this a one-time Acknowledgement Award.
rules.quote: Pain and suffering to the victim;
rules.source_title: HRS 351-33 Award of compensation

params.scope: replacing or renting items taken as evidence

rules.summary: The reasonable replacement or rental cost of items taken as evidence can be covered as an other monetary loss, with verification. This rule is limited to items taken as evidence; it is not a general property replacement benefit.
rules.quote: Verification is required to establish other monetary losses and may include, but not limited to: (1) Reasonable cleaning of the crime scene; (2) Reasonable replacement or rental cost for items taken as evidence;
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Reasonable cleaning of the crime scene can be covered as an other monetary loss, with verification.
rules.quote: (1) Reasonable cleaning of the crime scene;
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Replacement dependent care can be covered when the victim's attending medical or other service provider supports the need.
rules.quote: (4) Replacement for dependent care or independent living support when evidenced by the attending medical or
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params.item: property damage, except in Good Samaritan claims

rules.summary: The program lists property damage as covered only for Good Samaritans, so property damage to a crime victim (for example a phone or other belongings) is not listed as covered, apart from items taken as evidence.
rules.quote: Property damage (“Good Samaritans” only)
rules.source_title: CVCC: Crime-Related Expenses

params.item: any injury suffered while confined in a jail, prison or other correctional facility

rules.summary: No compensation is paid for an injury suffered while confined in a jail, prison or other correctional facility.
rules.quote: No compensation of any kind shall be awarded to a victim or intervenor who suffered injury or death while confined in any federal, state, or county jail, prison, or other correctional facility.
rules.source_title: HRS 351-31 Eligibility for compensation

params.item: therapy sessions the victim or applicant does not show up for

rules.summary: The commission's rules say charges for therapy sessions the victim or applicant misses are not normally considered customary therapy expenses.
rules.quote: Sessions in which the victim or applicant fails to show up;
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params.note: A list of the providers who treated or served the victim.

params.note: Not needed in the packet: the Commission requests the police report from the law enforcement agency. The form asks for the police report number.

params.note: For lost wages: a statement from the medical or mental health provider certifying the nature and duration of the disability.

rules.summary: For lost wages, your medical or mental health provider must certify the nature and length of the disability.
rules.quote: The service provider must certify the nature and duration of disability.
rules.source_title: Haw. Admin. R. Title 23, Chapter 605 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params.note: For a child victim under 18, the parent or legal guardian completes and signs the application.

rules.summary: For a victim under 18, a parent or legal guardian must complete and sign the application.
rules.quote: APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED FOR CHILD VICTIMS UNDER THE AGE OF 18 MUST BE COMPLETED AND SIGNED BY THE CHILD'S PARENT OR LEGAL GUARDIAN
rules.source_title: CVCC Application Form (English, fillable)

params.enroll: Applicants do not apply directly with DLE. Applicants must meet with a designated application assistant from an ACP certified victim services organization. Application assistants will discuss ACP guidelines, help applicants complete a program application, and send completed applications to ACP.

rules.summary: Hawaii's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Law Enforcement, is free and lets survivors of domestic abuse, sexual offenses, or stalking use a substitute address instead of their home, work, and school addresses with state and county agencies. It also forwards mail and accepts legal service for participants. Survivors apply through an application assistant at a certified victim services organization, not directly with the Department.
rules.quote: The Hawaii Address Confidentiality Program is a free resource that helps to protect survivors of domestic abuse, sexual offenses, and stalking. The program enables participants to use a substitute address in place of their residential, work, and school addresses with state and county government agencies.
rules.pinpoint: Dept. of Law Enforcement, Hawaii ACP page, "What is Hawaii ACP?"; see HRS 801G-1, 801G-2, 801G-3
rules.source_title: Department of Law Enforcement: Hawaii Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

rules.summary: A provider may not bill the survivor or the survivor's insurance for any cost of a sexual abuse exam that the state program finds eligible.
rules.quote: A victim of sexual abuse is not responsible for the payment of the costs of a sexual abuse examination determined to be eligible for payment by the department. A medical provider must not submit any costs associated with a sexual abuse examination to a victim's insurance or to the sexual abuse victim.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: After the exam program pays, the provider may not send the survivor a bill for any leftover balance.
rules.quote: A medical provider must not submit any remaining balance to the sexual abuse victim after the sexual abuse examination program has determined payment.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

params.payer: Iowa Department of Justice, Crime Victim Compensation Fund (Sexual Abuse Examination Payment Program)

rules.summary: The state's crime victim compensation fund pays for the evidence-gathering exam and for treatment to prevent sexually transmitted infections.
rules.quote: The cost of a medical examination of a victim for the purpose of gathering evidence and the cost of treatment of a victim for the purpose of preventing venereal disease shall be paid from the fund established in section 915.94.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.payer: State of Iowa (Attorney General's Sexual Abuse Examination Payment Program)

rules.summary: The state pays for the exam even if the survivor does not report to police.
rules.quote: The State of Iowa pays for the sexual assault examination regardless of whether the victim reports the crime to law enforcement.
rules.pinpoint: Iowa AG, Sexual Assault Examination Payment Program page
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Examination Payment Program (Iowa Attorney General page)

params.payer: Iowa Attorney General's Sexual Abuse Examination Payment Program

rules.summary: If a survivor was billed by mistake and paid for the evidence collection, the program pays the survivor back.
rules.quote: In the event that a victim is erroneously billed and pays for the cost of the evidence collection, the program will reimburse that victim.
rules.pinpoint: Iowa AG, Sexual Assault Examination Payment Program page
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Examination Payment Program (Iowa Attorney General page)

rules.summary: Medical care is covered up to $25,000.
rules.quote: Reasonable charges incurred for medical care not to exceed twenty-five thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Medical costs of a pregnancy resulting from sexual abuse can be paid, counted under the medical benefit.
rules.quote: Compensation may be paid for medical care costs related to pregnancy resulting from the crime of sexual abuse.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: Glasses, hearing aids, dentures, prosthetics, wheelchairs, and medication taken, lost, or destroyed in the crime can be replaced.
rules.quote: Compensation may be paid for the replacement of a medical device including but not limited to a sight or hearing device, dentures, a prosthetic device, a wheelchair, and medication that was taken, lost or destroyed during the crime.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: Mental health care for the victim is covered up to $5,000.
rules.quote: Reasonable charges incurred for mental health care not to exceed five thousand dollars
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Mental health care for a secondary victim (spouse, child, parent, sibling, or household member) is covered up to $2,000 each.
rules.quote: The allowable charges under this subsection shall not exceed two thousand dollars per secondary victim.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Wages lost because of the injury are covered up to $6,000.
rules.quote: Loss of income from work the victim would have performed and for which the victim would have received remuneration if the victim had not been injured, not to exceed six thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Wages lost to cooperate with the investigation or attend court are covered up to $1,000 per person.
rules.quote: Loss of income from work that the victim, the victim's parent or caretaker, or the survivor of a deceased victim would have performed and for which that person would have received remuneration, where the loss of income is a direct result of cooperation with the investigation and prosecution of the crime or attendance at criminal justice proceedings including the trial and sentencing in the case, or due to the planning of or attendance at a funeral, memorial, or burial service, not to exceed one thousand dollars per person.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Lost wages are figured from gross pay for scheduled hours missed, then reduced by 25 percent.
rules.quote: Lost wages are computed as the gross rate of pay multiplied by the number of scheduled hours of work missed, decreased by 25 percent
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: Wages lost in the first two weeks after the crime need no disability statement; longer periods need one from a licensed medical or mental health provider.
rules.quote: Compensation for lost wages or income incurred within the first two weeks following the crime shall be paid to an eligible crime victim without an authorized disability statement.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: Wages lost for up to 30 days because of health or safety concerns about going to work after the crime, stalking, or harassment can be paid.
rules.quote: Compensation for lost wages or income shall be paid to an eligible crime victim for up to 30 days following an event that compromises the health or safety of the victim including but not limited to the approved crime, stalking, or harassment.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: Travel to medical care, counseling, or court is covered up to $1,000 per person.
rules.quote: Reasonable expenses incurred by the victim, a secondary victim, the parent or guardian of a victim, or a survivor of a deceased victim for transportation to medical or counseling services, criminal justice proceedings, or a funeral, memorial, or burial service, not to exceed one thousand dollars per person.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Driving your own car is paid at the state employee mileage rate.
rules.quote: Use of a privately owned vehicle shall be paid at the per-mile rate established by the department of administrative services for state employees using a private vehicle for state business.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: Emergency relocation is covered up to $1,000 per person, once in a lifetime.
rules.quote: Reasonable charges incurred by a victim, a secondary victim, a survivor of a deceased victim, or by a victim service program on behalf of a victim, for emergency relocation expenses, not to exceed one thousand dollars per person per lifetime.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: To count as emergency relocation, the move must happen within 30 days of the crime, its discovery, or when it could reasonably be reported, or within 30 days before or after the offender's release from incarceration.
rules.quote: "Emergency relocation" means a relocation that takes place within thirty days of the date of a crime or the discovery of a crime, or within thirty days after a crime could reasonably be reported. "Emergency relocation" also includes a relocation that takes place within the thirty days before or after an offender related to the crime is released from incarceration.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: The statute allows up to 3 months of housing assistance, up to $2,000 per person per lifetime, but the program's facts page lists this benefit as currently unavailable.
rules.quote: Reasonable expenses incurred by a victim, or by a victim service program on behalf of a victim, for up to three months of housing assistance, not to exceed two thousand dollars per person per lifetime.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: New or replacement locks, windows, and other home security items are covered up to $500 per residence.
rules.quote: Reasonable crime-related expenses incurred by a victim, the victim's parent or caretaker, or a survivor of a deceased victim to replace inadequate or damaged locks, windows, and other residential security items or install new locks, windows, and other residential security items, not to exceed five hundred dollars per residence.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Doors, locks, windows, security cameras, and security systems can be paid under the security benefit.
rules.quote: Compensation may be paid for doors, locks, windows, security cameras, security systems or devices, or other reasonable expenses that provide for the safety of the victim or the security of the residence.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: Clothing kept as evidence is replaced up to $200.
rules.quote: Reasonable replacement value of clothing that is held for evidentiary purposes not to exceed two hundred dollars.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.scope: clothing and bedding held as evidence by law enforcement

rules.summary: Clothing and bedding held as evidence by police can be paid for.
rules.quote: Compensation may be paid for clothing and bedding held as evidence by law enforcement.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: Cleaning the crime scene is covered up to $1,000 per scene.
rules.quote: Reasonable expenses incurred by the victim, secondary victim, or survivor of a deceased victim for cleaning the scene of a crime, not to exceed one thousand dollars per crime scene.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Child or dependent care while attending court, medical, or counseling appointments is covered up to $1,000 per person.
rules.quote: Reasonable dependent care expenses incurred by the victim, the victim's parent or caretaker, or the survivor of a deceased victim for the care of dependents while attending criminal justice proceedings, medical or counseling services, or funeral, burial, or memorial services, not to exceed one thousand dollars per person.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Funeral and burial costs are covered up to $7,500.
rules.quote: Reasonable funeral and burial expenses not to exceed seven thousand five hundred dollars.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: The program does not pay for property loss or repair, legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.
rules.quote: The program cannot pay for property loss, property repair, legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.
rules.pinpoint: Iowa AG, Crime Victim Compensation Facts page
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Facts (Iowa Attorney General FAQ page)

rules.summary: Legal fees are not covered.
rules.quote: The program does not cover property crime, property loss, legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.
rules.pinpoint: Iowa AG, Crime Victim Compensation Facts page
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Facts (Iowa Attorney General FAQ page)

params.item: phone bills, meals, pain and suffering

rules.summary: Phone bills, meals, and pain and suffering are not covered.
rules.quote: The program does not cover property crime, property loss, legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.
rules.pinpoint: Iowa AG, Crime Victim Compensation Facts page
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Facts (Iowa Attorney General FAQ page)

params.item: care of a newborn child

rules.summary: The program does not pay for the care of a newborn child.
rules.quote: Expenses incurred for the care of a newborn child are not compensable.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

params.extension: or later if the crime was discovered later or you show good cause

rules.summary: Apply within two years of the crime or its discovery. The program can waive the deadline for good cause.
rules.quote: file the application with the department within two years after the date of the crime, the discovery of the crime, or the date of death of the victim. The department may waive the time limitation if good cause is shown.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.exception: or within 72 hours of when you reasonably could, and the program may waive this for good cause

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to police or the sheriff within 72 hours, or within 72 hours of when a report could reasonably be made. The program may waive this for good cause.
rules.quote: A person is not eligible for compensation unless the crime was reported to the local police department or county sheriff department within seventy-two hours of its occurrence. If the crime cannot reasonably be reported within that time period, the crime shall have been reported within seventy-two hours of the time a report can reasonably be made. The department may waive this requirement if good cause is shown.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: For sexual abuse, the 72-hour police report rule may be waived for good cause if a forensic exam was done within 72 hours or the survivor told a medical provider, mental health professional, or victim service provider.
rules.quote: For a victim of sexual abuse, the 72-hour reporting requirement may be waived for good cause if a sexual abuse evidentiary examination was completed within 72 hours of the crime or if the crime was disclosed to another provider including but not limited to a licensed medical provider, a licensed mental health professional, or a designated victim service provider.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

params.scope: claims a licensed professional files for a child victim's short-term care

rules.summary: When a licensed professional gives a child victim emergency or short-term medical care under the state's child victim services law, the professional files the claim. That claim does not need a police report.
rules.quote: When immediate or short-term medical services to a victim are provided pursuant to section 915.35 by a professional licensed or certified by the state to provide such services, the professional shall file the claim for compensation, unless the department of health and human services is required to file the claim under this section. The requirement to report the crime to the local police department or county sheriff department under subsection 3 does not apply to this subsection.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.scope: a child or dependent adult abused by a caregiver

rules.summary: A child or dependent adult who was sexually abused by a caregiver does not need a police report. The abuse must have been reported to the state health and human services department, and the department must verify the report.
rules.quote: a victim under the age of eighteen or dependent adult as defined in section 235B.2 who has been sexually abused or subjected to any other unlawful sexual conduct under chapter 709 or 726 or who has been the subject of a forcible felony is not required to report the crime to the local police department or county sheriff department to be eligible for compensation if the crime was allegedly committed upon a child by a person responsible for the care of a child, as defined in section 232.68, subsection 8, or upon a dependent adult by a caretaker as defined in section 235B.2, and was reported to an employee
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: The victim must cooperate with reasonable requests from law enforcement in the investigation or prosecution of the crime.
rules.quote: The victim shall cooperate with reasonable requests by the appropriate law enforcement agencies in the investigation or prosecution of the crime.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by money from the offender, insurance (including workers' compensation or unemployment), public funds, or an earlier emergency award.
rules.quote: Compensation shall be reduced by the amount of any payment received, or to be received, as a result of the injury or death: a. From or on behalf of a person who committed the crime or who is otherwise responsible for damages resulting from the crime. b. From an insurance payment or program, including but not limited to workers' compensation or unemployment compensation. c. From public funds. d. As an emergency award under section 915.91.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: The program pays only after insurance, other government programs, and other sources.
rules.quote: The program is the payer-of-last-resort after insurance, other government programs, and other sources.
rules.pinpoint: Iowa AG, Crime Victim Compensation Facts page
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Facts (Iowa Attorney General FAQ page)

rules.summary: No award is made when the injury was caused by the victim's consent, provocation, or incitement, or by the victim's own criminal act. The criminal-act bar does not apply to a minor involved in commercial sexual activity.
rules.quote: Compensation shall not be made when the bodily injury or death for which a benefit is sought was caused by any of the following: a. Consent, provocation, or incitement by the victim. b. The victim assisting, attempting, or committing a criminal act. This paragraph shall not apply to a victim under the age of eighteen involved in commercial sexual activity as defined in section 710A.1.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: The program may reduce or deny an award only when the victim's conduct had a causal relationship to the injury.
rules.quote: The program shall reduce or disqualify compensation when there is a causal relationship between the contributory conduct on the part of the victim and the victim's injury or death.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: An emergency payment of up to $500 is possible when waiting would cause undue hardship. It is later subtracted from the final award.
rules.quote: If the department determines that compensation may be made and that undue hardship may result to the person if partial immediate payment is not made, the department may order emergency compensation to be paid to the person, not to exceed five hundred dollars.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rules.summary: Sexual assault is listed as a covered violent crime.
rules.quote: Homicide • Assault • Domestic Abuse • Sexual Assault
rules.pinpoint: Iowa AG Quick Reference Guide, Who
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program Quick Reference Guide for Primary Victims (2023)

rules.summary: Injury includes emotional harm, not only physical harm, and includes pregnancy resulting from the crime.
rules.quote: "Personal injury" or "injury" means bodily harm or mental suffering and shall include a victim's pregnancy or miscarriage resulting from a crime.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

params.rule: Crimes committed or attempted in Iowa, regardless of the victim's residence.

rules.summary: The crime must have happened in Iowa. The victim does not need to be an Iowa resident.
rules.quote: "Crime" means conduct that occurs or is attempted in this state, poses a substantial threat of personal injury or death, and is punishable as a felony or misdemeanor
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.rule: Iowa residents victimized in a state without an eligible VOCA compensation program.

rules.summary: Under the statute, an Iowa resident hurt in another state can apply to Iowa if the act would be covered had it happened in Iowa and that state has no eligible compensation program. The program's administrative rules go further.
rules.quote: To a victim of an act committed outside this state who is a resident of this state, if the act would be compensable had it occurred within this state and the act occurred in a state that does not have an eligible crime victim compensation program
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.rule: Iowa residents victimized outside Iowa where there is no victim compensation program, where that program's benefits are insufficient or inadequate, or on an aircraft in flight or waters outside any state's jurisdiction.

rules.summary: An Iowa resident hurt outside Iowa can apply if the place where it happened has no compensation program or one with insufficient or inadequate benefits, or if it happened on a plane in flight or on waters outside any state's jurisdiction.
rules.quote: A resident of Iowa who is the victim of an act that would be compensable had it occurred within the state of Iowa and any of the following apply: The act occurred in a state or foreign country that does not have a victim compensation program as defined in the federal law; The act occurred in a state or foreign country whose victim compensation program has insufficient or inadequate benefits; or The act occurred on an aircraft while in flight or occurred on waters outside of the jurisdiction of any particular state or country.
rules.pinpoint: Iowa Admin. Code r. 61-9.26 (definition of "Applicant", item 3)
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: Apply online starting from the Attorney General's site; its online application page links to the program's portal, where you create an account to file.
rules.quote: Apply online by visiting www.iowaattorneygeneral.gov.
rules.pinpoint: Application brochure, To Apply for Crime Victim Compensation panel
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (English)

params.target: Office of the Attorney General of Iowa Victim Assistance Section Hoover Building, First Floor 1305 E Walnut Street Des Moines, Iowa 50319

rules.summary: Send the paper application and signed forms to the Victim Assistance Section at the Hoover Building in Des Moines.
rules.quote: Office of the Attorney General of Iowa Victim Assistance Section Hoover Building, First Floor 1305 E Walnut Street Des Moines, Iowa 50319
rules.source_title: Iowa Crime Victim Compensation Application portal home page (ccvcia.org)

params.note: Signed Repayment and Subrogation Agreement (Section 1 of the release page); the application is not complete without it.

rules.summary: Sign Section 1, the repayment and subrogation agreement; the application is not complete without that signature.
rules.quote: Section 1 MUST BE SIGNED TO COMPLETE your Application for Crime Victim Compensation (CVC)
rules.pinpoint: Application, Release of Information and Repayment Agreements page
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (English)

params.note: Signed Information Release and Mental Health Special Medical Information Release (Sections 2 and 3), listing your medical and counseling providers.

rules.summary: Fill in and sign Sections 2 and 3, the medical and mental health information releases, to get medical and counseling benefits.
rules.quote: SECTIONS 2 AND 3 MUST BE COMPLETED AND SIGNED to receive Medical and Counseling Benefits
rules.pinpoint: Application, Release of Information and Repayment Agreements page
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (English)

params.note: Insurance company name, address, and policy number for health, Medicaid or Medicare, worker compensation, and auto, home, or boat insurance.

rules.summary: Have the name, address, and policy number for each insurance you carry; the application asks for them.
rules.quote: List your insurance company name, address, and policy number for each of these insurance types:
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (English)

params.note: Disability statement signed by a physician or licensed mental health practitioner, only for lost wages beyond two weeks.

rules.summary: Lost wages for more than two weeks need a disability statement from a physician or licensed mental health practitioner who treated the victim.
rules.quote: *Compensation paid for more than two weeks of a crime victim's lost wages requires a disability statement.
rules.pinpoint: What are Covered Costs?, lost wages footnote
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Facts (Iowa Attorney General FAQ page)

params.note: Self-employed or small business workers: recent federal or state income tax forms, or proof of average income for the past six months.

rules.summary: If you are self-employed, provide your most recent income tax forms or proof of your average income over the past six months.
rules.quote: Self-employed persons or small business employees must provide federal or state income tax forms for the most recent year completed or verification of average income for a minimum of the past six months.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

params.note: The medical provider sends these to the program; your signed release lets the program request them.

rules.summary: For medical costs, the provider sends the program records showing the care was for a crime injury.
rules.quote: When compensation for medical care is requested, the provider shall submit medical records that document the care provided and show that the medical care is for injury from crime.
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

params.note: The counselor completes a treatment plan and certification form (and progress forms every six months); you do not fill these out.

rules.summary: For counseling costs, the counselor completes the program's treatment plan and certification forms.
rules.quote: When compensation for mental health counseling is requested, the provider shall complete verification forms related to the counseling as follows:
rules.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rules.summary: Deciding eligibility may take eight weeks.
rules.quote: Eligibility determination may take eight weeks.
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Facts (Iowa Attorney General FAQ page)

params.enroll: Download and complete the application, then mail it to Safe At Home, P.O. Box 959, Des Moines, IA 50304. Questions: safeathome@iowa.gov or 515-725-7233.

rules.summary: Iowa's Safe at Home program gives participants a substitute address. Its page lists survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, trafficking, stalking, and assault.
rules.quote: Safe at Home is an address confidentiality program that provides participants with a substitute address. Who Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, trafficking, stalking, and assault.
rules.pinpoint: Safe at Home home page, program description (Who)
rules.source_title: Iowa Safe at Home (Iowa Secretary of State address confidentiality program home page)

rules.summary: Records that Iowa's public records law already keeps confidential, and information taken from them, stay confidential when the program gets them.
rules.quote: Information and records which are confidential under section 22.7 and information or records received from the confidential information or records remain confidential under this section.
rules.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.payer: Idaho crime victims compensation account (Industrial Commission)

rules.summary: By statute, the cost of a sexual assault forensic or medical exam is paid from the state crime victims compensation account rather than by the law enforcement agency.
rules.quote: the cost of forensic and/or medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault shall be paid for from the crime victims compensation account
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 19-5303 (Cost of medical exams)

params.payer: Industrial Commission, after any federal or federally financed third party for adults; after any liable third party, including private insurance, for minors

rules.summary: The commission pays for evidence-gathering sexual assault exams after any federal or federally financed payer (such as Medicaid or Medicare); for victims under 18 it pays after any liable third party.
rules.quote: Payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault performed for the purposes of gathering evidence for possible prosecution, after collections from any federal or federally financed third party who has liability, shall be made by the commission; provided however that payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims under eighteen (18) years of age shall be made by the commission after collections from any third party who has liability.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params.payer: Idaho Crime Victims Compensation Program, instead of an adult's private insurance

rules.summary: The program says an adult's (18 or older) private insurance should not be billed for a sexual assault forensic and medical exam.
rules.quote: an adult victim's (18 years of age and older) private insurance should not be billed for a sexual assault forensic and medical examination.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

params.payer: Idaho Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: The program says it will pay for an adult survivor's sexual assault forensic and medical exam, and to call the program right away if the facility sends a bill for the exam.
rules.quote: Please note that if you are an adult victim of a Sexual Assault, we will pay for the costs of your Sexual Assault Forensic and Medical Examination. If you receive a bill from the medical facility for the Forensic Examination, please contact us immediately
rules.pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, Will you bill my insurance?
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params.payer: Industrial Commission; a provider it has paid may not collect more from the victim for the same services, except as subsection (3) allows

rules.summary: A medical provider that the program has paid may not try to collect more from the victim for the same services, except when the program cannot pay the full allowable amount.
rules.quote: Except as provided in subsection (3) herein, a medical provider who has received payment from the commission for medical services provided to a victim or claimant under this chapter may not attempt to collect any further payment from the victim or the claimant for those same services.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1026 (Payments to medical providers)

params.payer: Idaho Crime Victims Compensation Program, once it has the victim's signed application

rules.summary: If the program gets a bill for your exam but no signed application from you, it holds the bill for 30 days and contacts you. If no signed application comes within 60 days, the bill is destroyed.
rules.quote: If the Program received a medical bill for a sexual assault forensic and medical examination but does not receive a signed application from the victim, CVCP will hold the medical bill(s) for 30 days. The program will contact the victim to request completion of the application. The medical bills will be destroyed if no signed application is received within 60 days.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, Medical bills received by CVCP, but no application received
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

rules.summary: Compensation to a victim, and to the victim's dependents if the victim dies, for crimes by the same offender within a 6 month period may not exceed $25,000 in total. The statute's wording is built around death cases; the program applies $25,000 as its maximum for all claims.
rules.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and all of the victim's dependents in cases of the victim's death, because of injuries suffered due to an act or acts of criminally injurious conduct involving the same offender and occurring within a six (6) month period, may not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) in the aggregate.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rules.summary: The program pays treatment expenses after all other payment sources are used, up to a maximum of $25,000.
rules.quote: The Idaho Crime Victims Compensation Program reimburses providers and victims for treatment expenses incurred on behalf of the victim after all other payment sources have been exhausted, up to a maximum of $25,000.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP Benefits You May Be Eligible For page
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Benefits You May Be Eligible For

rules.summary: Mental health treatment for the victim is capped at $2,500 unless the commission finds extenuating circumstances, in which case it can go up to the overall maximum.
rules.quote: payments for mental health treatment received as a result of the victim's injury may not exceed two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) unless the industrial commission finds extenuating circumstances.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params.applies_to: family members of the victim (spouse, parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, sibling)

rules.summary: Family members of a sexual assault victim can get mental health treatment reimbursed, up to $500 per person or $1,500 per family, if the victim was also awarded benefits.
rules.quote: Total payments made under paragraph (a) of this subsection may not exceed five hundred dollars ($500) for each person or one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) for a family.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "family members of the victim (spouse, parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, sibling)"

rules.summary: A victim with total wage loss gets 66 2/3 percent of their wages, up to $175 per week.
rules.quote: The weekly benefit amount is sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66 2/3%) of the wages received at the time of the criminally injurious conduct, subject to a maximum of one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175).
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params.applies_to: victims who were employable but not employed

rules.summary: A victim who was employable but not employed at the time of the injury may get up to $150 per week, at the commission's discretion.
rules.quote: who was employable but was not employed at the time of such injury, may in the discretion of the commission be awarded weekly compensation benefits in an amount determined by the commission not to exceed one hundred fifty dollars ($150) per week.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params.applies_to: victims who were employable but not employed

rules.summary: Weekly benefits for a victim who was employable but not employed may not exceed $20,000 in total.
rules.quote: Compensation payable to a victim or a victim's dependents under this subsection may not exceed twenty thousand dollars ($20,000), and the limitations of subsection (5) of this section apply to compensation under this subsection.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rules.summary: Reasonable funeral, burial or cremation costs, plus transporting the victim's body, are paid up to $5,000 after other collateral sources have paid.
rules.quote: Reasonable funeral and burial or cremation expenses of the victim, together with actual expenses of transportation of the victim's body, shall be paid in an amount not exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) if all other collateral sources have properly paid such expenses but have not covered all such expenses.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rules.summary: The commission may pay reasonable doctor, hospital, and medicine costs for crime injuries.
rules.quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rules.summary: Mental health counseling and care for crime injuries can be paid.
rules.quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params.scope: necessary travel to get benefits the program covers

rules.summary: The claimant or a close family member can be reimbursed for necessary travel to get covered benefits, under the commission's rules.
rules.quote: A claimant or a spouse, parent, child or sibling of a claimant or victim may be reimbursed for his or her expenses for necessary travel incurred in connection with obtaining benefits covered pursuant to this chapter and in accordance with rules of the commission.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rules.summary: Covered exam costs include examiner, facility, and lab fees, STI antibiotics, HIV prophylaxis, and other medications; follow-up visits may also be covered.
rules.quote: Sexual assault forensic and medical examination costs covered by the program include but are not limited to examiner fees, facility fees, laboratory fees, antibiotics for Sexually Transmitted Infections, HIV prophylaxis, medical prescriptions, and other medications. Follow up visits as prescribed by the treating physician due to an assault may also be covered.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, What benefits are offered by CVCP?
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params.item: medically necessary items such as eyeglasses, contacts, prostheses, medical devices

rules.summary: The program does not pay for property damage, but it can pay for medically necessary items such as eyeglasses, contacts, prostheses, and other medical devices.
rules.quote: CVCP cannot pay Property Damages. However, the Program can pay for certain medically necessary items, such as eyeglasses, contacts, medical and dental prostheses, and other medical devices or aids.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, Billing
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

rules.summary: Covered medical costs include dental, vision, hearing, prescriptions, ambulance, physical therapy, imaging, chiropractic care, and medical devices and prostheses.
rules.quote: Examples include medical, surgical, dental, vision, hearing, medication/prescription, ambulance transport, physical therapy, diagnostic imaging, chiropractic care, medical devices, medical aids, medical and dental prostheses.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, What benefits are offered by CVCP? (Medical)
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

rules.summary: Medications and prescriptions for crime injuries are covered medical costs.
rules.quote: Examples include medical, surgical, dental, vision, hearing, medication/prescription, ambulance transport, physical therapy, diagnostic imaging, chiropractic care, medical devices, medical aids, medical and dental prostheses.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, What benefits are offered by CVCP? (Medical)
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params.item: property damage or loss (for example a phone, clothing, or other personal items)

rules.summary: Property damage is not paid, so replacing personal property such as a phone is not covered. Pain and suffering is not paid either.
rules.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: Pain and suffering is not compensated.
rules.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params.item: missed or cancelled appointment fees; sessions that included the offender

rules.summary: The program will not pay counseling cancellation or missed-appointment fees, or sessions that included the offender.
rules.quote: CVCP will not reimburse for cancellation or missed appointment fees nor will they consider payments for sessions that included the offender.
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params.item: first 15 miles of any round trip, and round trips of 15 miles or less

rules.summary: Mileage is not paid for the first 15 miles of a round trip, or for round trips of 15 miles or less; one round trip per day.
rules.quote: Reimbursement is limited to one (1) round trip per day. The claimant shall not be reimbursed for the first fifteen (15) miles of any round trip, nor for traveling any round trip of fifteen (15) miles or less.
rules.source_title: IDAPA 17.10.01, Administrative Rules Under the Crime Victims Compensation Act

params.item: crime-scene cleanup

rules.summary: The program's FAQ lists crime-scene cleanup among costs it does not cover and points victims to court-ordered restitution from the offender instead. The same FAQ sentence also lists wage loss, which the statute does cover.
rules.quote: A victim may request the criminal court to order the offender to pay restitution for expenses that are not covered by the program, such as property damage, wage loss, expenses to attend criminal court, or costs for crime-scene cleanup.
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params.extension: or later if the commission extends it for good cause

rules.summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the crime; the commission can extend this for good cause.
rules.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the claim is filed with the commission within one (1) year after the day the criminally injurious conduct occurred causing the injury or death upon which the claim is based. The time for filing a claim may be extended by the commission for good cause shown.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

params.exception: or later if the commission finds good cause for the delay

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, unless the commission finds good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence or the commission finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

params.scope: exam costs only, adult victims

rules.summary: An adult who does not want to report to police can use a separate application. It is meant for people who mainly want only the cost of the sexual assault forensic and medical exam paid. It is not for minors.
rules.quote: This application should be used by victims who did not or do not wish to disclose to law enforcement at this time and are primarily seeking reimbursement for only the cost of sexual assault forensic and medical examination This form is not applicable for minor victims.
rules.pinpoint: Adult Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Reimbursement Application, page 1
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP Adult Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Reimbursement Application (April 2026)

rules.summary: To get benefits, the claimant must fully cooperate with all law enforcement agencies and prosecutors in catching and prosecuting the offender.
rules.quote: In order to be entitled to benefits under this chapter, a claimant must fully cooperate with all law enforcement agencies and prosecuting attorneys in the apprehension and prosecution of the offender causing the criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rules.summary: Except for the sexual assault exam rules in 72-1019(2), compensation is reduced or denied to the extent it can be recovered from insurance or other collateral sources.
rules.quote: Subject to the limitations on payments for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault described in section 72-1019 (2), Idaho Code, compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced or denied to the extent the compensation benefits payable are or can be recouped from collateral sources.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rules.summary: An award may be reduced or denied in proportion to how much the commission finds the victim contributed to the injury.
rules.quote: Compensation may be denied or reduced if the victim contributed to the infliction of death or injury with respect to which the claim is made.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rules.summary: Compensation is cut by 50 percent if the claimant was committing a felony or certain impaired-driving or boating violations when injured.
rules.quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced by fifty percent (50%) if at the time the injury was incurred the claimant was engaged in a felony or was in violation of section 18-8004 or 67-7034 , Idaho Code
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rules.summary: The commission may deny or reduce an award if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement or prosecutors.
rules.quote: The commission, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies or prosecuting attorneys, may deny or reconsider and reduce an award of compensation.
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rules.summary: If the claimant would face financial hardship and a final award looks likely, the commission may pay a tentative award, deducted from the final award later.
rules.quote: If the commission determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant, to be deducted from the final award
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1017 (Tentative award of compensation)

rules.summary: Covered injury includes physical harm and, for a victim, pregnancy, sexually transmitted disease, mental or nervous shock, or extreme mental distress.
rules.quote: means actual bodily harm or disfigurement and, with respect to a victim, includes pregnancy, venereal disease, mental or nervous shock, or extreme mental distress
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1003 (Definitions)

rules.summary: An award may be made whether or not anyone is prosecuted or convicted.
rules.quote: the offender does not have to be convicted for the victim to be eligible for compensation.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, Does the offender have to be convicted?
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

rules.summary: A sexual assault victim who has reported or will report to police can file the full application; the program first pays the exam, and an eligible victim can then get other benefits such as medical, mental health, and wage loss.
rules.quote: Additionally, if the victim is found eligible, they may access additional benefits available through the Program, including but not limited to medical (including imaging), mental health, and wage loss benefits.
rules.pinpoint: CVCP Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, Applying for CVCP
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

params.rule: Crimes in Idaho are covered; crimes outside Idaho are covered only for Idaho residents when the other state has no compensation program the victim is eligible for.

rules.summary: Crimes committed in Idaho qualify. An Idaho resident hurt in another state qualifies only if that state has no compensation program the victim is eligible for.
rules.quote: Occurs or is attempted in this state or occurs outside the state of Idaho against a resident of the state of Idaho and which occurred in a state which does not have a crime victims compensation program for which the victim is eligible
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1003 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Email the completed and signed application to cvcp.admin@iic.idaho.gov.
rules.quote:
Completed and signed applications can be sent via:
Email to: cvcp.admin@iic.idaho.gov
rules.pinpoint: Application for Compensation, page 4, submission box
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP Application for Compensation (June 2026)

rules.summary: Fax the completed and signed application to 208-332-7559.
rules.pinpoint: Application for Compensation, page 4, submission box
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP Application for Compensation (June 2026)

params.target: IDAHO CRIME VICTIMS COMPENSATION PROGRAM P.O. BOX 83720 BOISE, ID 83720-0041

rules.summary: Mail the completed and signed application to Idaho Crime Victims Compensation Program, P.O. Box 83720, Boise, ID 83720-0041.
rules.quote:
Mail to: IDAHO CRIME VICTIMS COMPENSATION PROGRAM
P.O. BOX 83720
BOISE, ID 83720-0041
rules.pinpoint: Application for Compensation, page 4, submission box
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP Application for Compensation (June 2026)

params.note: Signed application; the victim or claimant signs the release of information, the repayment and subrogation agreement, and the application certification.

rules.summary: The application must be completed and signed before it is sent.
rules.quote: Completed and signed applications can be sent via:
rules.pinpoint: Application for Compensation, page 4, submission box
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP Application for Compensation (June 2026)

params.note: Copy of the court order, only if the person signing is the victim's legal guardian or conservator.

rules.summary: If you sign as the victim's legal guardian or conservator, include a copy of the court order.
rules.quote:
IF LEGAL GUARDIAN and /or
CONSERVATOR
