rules.pinpoint: Application for Compensation, page 2, Claimant Information
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP Application for Compensation (June 2026)

params.note: For co-pays, deductibles, prescriptions, or other crime-related costs you paid yourself; contact your case manager.

rules.summary: To be paid back for co-pays, deductibles, or prescriptions you paid yourself, contact your case manager; receipts are required.
rules.quote: If you have paid co-pays, deductibles, prescriptions, then please reach out to your Case Manager. Receipts are required.
rules.pinpoint: Complete an Application page, Out of Pocket Expenses
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Complete an Application

params.note: The program requests this from the medical providers (UB04, CMS1500, or itemized billing statement), not from the survivor.

rules.summary: For exam and medical costs, the program asks the medical providers for itemized bills.
rules.quote: The Program will request the following from medical providers who assisted the victim: UB04, CMS1500, or itemized billing statements with CPT and REV codes.
rules.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, provider documentation list
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

params.note: The program requests the Sexual Assault Nurse Examination records from the medical provider.

rules.summary: The program asks the medical provider for the sexual assault nurse examination records.
rules.quote: Sexual Assault Nurse Examination Records
rules.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, provider documentation list
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

params.note: Explanation of Benefits, only if the victim has federal or state insurance; requested from the medical provider.

rules.summary: If the victim has federal or state insurance, the program asks the provider for the Explanation of Benefits.
rules.quote: Explanation of Benefits if the victim has federal/state insurance.
rules.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, provider documentation list
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

params.note: Bills, initial intake, and the CVCP Mental Health Treatment Plan; the program gathers these from the mental health provider.

rules.summary: For counseling, the program works with your mental health provider to collect bills, the initial intake, and a treatment plan.
rules.quote: CVCP will work with your mental health providers directly to gather the required CVCP documentation (bills, Initial Intake, CVCP Mental Health Treatment Plan, etc.).
rules.pinpoint: Complete an Application page, Mental Health
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Complete an Application

params.note: W-9 form, which the claimant may be asked for before payment is sent.

rules.summary: Before paying, the program may ask the claimant for documents such as a W-9 form.
rules.quote: For the purpose of dispersing payment, the claimant may be required to provide certain documentation, including a W-9 form.
rules.source_title: IDAPA 17.10.01, Administrative Rules Under the Crime Victims Compensation Act

params.note: The FAQ gives a range of 60 to 90 days for the review after the application is received.

rules.summary: After the program receives the application, its review can take 60 to 90 days.
rules.quote: The next step of the process involves a thorough review of your application, which can take 60-90 days.
rules.pinpoint: FAQ, What happens after my application is received?
rules.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params.enroll: Complete an application and submit it directly to the Office of the Secretary of State.

rules.summary: Idaho's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Secretary of State, gives survivors of sexual assault and other listed crimes a substitute mailing address and mail forwarding so their new address stays confidential; state and local agencies must accept the substitute address.
rules.quote: If you move to a new location to escape domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, malicious harassment or human trafficking, the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) helps keep your new address confidential using a mail-forwarding service and substitute address.
rules.pinpoint: Address Confidentiality Program page, introduction; Idaho Code 19-5701 and 19-5703
rules.source_title: Idaho Secretary of State, Address Confidentiality Program page

rules.summary: The information and records the Industrial Commission keeps for crime victim compensation claims are confidential and exempt from public disclosure, with limited exceptions (the claimant, a court in camera review, public officials doing their duties, and treating or advising health care providers).
rules.quote: The information and records the commission maintains in its possession in the administration of this chapter shall be kept confidential and are exempt from public disclosure under chapter 1, title 74 , Idaho Code
rules.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1007 (Public inspection and disclosure of commission records)

rules.summary: A hospital or other provider giving a sexual assault survivor a medical forensic exam, medical care and treatment, transportation, follow-up care, or medication may not bill the survivor for any part of those costs, including insurance deductibles, co-pays, co-insurance, or denied claims.
rules.quote: shall not: (1) charge or submit a bill for any portion of the costs of the services, transportation, or medications to the sexual assault survivor, including any insurance deductible, co-pay, co-insurance, denial of claim by an insurer, spenddown, or any other out-of-pocket expense
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params.payer: Survivor's health insurance or coverage program is billed first; leftover deductibles, co-pays, co-insurance, and denials go to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program (Department of Healthcare and Family Services)

rules.summary: If the survivor has health insurance or a coverage program, the provider bills that insurer or program, and the survivor's out-of-pocket share goes to the state Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program instead of the survivor.
rules.quote: the ambulance provider, hospital, approved pediatric health care facility, health care professional, laboratory, or pharmacy shall bill the insurance company or program. With respect to such insured patients, applicable deductible, co-pay, co-insurance, denial of claim, or any other out-of-pocket insurance-related expense may be submitted to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program of the Department of Healthcare and Family Services
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params.payer: Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program (Department of Healthcare and Family Services) for uninsured survivors and survivors who opt out of private insurance

rules.summary: When the survivor has no Medicaid or insurance, or has opted out of billing private insurance, the provider sends the bill to the state Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program.
rules.quote: the ambulance provider, hospital, approved pediatric health care facility, health care professional, laboratory, or pharmacy shall submit the request for reimbursement to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program under the Department of Healthcare and Family Services
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params.payer: Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program when a survivor who is not the policyholder opts out of private insurance

rules.summary: A survivor who is not the subscriber or primary policyholder on the insurance (for example, someone on a parent's or partner's plan) may opt out of billing that private insurance; the exam bill then goes to the state program.
rules.quote: a sexual assault survivor who is not the subscriber or primary policyholder of the sexual assault survivor's insurance policy may opt out of billing the sexual assault survivor's private insurance provider
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params.payer: Survivor or survivor's insurance may be billed for inpatient services

rules.summary: The billing ban does not cover inpatient care: if the survivor is admitted to the hospital, the survivor or their insurance may be billed for inpatient services.
rules.quote: Nothing in this Section precludes a hospital, health care provider, ambulance provider, laboratory, or pharmacy from billing the sexual assault survivor or any applicable health insurance or coverage for inpatient services.
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params.payer: Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program (Department of Healthcare and Family Services), billed with the sexual assault services voucher

rules.summary: Follow-up care, lab work, and prescriptions after the exam are billed to the state Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program when the survivor presents the sexual assault services voucher the hospital issues.
rules.quote: If a sexual assault survivor presents a sexual assault services voucher for follow-up healthcare, the healthcare professional, pediatric health care facility, or laboratory that provides follow-up healthcare or the pharmacy that dispenses prescribed medications to a sexual assault survivor shall submit the request for reimbursement for follow-up healthcare, pediatric health care facility, laboratory, or pharmacy services to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program under the Department of Healthcare and Family Services
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params.payer: Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program via the sexual assault services voucher, for follow-up healthcare

rules.summary: Follow-up healthcare covered this way means care related to the assault, including lab and pharmacy services, given within 180 days of the first visit.
rules.quote: "Follow-up healthcare" means healthcare services related to a sexual assault, including laboratory services and pharmacy services, rendered within 180 days of the initial visit as a result of the sexual assault.
rules.pinpoint: 410 ILCS 70/1a (text in effect before P.A. 104-837, eff. 1-1-27; definition unchanged in the amended text)
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params.applies_to: crimes committed on or after August 7, 2022

rules.summary: For a crime committed on or after August 7, 2022, the final award may not exceed $45,000 per victim.
rules.quote: or $45,000 per victim for a crime committed on or after August 7, 2022
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "crimes committed on or after august 7, 2022"

params.applies_to: crimes committed on or after August 7, 1998 and before August 7, 2022

rules.summary: For a crime committed on or after August 7, 1998 and before August 7, 2022, the final award may not exceed $27,000.
rules.quote: $27,000 for a crime committed on or after August 7, 1998 and prior to August 7, 2022
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "crimes committed on or after august 7, 1998 and before august 7, 2022"

rules.summary: Lost earnings are figured from the victim's average net monthly earnings for the 6 months before the injury, or $2,400 per month, whichever is less.
rules.quote: loss of earnings and loss of future earnings shall be determined on the basis of the victim's average net monthly earnings for the 6 months immediately preceding the date of the injury or on $2,400 per month, whichever is less
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Legal fees for proceedings needed solely because of the crime, such as getting an order of protection or no contact order, can be paid up to $3,500.
rules.quote: legal fees resulting from proceedings that became necessary solely because of the crime, including, but not limited to, establishing a legal guardian for the minor victim or the minor child of a victim, or obtaining a restraining order, no contact order, or order of protection, awarded up to a maximum of $3,500
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Funeral, burial, headstone, cremation, and related travel costs can be paid up to $10,000 for each victim.
rules.quote: in the case of death, expenses for reasonable funeral, burial, headstone, cremation, and travel and transport for survivors of homicide victims to secure bodies of deceased victims and to transport bodies for burial all of which may be awarded up to a maximum of $10,000 for each victim
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Towing and storage of the victim's vehicle in connection with the crime can be paid up to $1,000.
rules.quote: expenses incurred for the towing and storage of a victim's vehicle in connection with a crime of violence, to a maximum of $1,000
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Medical and hospital expenses from the injury are covered, including medical examinations, rehabilitation, and needed nursing care.
rules.quote: in the case of injury, appropriate medical expenses and hospital expenses including expenses of medical examinations, rehabilitation, medically required nursing care expenses
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Counseling is covered when given by a psychiatrist or a licensed clinical psychologist, licensed clinical social worker, licensed professional counselor, or licensed clinical professional counselor. No dollar cap on counseling appears in the Act.
rules.quote: appropriate psychiatric care or psychiatric counseling expenses, appropriate expenses for care or counseling by a licensed clinical psychologist, licensed clinical social worker, licensed professional counselor, or licensed clinical professional counselor
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.scope: trips to and from medical and counseling treatment

rules.summary: Travel to and from medical and counseling appointments is covered.
rules.quote: transportation expenses to and from medical and counseling treatment facilities
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Temporary lodging or relocation needed because of the crime is covered, including the first 2 months' rent and the security deposit at the new home. The Act sets no dollar cap for it.
rules.quote: costs associated with temporary lodging or relocation necessary as a result of the crime, including, but not limited to, the first 2 months' rent and security deposit of the dwelling that the claimant relocated to and other reasonable relocation expenses incurred as a result of the violent crime
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.scope: locks, doors, or windows needed or damaged because of the crime

rules.summary: Locks, doors, or windows that are needed or were damaged because of the crime are covered.
rules.quote: locks, doors, or windows necessary or damaged as a result of the crime
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.scope: replacing clothing and bedding used as evidence

rules.summary: Replacing clothing and bedding kept as evidence is covered.
rules.quote: replacement costs for clothing and bedding used as evidence
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Crime scene clean-up is covered.
rules.quote: the costs of appropriate crime scene clean-up
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.scope: lost tuition, if the crime leaves the victim unable to keep attending school

rules.summary: Lost tuition is covered when the victim was enrolled in school or college and cannot keep attending because of the crime.
rules.quote: loss of tuition paid to attend grammar school or high school when the victim had been enrolled as a student prior to the injury, or college or graduate school when the victim had been enrolled as a day or night student prior to the injury when the victim becomes unable to continue attendance at school as a result of the crime of violence
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Prosthetic appliances, eyeglasses, and hearing aids that are needed or were damaged because of the crime are covered.
rules.quote: prosthetic appliances, eyeglasses, and hearing aids necessary or damaged as a result of the crime
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: The program's sexual assault FAQ lists medical, hospital, and dental expenses as payable.
rules.quote: Medical, hospital, and dental expenses.
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims, What types of expenses may the Crime Victims Compensation Program pay?
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25)

params.item: pain and suffering; property loss or damage (for example a stolen or broken phone)

rules.summary: Pain and suffering and lost or damaged property are not covered, so a stolen or broken phone will not be replaced. The Act does separately cover locks, doors, and windows, eyeglasses, hearing aids, prosthetic appliances, and clothing and bedding taken as evidence.
rules.quote: "Pecuniary loss" does not include pain and suffering or property loss or damage.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.item: stolen, damaged or lost property, except locks, doors and windows

rules.summary: The program's sexual assault FAQ says stolen, damaged, or lost property cannot be paid, except locks, doors, and windows.
rules.quote: Stolen, damaged or lost property (except locks, doors and windows)
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims, What types of expenses cannot be paid
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25)

params.item: expenses not yet paid or billed by a vendor

rules.summary: The program guide says it does not pay for expenses that have not already been paid or billed by a vendor.
rules.quote: Compensation is not available for expenses that have not been previously paid or billed by a vendor.
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation Program guide, Do I get the money for compensation?
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Program guide (Rev. 11/24)

params.item: counseling by an unlicensed person working with a licensed person

rules.summary: The program's sexual assault FAQ says counseling by an unlicensed person working under a licensed provider cannot be paid.
rules.quote: Services by an unlicensed person working with a licensed person cannot be paid.
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims, What types of expenses may the Crime Victims Compensation Program pay?
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25)

params.extension: or within 1 year after someone is charged with the crime

rules.summary: Apply within 5 years of the crime, or within one year after someone is criminally charged for it.
rules.quote: Within 5 years of the occurrence of the crime, or within one year after a criminal charge of a person for an offense, upon which the claim is based, the applicant presents an application
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.extension: also runs from removal of a legal disability; legal disability includes a PTSD diagnosis

rules.summary: A victim who was under 18, or under a legal disability, when it happened can apply within 3 years after turning 18 or after the disability is removed. The Act counts a diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder as a legal disability.
rules.quote: he or she may present the application required by this subsection within 3 years after he or she attains the age of 18 years or the disability is removed, as the case may be. Legal disability includes a diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: The Attorney General may accept a late application if it finds you had good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: The Attorney General and the Court of Claims may accept an application presented after the period provided in subsection (a) if the Attorney General determines that the applicant had good cause for a delay.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: For sexual assault and sexual abuse offenses, law enforcement must be notified within 7 days, or later if the applicant shows the notice was timely under the circumstances.
rules.quote: For victims of offenses defined in Sections 10-9, 11-1.20, 11-1.30, 11-1.40, 11-1.50, 11-1.60, 12-13, and 12-14 of the Criminal Code of 1961 or the Criminal Code of 2012, the appropriate law enforcement officials were notified within 7 days of the perpetration of the crime allegedly causing death or injury to the victim or, if the notification was made more than 7 days after the perpetration of the crime, the applicant establishes that the notice was timely under the circumstances.
rules.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Instead of a police report, going to a medical facility for care or sexual assault evidence collection, getting an order of protection or no contact order, or getting an independent medical evaluation from a mental health provider counts as notice.
rules.quote: If, in lieu of a law enforcement report, the applicant or victim has obtained an order of protection, a civil no contact order, or a stalking no contact order, has presented to a medical facility for medical care or sexual assault evidence collection, has presented to a mental health provider for an independent medical evaluation, or is engaged in a legal proceeding involving a claim that the applicant or victim is a victim of human trafficking or law enforcement use of force, such action shall constitute appropriate notification under this Section.
rules.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b-1) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.scope: what a survivor must tell the medical facility for the visit to count as notice

rules.summary: A survivor who uses a medical facility visit as notice has to give the facility enough information to meet the Act's notice rules.
rules.quote: For purposes of notification under this Act, a victim who presents to a medical facility shall provide information sufficient to fulfill the requirements of this Section
rules.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b-2) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: A survivor who uses a medical facility visit as notice does not have to name the offender to the medical provider.
rules.quote: except that the victim shall not be required to identify the offender to the medical provider
rules.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b-2) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: The same steps also count as cooperating with law enforcement. One is getting an order of protection or a no contact order. Another is going to a medical facility for care or evidence collection. Another is getting an independent exam from a mental health provider.
rules.quote: If the applicant or victim has obtained an order of protection, a civil no contact order, or a stalking no contact order, has presented to a medical facility for medical care or sexual assault evidence collection, obtained an independent medical examination from a mental health provider as described in subsection (b-4), has taken any of the actions described in subsection (b-3), or is engaged in a legal proceeding involving a claim that the applicant or victim is a victim of human trafficking, such action shall constitute cooperation under this subsection (c).
rules.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(c) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: When the victim was under 18, cooperation is met if the applicant or victim files a police report, a mandated reporter reports the crime, or someone with firsthand knowledge reports it.
rules.quote: If the victim is under 18 years of age at the time of the commission of the offense, the following shall constitute cooperation under this subsection (c): (1) the applicant or the victim files a police report with a law enforcement agency; (2) a mandated reporter reports the crime to law enforcement; or (3) a person with firsthand knowledge of the crime reports the crime to law enforcement.
rules.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(c) (same text before and after P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: The program pays only after other sources, such as health insurance, public aid, Medicare, or workers' compensation, have been used.
rules.quote: Compensation under this Act is a secondary source of compensation and the applicant must show that he or she has exhausted the benefits reasonably available under the Criminal Victims' Escrow Account Act or any governmental or medical or health insurance programs
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Money raised through crowdfunding does not count as another source of payment and does not reduce the award.
rules.quote: Crowdfunding resources available to applicants are not considered collateral sources of payment, regardless of any statements made about what expenses the crowdfunding resources will be used to pay.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: An award can be reduced or denied to the extent the victim's injury was caused by the victim's provocation or incitement or by the victim committing a criminal act.
rules.quote: an award shall be reduced or denied according to the extent to which the victim's injury or death was caused by provocation or incitement by the victim or the victim assisting, attempting, or committing a criminal act.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: A victim's criminal history or felony status does not prevent compensation.
rules.quote: A victim's criminal history or felony status shall not prevent compensation to that victim or the victim's family.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: No award is paid while the applicant is held in a correctional institution, though they can apply at any time.
rules.quote: No compensation may be granted to an applicant under this Act while the applicant is held in a correctional institution. An applicant who is held in a correctional institution may apply for assistance under this Act at any time
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Compensation cannot be denied just because the victim is related to the offender or lived with the offender.
rules.quote: In no event shall an applicant be denied compensation solely because of the applicant's or the victim's familial relationship with the offender or because of the sharing of a dwelling by the victim or applicant and the offender.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: If compensation is probable and waiting would cause undue hardship, an emergency award can be made before the final decision, but only for funeral and burial costs paid to a funeral home and for relocation expenses. It is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: the Attorney General may recommend and the Court may make an emergency award of compensation to the applicant, pending a final decision in the case. Emergency awards may be issued to the applicant for the purpose of paying funeral and burial expenses directly to a funeral home and for relocation expenses incurred by an applicant.
rules.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/10.2(a) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Criminal sexual assault and aggravated criminal sexual abuse are listed among the violent crimes the program covers.
rules.quote: Aggravated Criminal Sexual Abuse • Criminal Sexual Assault
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation Program guide, What violent crimes are compensable (citing 740 ILCS 45/2(c))
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Program guide (Rev. 11/24)

rules.summary: The program's sexual assault FAQ says a person who was sexually assaulted in Illinois is eligible.
rules.quote: A person who was sexually assaulted in Illinois.
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims, Who is eligible?
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25)

params.rule: A person injured in Illinois by a crime of violence is a victim; the Act states no Illinois residency requirement for crimes in Illinois. Illinois residents hurt outside Illinois are covered only as described in IL-RES-2.

rules.summary: A person injured in Illinois as a result of a crime of violence counts as a victim.
rules.quote: a person killed or injured in this State as a result of a crime of violence perpetrated or attempted against him or her
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.rule: Illinois residents victimized outside Illinois qualify only if the place where the crime happened has no compensation law the resident is eligible for.

rules.summary: An Illinois resident hurt outside Illinois can apply only if the place where the crime happened has no victim compensation program they qualify for.
rules.quote: if the crime occurred outside this State, the resident has the same rights under this Act as if the crime had occurred in this State upon a showing that the state, territory, country, or political subdivision of a country in which the crime occurred does not have a compensation of victims of crimes law for which that Illinois resident is eligible
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: Apply online through the Attorney General's web form. The AG calls online submission the preferred method.
rules.quote:
Applications can be submitted online at
https://forms.illinoisattorneygeneral.gov/Forms/CrimeVictims_CompensationRequest
rules.pinpoint: FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25), closing paragraph
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25)

rules.summary: Fill out the fillable PDF application electronically and email it to the Attorney General's office.
rules.quote: For those who may require a form complete the fillable application electronically and return by email at CVA@ilag.gov
rules.pinpoint: AG Crime Victim Compensation page, Crime Victim Compensation Application section
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victim Compensation

params.target:
Office of the Illinois Attorney General
Crime Victim Compensation Bureau
115 South LaSalle Street
Chicago, IL 60603

rules.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Attorney General's Crime Victim Compensation Bureau in Chicago.
rules.quote:
Mail your completed application
to:
Office of the Illinois Attorney General
Crime Victim Compensation Bureau
115 South LaSalle Street
Chicago, IL 60603
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

params.note: Send a copy if available; the AG will request the report itself. Include the police report number in Section 2.

rules.summary: Send copies of supporting documents you have, such as the police report, with the application. If you do not have them yet, keep collecting them for when the office contacts you.
rules.quote:
If available, please send copies of all the documents you have with the completed
application (e.g., police report, plenary order of protection, civil no-contact order, hospital, or
doctor bills).
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

params.note: Copy of a plenary order of protection or civil no-contact order, if one was obtained

rules.summary: If you have a plenary order of protection or civil no-contact order, send a copy with the application.
rules.quote:
If available, please send copies of all the documents you have with the completed
application (e.g., police report, plenary order of protection, civil no-contact order, hospital, or
doctor bills).
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

params.note: Itemized medical, dental, or counseling bills; bills must also go to insurance and other payment sources first

rules.summary: For medical, dental, or counseling expenses, send copies of itemized bills, and submit those bills to insurance or other payment sources too.
rules.quote:
Please submit copies of itemized bills. All bills must be submitted to other sources of recovery available to
the victim.
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

params.note: Keep proof of payment; it is requested as proof of losses after the claim is found eligible

rules.summary: Keep receipts, bills, and other proof of payment for every expense you want reimbursed.
rules.quote: Keep receipts, bills, and any other proof of payment for all items you are seeking to receive compensation for.
rules.pinpoint: Compensation guide (Rev. 11/24), What proof of my expenses should I keep?
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Program guide (Rev. 11/24)

params.note: Proof of legal guardianship when applying for a minor or incapacitated adult victim

rules.summary: If you are the legal guardian of a minor or incapacitated adult victim, include documentation showing guardianship.
rules.quote: If the answer is YES, please provide documentation to show guardianship.
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

params.note: May be required when eligibility depends on living in the same dwelling as the victim

rules.summary: When eligibility depends on where you live, you may be asked for proof of residence such as a lease, utility bill, pay stub, tax form, or notarized statement.
rules.quote:
A person may be required to provide verification or proof of residence including, but not limited to,
a lease agreement, utility bill, license registration, document showing the mailing address, pay stub, tax form, or notarized statement.
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Program guide (Rev. 11/24)

params.note: Only for claims involving a law enforcement officer's use of force: documentation of related complaints, proceedings, or settlements

rules.summary: If the crime involved a law enforcement officer's use of force and you filed a complaint, lawsuit, or got a settlement, provide documentation of it.
rules.quote: If yes, please explain and provide documentation for all complaints, proceedings or settlements
rules.pinpoint: Application (Rev. 12/2024), Section 2, Use of Force Claims
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

params.agency: Office of the Illinois Attorney General
params.enroll: Complete the secure online application below or download and complete the PDF version of the ACP Application. The PDF application contains instructions on how to submit the application.

rules.summary: The Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, human trafficking, and stalking a substitute address to use with State and local government agencies instead of their home, school, or work address.
rules.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) provides a substitute address for victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, and stalking to use instead of their home, school, or work addresses when interacting with State and local government agencies.
rules.pinpoint: Illinois AG ACP page, opening paragraph; statutory basis 750 ILCS 61/11 and 61/15
rules.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Illinois Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

rules.summary: Under the Freedom of Information Act, the Attorney General's office does not have to release the records it gets to process a compensation application, such as the application, documents, and photographs.
rules.quote: Any records obtained by the Attorney General's office to process the application, including but not limited to applications, documents, and photographs, shall be exempt from disclosure by the Attorney General's office under the Freedom of Information Act.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rules.summary: A provider that gives a forensic medical exam under Indiana's sex crime victim law may not charge the victim, even if the state is slow to reimburse.
rules.quote: A provider may not charge the victim for services required under this chapter despite delays in reimbursement from the division.
rules.source_title: IC 16-21-8-6 (services without charge; reimbursement) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: A licensed medical provider other than a hospital that chooses to do a forensic exam must also do it free and may not charge the victim.
rules.quote: A medical service provider may not charge the victim for a forensic medical exam required under this chapter even if there is a delay in receiving reimbursement from the division.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-39 (payment of forensic medical exams) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: A provider that gives a forensic medical exam and additional forensic services to a sex crime victim must provide them without charge.
rules.quote: When a provider provides forensic medical exams and additional forensic services under this chapter to a victim, the provider shall furnish the services without charge.
rules.source_title: IC 16-21-8-6 (services without charge; reimbursement) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

params.payer: Indiana Criminal Justice Institute, Victim Services Division (violent crime compensation fund), paid to the provider

rules.summary: The state's Victim Services Division pays for the forensic medical exam. Payment for additional forensic services beyond the exam has extra conditions in the same section.
rules.quote: The division shall award compensation or reimbursement under this chapter for forensic medical exams.
rules.source_title: IC 16-21-8-5 (payment of forensic medical exams) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: An award may not exceed $15,000 and does not cover the first $100 of the claim.
rules.quote: (a) An award to a claimant under this chapter: (1) may not exceed fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000); and (2) may not cover the first one hundred dollars ($100) of the claim.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-35 (amount of awards) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: Outpatient mental health counseling related to the crime is covered up to $3,000.
rules.quote: (7) Outpatient mental health counseling, not to exceed three thousand dollars ($3,000), concerning mental health issues related to the violent crime.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: Child care that replaces care the victim would have provided is covered up to $1,000.
rules.quote: (4) Expense incurred for child care, not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000), to replace child care the victim would have supplied had the victim not died or been injured.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: Funeral, burial, or cremation expenses are covered up to $5,000.
rules.quote: (6) Expenses incurred for funeral, burial, or cremation of the victim that do not exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000).
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: Necessary medical, hospital, dental, optometric, chiropractic and ambulance services, prescription drugs, and prosthetic devices are covered if incurred within 180 days of the crime.
rules.quote: the division may order the payment of compensation under this chapter for any of the following reasonable, documented expenses incurred within one hundred eighty (180) days after the date of the violent crime: (1) Necessary: (A) medical, chiropractic, hospital, dental, optometric, and ambulance services; (B) prescription drugs; and (C) prosthetic devices;
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: The director may extend the 180-day expense window up to 2 years after the crime when the victim asks and medical records support it.
rules.quote: The director may extend the one hundred eighty (180) day compensation period established by subsection (d) for a period not to exceed two (2) years after the date of the violent crime if: (1) the victim or the victim's representative requests the extension; and (2) medical records and other documentation provided by the attending medical providers indicate that an extension is appropriate.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: Lost income is covered if the victim was employed at the time of the crime.
rules.quote: (2) Loss of income: (A) the victim would have earned had the victim not died or been injured, if the victim was employed at the time of the violent crime;
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

params.scope: emergency shelter to stay away from the offender, up to 30 days

rules.summary: Emergency shelter care to avoid contact with the offender is covered for up to 30 days of expenses.
rules.quote: (3) Emergency shelter care expenses, not to exceed the expenses for thirty (30) days, that are incurred for the claimant or a dependent of the claimant to avoid contact with a person who committed the violent crime.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

params.scope: replacing windows or door locks

rules.summary: Replacing windows or door locks is covered.
rules.quote: (9) Replacement of windows or door locks.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: Cleanup of the crime scene is covered.
rules.quote: (10) Cleanup of the scene of a violent crime.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: Prescription drugs are covered as part of necessary medical expenses.
rules.quote: (B) prescription drugs; and (C) prosthetic devices;
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: Counseling costs must fall within 180 days of the crime, unless the director extends this where justice requires, up to 2 years.
rules.quote: The director may extend the one hundred eighty (180) day compensation period established by subsection (d) for outpatient mental health counseling, established by subsection (d)(7) where justice requires, but for a period not to exceed two (2) years.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

params.item: property damage other than windows or door locks; replacement of property or cash

rules.summary: The program does not pay for property damage, other than replacing windows or door locks, or for replacing property or cash, so replacing something like a phone is not covered.
rules.quote: Property damage (other than the replacement of windows or door locks) and replacement of property or cash.
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

params.item: moving, relocation, or daily living expenses

rules.summary: The program lists moving, relocation, and daily living expenses as not reimbursable.
rules.quote: Moving, relocation or daily living expenses.
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

params.item: rent, utilities, food, travel, or lodging

rules.summary: The program lists rent, utilities, food, travel, and lodging as not reimbursable (ambulance services are covered as medical).
rules.quote: Rent, utilities, food, travel, or lodging.
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: Pain and suffering is not compensated.
rules.quote: Pain and suffering.
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

params.item: paid vacation, sick, or personal leave

rules.summary: Paid leave must be used first, and the program will not reimburse time covered by paid vacation, sick, or personal leave.
rules.quote: The division may not reimburse the claimant for the use of paid or otherwise compensated vacation leave, sick leave, personal leave, or other compensatory time.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-32 (reduction of awards; collateral sources) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

params.item: costs incurred more than 180 days after the crime

rules.summary: The program pays the costs this law lists only if they are reasonable, documented, and incurred within 180 days after the crime, unless the director extends that period.
rules.quote: (d) Subject to subsections (b) and (c), the division may order the payment of compensation under this chapter for any of the following reasonable, documented expenses incurred within one hundred eighty (180) days after the date of the violent crime:
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

params.extension: or later if the division gives you more time for good cause. In most cases, the division cannot take an application more than 2 years after the crime

rules.summary: The application must reach the division within 180 days of the crime. The division may give more time for good cause, but in most cases it cannot accept an application more than 2 years after the crime.
rules.quote: the application must be received by the division not more than one hundred eighty (180) days after the date the crime was committed. The division may grant an extension of time for good cause shown by the claimant. However, and except as provided in subsections (e) and (f), the division may not accept an application that is received more than two (2) years after the date the crime was committed.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-16 (applications for assistance) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: A victim of a child sex crime can apply until turning 31, or later in some cases.
rules.quote: (e) An alleged victim of a child sex crime may submit an application to the division until the victim becomes thirty-one (31) years of age or in accordance with subsection (f).
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-16 (applications for assistance) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: For some child sex crimes, a victim can also apply within 5 years after the earliest of these: the state first finds DNA evidence or a recording that is enough to charge the offender, or someone confesses.
rules.quote: (f) An alleged victim of a child sex crime described in IC 35-41-4-2 (e) which meets the requirements of IC 35-41-4-2 (p) may submit an application to the division not later than five (5) years after the earliest of the date on which: (1) the state first discovers evidence sufficient to charge the offender with the offense through DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) analysis; (2) the state first becomes aware of the existence of a recording (as defined in IC 35-31.5-2-273 ) that provides evidence sufficient to charge the offender with the offense; or (3) a person confesses to the offense.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-16 (applications for assistance) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: Except for child sex crime victims, the crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours.
rules.quote: (a) Except for an alleged victim of a child sex crime, the division may not award compensation under this chapter unless the violent crime was reported to a law enforcement officer not more than seventy-two (72) hours after the occurrence of the crime.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-17 (requirements for compensation) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: The division may accept proof that evidence was collected in a forensic exam in place of the police report and cooperation requirements.
rules.quote: (d) The division may accept proof that evidence was collected through a forensic exam described in IC 16-21-8 as compliance with subsection (a) and as cooperation with law enforcement, as required by sections 18 and 19 of this chapter.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-17 (requirements for compensation) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: The division may waive the reporting and cooperation requirements if it finds a compelling reason and justice requires.
rules.quote: the division finds a compelling reason for failure to report to or cooperate with law enforcement officials; and (2) justice requires; the division may suspend the requirements of section 17, 18, or 19 of this chapter.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-20 (suspension of reporting and cooperation requirements) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: A hospital must give the forensic exam and additional forensic services whether or not the victim reports to or cooperates with police.
rules.quote: The provision of services may not be dependent on a victim's reporting to, or cooperating with, law enforcement.
rules.source_title: IC 16-21-8-1 (forensic medical exams; sex crimes) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: A claimant must have more than $100 in out-of-pocket expenses or more than $100 in lost income; this does not apply to forensic exam reimbursement.
rules.quote: (b) This section does not apply to reimbursement for forensic and evidence gathering services provided under section 39 of this chapter. (c) An award may not be made unless the claimant has incurred an out-of-pocket expense that exceeds one hundred dollars ($100) or has incurred loss of income that exceeds one hundred dollars ($100).
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: The program pays last: awards are reduced or denied to the extent the loss is recovered from insurance or other collateral sources.
rules.quote: Compensation must be further reduced or denied to the extent that the claimant's loss is recouped from other collateral sources.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-32 (reduction of awards; collateral sources) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: If the division finds the victim contributed to the injury, it may deny the award.
rules.quote: If the division finds that the victim contributed to the infliction of the victim's injury or death, the division may deny an award.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-34 (victim's contributory conduct) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: The bar on benefits for a victim who was intoxicated and contributed to an unrelated felony does not apply to victims of sex crimes or domestic or family violence.
rules.quote: Benefits may be awarded to a person described in subsection (a)(4) who is the victim of a sex crime under IC 35-42-4 , a crime involving domestic or family violence
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-13 (participants in criminal acts; exceptions) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: If the director finds a severe financial hardship, the director may give an emergency award of up to $500 before the final decision.
rules.quote: An emergency award of not more than five hundred dollars ($500) may be made by the director or his or her designee prior to the determination of final award if it is determined by the director that a severe financial hardship exists.
rules.source_title: 203 IAC 1 (Victim Services Division administrative procedure), Indiana Administrative Code

rules.summary: Sexual assault victims who had a forensic exam are eligible for compensation whether or not they involve the police.
rules.quote: victims of sexual assault who have had a forensic exam conducted are eligible for compensation, whether or not they choose to involve the police.
rules.pinpoint: ICJI program page, Additional eligibility requirements
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

rules.summary: A covered violent crime is any felony or Class A misdemeanor that causes bodily injury or death.
rules.quote: A crime under the Indiana Code that is a felony of any kind or a Class A misdemeanor that results in bodily injury or death to the victim
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-8 (violent crime) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

params.rule: Indiana residents hurt in Indiana, or elsewhere if that place has no substantially similar program; nonresidents hurt in Indiana.

rules.summary: Indiana residents can apply for crimes in Indiana, or in another place that has no similar program; nonresidents can apply for crimes committed in Indiana.
rules.quote: (1) A resident of Indiana who is a victim of a violent crime committed: (A) in Indiana; or (B) in a jurisdiction other than Indiana, including a foreign country, if the jurisdiction in which the violent crime occurs does not offer assistance to a victim of a violent crime that is substantially similar to the assistance offered under this chapter. (2) A nonresident of Indiana who is a victim of a violent crime committed in Indiana.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-12 (persons eligible) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

params.target: Indiana Government Center South, 402 W. Washington Street, Room W469, Indianapolis, IN 46204

rules.summary: Mail the paper application to the Indiana Criminal Justice Institute, 402 W. Washington Street, Room W469, Indianapolis, IN 46204.
rules.quote: If applying online isn't an option, PDF applications can be mailed or hand delivered to the Indiana Criminal Justice Institute at: Indiana Government Center South, 402 W. Washington Street, Room W469, Indianapolis, IN 46204.
rules.pinpoint: Apply for Violent Crime Compensation, File a PDF claim
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

params.target: Indiana Government Center South, 402 W. Washington Street, Room W469, Indianapolis, IN 46204

rules.summary: The paper application can also be hand delivered to the same office in the Indiana Government Center South.
rules.quote: If applying online isn't an option, PDF applications can be mailed or hand delivered to the Indiana Criminal Justice Institute at: Indiana Government Center South, 402 W. Washington Street, Room W469, Indianapolis, IN 46204.
rules.pinpoint: Apply for Violent Crime Compensation, File a PDF claim
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

rules.summary: The paper application can be faxed to 317-232-7103.
rules.quote: They can also be faxed to: 317-232-7103.
rules.pinpoint: Apply for Violent Crime Compensation, File a PDF claim
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

params.note: Not needed at filing; the claims analyst gets it later. Survivors who had a forensic exam do not have to report.

rules.summary: The claims analyst gathers the police report and supplemental reports during the review; you do not have to send it with the application.
rules.quote: (1) A police report including all supplemental reports and victim and witness statements made to law enforcement personnel.
rules.source_title: 203 IAC 1 (Victim Services Division administrative procedure), Indiana Administrative Code

params.note: Not needed at filing; bills are requested during the review.

rules.summary: Expenses are paid only when an itemized bill verifies them, so keep itemized bills for every crime-related cost.
rules.quote: Expenses that cannot be verified via an itemized bill.
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

params.note: Proof of payment for anything you paid yourself.

rules.summary: Out-of-pocket costs are reimbursed only with proof of payment, so keep receipts.
rules.quote: Out of pocket expenses without proof of payment.
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

params.note: Employment or earnings information, and child care cost records if claiming child care.

rules.summary: For lost wages or child care, the program collects documentation of employment, earnings, or substitute child care costs.
rules.quote: (4) Documentation regarding substitute child care expenses, employment, or earnings information.
rules.source_title: 203 IAC 1 (Victim Services Division administrative procedure), Indiana Administrative Code

params.note: Insurance, Social Security, pension, workers' compensation, or unemployment benefit information.

rules.summary: Because the program pays last, it collects records of insurance and other benefits that covered any of the costs.
rules.quote: (5) Documentation concerning the following: (A) Medical or life insurance benefits, or both. (B) Social Security, pension, or retirement benefit information. (C) Worker's compensation or unemployment compensation benefits.
rules.source_title: 203 IAC 1 (Victim Services Division administrative procedure), Indiana Administrative Code

params.note: Loss of support only: proof of legal dependent status, marriage and support, or paternity and support.

rules.summary: Dependents claiming loss of support must verify their dependent status and the support the victim provided.
rules.quote: (Note: This requires verification of legal dependent status, marriage and support, or paternity and support).
rules.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

params.note: Parent or legal guardian signature and date if the claimant is under 18.

rules.summary: If the claimant is under 18, a parent or legal guardian signs and dates the application.
rules.quote: If the claimant is less than eighteen (18) years old, a parent or legal guardian must sign and date the application.
rules.source_title: Application for Benefits from Violent Crimes Compensation Fund, State Form 23776 (R14 / 9-21)

rules.summary: Once an award is computed, it must be paid within 30 days; the FAQ says claims are typically processed within a few months.
rules.quote: an award must be paid not more than thirty (30) days after the date on which the award is computed
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-43 (computation and payment of awards) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

params.agency: Office of the Indiana Attorney General
params.enroll: Your application must be signed by a trained victim advocate. Your victim advocate has all the required documents. If you need help finding a list of trained advocates in your area, click here . To learn more about the program e-mail confidential@atg.in.gov .

rules.summary: Indiana's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Attorney General's Office, is free and lets survivors of sexual assault and other listed crimes keep a confidential address: first-class mail goes to a secure substitute address and is forwarded, and the substitute address is used for state and local government services.
rules.quote: The ACP is a free program that allows victims of domestic violence, sexual assault stalking, human trafficking, harassment, intimidation, or invasion of privacy to maintain a confidential address through the Attorney General's Office.
rules.pinpoint: Attorney General, Address Confidentiality Program page, opening paragraphs
rules.source_title: Indiana Attorney General, Address Confidentiality Program

rules.summary: Indiana law makes a compensation claimant's personal information and medical records confidential, along with records from the division's claim investigation that are not publicly available.
rules.quote: The following are confidential: (1) A claimant's: (A) personal information (as defined in IC 9-14-6-6 ); and (B) medical records. (2) Records obtained during an investigation under section 26 of this chapter that are not publicly available.
rules.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-11.5 (confidentiality) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rules.summary: The fee for a sexual assault forensic exam may not be charged or billed to the survivor or to the survivor's insurance.
rules.quote: The fee for conducting an examination of a victim pursuant to this section shall not be charged or billed to the victim or to the victim's insurance carrier.
rules.pinpoint: K.S.A. 65-448(h) as amended by 2026 HB 2613, sec. 1
rules.source_title: 2026 HB 2613, enrolled (amends K.S.A. 65-448)

params.payer: Kansas Crime Victims Compensation Board (crime victims compensation fund)
params.condition: if the crime was in Kansas

rules.summary: For assaults in Kansas, the state Crime Victims Compensation program pays for sexual assault forensic exams starting July 1, 2026.
rules.quote: Effective July 1, 2026, sexual assault forensic examinations for assaults that occur in Kansas, are to be paid by Kansas Crime Victims Compensation.
rules.pinpoint: Kansas AG Crime Victims Compensation page, SAFE Program section
rules.source_title: Kansas Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Board page

params.payer: Kansas Crime Victims Compensation Board

rules.summary: Payment of the exam fee does not depend on the survivor otherwise qualifying for a compensation award.
rules.quote: Payment of such fee is not contingent on a victim or claimant being otherwise eligible for compensation under K.S.A. 74-7301 et seq., and amendments thereto.
rules.source_title: 2026 HB 2613, enrolled (amends K.S.A. 65-448)

params.payer: Kansas Crime Victims Compensation Board (exam only, not treatment)

rules.summary: The exam payment covers the forensic exam only. Other medical treatment from the same visit is billed to the survivor or their insurance, and the survivor can apply for compensation for it.
rules.quote: The CVCB will only pay for the exam, not the medical treatment, of sexual assault victims.
rules.pinpoint: SAFE Program Reimbursement Invoice, Billing Instructions
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Forensic Examination (SAFE) Program Reimbursement Invoice

rules.summary: All compensation paid for one victim's injury, to the victim and every other claimant combined, may not exceed $25,000.
rules.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of that victim may not exceed $25,000 in the aggregate.

rules.summary: Lost wages are paid at the actual loss or $800 per week, whichever is less.
rules.quote: Compensation for work loss, replacement services loss, dependent's economic loss and dependent's replacement service loss may not exceed $800 per week or actual loss, whichever is less.

rules.summary: Mental health counseling is covered up to $5,000; the board can approve more in extenuating circumstances.
rules.quote: Any victim of a crime may be considered for up to a $5,000 mental health counseling award.
rules.source_title: K.A.R. 20-2-3 Mental health counseling award

rules.summary: Outpatient individual or family counseling in a nonmedical setting is paid at up to $90 per hour.
rules.quote: Individual and family mental health counseling in a nonmedical setting $90 per hour
rules.source_title: K.A.R. 20-2-3 Mental health counseling award

rules.summary: Group therapy is paid at up to $60 per hour.
rules.quote: Group therapy $60 per hour
rules.source_title: K.A.R. 20-2-3 Mental health counseling award

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is covered up to $2,500.
rules.quote: "Allowance expense" includes a total charge not in excess of $2,500 for expenses in any way related to crime scene cleanup.

rules.summary: Funeral, cremation or burial expenses are covered up to $7,500.
rules.quote: "Allowance expense" includes a total charge not in excess of $7,500 for expenses in any way related to funeral, cremation or burial

rules.summary: Reasonable medical care, mental health counseling and other services needed because of the injury are covered.
rules.quote: This includes reasonable medical care, mental health counseling or other services necessary as a result of the injury.
rules.pinpoint: Kansas AG Crime Victims Compensation page, overview
rules.source_title: Kansas Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Board page

params.scope: mileage for medically necessary travel

rules.summary: Mileage for medically necessary travel can be covered, at no more than the state mileage rate.
rules.quote: Mileage costs may be deemed allowable expenses for medically necessary travel.
rules.source_title: K.A.R. 20-2-9 Allowable expenses

params.scope: moving costs, if a law enforcement officer, a prosecutor, or a victim advocate at a law enforcement agency or prosecutor's office recommends the move in writing

rules.summary: Moving costs can be covered when a law enforcement officer, a prosecutor, or a victim advocate at a law enforcement agency or prosecutor's office recommends the move in writing for reasons related to the crime.
rules.quote: Moving costs may be deemed allowable expenses if one of the following individuals has recommended the move in writing for reasons related to the crime: (1) A law enforcement officer; (2) a prosecutor; or (3) a victims' advocate working for a law enforcement agency or prosecutor's office.
rules.source_title: K.A.R. 20-2-9 Allowable expenses

params.scope: replacing clothing and bedding seized as evidence

rules.summary: Reasonable costs to replace clothing and bedding seized as evidence are covered.
rules.quote: Reasonable costs for replacement of clothing and bedding seized as evidence are compensable.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.item: personal property loss (for example a phone), except clothing and bedding seized as evidence or property removed during crime scene cleanup

rules.summary: Lost or damaged personal property, such as a phone, is not covered. The exceptions are clothing and bedding seized as evidence and property removed during crime scene cleanup.
rules.quote: Personal property loss is not covered, with the exception of clothing and bedding seized as evidence, or property that had to be removed during the crime scene clean-up process.
rules.pinpoint: Kansas AG Crime Victims Compensation page, overview
rules.source_title: Kansas Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Board page

params.item: pain and suffering; other property loss and property damage

rules.summary: Pain and suffering, and property loss or damage other than the listed exceptions, are not paid.
rules.quote: Other property loss, property damage and pain and suffering are ineligible expenses.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.item: meals

rules.summary: Meal costs are not covered.
rules.quote: Meal costs shall not be deemed allowable expenses.
rules.source_title: K.A.R. 20-2-9 Allowable expenses

params.extension: or within 2 years of being told a suspect was identified, through DNA or otherwise

rules.summary: Most claims must be filed within five years of the injury. If a survivor is told that DNA testing of a sexual assault kit or other evidence matched a suspect, or that a suspect was identified, they have two years from that notice.
rules.quote: (A) The claim has been filed with the division within five years after the injury or death upon which the claim is based; (B) in a case where a victim who is notified that DNA testing of a sexual assault kit or other evidence has revealed a DNA profile of a suspected offender who victimized the victim or the victim on whose behalf the claim is made, or is notified of the identification of a suspected offender who victimized the victim or the victim on whose behalf the claim is made, the claim has been filed with the division within two years of such notification

rules.summary: For a sexually violent crime, the board may accept a claim filed within 10 years after the crime. "Sexually violent crime" is a defined list in K.S.A. 22-3717 that includes rape and aggravated sexual battery but not every sexual offense.
rules.quote: a victim of a sexually violent crime as defined in K.S.A. 22-3717, and amendments thereto, if: (a) The claim has been filed with the division within 10 years after the date such crime was committed

rules.summary: If the survivor of a sexually violent crime was under 18 when it happened, the board may accept a claim filed up to 10 years after they turn 18.
rules.quote: the victim was less than 18 years of age at the time such crime was committed, and the claim has been filed within 10 years after the date the victim turns 18 years of age

rules.summary: If the victim was under 16, a claim is due within 2 years of the report to police. This applies to a sexually violent crime and to some trafficking or enticement crimes.
rules.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless an application has been filed with the division within two years of the reporting of the incident to law enforcement officials if the victim was less than 16 years of age

rules.summary: The board may still award compensation if denying it would be a severe injustice to the victim. If more than one time limit applies, the longest one counts.
rules.quote: (D) the board determines that denying compensation would be a severe injustice to the victim. (3) If more than one of the time limitations described in subsection (b)(1) or (b)(2) apply to a victim, the longest time limitation to file a claim shall apply to the victim.

rules.summary: To qualify, the crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, OR the survivor must have had a forensic medical exam within seven days, OR the board must find good cause for missing both.
rules.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless: (1) The criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within 72 hours after the occurrence of the criminally injurious conduct; (2) the victim obtained a forensic medical examination within seven days after the occurrence of the criminally injurious conduct; or (3) the board finds there was good cause for the failure to report or obtain an examination within the time limits provided in this subsection.

params.scope: forensic exam fee only

rules.summary: The board must pay the forensic exam fee even if the survivor chooses not to report the assault to law enforcement.
rules.quote: refusal of the victim to report the alleged offense to law enforcement shall not excuse
rules.pinpoint: K.S.A. 65-448(h) as amended by 2026 HB 2613, sec. 1
rules.source_title: 2026 HB 2613, enrolled (amends K.S.A. 65-448)

rules.summary: The board can deny, withdraw or reduce an award if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement.
rules.quote: The board, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies, may deny, withdraw or reduce an award of compensation.

rules.summary: Compensation is reduced by anything already recovered from other sources, such as insurance.
rules.quote: Economic loss upon which the claimant's claim is based is recouped from other persons, including collateral sources

rules.summary: Kansas pays only if the board finds that, without an award, the costs of the crime would cause the claimant financial stress. That means the claimant could not keep up their usual level of health, safety, and education for themselves and their dependents without undue financial hardship.
rules.quote: Compensation may be awarded only if the board finds that unless the claimant is awarded compensation the claimant will suffer financial stress as the result of economic loss otherwise reparable. A claimant suffers financial stress only if the claimant cannot maintain the claimant's customary level of health, safety and education for self and dependents without undue financial hardship.

rules.summary: The board may reduce or deny an award for the claimant's or victim's contributory misconduct.
rules.quote: board deems reasonable because of the contributory misconduct of the claimant or of a victim through whom the claimant claims

rules.summary: The reduction for a victim likely engaging in unlawful activity at the time of the crime may not be used against victims of domestic abuse or sexual assault.
rules.quote: The provisions of subsection (d)(1)(C) shall not be construed to reduce or deny compensation to a victim of domestic abuse or sexual assault.

rules.summary: If the claimant would face financial hardship and a final award looks likely, the board may pay a tentative award that is later deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: If the board determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made, and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant and shall be deducted from the final award

rules.summary: Adult sexual assault is a listed crime type on the state compensation application.
rules.quote: Sexual Assault (Adult)
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.rule: Crime occurred in Kansas; or Kansas domiciliary victimized in a U.S. state or territory with no eligible compensation program; or Kansas domiciliary victimized outside the United States (74-7301(e)(2)).

rules.summary: Crimes that happen in Kansas are covered. A Kansas resident hurt by a violent crime in another U.S. state or territory can apply only if that place has no eligible compensation program and the crime would be covered in Kansas.
rules.quote: Occurs or is attempted in this state or occurs to a person whose domicile is in Kansas who is the victim of a violent crime which occurs in another state, possession, or territory of the United States of America may make an application for compensation if: (i) The crimes would be compensable had it occurred in the state of Kansas; and (ii) the places the crimes occurred are states, possessions or territories of the United States of America not having eligible crime victim compensation programs

params.rule: Kansas domiciliary victimized outside the United States

rules.summary: A violent crime committed outside the United States against a Kansas resident can also qualify.
rules.quote: a violent crime that posed a substantial threat or caused personal injury or death, committed outside of the United States against a person whose domicile is in Kansas

params.target: Division of Crime Victims Compensation 120 SW 10th Ave, 2nd Floor Topeka, KS 66612-1597

rules.summary: Mail the paper application to the Division of Crime Victims Compensation at the Attorney General's office in Topeka (the contact address on the board's page; the form itself has no mail-to line).
rules.quote: Contact Division of Crime Victims Compensation 120 SW 10th Ave, 2nd Floor Topeka, KS 66612-1597
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation Board page, Contact
rules.source_title: Kansas Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Board page

params.note: Itemized statements or bills for hospital, doctor, ambulance, x-ray, prescription and dental charges, if available.

rules.summary: For medical costs, attach itemized statements or bills if you have them.
rules.quote: including hospital and doctor charges, ambulance fees, x-rays, prescriptions and dental. Please attach itemized statements or bills, receipts and insurance statements if they are available.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.note: Receipts for medical costs, if available.

rules.summary: For medical costs, attach receipts if you have them.
rules.quote: including hospital and doctor charges, ambulance fees, x-rays, prescriptions and dental. Please attach itemized statements or bills, receipts and insurance statements if they are available.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.note: Insurance statements for medical costs, if available.

rules.summary: For medical costs, attach insurance statements if you have them.
rules.quote: including hospital and doctor charges, ambulance fees, x-rays, prescriptions and dental. Please attach itemized statements or bills, receipts and insurance statements if they are available.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.note: Itemized counseling statements or bills, if available.

rules.summary: For counseling, attach itemized statements or bills if you have them.
rules.quote: Section I – Counseling Information (Please attach itemized statements or bills, receipts and insurance statements if they are available.)
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.note: Receipts for counseling, if available.

rules.summary: For counseling, attach receipts if you have them.
rules.quote: Section I – Counseling Information (Please attach itemized statements or bills, receipts and insurance statements if they are available.)
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.note: Insurance statements for counseling, if available.

rules.summary: For counseling, attach insurance statements if you have them.
rules.quote: Section I – Counseling Information (Please attach itemized statements or bills, receipts and insurance statements if they are available.)
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.note: Most recent federal income tax return and/or pay stubs.

rules.summary: For lost wages, attach your most recent federal income tax return and/or pay stubs.
rules.quote: Applicants for wage loss must attach a copy of their most recent Federal Income Tax Return and/or pay stubs.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.note: Copies of funeral and burial bills.

rules.summary: For funeral benefits for a deceased victim, attach copies of the bills.
