rules.quote: Complete section if you are seeking funeral benefits for a deceased victim and attach copies of bills.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.note: Loss of support (death claims): marriage certificate, birth certificates and/or child support orders.

rules.summary: For loss of support in a death claim, attach a marriage certificate, birth certificates and/or child support orders.
rules.quote: If yes, please attach copies of a marriage certificate, birth certificate(s) and/or child support order(s).
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.note: The completed and signed application; unsigned or incomplete applications are returned.

rules.summary: Send the application completed and signed; incomplete or unsigned applications are sent back, which delays the decision.
rules.quote: Applications which are not completed and signed will be returned, thus delaying a decision on your claim.
rules.pinpoint: Application, How to File Your Application for Compensation
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

rules.summary: The full application and investigation process may take about 3 months.
rules.quote: The complete application/investigation process may take approximately 3 months.
rules.pinpoint: Application, How to File Your Application for Compensation
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victim Compensation (revised May 2025)

params.agency: Office of the Kansas Attorney General, Victim Services Division
params.enroll: All victims must go through a certified enrolling assistant to apply to participate in the program. A person seeking enrollment cannot apply directly to the Attorney General's office.

rules.summary: A survivor of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking or human trafficking who fears for their safety may apply to Kansas's Safe at Home program.
rules.quote: Anyone who is a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, trafficking, or stalking and fears for their safety may apply to Safe at Home.
rules.pinpoint: How Safe at Home Works, Eligibility Criteria
rules.source_title: How Safe at Home Works (Kansas Address Confidentiality Program)

rules.summary: All records and information given to the Crime Victims Compensation Board and division to process a claim are confidential, and the records gathered to evaluate a claim cannot be obtained through discovery in a civil or criminal case except in situations the law lists.
rules.quote: All records and information given to the board and the crime victims compensation division created by K.S.A. 75-773, and amendments thereto, to process a claim on behalf of a crime victim shall be confidential.
rules.source_title: K.S.A. 74-7308 (confidentiality of records given to the Crime Victims Compensation Board)

rules.summary: When a sexual assault exam is given, no hospital, exam facility, clinician, pharmacist, health department, the survivor's insurer, or the state may charge the survivor for the exam, even if the exam is not completed.
rules.quote: When an examination of a victim of a sexual offense is provided in accordance with this section, no charge shall be made to the victim by the hospital, the sexual assault examination facility, the physician, the pharmacist, the health department, the sexual assault nurse examiner, other qualified medical professional, the victim's insurance carrier, or the Commonwealth for: (a) Sexual assault examinations, whether or not the exam is completed;
rules.source_title: KRS 216B.400 (sexual offense examinations)

rules.summary: The no-charge rule also covers preventive medication, strangulation assessments, and other tests or services tied to the assault or exam on the same date as the exam, including triage and ambulance costs.
rules.quote: (b) Prophylactic medical treatment; (c) Strangulation assessments; or (d) Other medical tests or services, including triage and ambulance expenses, related to the incident, exam, or treatment which occur on the same date as the original exam.
rules.source_title: KRS 216B.400 (sexual offense examinations)

rules.summary: A survivor cannot be refused an exam or billed for it because they choose not to file a police report, cooperate with law enforcement, or take part in the criminal case.
rules.quote: No victim shall be denied an examination, or billed in violation of subsection (10) of this section, because the victim chooses not to file a police report, cooperate with law enforcement, or otherwise participate in the criminal justice system.
rules.source_title: KRS 216B.400 (sexual offense examinations)

rules.summary: The exam program's FAQ says providers should bill the patient's Medicaid or private insurance first, but may not charge a co-pay or deductible.
rules.quote: If a patient has insurance, whether Medicaid or Private insurance, that insurance should be billed first before billing the SAEP, but no co-pay or deductible may be charged as a condition for payment.
rules.pinpoint: SAEP FAQ, "Can we bill the patient's Insurance?"
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Examination Program FAQ (revised 11/2023)

params.payer: Crime Victims Compensation Board (Sexual Assault Examination Program), paid to the provider

rules.summary: The Crime Victims Compensation Board pays for sexual assault exams and the related no-charge services, at rates set by its regulation.
rules.quote: The examinations provided in accordance with this section and other services provided to a victim pursuant to subsection (10) of this section shall be paid for by the Crime Victims Compensation Board at a rate to be determined by the administrative regulation promulgated by the board
rules.source_title: KRS 216B.400 (sexual offense examinations)

rules.summary: The total award for a claimant cannot exceed $50,000.
rules.quote: Any award made under KRS 49.270 to 49.490 shall not exceed fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) in total compensation to be received by or paid on behalf of a claimant from the fund.
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

rules.summary: Lost earnings or lost support are paid at net earnings, up to $500 for each week.
rules.quote: the award shall be equal to net earnings at the time of the criminally injurious conduct; however, no award under this subsection shall exceed five hundred dollars ($500) for each week of lost earnings or financial support.
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

rules.summary: When the crime happened at the victim's home, moving to a new primary residence for safety within 6 months of the crime is covered up to $2,000. The board may allow relocation costs incurred after 6 months at its discretion.
rules.quote: For the victim and for any child who is the victim's dependent, when the crime was committed at the primary residence of the victim: a. Relocation if the victim is moving from one (1) primary residence to another due to concern for the safety of themselves or other persons at the residence as a result of a crime within six (6) months of the crime, not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000). The board may, in its discretion, allow relocation expenses incurred after six (6) months
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

rules.summary: Temporary housing within 30 days of the crime, when the victim cannot stay at home because of the crime, is covered up to $2,000 (this applies when the crime happened at the victim's home).
rules.quote: Temporary housing costs incurred within thirty (30) days of the crime, when the victim is unable to stay in the primary residence due to the crime, not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000);
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

rules.summary: Replacing or repairing windows and locks at the victim's home or business damaged in the crime is covered up to $1,500.
rules.quote: Replacement or repair of windows and locks at the primary residence or business of the victim which were damaged by the commission of the crime, not to exceed one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500);
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup within 30 days at the victim's home or business is covered up to $2,000.
rules.quote: Crime scene cleanup within thirty (30) days of the crime when the crime was committed at the primary residence or business of the victim, not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000);
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

rules.summary: Funeral and burial costs cannot exceed $10,000.
rules.quote: In no event shall an award for funeral expenses exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000).
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

rules.summary: Mental health counseling needed because of the crime is paid for up to 2 years. It is paid only after proper documentation is sent to the board.
rules.quote: Mental health counseling, necessary as a result of the injury upon which the claim is based. Mental health counseling: a. Shall be paid for a maximum of two (2) years, but only after proper documentation is submitted to the board
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

rules.summary: Awards cover out-of-pocket expenses, including lost earnings or support and debts reasonably incurred for medical or other services.
rules.quote: Any award made pursuant to KRS 49.270 to 49.490 shall be in an amount not exceeding out-of-pocket expenses, including loss of earnings or support resulting from the injury on which the claim is based and indebtedness reasonably incurred for medical or other services
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

rules.summary: The program lists medical and dental expenses as compensable.
rules.quote: Medical/dental expenses;
rules.pinpoint: CVCB FAQ, "What categories of expenses are compensable by the Board?"
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Board FAQ (updated August 2024)

params.scope: replacing items police seized as evidence, up to $500 per item

rules.summary: The program can pay back the cost of replacing items that police seized as evidence of the crime, up to $500 per item. This covers items owned by the victim or by the victim's dependent child.
rules.quote: Reimbursement for the replacement of items owned by the victim and for any child who is the victim's dependent that were seized by law enforcement as evidence of the commission of the crime, not to exceed five hundred dollars ($500) per item;
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

params.item: replacing eyeglasses or other corrective lenses stolen, destroyed, or damaged during the crime

rules.summary: Replacing eyeglasses or other corrective lenses stolen, destroyed, or damaged in the crime is covered.
rules.quote: Replacement of eyeglasses and other corrective lenses stolen, destroyed, or damaged during the crime.
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

params.item: rehabilitative or wellness practices a healthcare provider recommends, up to $1,000 a year per person for up to 2 years

rules.summary: Rehabilitative or wellness practices recommended by a healthcare provider are covered up to $1,000 per year per person, for at most 2 years.
rules.quote: Rehabilitative or wellness practices recommended by a healthcare provider, engaged in by the victim and any juveniles dependent upon the victim due to the crime, not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) per year per person, for a maximum of two (2) years;
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

params.scope: travel, parking, lodging, and meals to attend criminal court proceedings about the crime

rules.summary: Travel, parking, lodging, and meals for attending criminal court proceedings related to the crime can be covered for the victim and the victim's caregiver.
rules.quote: A victim and the victim's caregiver, if applicable, may recover the following types of expenses incurred for purposes of attending criminal court proceedings related to the crime: (1) Travel; (2) Parking; (3) Lodging; (4) Meals;
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:030 Crime victims compensation awards

params.item: a $5,000 lump sum when a claim is filed more than 10 years after the crime because testing or DNA matching of a sexual assault kit was delayed

rules.summary: If a claim is filed more than 10 years after the crime because testing or DNA matching of a sexual assault kit was delayed, the victim may collect a $5,000 lump sum.
rules.quote: An award may be made for a claim filed more than ten (10) years after the criminally injurious conduct, due to a delay in the testing of or DNA profile matching from a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, in which case the victim may collect a lump sum in the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000)
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

params.item: property loss or damage (for example a stolen or broken phone), unless the statute allows it, such as items seized as evidence or windows and locks

rules.summary: No award is made for property loss or damage, such as a phone, except where the statute allows it (for example, items seized by police as evidence, or windows and locks).
rules.quote: An award shall not be made for any type of property loss or damage, except as otherwise permitted in KRS 49.270 to 49.490.
rules.source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

params.item: pain and suffering, emotional distress, loss of consortium

rules.summary: The program does not pay for pain and suffering, emotional distress, or loss of consortium.
rules.quote: Property damage or loss, except as provided in KRS Chapter 49, and pain and suffering, emotional distress, and loss of consortium.
rules.pinpoint: CVCB FAQ, "What types of expenses are NOT compensable by the Board?"
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Board FAQ (updated August 2024)

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by money received or to be received from the offender, required insurance, public funds, the claimant's own insurance, an emergency award, or donations toward crime expenses.
rules.quote: Any award made pursuant to KRS 49.270 to 49.490 shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received by the claimant as a result of the injury from the following sources: (a) From or on behalf of the person who committed the crime; (b) Under insurance programs mandated by law; (c) From public funds; (d) Under any contract of insurance wherein the claimant is the insured or beneficiary; (e) As an emergency award pursuant to KRS 49.360; and (f) From donations made on behalf of the victim or claimant toward expenses incurred as a result of the crime.
rules.source_title: KRS 49.390 (reduction of award)

rules.summary: The board may deny, reconsider, or reduce an award if the victim or claimant was charged with an offense, was offered immunity, knowingly took part in the conduct, or engaged in mutual aggression, in relation to the crime in the claim.
rules.quote: The board may deny, reconsider, or reduce an award if the board finds that, in relation to the criminally injurious conduct alleged in the claim, the victim or claimant: (a) Has been charged with a criminal offense; (b) Has been offered immunity from prosecution in exchange for testimony; (c) Knowingly participated in the conduct; or (d) Engaged in conduct which may constitute mutual aggression with another person.
rules.source_title: KRS 49.390 (reduction of award)

rules.summary: An emergency award of up to $1,000 can be paid before the final decision, and it is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: The amount of an emergency award shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000); (b) The amount of an emergency award shall be deducted from any final award made to the claimant;
rules.source_title: KRS 49.360 (emergency award)

rules.summary: Compensation covers victims of criminally injurious conduct, meaning conduct in Kentucky that poses a substantial threat of physical or psychological injury and is punishable as a crime.
rules.quote: "Criminally injurious conduct" means conduct that occurs or is attempted in this jurisdiction, poses a substantial threat of personal physical or psychological injury or death, and is punishable by fine, imprisonment, or death.
rules.source_title: KRS 49.280 (definitions)

rules.summary: The official claim form lists adult sexual assault as a crime type.
rules.quote: Sexual Assault (Adult)
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Form (revised July 2024)

params.rule: Victims who suffer physical or psychological injury from a criminal act in Kentucky

rules.summary: A victim is a person who suffers physical or psychological injury, or death, from a criminal act in Kentucky.
rules.quote: "Victim" means a person who suffers personal physical or psychological injury or death from a criminal act in Kentucky as a result of:
rules.source_title: KRS 49.280 (definitions)

params.rule: Nonresidents hurt by crimes in Kentucky, while federal funds are available

rules.summary: Nonresidents who suffer losses from crimes in Kentucky are covered during periods when the board finds federal funds are available.
rules.quote: "Victim" shall also include nonresidents of this state who suffer losses as a direct result of criminal acts occurring within this state. This section shall be operative only during those time periods during which the Crime Victims Compensation Board determines that federal funds are available to the state for the compensation of victims of crime.
rules.source_title: KRS 49.290 (nonresident victims)

params.rule: Kentucky residents victimized in a state with no compensation program

rules.summary: A Kentucky resident hurt by a crime in another state can apply in Kentucky only if that state has no compensation program the victim is eligible for and the crime would be covered had it happened in Kentucky.
rules.quote: "Victim" shall also mean a resident who is a victim of a crime occurring outside this state if: 1. The crime would be compensable had it occurred inside this state; and 2. The crime occurred in a state which does not have a crime victim compensation program, for which the victim is eligible as eligibility is set forth in KRS 49.310.
rules.source_title: KRS 49.280 (definitions)

params.target: Crime Victims Compensation Board, 500 Mero Street, 2 SC1, Frankfort, Kentucky 40601

rules.summary: A claim can be dropped off in person or sent by private delivery to the Board's office in Frankfort.
rules.quote: (a) In person or by private delivery to the Crime Victims Compensation Board, 500 Mero Street, 2 SC1, Frankfort, Kentucky 40601;
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

params.target: Crime Victims Compensation Board, 500 Mero Street, 2 SC1, Frankfort, Kentucky 40601

rules.summary: A claim can be mailed to the Board's office in Frankfort.
rules.quote: (a) In person or by private delivery to the Crime Victims Compensation Board, 500 Mero Street, 2 SC1, Frankfort, Kentucky 40601; (b) By mail to the address listed above;
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

rules.summary: A claim can be emailed to the Board if the whole claim fits in a single email.
rules.quote: (c) By electronic mail to crimevictims@ky.gov, if the document can be sent in one (1) electronic message;
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

rules.summary: A claim can be filed through the Board's online claims portal.
rules.quote: (d) Through the online claims portal at: https://kycc.ky.gov/CVOnline/home
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

rules.summary: The Board's FAQ says a paper claim form can also be faxed.
rules.quote: Paper claim forms can be submitted to the Board by fax (502-573-4817)
rules.pinpoint: CVCB FAQ (updated August 2024), Where should I send my paper claim form?
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Board FAQ (updated August 2024)

params.note: if applicable; the sexual assault exam program itself does not require reporting

rules.summary: The Board's checklist asks for a police report along with the claim form, if applicable.
rules.quote: In addition to the claim form, you will need to submit, if applicable, 1) Police Report
rules.source_title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

params.note: for medical expenses

rules.summary: For medical expenses, the claimant must send copies of itemized medical billing statements.
rules.quote: Claimants requesting reimbursement or payment for medical expenses incurred as a result of the crime shall submit the following documentation as proof of the eligible expenses: (1) Copies of itemized medical billing statements for medical treatment provided to the claimant as a direct result of the crime.
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:030 Crime victims compensation awards

params.note: only when itemized bills are not available

rules.summary: If itemized medical bills are not available, non-itemized bills are accepted when the medical records from the visit are sent with them.
rules.quote: (2) If itemized billing statements are not available, non-itemized medical billing statements shall be accepted if: (a) The medical records from the visit are submitted along with the non-itemized medical billing statements;
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:030 Crime victims compensation awards

params.note: proof of payment or balance due for each listed expense

rules.summary: The claim form says each listed expense needs documentation such as itemized bills, receipts, service contracts, invoices, or other proof of payment or balance due.
rules.quote: You must include documentation of the expense, such as itemized bills, receipts, service contracts, invoices, or other proof of payment and/or balance due.
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Form (revised July 2024)

params.note: for mental health counseling; also the treatment plan and itemized bills

rules.summary: For counseling expenses, the claimant must send a Mental Health Counselor's Report from the therapist and the treatment plan, along with itemized bills.
rules.quote: (1) Claimants requesting reimbursement or payment of mental health counseling expenses shall submit the following documentation as proof of the eligible expenses: (a) Mental Health Counselor's Report completed by the claimant's or victim's therapist or mental health clinician; (b) Treatment plan devised by the claimant or victim's therapist or mental health clinician;
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:030 Crime victims compensation awards

params.note: for lost wages or loss of support; the form must be notarized

rules.summary: A claim for lost wages or loss of support must include a notarized Employment Verification form, plus a Physician Statement or Mental Health Counselor's Report if Board staff ask for one.
rules.quote: (3) If applying for lost wages or loss of support, a claim shall be supplemented by: (a) A notarized Employment Verification form; and (b) If requested by Board staff: 1. A Physician Statement form; or 2. A Mental Health Counselor's Report form.
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

params.note: self-employed claimants send tax returns

rules.summary: A self-employed claimant seeking lost earnings sends the preceding two years of tax returns.
rules.quote: If you are selfemployed, please submit the preceding two years' worth of tax returns.
rules.source_title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

params.note: Emergency Award Request Form, only when requesting an emergency award

rules.summary: Anyone asking for an emergency award completes, signs, and dates the Emergency Award Request Form and attaches it to the claim form.
rules.quote: If yes, please complete, sign, and date the attached Emergency Award Request Form and attach it to your claim form.
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Form (revised July 2024)

params.note: lump sum for sexual assault claims delayed more than ten years by kit testing or DNA matching: proof of crime date, kit collection, collection date, testing delay, and damages

rules.summary: A survivor seeking the lump sum for a sexual assault claim filed more than ten years after the crime must send proof of the crime date, that the kit was collected and when, that it went untested for a long time, and anecdotal proof of damages.
rules.quote: (1) For purposes of KRS 49.370(7), a claimant seeking an award under this provision shall submit: (a) Proof that the crime occurred more than ten (10) years prior to the date of filing of the claim; (b) Proof that the sexual assault kit was collected; (c) Proof of the collection date of the biological material; (d) Proof that the biological material went untested for an extended period; and (e) Anecdotal proof of the damages incurred as a result of the crime.
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

params.note: signed funeral service contract, for funeral expenses

rules.summary: For funeral expenses, the checklist asks for the signed funeral service contract.
rules.quote: 3) Signed funeral service contract for funeral expenses
rules.source_title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

params.note: proof of household support, for loss of support

rules.summary: For loss of support, the checklist asks for documentation of the support the supporter brought into the household at the time of the crime.
rules.quote: a. Documentation outlining amount of support brought into household by the supporter at the time of the crime.
rules.source_title: CVCB Documents to include (claim checklist)

rules.summary: For claims filed after July 1, 2026, the investigator must finish the investigative report within 90 days after the claim is assigned; this is the investigation step, not the Board's final decision.
rules.quote: (3) For claims filed after July 1, 2026, the claims investigator shall complete an investigative report on the claim within ninety (90) days after it is assigned by the Board Clerk to the claims investigator.
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

params.agency: Office of the Secretary of State
params.enroll: Applications shall be filed with the Office of the Secretary of State. Applicants may choose to consult with an application assistant for assistance with the application process or apply online directly through the portal designated by the Secretary of State.

rules.summary: Kentucky's Safe at Home Program, in the Secretary of State's office, is meant to protect victims of sexual assault, rape, other sexual crimes, domestic violence, human trafficking, and stalking. It lets victims, their minor children, and everyone who lives with them use a designated address. It is open to victims who are U.S. citizens and Kentucky residents, at no cost to them.
rules.quote: The Safe at Home Program is hereby established within the Office of the Secretary of State. The Safe at Home Program shall be operated with the intent to protect victims of: (a) Domestic violence; (b) Human trafficking; (c) Stalking; (d) Sexual assault; (e) Rape; and (f) Other sexual crimes as defined by KRS 17.500. The Safe at Home Program shall authorize the use of designated addresses for victims, their minor children, and all other individuals residing with the victim. The Safe at Home Program shall be open to victims of a specified offense who are United States citizens and residents of Kentucky, without any cost to the program participant.
rules.source_title: KRS 14.302 (Safe at Home Program established, designated addresses)

rules.summary: In its section on the claim tracking portal, the Board's regulation says a claimant's or victim's personally identifiable information must stay secure and confidential, and information that could show whether someone filed a claim may not be shared with people who are not authorized.
rules.quote: A claimant or victim's personally identifiable information shall remain secure and confidential. (4) Information that may be used to determine whether an individual filed a claim with the Board shall not be disclosed to unauthorized individuals.
rules.source_title: 802 KAR 3:010 Crime victims compensation

rules.summary: A survivor of a sexually oriented offense cannot be billed, directly or indirectly, for a forensic medical exam.
rules.quote: A survivor of a sexually oriented criminal offense shall not be billed directly or indirectly for the performance of any forensic medical exam.
rules.source_title: La. R.S. 40:1216.1 (2025 text, Justia)

rules.summary: Louisiana law says a sexual assault survivor cannot be billed, directly or indirectly, for a forensic medical exam. The provider or facility sends the claim to the compensation program instead.
rules.quote: Under Louisiana law, a victim cannot be billed directly or indirectly for a forensic medical exam.
rules.pinpoint: LCLE CVC Downloads page, Forensic Medical Examinations
rules.source_title: LCLE CVC Downloads page (forms and forensic exam billing note)

rules.summary: The program's provider instructions say the patient's health insurance should not be billed for the forensic exam; the program is the primary payer.
rules.quote: The patient’s health insurance should not be billed. Our program is the primary payer for healthcare services rendered in conducting a forensic medical exam.
rules.pinpoint: LCLE Forensic Medical Exam Reimbursement, Policy and Procedures
rules.source_title: Forensic Medical Exam Reimbursement policy, claim and attestation forms (revised Aug 1, 2023)

rules.summary: No hospital or healthcare provider may directly bill a survivor for the healthcare services that make up the forensic medical exam.
rules.quote: No hospital or healthcare provider shall directly bill a survivor of a sexually oriented criminal offense for any healthcare services rendered in conducting a forensic medical examination
rules.source_title: La. R.S. 40:1216.1 (2025 text, Justia)

params.payer: Louisiana Crime Victims' Compensation program (LCLE), paid directly to the examiner and the facility

rules.summary: The program pays the forensic exam directly to the examining provider and the facility, not the survivor. The board rule caps the provider payment at $600 and the facility payment at $1,000.
rules.quote: Payments for forensic medical examinations shall not exceed $600 for the healthcare provider, and $1,000 for the healthcare facility.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: Awards to all claimants for one victim's injury are capped at $15,000 in total.
rules.quote: Fifteen thousand dollars in the aggregate.
rules.pinpoint: La. R.S. 46:1810(1), as amended by Acts 2026, No. 684
rules.source_title: Acts 2026, No. 684 (HB 969), enrolled act amending La. R.S. 46:1801 et seq.

params.exception: or up to $25,000 if the crime leaves you fully disabled for life

rules.summary: The board's rule sets a $15,000 limit, except for a victim the crime leaves totally and permanently disabled. For that victim, the board may award up to $25,000, depending on funds, its rule limits, and other payment sources.
rules.quote: There will be a $15,000 limit for awards for all victims with the exception of those primary victims who become totally and permanently disabled as a result of the crime. For those awards, the board may, at its discretion, award up to $25,000, depending on availability of funds, its administrative rule limits for certain award benefits, and the extent, if any, of collateral resources.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: While an application is pending, the board can make an emergency award of up to $1,000 if a final award is likely and the claimant would face undue hardship without quick help. The emergency award is taken out of the final award. The claimant must pay back any amount above the final award, or all of it if no final award is made.
rules.quote: An emergency award shall not exceed one thousand dollars.
rules.pinpoint: La. R.S. 46:1813(B), as amended by Acts 2026, No. 684
rules.source_title: Acts 2026, No. 684 (HB 969), enrolled act amending La. R.S. 46:1801 et seq.

rules.summary: This law changed the time to apply from one year to three years, counted from the date of the crime.
rules.quote: Changes the time period for filing from one year to three years and provides this period begins from the date the crime is committed.
rules.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 (HB 969) on La. R.S. 46:1806(A)(1)
rules.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

rules.summary: An adult victim does not have to report the crime to law enforcement to apply; other reasonable documentation of the crime is accepted instead.
rules.quote: An adult victim of a criminal offense is not required to report the crime to any law enforcement officer in order to file an application.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: An application needs reasonable documentation of the crime, which can be a law enforcement report, court records, an attestation from a healthcare provider who examined the injury, or an attestation from the provider or coroner who did a forensic medical exam.
rules.quote: (a) A report from law enforcement, rather than a police report. (b) Court records pertaining to the crime, rather than evidencing the criminal prosecution. (c) An attestation from a healthcare provider who conducted an examination of the personal injury suffered by the victim. (d) An attestation from a healthcare provider or coroner who conducted a forensic medical examination on the victim.
rules.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 on La. R.S. 46:1806(A)(2)
rules.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

rules.summary: The fund is the payer of last resort and pays crime-related out-of-pocket costs that insurance and other sources do not cover.
rules.quote: The Crime Victims’ Compensation Fund is regarded as the “payer of last resort.” It is a secondary source that pays for certain out-of-pocket expenses related to the crime that the victim has no other way to pay.
rules.pinpoint: LCLE CVC program page, Recoveries from Other Sources
rules.source_title: LCLE Crime Victims' Compensation Fund program page

rules.summary: For sexual offense claims, the victim can choose whether or not to file with private insurance or Medicaid.
rules.quote: the victim has the discretion to choose whether or not to file for private insurance or Medicaid coverage.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: The board may deny or reduce an award because of the victim's conduct. The current statute says the behavior-based reduction does not apply when the injury came from a sexually oriented criminal offense.
rules.quote: The Crime Victims Reparations Board may vote to deny or reduce an award to a claimant who is a victim, or who files an application on behalf of a victim.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: For a sexual assault victim, the board may not deny or reduce an award based on things like how the victim was dressed, where they were, alcohol or drug use, a prior relationship with the offender, or living with the offender afterward.
rules.quote: The following factors shall not be considered a reason for denying or reducing an award to a claimant who is a victim of a sexually oriented criminal offense, or who submits a claim on behalf of a victim of sexual assault:
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: Sexually oriented criminal offenses are listed as covered crimes in the current statute.
rules.quote: (3) A sexually oriented criminal offense.
rules.pinpoint: La. R.S. 46:1805(A)(3), as amended by Acts 2026, No. 684
rules.source_title: Acts 2026, No. 684 (HB 969), enrolled act amending La. R.S. 46:1801 et seq.

params.rule: Crimes in Louisiana, or Louisiana residents victimized in a state with no eligible compensation program

rules.summary: The crime must happen in Louisiana, or the victim must be a Louisiana resident hurt in another state that has no compensation program they qualify for.
rules.quote: The crime must occur in Louisiana or the crime must involve a Louisiana resident who becomes a victim in another state that does not have a crime victim compensation program for which the victim would be eligible.
rules.source_title: LCLE Crime Victims' Compensation Fund program page

rules.summary: Mental health charges are capped at $2,500 for the life of a claim; the victim can ask for another $2,500 with documented need for long-term care.
rules.quote: For the life of each claim, reimbursable charges may not exceed $2,500.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: Doctoral-level providers (MD, PhD, PsyD) are paid up to $110 per session.
rules.quote: (a). Doctoral Level Providers (e.g. M.D. PhD., PsyD.), $110/session).
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: Master's-level counselors and social workers (LPC, LCSW, LMFT and provisional licensees) are paid up to $90 per session.
rules.quote: (b). Master’s Level Providers (e.g., L.P.C., L.C.S.W., L.M.F.T., P.L.P.C, P.L.C.S.W, P.L.M.F.T., D.S.W. ) $90/session.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: Mental health counseling related to the crime is an eligible expense.
rules.quote: Approved claims may be awarded compensation for the following only if they are related to the crime (Some expenses are limited): Reasonable medical and prescription expenses Dental expenses Mental health counseling
rules.pinpoint: LCLE CVC program page, What Expenses are Eligible
rules.source_title: LCLE Crime Victims' Compensation Fund program page

rules.summary: For outstanding medical bills, the board pays up to 70 percent of what is left after insurance and other third-party payers, within the award limits.
rules.quote: The board will pay up to 70 percent of all outstanding charges after any third-party payment sources up to the statutory limits.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: Medical costs the victim already paid out of pocket are reimbursed before the percentage schedule for unpaid bills is applied.
rules.quote: Out-of-pocket paid monies will be reimbursed to the victim prior to applying this payment schedule.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: Lost wages are paid at 80 percent of the victim's gross weekly wage, or 80 percent of the average weekly wage for seasonal or part-time work.
rules.quote: 80 percent of the gross weekly wage of the victim. For seasonal or part time wages, the amount shall be calculated at 80 percent of the average weekly wage;
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: Moving costs are paid only when the claimant must move because of the crime for reasons of imminent danger, personal safety, or a threat of injury, up to $5,000 per household. The board rule says a police or incident report should be sent with the claim to show why the move was needed.
rules.quote: Reimbursement for relocation expenses is limited up to $5,000 per household of the claimant.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

params.scope: temporary lodging or a move when moving right away is needed for the health and safety of the victim or a household member

rules.summary: Under the amended statute, temporary lodging or permanent relocation is a covered loss when moving right away is needed for the safety of the victim or a household member.
rules.quote: Temporary lodging or permanent relocation when immediate relocation is necessary for the health and safety of the victim or the victim's household member.
rules.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 on La. R.S. 46:1802 (pecuniary loss)
rules.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

params.scope: trips to medical care that is not available nearby, when the doctor certifies it

rules.summary: Travel beyond the first ambulance ride is paid only when needed medical care is not available locally and the treating physician certifies that; private mileage is paid at the state travel rate.
rules.quote: Transportation costs other than the initial ambulance services are reimbursable only when required medical care is not locally available. Certification is required by the physician of record that local medical care is unavailable. Allowable private vehicle mileage for out-of-town travel is reimbursed at the rate published in the current state travel regulations.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

params.scope: replacing clothing, bedding, or other property taken as evidence or ruined by the investigation or lab tests

rules.summary: Reasonable replacement of clothing, bedding, or property taken as evidence or ruined by the investigation or lab testing is covered.
rules.quote: Expenses associated with the collection and securing of crime scene evidence are limited to: a. reasonable replacement costs for clothing; b. bedding; or c. property seized as evidence or rendered unusable as a result of a criminal investigation or lab test.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

rules.summary: Care of a child or dependent is listed as a pecuniary loss the program can cover under the amended statute.
rules.quote: Care of a child or dependent.
rules.pinpoint: La. R.S. 46:1802(16)(c), as amended by Acts 2026, No. 684
rules.source_title: Acts 2026, No. 684 (HB 969), enrolled act amending La. R.S. 46:1801 et seq.

rules.summary: Cleaning the victim's residential crime scene is capped at $2,500.
rules.quote: Expenses submitted for cleaning the residential crime scene of the victim may not exceed $2500.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

params.item: property damage or loss, such as a stolen or broken phone (items taken as evidence or ruined by the investigation are the exception)

rules.summary: Property damage or loss, like a stolen or broken phone, is not reimbursed. Items seized as evidence or ruined by the investigation are a separate covered expense.
rules.quote: Reimbursement for property damage or loss is not an eligible expense.
rules.pinpoint: LCLE CVC program page, What Expenses are Eligible
rules.source_title: LCLE Crime Victims' Compensation Fund program page

rules.summary: Attorney fees to prepare an application or represent the victim are not reimbursed unless they come from a hearing the board ordered.
rules.quote: The board does not reimburse victims for fees charged by an attorney to prepare an application or represent the victim in any way unless the fees result from a hearing ordered by the board.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

params.target: Crime Victims’ Compensation Louisiana Commission on Law Enforcement PO Box 3133 Baton Rouge, LA 70821
params.note: The board office. The application form prints the same P.O. Box under its older name (Crime Victims Reparations).

rules.summary: You can mail the application to the Crime Victims' Compensation board office at LCLE in Baton Rouge.
rules.quote: Or Write to: Crime Victims’ Compensation Louisiana Commission on Law Enforcement PO Box 3133 Baton Rouge, LA 70821
rules.pinpoint: LCLE CVC program page, For More Information
rules.source_title: LCLE Crime Victims' Compensation Fund program page

params.note: For an adult victim of a sexually oriented offense, the application goes straight to the board office, not the parish sheriff.

rules.summary: Applications for an adult victim of a sexually oriented offense are sent directly to the board office.
rules.quote: Applications involving an adult victim of a sexually-oriented criminal offense are sent directly to the board’s office.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

params.target: you Parish Claim’s Investigator or the CVR Board Office
params.note: Other applicants can send the packet to the sheriff's claim investigator in the parish where the crime happened; adult sexual offense applications go to the board office (LA-SUBMIT-2).
params.applies_to: cases other than adult sexual offenses, which go straight to the board office

rules.summary: The form says to mail the original application, police report, and itemized claims to the parish claim investigator or the board office.
rules.quote: Please mail the original application, along with the Claim Investigator Review, the complete police report, newspaper articles (if available) and any claims (including claim forms and itemized invoices) to you Parish Claim’s Investigator or the CVR Board Office.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victims Reparations (form revised Feb 2025)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "cases other than adult sexual offenses, which go straight to the board office"

params.note: The completed, signed application; the claimant must sign it and be at least 18 when signing (a parent or guardian signs for a minor victim).

rules.summary: The claimant must sign the application.
rules.quote: The claimant MUST sign the application.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victims Reparations (form revised Feb 2025)

params.note: Reasonable documentation of the crime must come with the application; the accepted kinds are listed in LA-DOC-POLICE, LA-DOC-COURT, LA-DOC-HEALTH and LA-DOC-EXAM.

rules.summary: An application is valid only if reasonable documentation of the crime is submitted with it.
rules.quote: Crime Victims Reparations applications shall be valid only if reasonable documentation of the crime is submitted with the application.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victims Reparations (form revised Feb 2025)

params.note: One accepted form of reasonable documentation, not required: an adult victim does not have to report to law enforcement (LA-REPORT-1).

rules.summary: A report from law enforcement counts as reasonable documentation of the crime.
rules.quote: A report from law enforcement, rather than a police report.
rules.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 on La. R.S. 46:1806(A)(2)(a)
rules.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

params.note: Court records about the crime; one accepted form of reasonable documentation.

rules.summary: Court records about the crime count as reasonable documentation.
rules.quote: Court records pertaining to the crime, rather than evidencing the criminal prosecution.
rules.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 on La. R.S. 46:1806(A)(2)(b)
rules.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

params.note: An attestation from the healthcare provider who examined the injury; one accepted form of reasonable documentation.

rules.summary: An attestation from a healthcare provider who examined the injury counts as reasonable documentation.
rules.quote: An attestation from a healthcare provider who conducted an examination of the personal injury suffered by the victim.
rules.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 on La. R.S. 46:1806(A)(2)(c)
rules.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

params.note: An attestation that a forensic medical exam was done, from the provider or coroner; one accepted form of reasonable documentation, so a survivor who had an exam can apply without a police report.

rules.summary: An attestation from the provider or coroner who did a forensic medical exam counts as reasonable documentation.
rules.quote: An attestation from a healthcare provider or coroner who conducted a forensic medical examination on the victim.
rules.pinpoint: Resume Digest of Act 684 on La. R.S. 46:1806(A)(2)(d)
rules.source_title: Resume Digest, Act 684 (HB 969), 2026 Regular Session

params.note: An itemized bill (not a billing statement) for each expense other than the forensic exam.

rules.summary: Each expense other than the forensic exam needs an itemized bill, not a billing statement.
rules.quote: An itemized bill, not a billing statement, must accompany the application for each non-FME expense claimed.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

params.note: Invoices and bills must name the victim or claimant as guarantor and show the balance owed.

rules.summary: Bills must show the victim or claimant as guarantor and the balance owed.
rules.quote: All invoices, bills, etc. must indicate the victim/claimant as the guarantor and indicate balances owed.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

params.note: The claim form for each expense type (medical, mental health, lost wages, relocation, and so on, from the CVC Downloads page); each claim form lists the documents it needs.

rules.summary: Each type of claim form says which documents support that expense.
rules.quote: Each type of claim form used by the board should identify the documents that must be submitted by the victim/claimant to support and verify a claimed expense.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

params.note: Lost wages claims need verification from the employer.

rules.summary: Lost wages need verification from the employer.
rules.quote: wage verification by the employer is required.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

params.note: Lost wages claims: the inability to work must be documented by a medical doctor.

rules.summary: For lost wages, a medical doctor must document that the survivor could not work because of the crime.
rules.quote: The inability to work must be directly related to the victimization and documented by the appropriate medical doctor.
rules.source_title: LAC Title 22, Part XIII, Crime Victims Reparations Board rules (Feb 2025)

params.note: Newspaper articles or press releases about the incident, only when available.

rules.summary: Send news articles about the incident if there are any.
rules.quote: Submit copies of newspaper articles, press releases, etc., that describe the incident, when available.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victims Reparations (form revised Feb 2025)

params.note: A letter of explanation when filing late. The form still says one year, but Act 684 (effective Aug. 1, 2026) gives three years from the crime, so this matters only past the statutory period.

rules.summary: The form asks for a letter of explanation when filing after the deadline it prints.
rules.quote: If you are filing later than one year, you must attach a letter of explanation.
rules.source_title: Application for Crime Victims Reparations (form revised Feb 2025)

params.note: usually 30 to 45 days

rules.summary: An eligibility decision usually comes within 30 to 45 days.
rules.quote: A decision about whether the victim or claimant is eligible is usually made within 30 to 45 days.
rules.pinpoint: LCLE CVC program page, How the Application is Reviewed
rules.source_title: LCLE Crime Victims' Compensation Fund program page

params.enroll: Once a victim of abuse, sexual assault or stalking moves to a new location in Louisiana that is unknown to his/her abuser where no public record of the new address has been created (e.g., telephone number, driver's license, utilities, etc), the victim should call the ACP. The victim is then referred to an agency with a certified ACP application assistant to meet with and apply for participation in the program. When the application is complete, the application assistant sends the application to the Secretary of State's Office where it is reviewed to verify requirements are met before certifying the victim as a program participant.

rules.summary: Louisiana's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Secretary of State, gives relocated victims of abuse, sexual assault, or stalking a substitute address to use for state and local government services, and forwards their first-class, certified, and registered mail. Applicants call the ACP and apply with a certified application assistant.
rules.quote: The ACP provides relocated victims of abuse, sexual assault or stalking with a substitute address to use in place of their actual address when they apply for or receive state or local government services (e.g., driver's license, voter registration, public school records, etc.).
rules.pinpoint: Secretary of State, Address Confidentiality Program page, program description and How to apply
rules.source_title: Louisiana Secretary of State, Address Confidentiality Program page

rules.summary: Public agencies, including the crime victims compensation board by name, may not publicly disclose the name, address, contact information, or identity of sex offense victims. The victim can waive this.
rules.quote: all public officials and officers and public agencies, including but not limited to all law enforcement agencies, sheriffs, district attorneys, judicial officers, clerks of court, the Crime Victims Reparations Board, and the Department of Children and Family Services or any division thereof, shall not publicly disclose the name, address, contact information, or identity of crime victims who at the time of the commission of the offense are minors under eighteen years of age or of victims of sex offenses
rules.source_title: La. R.S. 46:1844, Basic rights for victim and witness (2025 text, Justia)

rules.summary: Hospitals may not bill sexual assault exam patients for co-payments or other costs tied to their own health insurance; those amounts go to the state victim compensation program instead.
rules.quote: Hospitals may not bill patients for any co-payments or other patient-incurred costs related to their primary health insurance and those should be submitted to the VCAD.
rules.pinpoint: MA SANE Protocol, Section X (Victim compensation)
rules.source_title: Mass.gov DPH, MA SANE Protocol Section X: Victim Compensation

rules.summary: The protocol says a patient's own health insurance can be used for the exam if the patient opts in, and that hospitals should bill the victim compensation program directly for patients who have privacy or other concerns about billing their insurance.
rules.quote: While a patient’s primary health care can be used if the patient affirmatively opts in, direct billing to VCAD should be implemented for patients who have privacy/confidentiality or other concerns about their primary health insurance being billed.
rules.pinpoint: MA SANE Protocol, Section X (Victim compensation)
rules.source_title: Mass.gov DPH, MA SANE Protocol Section X: Victim Compensation

rules.summary: State guidance says a survivor who receives a forensic exam should not get a bill, including a co-pay, for the exam or the related hospital visit.
rules.quote: In Massachusetts, survivors of sexual violence who receive a forensic exam should not receive a bill (including co-pay) for the exam and/or hospital visit related to the assault.
rules.pinpoint: MSAECK survivor brochure, Payment of Related Expenses
rules.source_title: Information on the Massachusetts Sexual Assault Evidence Collection Kit (survivor brochure)

rules.summary: Covered emergency department exam expenses, including co-payments, co-insurance and deductibles, should never be billed to the survivor.
rules.quote: The expenses outlined below, including the applicable co-payment, co-insurance, and/or deductible, should never be billed to the survivor.
rules.pinpoint: Coverage and Billing Procedures for Sexual Assault Exams in Massachusetts (2018), If a Sexual Assault Forensic Exam is Administered
rules.source_title: Coverage and Billing Procedures for Sexual Assault Exams in Massachusetts (MHA/AGO/EOHHS/EOPSS guidance, approved December 2018)

params.payer: Massachusetts Office for Victim Assistance (victim compensation program), billed directly by the provider

rules.summary: Medical care given in response to a sexual assault report, including the forensic exam and surrounding medical care, is compensable, and providers may bill the program directly. The same section says ambulance, inpatient care after the kit, and follow-up visits may not be covered through direct billing; the survivor can still claim those through their own application.
rules.quote: Expenses incurred for medical care in response to reports in accordance with 124 CMR 2.04 and 2.05(1)(d), including the provision of forensic sexual assault examinations and/or surrounding medical care shall be compensable.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.payer: Victim Compensation and Assistance Division, billed directly by the Massachusetts hospital
params.condition: if the crime was in Massachusetts

rules.summary: Massachusetts hospitals can bill the state's victim compensation division directly for emergency room costs. This applies when the assault happened in Massachusetts and the forensic exam is done at a Massachusetts hospital.
rules.quote: As of March 2016, MA hospitals are allowed to directly bill the VCAD for all Emergency Department (ED) expenses incurred as the result of a sexual assault that involve a patient whose assault occurs in Massachusetts and who receives a forensic sexual assault examination at a Massachusetts hospital.
rules.pinpoint: MA SANE Protocol, Section X (Victim compensation)
rules.source_title: Mass.gov DPH, MA SANE Protocol Section X: Victim Compensation

params.payer: Massachusetts Office for Victim Assistance (victim compensation program)

rules.summary: Exam payments do not count toward the survivor's maximum award for other crime-related expenses.
rules.quote: To ensure compliance with 28 CFR § 90.13 requiring states to provide forensic sexual assault examinations without cost to the victim, compensation paid in this section will not be considered toward the maximum award for victim's other related claims.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: Victim compensation can cover the forensic exam and other emergency department costs whether or not the survivor reports to police.
rules.quote: Victim’s Compensation may be used to cover the cost of forensic exam/evidence collection and other emergency department expenses whether or not they choose to report their assault to police.
rules.pinpoint: MA SANE Protocol, Section X (Direct billing process)
rules.source_title: Mass.gov DPH, MA SANE Protocol Section X: Victim Compensation

rules.summary: A survivor does not have to have a forensic exam for sexual assault medical expenses to be eligible under this section.
rules.quote: Victims are not required to receive a forensic sexual assault examination for expenses to be deemed eligible under this section.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.exception: or $50,000 for a catastrophic injury

rules.summary: The maximum award is $25,000 per claimant, or $50,000 for a catastrophic injury.
rules.quote: The maximum award for compensation to a claimant pursuant to this chapter shall be $25,000; provided, however, that the maximum award for compensation to a claimant with a catastrophic injury pursuant to this chapter shall be $50,000.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 3, Maximum award; compensable expenses

rules.summary: A victim, or a family member living with the victim, can be compensated for security measures up to $3,000.
rules.quote: A victim or a family member residing with the victim at the time a crime is committed, shall be eligible for compensation for the costs associated with the implementation of security measures; provided, however, that the maximum compensable amount shall not exceed $3,000.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 3, Maximum award; compensable expenses

rules.summary: Clothing and bedding seized as evidence or ruined by the investigation can be replaced up to $250.
rules.quote: A victim shall be eligible for compensation for the reasonable replacement costs of clothing and bedding seized as evidence or rendered unusable as the result of a criminal investigation that is the direct result of a crime; provided, however, that the maximum compensable amount shall not exceed $250.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 3, Maximum award; compensable expenses

rules.summary: Professional crime scene cleanup at a private residence or a victim's vehicle is capped at $1,500.
rules.quote: Expenses incurred for professional crime scene cleanup services necessary as the direct result of the commission of a crime at a private residence or in a motor vehicle that is owned or leased by a victim, family member or other dependent shall be compensable in accordance with this chapter; provided, however, that the maximum amount of compensation shall not exceed $1,500.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 3, Maximum award; compensable expenses

rules.summary: Funeral and burial expenses are capped at $13,000.
rules.quote: The maximum award or compensation for funeral and burial expenses shall be $13,000.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 3, Maximum award; compensable expenses

rules.summary: If an attorney helps with the claim, fees are paid at no more than $75 per hour, capped at 15% of the award, and come out of the award rather than on top of it.
rules.quote: Attorneys shall be compensated at a rate of no more than $75 per hour. In no event shall an attorney's fee award exceed 15% of the total award for compensation.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: A victim, or a parent or guardian of a minor victim, can be compensated for reasonable mental health counseling obtained because of the crime.
rules.quote: A victim, parent or legal guardian of a victim who is a minor in accordance with section 4 or, where death results from the crime, the dependents and family members of the victim, shall be eligible for compensation for reasonable mental health counseling obtained as a result of the crime.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 3, Maximum award; compensable expenses

rules.summary: Physician, dental, ambulance and other medically necessary services caused by the crime are covered when the claimant shows an out-of-pocket loss or a legal liability to pay.
rules.quote: Expenses incurred for physician, dental, ambulance, or other medically necessary services or prosthetic devices as the direct result of injury to the victim shall be compensable in accordance with this chapter; provided however, that when claiming compensation for such expenses, the claimant must demonstrate an out-of-pocket loss or legal liability for payment of such expenses.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 3, Maximum award; compensable expenses

rules.summary: A victim who was employed, or had a real job offer, can be compensated for lost earnings while medically disabled from work because of the crime, based on net earnings.
rules.quote: If the victim was employed or had received a bona fide employment offer at the time of the crime, the victim shall be eligible for compensation for loss of actual earnings due to disability from work as the result of injuries caused by the crime.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 3, Maximum award; compensable expenses

rules.summary: Medical and dental expenses, including equipment, supplies and medications, are listed as covered to the extent insurance or other funds do not pay.
rules.quote: Medical and dental expenses (including equipment, supplies and medications)
rules.pinpoint: MOVA, Applying for Victims of Violent Crime Assistance, What expenses are covered?
rules.source_title: Mass.gov, Applying for Victims of Violent Crime Assistance (MOVA)

rules.summary: Dental care is part of compensable medical care.
rules.quote: "Medical care'', the medical, psychological, surgical, dental, optometric, chiropractic, podiatric and hospital care provided to a victim including, but not limited to, medicines, medical, dental and surgical supplies, crutches, artificial members and appliances and training in the use of artificial members and appliances.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 1, Definitions

params.scope: rides to medical care by ambulance, chair car, dial-a-ride, taxi, or rideshare

rules.summary: Transportation to medical care is covered only for ambulance, chair car, dial-a-ride, taxi or rideshare costs.
rules.quote: Compensation for transportation costs incurred while obtaining medical care is limited to costs incurred for emergency and non-emergency ambulance service, chair car service, dial-a-ride, taxi, or ridesharing service obtained.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: Security measures can include doors, locks, exterior windows, security systems and reprogramming security codes.
rules.quote: Security measures may include but are not limited to, external and internal doors and locks, exterior windows and locks, security systems, and reprogramming security codes.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.item: Property losses, pain and suffering, and all other losses not listed as covered

rules.summary: The program page lists property losses, pain and suffering, and all other losses outside the covered list as not covered. The only property-type item on the covered list is replacement of clothing and bedding taken as evidence or ruined by the investigation.
rules.quote: Property losses, compensation for pain and suffering, and all other losses
rules.pinpoint: MOVA, Applying for Victims of Violent Crime Assistance, What expenses are not covered?
rules.source_title: Mass.gov, Applying for Victims of Violent Crime Assistance (MOVA)

params.item: Public transportation, and mileage or parking when private transportation is used

rules.summary: Bus or train fares, and mileage or parking for a personal car, are not reimbursed for trips to medical or mental health care.
rules.quote: It does not include compensation for public transportation, or mileage or parking when private transportation is used.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.item: Missed or cancelled counseling appointments, non-therapeutic court appearances and consultations, photocopying and report writing

rules.summary: Counseling compensation may be denied for missed or cancelled appointments and for non-therapeutic court or investigative work by the provider.
rules.quote: Compensation for mental health counseling may be denied for expenses incurred in the following instances: 1. missed or cancelled appointments; 2. non-therapeutic testimonial court appearances by a health care provider; 3. non-therapeutic investigatory consultations; 4. photocopying and report writing;
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within three years of the date of the crime.
rules.quote: A claim for compensation under this chapter shall be filed within three years of the date of the crime.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 5, Filing and proof of claims

params.extension: Applies when the victim was a minor at the time of the crime; does not apply to claims based on the death of a minor victim.

rules.summary: If the victim was a minor, the three-year filing period does not start until the victim turns 18.
rules.quote: The three-year filing period shall not commence until the victim reaches the age of 18.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: If the victim was a minor and a criminal complaint or indictment came after the victim turned 18, the time to file starts on the date it was issued.
rules.quote: If the victim was a minor when the crime was committed and the crime results in the issuance of a criminal complaint or indictment after the victim's 18th birthday, the filing period shall not commence until the date of issuance of the criminal complaint or indictment provided, however, that this exception shall not apply to claims based on the death of a minor victim.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.extension: Only if the crime resulted in a criminal complaint, indictment, or other judicial or administrative probable cause determination.

rules.summary: If you did not discover the crime until more than 3 years after it happened, the 3 years start when you discovered it, or should have. This applies only if there was a criminal complaint, an indictment, or another finding of probable cause.
rules.quote: If the claimant did not discover the act which constitutes a crime until more than three years after the crime was committed, the filing period shall not commence until the claimant discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the act which constitutes a crime; provided, however, that in such cases, the crime for which the claimant seeks compensation must have resulted in the issuance of a criminal complaint or indictment, or any other judicial or administrative determination of probable cause that an act constituting a crime has occurred.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.exception: or later if the program finds good cause or you were under 18

rules.summary: The crime must be reported within five days unless the agency finds good cause for the delay. Victims under 18 are not held to the five-day limit.
rules.quote: Except in the case where the agency finds such report to have been delayed for good cause, such report shall have been made within five days after the occurrence of such crime; provided, however, that a claimant who was a victim under 18 years of age shall not be required to file such report within 5 days.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 2, Eligibility for compensation

rules.summary: A Provider Sexual Crime Report filed by a medical provider counts as a report to law enforcement.
rules.quote: Reports to local law enforcement, via a Provider Sexual Crime Report (PSCR), in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, § 12A½, shall constitute a report to law enforcement authorities.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: Applying to a court for a restraining or harassment prevention order with a supporting affidavit, or applying for a criminal complaint, counts as a report to law enforcement.
rules.quote: The reporting of a crime to a court through a citizen application for a restraining order under M.G.L. c. 209A, and M.G.L. c. 258E, accompanied by an affidavit in support of the application for protection, or through a citizen application for a criminal complaint, shall constitute a report to law enforcement authorities.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: Telling a rape crisis center, private security, or the agency itself does not count as a report to law enforcement.
rules.quote: Reports to private security personnel, rape crisis centers, or the Agency do not constitute reports to law enforcement authorities.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: Good cause for a late report includes physical or psychological incapacity, or reasonable fear for the safety of the victim or others.
rules.quote: Good cause for delay shall include delay caused by physical or psychological incapacity which prevented the making of a report; or by (c) reasonable fear of safety for themselves or others.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: For a minor victim, a report to the Department of Children and Families under the state's mandated child abuse reporting law counts as a report for compensation purposes.
rules.quote: Crimes involving minor victims may be reported to the Department of Children and Families pursuant to the reporting requirements of M.G.L. c. 119, § 51A.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: To get compensation, the claimant must cooperate with law enforcement in the investigation and prosecution of the crime. This does not apply if the claimant shows a reasonable excuse for not cooperating.
rules.quote: A claimant shall be eligible for compensation only if such claimant cooperates with law enforcement authorities in the investigation and prosecution of the crime in which the victim was injured or killed unless the claimant demonstrates that he possesses or possessed a reasonable excuse for failing to cooperate.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 2, Eligibility for compensation

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: The program may accept the physical or psychological effects of the crime as a reasonable excuse for not cooperating. A reasonable fear for the safety of the claimant or others can count too.
rules.quote: The Agency may find that the physical or psychological impact of the crime and/or a reasonable fear of safety for themselves or others shall constitute a reasonable excuse and shall not constitute lack of cooperation.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: The program pays only for losses not covered by insurance, public benefits, restitution, civil suits or institutional gifts.
rules.quote: No compensation shall be awarded or paid unless the out-of-pocket expenses or legal liability of the claimant for services rendered as the result of the crime exceeds any and all of the amounts received, applied for, or to be applied for as the result of the crime from any of the following or any combination of the following:
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 10, Amounts received by claimant from other sources; offset

rules.summary: Crowdfunding raised for a victim does not have to be reported and is not treated as a source that must be used first.
rules.quote: Claimants have no obligation to notify the Agency of crowd funding dollars raised on their behalf, as this funding will not be considered as a source of payment that must be exhausted
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: An award may be reduced or denied to the extent the victim's conduct provoked or contributed to the injuries.
rules.quote: To the extent that the victim's acts or conduct provoked or contributed to the injuries, the agency may reduce or deny an award to the claimant or claimants in accordance with regulations enacted pursuant to section four.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 2, Eligibility for compensation

rules.summary: The regulations say sexual assault is, in general, not a circumstance that warrants reducing or denying an award for contributory conduct.
rules.quote: Circumstances that, in general, do not warrant the denial or reduction of an award based on contributory conduct include: 1. acts of negligence or poor judgment such as entering a motor vehicle operated by an intoxicated person; 2. crimes in which the victim is a victim of sexual assault;
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: Victim compensation is available to crime victims, including sexual assault survivors.
rules.quote: Financial compensation from the Victim Compensation and Assistance Division (VCAD) of the Massachusetts Office for Victim Assistance (MOVA) is available to victims of crime, including sexual assault survivors.
rules.pinpoint: MA SANE Protocol, Section X (Victim compensation)
rules.source_title: Mass.gov DPH, MA SANE Protocol Section X: Victim Compensation

rules.summary: A compensable crime must involve force, intimidation or violence, or the threat of it, by the offender against the victim.
rules.quote: provided, however, that such act involves the application of force, intimidation or violence or the threat of force, intimidation or violence by the offender upon the victim.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.rule: Crimes committed in Massachusetts (any victim), plus terrorism abroad against a Massachusetts resident

rules.summary: The program covers crimes that happen in Massachusetts, and acts of terrorism outside the United States against a Massachusetts resident.
rules.quote: Crime shall apply to an act occurring within the commonwealth, and to an act of terrorism, as defined in 18 USC section 2331, occurring outside the United States or territories against a resident of the commonwealth.
rules.source_title: M.G.L. c. 258C, s. 1, Definitions

params.rule: A Massachusetts resident harmed in another state may apply only if that state has no compensation program the resident is eligible for

rules.summary: A Massachusetts resident victimized in another state is covered only when that state has no compensation program the resident would qualify for.
rules.quote: The word "crime" shall also apply to an act which occurs against a resident of the Commonwealth in a state which does not have a crime victim compensation program for which a resident of the Commonwealth would be eligible.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.target: Massachusetts Office for Victim Assistance, One Ashburton Place, Suite 1310, Boston, MA 02108

rules.summary: The signed application can be mailed to the MOVA office in Boston.
rules.quote:
Return signed and completed application via mail, fax, or email to:

Massachusetts Office for Victim Assistance
One Ashburton Place, Suite 1310
Boston, MA 02108
rules.pinpoint: MOVA Application for Victim Compensation (2026, English), page 4, after section 9 (Acknowledgement)
rules.source_title: MOVA Application for Victim Compensation (English)
