rules.summary: The signed application can be faxed to the MOVA Victim Compensation fax line.
rules.quote:
Return signed and completed application via mail, fax, or email to:

Massachusetts Office for Victim Assistance
One Ashburton Place, Suite 1310
Boston, MA 02108
Phone: (617) 586-1340 Fax: (617) 742-6262
rules.pinpoint: MOVA Application for Victim Compensation (2026, English), page 4, after section 9 (Acknowledgement)
rules.source_title: MOVA Application for Victim Compensation (English)

rules.summary: The signed application can be emailed to the Victim Compensation correspondence address printed on the form.
rules.quote:
Return signed and completed application via mail, fax, or email to:

Massachusetts Office for Victim Assistance
One Ashburton Place, Suite 1310
Boston, MA 02108
Phone: (617) 586-1340 Fax: (617) 742-6262
Email: VCCorrespondence@state.ma.us
rules.pinpoint: MOVA Application for Victim Compensation (2026, English), page 4, after section 9 (Acknowledgement)
rules.source_title: MOVA Application for Victim Compensation (English)

params.note: copies of receipts for each expense type checked in section 5

rules.summary: Attach copies of receipts for the expenses being claimed.
rules.quote: Please check types of expenses for which you seek compensation and attach copies of bills and/or receipts.
rules.pinpoint: MOVA Application for Victim Compensation (2026, English), page 3, section 5 (Expenses)
rules.source_title: MOVA Application for Victim Compensation (English)

params.note: copies of bills and other supporting documentation needed to verify the claim

rules.summary: The claim must come with copies of bills and other documents that verify it.
rules.quote: The claim must be accompanied by copies of bills and other supporting documentation necessary to verify the claim
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.note: only when the survivor declined the forensic exam kit or the assault was too long ago for a kit; otherwise a report is not required for exam costs

rules.summary: A survivor who declined the forensic exam kit, or was past the kit window, must send a copy of the police report with the application.
rules.quote: In these circumstances, patients must submit a copy of their police report with their Victim Compensation Application.
rules.pinpoint: MA SANE Protocol, Section X (Patient declines MSAECK or patient ineligible for MSAECK)
rules.source_title: Mass.gov DPH, MA SANE Protocol Section X: Victim Compensation

params.note: only when claiming lost wages, and only when MOVA asks; employer verification of employment, dates absent, net weekly earnings and leave used

rules.summary: For lost wages, MOVA can ask for the employer's verification of employment, dates missed, net weekly pay and leave used.
rules.quote:
verification from the victim's employer (or, if self-employed, from the victim's own
records) that the victim was employed at the time of the crime
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

params.note: disability letter from a treating health care provider, only when claiming lost wages and MOVA asks

rules.summary: For lost wages, MOVA can ask for a letter from a treating provider saying the victim cannot work, or can work only part time, because of the crime.
rules.quote:
Upon request by the Agency, the victim must submit a disability letter from a treating health
care provider demonstrating that the victim is disabled from working full time, or limited to
working part time, as a direct result of the crime
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: MOVA says a decision generally comes 4 to 6 months after applying.
rules.quote: In general, you will receive a decision 4 to 6 months later.
rules.pinpoint: Mass.gov, Applying for Victims of Violent Crime Assistance, 'To apply'
rules.source_title: Mass.gov, Applying for Victims of Violent Crime Assistance (MOVA)

params.agency: Secretary of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts
params.enroll: You will need an application assistant to help you. Call 1-866-SAFE-ADD (1-866-723-3233) to find an application Assistant. The application assistant will provide the application and help you complete it. Your application assistant will submit the application to the Address Confidentiality Program. An ACP employee will contact you if your application is approved.

rules.summary: The Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Secretary of the Commonwealth, protects survivors of sexual assault, rape, domestic violence and stalking who move to get away from the person who hurt them. It is a mail-forwarding service that gives them a protected address to use with state and local agencies, so their new address is harder to find.
rules.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) protects survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, rape, and stalking as well as some legally protected healthcare providers. Survivors often move to get away from perpetrators of violence. The Address Confidentiality Program makes their new address harder to find. The ACP is a mail forwarding service that gives you a protected address to use with state and municipal agencies.
rules.pinpoint: Secretary of the Commonwealth, Address Confidentiality Program page, introduction
rules.source_title: Address Confidentiality Program (Secretary of the Commonwealth program page)

rules.summary: MOVA's regulation says all information it receives or keeps about a compensation claim is confidential and privileged, and anyone who gets those records from the agency may not disclose them.
rules.quote: All information received, obtained or maintained by the Agency in connection with any claim for crime victim compensation shall be confidential and privileged.
rules.source_title: 124 CMR 2.00, Compensation for Victims of Violent Crimes (MOVA; effective 8/4/25, Mass. Register #1564)

rules.summary: When a physician, qualified provider, or hospital gives a rape or sexual offense victim a forensic exam or the related emergency care listed in the statute, the services must be free to the survivor. The statute itself does not mention insurance; the exam billing regulation does.
rules.quote: the services shall be provided without charge to the individual
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-1007 (sexual assault exam payment)

params.payer: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit

rules.summary: The provider is paid by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (its Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit), not by the survivor.
rules.quote: is entitled to be paid by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy for the costs of providing the services
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-1007 (sexual assault exam payment)

params.payer: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit
params.condition: if done within 15 days of the assault

rules.summary: The free-exam rule covers a forensic exam done within 15 days of the assault (or longer if regulation allows) and emergency hospital treatment plus follow-up testing for up to 90 days after the exam.
rules.quote: a physical and sexual assault forensic examination to gather information and evidence as to an alleged crime when the examination is conducted within 15 days of the alleged crime or a longer period as provided by regulation; (2) emergency hospital treatment and follow-up medical testing for up to 90 days after the initial physical examination
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-1007 (sexual assault exam payment)

params.payer: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit

rules.summary: The state's reimbursement unit says the forensic exam is covered whether or not the survivor reports to police.
rules.quote: Yes, any victim of sexual assault or rape is entitled to a forensic medical examination regardless of their decision to report sexual assault to police.
rules.source_title: GOCPP: Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit page and FAQ

rules.summary: A provider may not bill the survivor, the survivor's family, or the survivor's private insurance for any difference between its charges and the state's payment, and must take the state's payment as payment in full.
rules.quote: May not bill a victim of an alleged rape, sexual offense, or child sexual abuse, or the victim's family or private insurance, for any difference between charges and Department reimbursement; and (3) Shall accept the Department's reimbursement as payment in full.
rules.source_title: COMAR 10.12.02 Rape and Sexual Offenses: Physician and Hospital Charges (within COMAR 10.12 full text)

rules.summary: Total compensation is capped at $45,000, including later and supplemental awards.
rules.quote: a total of $45,000, including any subsequent and supplemental awards
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)

params.exception: or up to $25,000 more if the injury leaves you fully disabled for life

rules.summary: If the injury results in permanent total disability, up to $25,000 more can be awarded after a disability-related claim has been awarded to the victim.
rules.quote: (ii) if the injury to the victim results in permanent total disability, up to an additional $25,000 after a disability–related claim has been awarded to the victim
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)

rules.summary: Medical claims are capped at $45,000.
rules.quote: $45,000 for a medical claim
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)

rules.summary: Counseling for a person eligible because of psychological injury is capped at $45,000 per claimant.
rules.quote: $45,000 for each claimant for psychiatric, psychological, or mental health counseling under subsection (a)(5) of this section
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)

params.applies_to: household family members of an injured victim (parent, child, domestic partner, dependent, or spouse living with the victim), not the victim

rules.summary: Household family members of an injured victim can get their own counseling, capped at $10,000 per claimant and $20,000 per incident. This cap is for those family members, not for the victim's own counseling.
rules.quote: for an award for psychiatric, psychological, or mental health counseling made under subsection (a)(6) of this section: (i) $10,000 for each claimant; and (ii) $20,000 for each incident
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "household family members of an injured victim (parent, child, domestic partner, dependent, or spouse living with the victim), not the victim"

rules.summary: Disability-related claims, which is how Maryland pays lost earnings after an injury, are capped at $25,000, with up to another $25,000 for permanent total disability.
rules.quote: for a disability-related or dependency-related claim: (i) except as provided in item (ii) of this paragraph, $25,000
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)

rules.summary: Repairing, replacing, or cleaning property damaged by the crime or by the police investigation, including replacing locks, is capped at $2,000 per claimant.
rules.quote: $2,000 for each claimant for repair, replacement, or cleaning of property damaged, soiled, or littered as a result of a crime or law enforcement investigation of a crime, including the cost of replacing locks
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)

rules.summary: Funeral expenses are capped at $10,000.
rules.quote: An award for funeral expenses may not exceed $10,000.
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)

rules.summary: Medical care and medical supplies count as covered losses.
rules.quote: medical care, including the cost of medical supplies
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-810 (conditions for awards)

rules.summary: Mental health counseling counts as a covered loss.
rules.quote: mental health counseling;
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-810 (conditions for awards)

rules.summary: Lost earnings are covered at up to two-thirds of the victim's gross average wage.
rules.quote: An award for loss of earnings or support made under this subtitle may be up to two-thirds of the victim's gross average wage
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)

params.applies_to: parent or guardian living with a child victim

rules.summary: A parent or guardian who lives with a child victim can get up to 30 days of lost earnings for time spent caring for the child.
rules.quote: The parent or guardian of a victim who is a child and who resides with the victim may be eligible for an award of up to 30 days of lost earnings as a result of caring for the victim.
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "parent or guardian living with a child victim"

params.scope: one move, with any security deposit

rules.summary: A one-time relocation, including a security deposit, counts as a covered loss. No dollar cap for relocation was found in the statute.
rules.quote: the costs of one-time relocation, including any security deposit
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-810 (conditions for awards)

params.scope: trips to get medical or mental health care

rules.summary: Travel costs to get medical or psychological care count as covered losses.
rules.quote: transportation costs incurred by travel to seek medical or psychological care
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-810 (conditions for awards)

params.scope: child care while you get medical or mental health care

rules.summary: Child care needed while seeking medical or psychological care counts as a covered loss.
rules.quote: child care expenses incurred as a result of seeking medical or psychological care
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-810 (conditions for awards)

rules.summary: Repairing, replacing, or cleaning property counts as a covered loss, subject to the separate property cap.
rules.quote: repairing, replacing, or cleaning property;
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-810 (conditions for awards)

params.scope: replacing locks

rules.summary: Replacing locks is covered inside the property cap.
rules.quote: including the cost of replacing locks
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)

rules.summary: Eyeglasses and other corrective lenses count as covered losses.
rules.quote: expenses for eyeglasses and other corrective lenses
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-810 (conditions for awards)

params.extension: Child abuse claims can be filed at any time; claims delayed by DNA testing of a sexual assault kit run from notification of the results; the Board can accept late claims for good cause.

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 4 years after the crime is discovered, or later in some cases.
rules.quote: a claimant shall file a claim within 4 years after the later of: (i) the discovery of the occurrence of the crime or delinquent act or the death of the victim
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-809 (filing claims)

rules.summary: In a case of child abuse, a claim can be filed at any time.
rules.quote: In a case of child abuse, a claimant may file a claim at any time.
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-809 (filing claims)

params.extension: Runs from notification of DNA testing or profile-matching results.

rules.summary: If filing was delayed because of a delay in testing a sexual assault kit or matching a DNA profile, the 4 years run from notification of the results.
rules.quote: In a case where the filing of a claim was delayed as the result of a delay in the testing of DNA or a delay in DNA profile matching from a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material related to a sexual offense, a claimant shall file a claim within 4 years after notification of the results of the testing or DNA profile matching.
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-809 (filing claims)

params.extension: good cause

rules.summary: The Board can accept a late claim if there was good cause for missing the deadline.
rules.quote: A claimant may file a claim at any time if the Board determines that there was good cause for failure to file a claim within the time limits
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-809 (filing claims)

rules.summary: A police report is one kind of evidence the Board must accept. It is not the only one. The Board must also accept medical records showing an injury that fits the crime. It must accept a sworn statement from a qualified third party, and a peace order or protective order. It must also accept any other evidence it thinks helps prove what happened.
rules.quote: The Board shall accept as evidence: (1) a report produced by a law enforcement agency; (2) medical records documenting an injury consistent with the alleged crime; (3) a sworn statement from a qualified third party; (4) a peace order issued under Title 3, Subtitle 15 of the Courts Article; (5) a protective order issued under Title 4, Subtitle 5 of the Family Law Article; and (6) any other evidence the Board considers probative.
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-810 (conditions for awards)

rules.summary: A sexual assault program advocate counts as a qualified third party whose sworn statement the Board accepts as evidence.
rules.quote: an advocate or victim service provider from a domestic violence or sexual assault prevention or assistance program
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-801 (definitions)

rules.summary: The claimant must have at least $100 in unreimbursed expenses, or have lost at least $100 in earnings or support.
rules.quote: The Board may make an award only if the claimant, as a result of the injury on which the claim is based, has: (1) incurred at least $100 in unreimbursed and unreimbursable expenses
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-810 (conditions for awards)

rules.summary: The award is reduced by money from the offender, insurance, workers' compensation, and other public or private sources. Life insurance counts only above a set amount.
rules.quote: An award made under this subtitle shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received as a result of the injury
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-811 (amount of award)

rules.summary: If the claimant has no private insurance, the program requires applying for Medicaid first.
rules.quote: If the claimant has no private insurance, CICB requires the claimant to apply for Medicaid.
rules.pinpoint: Application instruction sheet, Benefits and Required Documentation
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

rules.summary: The Board can make an emergency award before deciding the claim if an award is likely and the claimant faces undue hardship. It may not exceed $10,000 and is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: The amount of an emergency award under this section: (1) may not exceed $10,000
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-813 (emergency awards)

rules.summary: Unless an application is clearly without merit, the Board must make emergency awards for funeral costs, crime scene cleanup, and emergency relocation.
rules.quote: the Board shall make emergency awards for: (1) funeral expenses; (2) crime scene cleanup; and (3) emergency relocation
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-813 (emergency awards)

rules.summary: A victim is anyone who suffers physical or psychological injury from a crime, which includes sexual assault.
rules.quote: who suffers physical or psychological injury or death as a result of a crime or delinquent act
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-801 (definitions)

rules.summary: An award can rest on psychological injury that needed counseling, not only physical injury.
rules.quote: psychological injury to the victim that necessitated mental health counseling
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-810 (conditions for awards)

params.rule: Crimes in Maryland regardless of residency; crimes elsewhere against Maryland residents

rules.summary: Covers crimes committed in Maryland against anyone, and crimes in another state against a Maryland resident.
rules.quote: a criminal offense under state, federal, or common law that is committed in: 1. this State; or 2. another state against a resident of this State
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-801 (definitions)

params.rule: Maryland residents victimized out of state when the other state's program is unavailable

rules.summary: A Maryland resident hurt in another state can apply here if that state has no program, the victim is ineligible there, or that program has no money.
rules.quote: A resident of the State is eligible for an award under this subtitle if the resident becomes a victim in another state other than this State that: (1) does not operate a criminal injuries compensation program; (2) operates a criminal injuries compensation program for which the victim is ineligible
rules.source_title: Md. Code, Criminal Procedure 11-808 (eligibility)

rules.summary: The instructions say to mail, email, or deliver the completed application to the CICB office; this is the office address printed on the application and instruction sheet.
rules.quote: 6776 Reisterstown Rd, Ste. 206, Baltimore, MD 21215
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet header and Application Instructions
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

rules.summary: The completed application can be emailed to the CICB office at cicb.info@maryland.gov. State law allows claims to be filed electronically under Board procedures.
rules.quote: Email: cicb.info@maryland.gov
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet header and Application Instructions
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

rules.summary: The completed application can also be delivered in person to the CICB office in Baltimore. State law lists in person, by mail, or electronically as the ways to file.
rules.quote: 6776 Reisterstown Rd, Ste. 206, Baltimore, MD 21215
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet header and Application Instructions
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

params.note: Signed authorizations on page 2 of the application; an unsigned application is sent back and not filed.

rules.summary: Sign the authorizations on page 2 of the application. Without the signatures the application is returned and not filed.
rules.quote: Authorization Signatures on Page 2 of the application (Failure to sign will result in the application being returned and not filed)
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet, Application Instructions
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

params.note: The 2021 instructions ask for a police report or report number for all claims. Current statute (11-810(b), after HB 575) makes a police report one of several accepted kinds of evidence, so it is not strictly required.

rules.summary: The application instructions ask for a police report or police report number for all claims; a report to a judicial authority may also be considered.
rules.quote: All claims: Police report or police report number. Report to judicial authority may also be considered.
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet, Benefits & Required Documentation
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

params.note: For medical or dental costs: itemized bills.

rules.summary: For medical or dental costs, include itemized bills.
rules.quote: Medical/Dental: Itemized bills; letter from a doctor or medical documentation relating the injury to the crime and the treatment; treatment plan; & medical insurance.
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet, Benefits & Required Documentation
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

params.note: For medical or dental costs: a doctor's letter or medical documentation tying the injury and treatment to the crime, plus a treatment plan.

rules.summary: For medical or dental costs, include a doctor's letter or medical records linking the injury and treatment to the crime, and a treatment plan.
rules.quote: Medical/Dental: Itemized bills; letter from a doctor or medical documentation relating the injury to the crime and the treatment; treatment plan; & medical insurance.
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet, Benefits & Required Documentation
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

params.note: Medical insurance information. With no private insurance, CICB requires the claimant to apply for Medicaid.

rules.summary: Include medical insurance information. If the claimant has no private insurance, CICB requires an application for Medicaid.
rules.quote: & medical insurance. If the claimant has no private insurance, CICB requires the claimant to apply for Medicaid.
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet, Benefits & Required Documentation
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

params.note: For counseling: a therapist's letter documenting crime-related treatment, plus itemized statements.

rules.summary: For counseling, include a letter from the therapist documenting crime-related treatment and itemized statements.
rules.quote: Counseling: Letter from a therapist documenting treatment related to crime; itemized statements; receipts if paid out of pocket by claimant.
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet, Benefits & Required Documentation
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

params.note: Receipts for anything the claimant paid out of pocket (named for counseling; crime scene clean-up also takes receipts).

rules.summary: Include receipts for costs the claimant paid out of pocket.
rules.quote: receipts if paid out of pocket by claimant
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet, Benefits & Required Documentation
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

params.note: For lost wages or disability: employer information and W-2 and/or pay stubs.

rules.summary: For lost wages or disability, include employer information and W-2s or pay stubs.
rules.quote: Lost Wages/Disability: Employer information; W-2 and/or pay stubs; letter from a doctor certifying inability to work.
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet, Benefits & Required Documentation
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

params.note: For lost wages or disability: a doctor's letter certifying inability to work.

rules.summary: For lost wages or disability, include a doctor's letter certifying the inability to work.
rules.quote: letter from a doctor certifying inability to work
rules.pinpoint: CICB Application with instructions (Rev. November, 2021), Instruction Sheet, Benefits & Required Documentation
rules.source_title: CICB Application for Crime Victim Compensation with instructions (rev. Nov 2021)

params.program_name: Address Confidentiality Program (Maryland Safe at Home)
params.enroll: Applications are available through Application Assistants, professional victim service providers registered with the Office of the Secretary of State. An Application Assistant will help you develop a safety plan and determine if participation in the ACP is a good fit. Please call the ACP at 410.260.3875 if you do not qualify for traditional victim services but would like to apply to the Address Confidentiality Program, or if you have trouble connecting with an Application Assistant.

rules.summary: Maryland's Secretary of State runs an Address Confidentiality Program. It is for survivors of threatened, attempted, or actual sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, harassment, or human trafficking.
rules.quote: The Secretary of State shall establish and administer an Address Confidentiality Program for survivors of threatened, attempted, or actual domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, harassment, or human trafficking.
rules.source_title: Md. Code, State Government 7-303 (Address Confidentiality Program)

rules.summary: The hospital or provider that does a sexual assault forensic exam may not bill the survivor or the survivor's insurer for the exam.
rules.quote: The hospital or health care practitioner that performs the examination may not bill the victim or the victim's insurer, nonprofit hospital or medical service organization or health maintenance organization for payment of the examination.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-M (Payment for forensic examinations for victims of sexual assault)

params.payer: Victims' Compensation Board, from the Victims' Compensation Fund

rules.summary: The Victims' Compensation Board pays the provider directly from the Victims' Compensation Fund for the forensic exam, up to $750. The exam includes evidence collection and related testing and treatment for pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases.
rules.quote: An examination must include at least all services directly related to the gathering of forensic evidence and related testing and treatment for pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases.  The board shall pay a licensed hospital or licensed health care practitioner the actual cost of the forensic examination up to a maximum of $750.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-M (Payment for forensic examinations for victims of sexual assault)

rules.summary: The survivor does not have to report the assault to law enforcement to get the forensic exam paid for. This applies to the exam payment only; a regular compensation claim still needs a report.
rules.quote: The victim is not required to report the offense to a law enforcement agency.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-M (Payment for forensic examinations for victims of sexual assault)

rules.summary: The hospital may not bill the survivor or their insurer for the exam or balance-bill anything over the $750 the program pays. Charges unrelated to the exam, such as x-rays, can still be billed to the survivor or their insurer.
rules.quote: The hospital may not bill you or your insurer for the sexual assault examination nor for any balance over the $750. This bill will be paid even if you do not report the assault to law enforcement. However: The hospital is allowed to bill you or your insurer for charges unrelated to the sexual assault examination, for x-rays for example.
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG SAFE page, Notice to sexual assault victims
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Sexual Assault Forensic Examinations (SAFE)

params.payer: Victims' Compensation Program, for sexual assaults in Maine
params.condition: if an evidence kit is used for a crime in Maine

rules.summary: The Attorney General's page says Maine makes sure survivors of sexual assaults that happen in Maine do not pay for evidence collection, and the program pays hospitals and providers directly. Its notice to survivors is about exams done with an evidence collection kit.
rules.quote: Maine ensures that survivors of sexual assaults that occur in Maine are not responsible for the cost of evidence collection, also known as a Sexual Assault Forensic Examination (SAFE). The Victims' Compensation Program provides direct reimbursement to hospitals and other healthcare providers who perform SAFE. Learn more about the SAFE Program on the Department of Health and Human Services' SAFE Program webpage . Notice to sexual assault victims If you have had a sexual assault forensic examination (with evidence collection kit) performed, you should know the following:
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG SAFE page, introduction and Notice to sexual assault victims
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Sexual Assault Forensic Examinations (SAFE)

params.payer: Victims' Compensation Board, only when a sexual assault evidence collection kit is used

rules.summary: Direct billing to the Victims' Compensation Board applies only when the exam is done with a sexual assault forensic examination kit. If no kit is used, the provider bills the usual way.
rules.quote: This direct billing and payment process is to be used only when a forensic examination is performed using a sexual assault forensic examination kit. If a kit is not used, use your customary billing procedures.
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG SAFE page, Notice to healthcare providers performing SAFE
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Sexual Assault Forensic Examinations (SAFE)

rules.summary: The maximum award is $15,000 for actual, unreimbursed losses and eligible expenses.
rules.quote: The board may award compensation to a claimant of up to $15,000 for actual and unreimbursed losses and eligible expenses of any person who is sexually assaulted
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-E (Payment of awards; limits)

rules.summary: The $15,000 limit covers all claims from one crime combined, including family members' claims.
rules.quote: The total compensation paid from the fund for all claims arising from the crime against the victim may not exceed $15,000.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-E (Payment of awards; limits)

rules.summary: Medical costs, including equipment, supplies and medications, are covered, usually limited to 75% of actual charges.
rules.quote: Medical (including equipment, supplies and medications) limited to 75% of actual charges in most cases
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG Victims' Compensation page, What Expenses Are Covered?
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Dental charges and denture replacement are covered.
rules.quote: Dental charges and replacement of dentures
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG Victims' Compensation page, What Expenses Are Covered?
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Psychological or mental health counseling expenses are eligible.
rules.quote: psychological or mental health counseling expenses
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Family or household members of a sexual assault victim can also get unreimbursed mental health treatment related to the crime covered.
rules.quote: a family or household member of a sexual assault victim for unreimbursed mental health treatment expenses directly related to the crime
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-B (Award of compensation; eligibility)

rules.summary: Lost wages are an eligible loss.
rules.quote: lost wages
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Lost income is covered for victims, with limited coverage when caring for dependents is necessary.
rules.quote: Lost income (for victims and limited coverage when care of dependents is necessary)
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG Victims' Compensation page, What Expenses Are Covered?
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation

params.applies_to: a claimant or family member who provides or obtains care for a minor or incapacitated victim

rules.summary: Travel expenses are listed only for a claimant or family member providing or obtaining care for a minor or incapacitated victim.
rules.quote: travel expenses and loss of income of a claimant or family member for providing or obtaining care for the personal injury of a minor or incapacitated victim
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360 (Definitions)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "a claimant or family member who provides or obtains care for a minor or incapacitated victim"

rules.summary: Costs to repair, replace or install locks or security devices are eligible.
rules.quote: costs to repair, replace or install locks or security devices
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Relocation expenses are eligible.
rules.quote: costs of crime scene cleanup and relocation expenses
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup costs are eligible.
rules.quote: costs of crime scene cleanup and relocation expenses
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures or other prosthetic devices taken, lost, destroyed or damaged in the crime are eligible.
rules.quote: costs of eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures or other prosthetic devices taken, lost, destroyed or damaged as a result of the crime
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Funeral and burial costs are covered up to $4,500, plus up to $500 for a marker.
rules.quote: Funeral/ burial costs up to $4,500, costs of a marker up to $500
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG Victims' Compensation page, What Expenses Are Covered?
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation

params.item: property losses and pain and suffering

rules.summary: The program does not pay for property losses or for pain and suffering.
rules.quote: Expenses NOT covered: property losses, compensation for pain and suffering, and other losses not medically related.
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG Victims' Compensation page, What Expenses Are Covered?
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation

params.item: property losses other than eyeglasses, dentures, prosthetic devices and some crime scene cleanup

rules.summary: Property losses are not covered, except replacement of eyeglasses, dentures and other prosthetic devices and some crime scene cleanup costs.
rules.quote: No property losses are covered other than replacement costs of eyeglasses, dentures and other prosthetic devices and some costs of crime scene cleanup.
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG Program Law and History, What Is an Eligible Expense?
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation Program Law and History

params.extension: or within 60 days after the injury or loss is discovered, if that is later

rules.summary: The claim must be filed within 3 years of the injury or loss, or within 60 days of discovering it, whichever is later.
rules.quote: B. The claim was filed with the board within 3 years of the occurrence of the injury or compensable loss, or within 60 days of the discovery of injury or compensable loss, whichever is later.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-C (Requirements and exclusions)

rules.summary: If the injury or loss is discovered later, the claim can be filed within 60 days of discovery when that is later than 3 years.
rules.quote: B. The claim was filed with the board within 3 years of the occurrence of the injury or compensable loss, or within 60 days of the discovery of injury or compensable loss, whichever is later.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-C (Requirements and exclusions)

params.extension: good cause; mandatory for child victims

rules.summary: The board may waive the filing and police-report time limits for good cause, and must waive them on behalf of a child.
rules.quote: The board may waive the time requirements of subsection 1 for good cause shown and shall waive the time requirements on behalf of a child
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-C (Requirements and exclusions)

params.exception: counted from the crime, the injury, or when either was discovered

rules.summary: For a compensation claim, the crime must be reported to law enforcement within 5 days of when the crime or the resulting injury happened or was discovered.
rules.quote: A. The crime was reported to a law enforcement officer within 5 days of the occurrence or discovery of the crime or of the resultant injury
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-C (Requirements and exclusions)

params.exception: or later if the board waives it for good cause or for a child

rules.summary: The board may waive the time limits to report and to apply for good cause. It must waive them on behalf of a child, or when the claimant is a child and an adult who learned of the crime and the injury properly reported the crime and the claim to police and the board.
rules.quote: The board may waive the time requirements of subsection 1 for good cause shown and shall waive the time requirements on behalf of a child or when the claimant is a child and the crime and the claim have been properly reported to law enforcement officers and the board by an adult who becomes aware of the crime and of the compensable injury.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-C (Requirements and exclusions)

rules.summary: For current or former Maine National Guard members, an unrestricted sexual assault report to the Guard counts as a report to law enforcement.
rules.quote: an unrestricted report of sexual assault made to the Maine National Guard by a current or former member of the Maine National Guard is a crime reported to a law enforcement officer
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-C (Requirements and exclusions)

rules.summary: The free forensic exam does not require a police report, but a regular compensation claim for other costs does.
rules.quote: If you need help with these expenses, you may file a Victims' Compensation Application, but, in that case, you will need to report the crime to law enforcement and other requirements of the Victims' Compensation Program will apply.
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG SAFE page, Notice to sexual assault victims
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Sexual Assault Forensic Examinations (SAFE)

rules.summary: Insurance, other coverage, free care or sliding-scale eligibility must be used first; the program pays after that.
rules.quote: If a victim has insurance and other coverage or eligibility for free care or a sliding scale, that must be applied to an expense or loss before Victims' Compensation pays
rules.pinpoint: Maine AG Victims' Compensation page, What Are the Requirements?
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Compensation may not be paid to someone whose own violation of a criminal law caused or contributed to the injury (information only).
rules.quote: B. To or on behalf of any person who violated a criminal law that caused or contributed to the injury or death for which compensation is sought
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-C (Requirements and exclusions)

rules.summary: Compensation may not be paid to a claimant who does not fully cooperate with the board or with reasonable requests of law enforcement or prosecutors.
rules.quote: A. To any claimant who does not fully cooperate with the board or with the reasonable requests of law enforcement officers or prosecution authorities
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-C (Requirements and exclusions)

rules.summary: Sexual assault in Maine is a covered crime, whether or not there was bodily injury or a threat of it.
rules.quote: B. Has been sexually assaulted within this State in violation of Title 17‑A, chapter 11 without regard to whether bodily injury or the threat of bodily injury occurred
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-B (Award of compensation; eligibility)

rules.summary: Aggravated sex trafficking and sex trafficking are covered crimes.
rules.quote: J. Aggravated sex trafficking or sex trafficking as described in Title 17‑A, sections 852 and 853
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Sexual exploitation of a minor is a covered crime.
rules.quote: H. Sexual exploitation of a minor as described in Title 17‑A, chapter 12
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360 (Definitions)

params.rule: crime committed in Maine

rules.summary: Victims of a covered crime committed in Maine can apply; the statute does not limit this to Maine residents.
rules.quote: A. Suffers personal injury as a direct result of a crime specified in section 3360 , committed within the jurisdiction of the State
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-B (Award of compensation; eligibility)

params.rule: Maine residents for out-of-state crimes only when that state has no program available to them

rules.summary: A Maine resident hurt in another state can apply here only if that state has no compensation program Maine residents can use.
rules.quote: (3) The crime occurred in another state, but only if the person is a resident of this State and the other state does not have a victim compensation program for which residents of this State are eligible
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-B (Award of compensation; eligibility)

params.note: The quote's link text on the AG program page points to this URL. The portal itself is a script-only page that could not be saved as text.

rules.summary: A survivor applies online through the Attorney General's victims' compensation portal.
rules.quote: Apply online for victims' compensation
rules.pinpoint: AG Victims' Compensation page, Victims links
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation

params.note: Signed application; release forms come with the application so staff can gather and verify records.

rules.summary: The application must be signed, and it includes release forms that let staff collect and verify information.
rules.quote: The application must be signed and sent to the Victims' Compensation Board. Release forms are included with the application to allow staff to compile and verify information.
rules.pinpoint: AG Program Law and History, Application Process
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Victims' Compensation Program Law and History

params.note: Medical reports and records for the expenses claimed.

rules.summary: A claim must include documentation of every expense claimed, including medical reports and records.
rules.quote: Claims must include documentation of all eligible expenses and losses for which the claimant seeks compensation, including but not limited to medical reports, records and bills, funeral bills and employment records when lost wages are sought.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

params.note: Medical bills (and funeral bills where relevant) for each expense claimed.

rules.summary: A claim must include the bills for the expenses claimed, such as medical bills.
rules.quote: Claims must include documentation of all eligible expenses and losses for which the claimant seeks compensation, including but not limited to medical reports, records and bills, funeral bills and employment records when lost wages are sought.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

params.note: Only when lost wages are claimed: employment records.

rules.summary: A survivor claiming lost wages must include employment records.
rules.quote: Claims must include documentation of all eligible expenses and losses for which the claimant seeks compensation, including but not limited to medical reports, records and bills, funeral bills and employment records when lost wages are sought.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

params.note: Records about insurance, workers' compensation, and state or federal benefit programs.

rules.summary: A claim must include records about insurance, workers' compensation, and state or federal assistance programs.
rules.quote: Claims must include records related to insurance, workers' compensation, federal and state entitlement and assistance programs.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

params.note: Not a document upload: the claim must name the crime date, what happened, and the law enforcement agency it was reported to.

rules.summary: The claim must give the date and circumstances of the crime and name the law enforcement agency it was reported to.
rules.quote: Claims must specify the date, the nature and circumstances of the crime and the law enforcement agency to which the crime was reported.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

params.note: The counselor completes and sends a treatment plan to Victims' Compensation; the Board will not consider counseling costs without it.

rules.summary: For counseling costs, the counselor must send a completed treatment plan; the case cannot go to the Board without it.
rules.quote: Your case cannot go before the Board without the completed treatment plan.
rules.source_title: Maine AG: Mental Health Counseling Guidelines

params.enroll: Upon recommendation of an application assistant, an adult person, a parent or guardian acting on behalf of a minor or a guardian acting on behalf of an incapacitated person may apply to the secretary to have a designated address assigned by the secretary to serve as the person's address or the address of the minor or incapacitated person.

rules.summary: The Secretary of State runs an Address Confidentiality Program that gives victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking or human trafficking a designated substitute address, which state and local agencies and courts must use instead of the real one. A survivor applies with the help of a registered application assistant, usually at a victim services program.
rules.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program is established to protect victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking or human trafficking; minor victims of kidnapping; and reproductive or gender-affirming health care services practitioners by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims and practitioners.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 90-B (Address Confidentiality Program)

rules.summary: Everything the Attorney General's office holds about a compensation application or award is confidential and stays confidential with the Board. The Attorney General may still share it, at its discretion, with law enforcement, courts and Corrections for restitution, a claimant in a hearing or appeal, or others to carry out the program.
rules.quote: All records and information obtained by or in the possession of the Department of the Attorney General concerning an application for or an award of compensation under this chapter are confidential and may not be disclosed.
rules.source_title: 5 M.R.S. 3360-D (Claims)

rules.summary: A health care provider may not bill a sexual assault survivor for any part of a forensic exam, including insurance deductibles, co-pays, or a denied insurance claim.
rules.quote: A health care provider shall not submit a bill for any portion of the costs of a sexual assault medical forensic examination to the victim of the sexual assault, including any insurance deductible or co-pay, denial of claim by an insurer, or any other out-of-pocket expense.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.355a (sexual assault medical forensic examination)

rules.summary: The provider must tell the survivor, orally and in writing, that the exam will not be billed to their insurance without their express written consent, and they may decline for privacy or safety reasons.
rules.quote: Advise the victim, orally and in writing, that a claim shall not be submitted to his or her insurance carrier without his or her express written consent, and that he or she may decline to consent if he or she believes that submitting a claim to the insurance carrier would substantially interfere with his or her personal privacy or safety.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.355a (sexual assault medical forensic examination)

params.payer: Crime Victim Services Commission (SAFE Response)

rules.summary: The Crime Victim Services Commission pays the provider up to $1,200 for a sexual assault forensic exam.
rules.quote: The commission shall pay a health care provider not more than $1,200.00 for the cost of performing a sexual assault medical forensic examination
rules.source_title: MCL 18.355a (sexual assault medical forensic examination)

params.payer: SAFE Response (Crime Victim Services Commission)

rules.summary: If you believe billing your insurance would substantially interfere with your privacy or safety, the doctor or nurse can bill SAFE Response for the exam instead.
rules.quote: If a victim believes submitting a claim to their insurance carrier would substantially interfere with his or her personal privacy or safety, the doctor or nurse can bill SAFE Response for the forensic examination.
rules.source_title: MDHHS SAFE Response (sexual assault forensic exam payment)

params.payer: Crime Victim Services Commission, or another entity other than the victim, when insurance cannot be billed or does not pay

rules.summary: If the victim's insurance does not pay or is not available, the provider can seek payment from the commission or another entity, but never from the victim.
rules.quote: A health care provider may seek payment from 1 or both of the following if reimbursement cannot be obtained from the victim's insurance or insurance is unavailable: (a) The commission under this section. (b) From another entity other than the victim.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.355a (sexual assault medical forensic examination)

rules.summary: The total award cannot exceed $45,000 per claimant.
rules.quote: The aggregate award under this act must not exceed $45,000.00 per claimant.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Counseling with a licensed or registered therapist or counselor is reimbursed at up to $80 per hourly session.
rules.quote: The maximum hourly reimbursement rate must not exceed $80.00 per hourly session for a therapist or counselor licensed or registered to practice in this state
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Counseling with a licensed psychologist or physician is reimbursed at up to $125 per hourly session.
rules.quote: except that the maximum hourly reimbursement rate must not exceed $125.00 per hourly session for a psychologist or physician licensed to practice in this state.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: The program's award table lists counseling limits of 35 sessions and 20 family sessions, at $80 an hour for a therapist or counselor and $125 an hour for a psychologist or physician.
rules.quote: 35 sessions, 20 family sessions $80/hour for a therapist/counselor $125/hour for a psychologist/physician
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS award limits table, Psychological Counseling
rules.source_title: MDHHS: What Costs May Be Covered for Crime Victims?

rules.summary: Lost earnings are paid at the actual loss, up to $1,000 for each week.
rules.quote: An award must not exceed $1,000.00 for each week of lost earnings.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Relocation expenses are capped at $3,800 per claimant.
rules.quote: An award for expenses under this subdivision may not exceed $3,800.00 per claimant.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

params.scope: temporary lodging for not more than 30 days

rules.summary: Temporary lodging is one of the relocation costs. It counts toward the same $3,800 limit per claimant as the first month of rent, a security deposit, starting utilities, and moving costs.
rules.quote: An award for expenses under this subdivision may not exceed $3,800.00 per claimant. Eligible relocation expenses under this subdivision include, but are not limited to, all of the following expenses: (i) The first month of rent, a security deposit, and the costs to start utilities in the dwelling unit to which the claimant relocates. The commission may require the claimant to provide a signed rental agreement to verify these expenses. (ii) Moving expenses, including, but not limited to, costs to rent a truck, travel, and for moving services. (iii) Costs for temporary lodging for not more than 30 days.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Transportation for trips of 50 miles or less each way is capped at $1,000 in total per claimant.
rules.quote: (i) If the expense is for travel of a distance of not more than 50 miles each way from the claimant's residence, $1,000.00.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Transportation is capped at $5,000 in total per claimant when the trip is at least 50 miles each way to care that is not available within 50 miles of home.
rules.quote: (ii) If the expense is for travel that meets 1 or more of the following, $5,000.00: (A) If the travel is a distance of not less than 50 miles from the claimant's residence each way and is to and from a health care provider, mental health professional as that term is defined in section 100b of the mental health code, 1974 PA 258, MCL 330.1100b, or health facility or agency that renders a specific treatment or care that is not available within 50 miles of the claimant's residence.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Residential security (security systems, window or lock repair or replacement, added locks) is covered up to $1,000 per residence.
rules.quote: (f) Reasonable costs of not more than $1,000.00 per residence for installing, increasing, or replacing residential security, which may include installing a home security device or system; replacing or repairing windows or locks; or increasing the number of locks
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Clothing or bedding held as evidence can be replaced up to $250.
rules.quote: (j) Replacement costs of not more than $250.00 for clothing or bedding of an individual listed in section 4(1)(a), (b), (e), or (f), that is held as evidence of a crime.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup at a home or vehicle is covered up to $5,000 per crime scene.
rules.quote: the crime scene cleanup services resulting from a crime for that residence or vehicle after crime scene cleanup is permitted by the investigating law enforcement agency, in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00 per crime scene.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Unreimbursed medical care for the victim is covered.
rules.quote: (a) Medical care for the victim or intervenor.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Psychological counseling is covered, subject to the session and rate limits.
rules.quote: (b) Subject to subsection (6), psychological or grief counseling for an individual listed in section 4(1)(a), (b), (c), (e), (f), or (g).
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Lost wages are covered, including time off work to seek medical care, recover, get counseling, or get help from a victim services organization.
rules.quote: A claimant may be awarded for loss of earnings under this subsection for lost wages as a result of the crime
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Moving costs are paid only if you move to protect your physical safety or your emotional or financial well-being because of the crime. Unless you show good cause, you must move within 1 year of the crime or of a new threat or sign of danger.
rules.quote: An award for expenses under this subdivision may be made only if the claimant is relocating to protect the claimant's physical safety or emotional or financial well-being as a result of the crime and, unless good cause is shown, is relocating within 1 year of the date the crime occurred, or of the date the claimant is threatened by a change in circumstance or by an indicator of danger.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: As part of relocation, temporary lodging is covered for up to 30 days.
rules.quote: (iii) Costs for temporary lodging for not more than 30 days.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Relocation can include the first month of rent, a security deposit, and the cost of starting utilities at the new home.
rules.quote: (i) The first month of rent, a security deposit, and the costs to start utilities in the dwelling unit to which the claimant relocates.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

params.scope: trips to medical care, mental health care, a victim services organization, or a victim's funeral

rules.summary: Transportation is covered to reach victim services, medical care, or mental health care.
rules.quote: (e) Transportation expenses for the purpose of an individual listed in section 4(1)(a), or if the victim or intervenor is deceased, for a person listed in section 4(1)(b), (e), or (f), to access services from a victim services organization, medical care, or mental health care, or to attend the funeral of a victim or intervenor.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

params.scope: paying someone else for child care or housework you can no longer do because of the injury or while you get victim services

rules.summary: Replacement services such as child care and homemaking are covered when the survivor cannot do them because of the injury or while attending victim services.
rules.quote: (d) Replacement services for homemaking tasks, child care, and other services previously performed by an individual listed in section 4(1)(a), (b), (e), or (f), that, because of the victim's injury, or the claimant's attendance at a victim services organization to receive services related to the crime, must temporarily or permanently be performed by another person.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: Reasonable and necessary medical, dental, optical, and counseling costs are covered.
rules.quote: Reasonable and necessary medical, dental, optical, counseling, and non-medical remedial treatment.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS What Costs May Be Covered, Costs that May Be Covered
rules.source_title: MDHHS: What Costs May Be Covered for Crime Victims?

params.item: eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures, prosthetic or other prescription devices

rules.summary: Eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures, and other prescription devices are covered if damaged during or needed because of the crime.
rules.quote: Eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures, prosthetic devices, or other prescription devices, if damaged during or needed because of the crime.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS What Costs May Be Covered, Costs that May Be Covered
rules.source_title: MDHHS: What Costs May Be Covered for Crime Victims?

params.item: personal property such as a purse or cell phone

rules.summary: Damage to or loss of some personal property or a vehicle, such as a purse or cell phone, is not covered.
rules.quote: Damage, repair or loss to some personal property or vehicle, such as a purse or cell phone.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS What Costs May Be Covered, Costs that are NOT Covered
rules.source_title: MDHHS: What Costs May Be Covered for Crime Victims?

params.item: pain, suffering, or emotional distress damages

rules.summary: Pain, suffering, or emotional distress damages are not covered.
rules.quote: Pain, suffering, or emotional distress damages.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS What Costs May Be Covered, Costs that are NOT Covered
rules.source_title: MDHHS: What Costs May Be Covered for Crime Victims?

params.item: costs of participating in a trial

rules.summary: Costs of taking part in a trial are not covered.
rules.quote: Costs of participating in a trial.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS What Costs May Be Covered, Costs that are NOT Covered
rules.source_title: MDHHS: What Costs May Be Covered for Crime Victims?

params.item: expenses paid by other sources such as insurance

rules.summary: Expenses already paid by insurance or other sources are not covered.
rules.quote: Expenses paid by other sources (public or private health insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, workers compensation, auto insurance, etc.).
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS What Costs May Be Covered, Costs that are NOT Covered
rules.source_title: MDHHS: What Costs May Be Covered for Crime Victims?

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 5 years after the crime.
rules.quote: a claim must be filed by the claimant not later than 5 years after the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based
rules.source_title: MCL 18.355 (filing a claim; deadline)

rules.summary: For criminal sexual conduct (first through third degree) where police records show the victim was under 18, a claim may be filed within 5 years after the crime was reported, if reported before age 28 or later with good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: a claim based on the crime of criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, or third degree may be filed by a claimant not later than 5 years after the crime was reported: (i) Police records show the victim of the crime was less than 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence and the victim reported the crime before attaining 28 years of age. (ii) Police records show the victim of the crime was less than 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence, the victim reported the crime after attaining 28 years of age, and the claimant shows that there was good cause for the delay in reporting the crime.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.355 (filing a claim; deadline)

params.extension: good cause

rules.summary: The commission may extend the filing deadline for good cause if the claimant asks.
rules.quote: Upon petition by the claimant and for good cause shown, the commission may extend the period in which a claim may be filed under subsection (2).
rules.source_title: MCL 18.355 (filing a claim; deadline)

rules.summary: For sexual assault, having a sexual assault forensic exam satisfies the prompt police-reporting and cooperation requirements for compensation.
rules.quote: For payments authorized under this section or for payments made to victims under section 6, administration to the victim of a sexual assault medical forensic examination satisfies the requirements for prompt law enforcement reporting and victim cooperation under sections 6 and 10.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.355a (sexual assault medical forensic examination)

rules.summary: In general, police records must show the crime was reported to the proper authorities.
rules.quote: (c) Police records show that the crime was reported to the proper authorities.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.360 (verification of facts; police report)

rules.summary: The program says a sexual assault forensic exam may be used in place of a police report.
rules.quote: The crime must be reported to law enforcement (waivers may apply). If the crime was a sexual assault, then a sexual assault forensic exam may be used in lieu of reporting to police.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS Do I Qualify?, Eligibility Requirements
rules.source_title: MDHHS Crime Victim Compensation: Do I Qualify?

params.scope: medical bills for injuries other than the forensic exam

rules.summary: The program's SAFE Response page covers medical bills for injuries other than the exam. To get that help, it says a victim would have to apply, report to police, and cooperate with the investigation. The victim would also have to use their medical insurance, including Medicaid or Medicare, or any other way to pay.
rules.quote: If a sexual assault victim sustains a personal physical injury that needs to be treated other than the forensic exam, he or she may be eligible for assistance with medical bills through the Crime Victim Services Commission compensation program. The victim would have to submit a compensation claim application, report the incident to the police, cooperate with the investigation and utilize their medical insurance, including Medicaid, Medicare, or any other resource available for payment.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS SAFE Response page, Other physical injuries
rules.source_title: MDHHS SAFE Response (sexual assault forensic exam payment)

waived_for: criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, or third degree (discretionary)
claimants retired by reason of age or disability (discretionary)

rules.summary: A claim needs at least $200 in out-of-pocket loss or at least 5 days of lost earnings or support; the commission may waive this for victims of criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, or third degree.
rules.quote: An award must not be made on a claim unless the claimant has incurred an out-of-pocket loss of not less than $200.00, or has lost at least 5 days' earnings or support, but the commission may waive the limitations of this subsection if a claimant is retired by reason of age or disability. If the claimant is a victim of criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, or third degree, the commission may waive the limitations of this subsection.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.354 (eligibility; minimum loss)

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by payments from the offender, insurance, or public funds received for the injury.
rules.quote: An award must be reduced by the amount of 1 or more of the following payments received or to be received as a result of the injury:
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: The program is the payer of last resort, so insurance and other public funds must be used first.
rules.quote: Please note that Crime Victim Compensation is the payer of last resort. This means that your private insurance or other public funds, if available, must be utilized first in order for you to be eligible for compensation.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS FAQ, What is Crime Victim Compensation?
rules.source_title: MDHHS Crime Victim Compensation: Frequently Asked Questions

rules.summary: Having insurance does not disqualify you; the program can cover copays and deductibles.
rules.quote: Yes, you may still qualify for Crime Victim Compensation if you have insurance. We can cover copays and deductibles.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS FAQ, Do I qualify if I have insurance?
rules.source_title: MDHHS Crime Victim Compensation: Frequently Asked Questions

rules.summary: The commission must consider whether the victim's misconduct contributed to the injury and may reduce or reject the award on that basis.
rules.quote: the commission shall determine whether the victim's misconduct contributed to his or her injury and shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether, in accordance with the determination.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.361 (amount of award; caps; reductions)

rules.summary: If the commission finds the victim or claimant chose not to cooperate with law enforcement or the prosecutor, it must turn down the claim.
rules.quote: In the event of determination of willful noncooperation by the victim or other claimant, the commission shall reject the claim.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.356 (investigation; willful noncooperation)

rules.summary: If an award is likely and waiting would cause undue hardship, the commission may make an emergency award of up to $4,000, which is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: The amount of an emergency award under this section must not exceed $4,000.00 and must be deducted from the final award made to the claimant.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.359 (emergency award)

rules.summary: Sexual assault victims are listed as eligible for crime victim compensation.
rules.quote: The following individuals may be considered a victim and qualify for crime victim compensation: A person who was physically, emotionally, psychologically, or mentally injured as the direct result of a crime. A sexual assault victim.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS Do I Qualify?, Who is considered a victim?
rules.source_title: MDHHS Crime Victim Compensation: Do I Qualify?

rules.summary: Personal injury includes bodily harm (including pregnancy) and psychological, mental, or emotional injury from a perceived or actual threat.
rules.quote: "Personal injury" means either of the following injuries: (i) Actual bodily harm, including pregnancy or death. (ii) Psychological, mental, or emotional injury resulting from a reasonably perceived or actual threat of injury or death.
rules.source_title: MCL 18.351 (definitions)

params.rule: Crimes in Michigan are covered regardless of residency or immigration status; a Social Security Number is not required.

rules.summary: You do not need to be a Michigan resident or a legal U.S. resident to apply for a crime that happened in Michigan.
rules.quote: No. You do not have to be a legal resident of the United States (or a resident of Michigan) in order to qualify for Crime Victim Compensation.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS FAQ, Do I need to be a U.S. citizen or have a Social Security Number in order to qualify?
rules.source_title: MDHHS Crime Victim Compensation: Frequently Asked Questions

params.rule: For a crime in another state, apply to that state's program.

rules.summary: If the crime happened in another state, the survivor generally applies to that state's program.
rules.quote: However, if the crime occurs in another state, then you must apply for that state’s Crime Victim Compensation program.
rules.pinpoint: MDHHS FAQ, What if the crime occurred on Tribal land or another state?
rules.source_title: MDHHS Crime Victim Compensation: Frequently Asked Questions

params.rule: Michigan residents injured in a state without a VOCA-eligible compensation program are covered by Michigan.

rules.summary: A Michigan resident hurt in a state that has no federally funded victim compensation program can apply to Michigan.
rules.quote: to a resident of this state or that poses a reasonably perceived or actual threat of injury or death to a resident of this state within a state that does not have a victim compensation program eligible for funding from the victims of crime act of 1984
rules.source_title: MCL 18.351 (definitions)
