params.enroll: To submit an application, you must first contact a victim advocate or application assistant. This application must be completed with the assistant of an Application Assistant or Victim Advocate. Completed application and notarized statement can be submitted by mail or email to the ACP (see the application for details).

rules.summary: Michigan's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Attorney General, gives victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, and human trafficking a designated substitute address to use instead of their real one on public records, plus free mail forwarding. Applicants must be planning to move and must apply with a certified application assistant or victim advocate.
rules.quote: The Program (ACP) was created to conceal the addresses of victims of stalking, domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, and of individuals at risk of being threatened or physically harmed from being located by their perpetrators through public records. ACP provides victims with a designated (substitute) address that can be used instead of their real address.
rules.source_title: Michigan Department of Attorney General: ACP Applicants

rules.summary: The record of a proceeding before the Crime Victim Services Commission is a public record. But a claimant's file and testimony before the commission are exempt from disclosure under Michigan's Freedom of Information Act.
rules.quote: The record of a proceeding before the commission is a public record, except that a claimant's file and his or her testimony before the commission is exempt from disclosure under the freedom of information act
rules.source_title: MCL 18.363 (record of proceeding; claimant's file exempt from FOIA; confidentiality)

rules.summary: A provider may bill the survivor's insurer for a sexual assault exam only if the survivor authorizes it, and may ask for that authorization only after the exam.
rules.quote: The hospital or other licensed health care provider performing the examination may seek insurance reimbursement from the victim's insurer only if authorized by the victim. This authorization may only be sought after the examination is performed.
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 609.35 (costs of medical examination)

rules.summary: When asking for that consent, the provider must tell the survivor that the state is required to pay and that the survivor owes nothing and does not have to authorize insurance billing.
rules.quote: the state is required by law to pay for the examination and that the victim is in no way liable for these costs or obligated to authorize the reimbursement
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 609.35 (costs of medical examination)

params.payer: State of Minnesota; providers submit exam costs to the Department of Public Safety Office of Justice Programs
params.condition: if the crime was in Minnesota

rules.summary: The state pays for the exam of a victim of criminal sexual conduct that occurred in Minnesota, including STI tests and treatment and emergency contraception. Providers send the costs to the Office of Justice Programs.
rules.quote: for the examination of a victim of criminal sexual conduct that occurred in the state shall be paid by the state. These costs include, but are not limited to, the cost of the medical forensic examination, associated tests and treatments relating to sexually transmitted infection, and pregnancy status, including emergency contraception. A hospital, emergency medical facility, or health care provider shall submit the costs for examination and any associated tests and treatment to the Office of Justice Programs for payment.
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 609.35 (costs of medical examination)

params.payer: State of Minnesota

rules.summary: State payment for the exam does not depend on reporting to police or on any investigation or prosecution.
rules.quote: The applicability of this section does not depend upon whether the victim reports the offense to law enforcement or the existence or status of any investigation or prosecution.
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 609.35 (costs of medical examination)

rules.summary: Reimbursement to all claimants for one victim's injury or death may not exceed $50,000.
rules.quote: reimbursement paid to all claimants suffering economic loss as the result of the injury or death of any one victim shall not exceed $50,000.
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.54 (amount of reimbursement)

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list a $7,500 limit for counseling with a licensed provider. The board sets this amount itself, so it can change.
rules.quote: Counseling with licensed provider$7,500
rules.source_title: Financial Assistance for Crime Victims (CVRB training slides, 10/4/2025)

rules.summary: Psychological and psychiatric care needed for the victim's recovery counts as economic loss, up to an amount the board sets.
rules.quote: reasonable expenses incurred for psychological or psychiatric products, services, or accommodations, not to exceed an amount to be set by the board
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.52 (definitions)

rules.summary: Lost income is usually paid for up to 26 weeks, with a possible extension of up to 26 more weeks if a physician documents continuing disability.
rules.quote: Compensation for loss of income usually may not exceed 26 weeks. If the victim's disability continues past 26 weeks, the victim may request an extension for up to 26 additional weeks.
rules.source_title: Minn. R. 3050.3200 (loss of income)

rules.summary: The board does not pay for more than 40 missed hours per week.
rules.quote: The board may not compensate for hours missed in excess of 40 hours per week.
rules.source_title: Minn. R. 3050.3200 (loss of income)

rules.summary: Moving expenses, storage fees, and phone and utility installation fees are covered up to $1,000 per claim when the move is needed because of a reasonable fear of danger related to the crime.
rules.quote: the claimant's moving expenses, storage fees, and phone and utility installation fees, up to a maximum of $1,000 per claim, if the move is necessary due to a reasonable fear of danger related to the crime for which the claim was filed
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.52 (definitions)

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list crime scene cleanup with a $10,000 limit.
rules.quote: scene clean up - $10,000
rules.source_title: Financial Assistance for Crime Victims (CVRB training slides, 10/4/2025)

rules.summary: Child care from a provider exempt from licensing is paid at no more than $3 an hour per child for daytime care or $4 an hour per child for evening care. Licensed facilities are paid up to their standard rate.
rules.quote: Licensed facilities must be paid at a rate not to exceed their standard rate of payment. Facilities exempted from licensing requirements must be paid at a rate not to exceed $3 an hour per child for daytime child care or $4 an hour per child for evening child care
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.52 (definitions)

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list a $1,500 limit for alternative healing methods such as cultural or religious healing services. The board sets this amount itself, so it can change.
rules.quote: Alternative Healing Methods - $1,500
rules.source_title: Financial Assistance for Crime Victims (CVRB training slides, 10/4/2025)

rules.summary: Necessary medical, hospital, dental, and related expenses, including ambulance and drugs, count as economic loss.
rules.quote: reasonable expenses incurred for necessary medical, chiropractic, hospital, rehabilitative, and dental products, services, or accommodations, including ambulance services, drugs, appliances, and prosthetic devices
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.52 (definitions)

rules.summary: Counseling by a licensed provider is covered for victims and their family members.
rules.quote: Counseling expenses by a licensed provider for victims and their family members
rules.source_title: Financial Help for Victims of Violent Crime (brochure, 9/24)

rules.summary: Income the victim would have earned had they not been injured counts as economic loss.
rules.quote: loss of income that the victim would have earned had the victim not been injured
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.52 (definitions)

params.scope: mileage to medical and counseling appointments for the injury from the crime

rules.summary: Mileage to crime-related medical and counseling appointments is reimbursed at the federal mileage rate.
rules.quote: The reparations program reimburses mileage to medical and counseling appointments that are related to the injury from the crime. Miles are calculated from your home address to the clinic/hospital address and are paid at the current federal mileage rate.
rules.source_title: Mileage Reimbursement Request form

rules.summary: Substitute child care or household services the victim would have provided count as economic loss.
rules.quote: reasonable expenses incurred for substitute child care or household services to replace those the victim or claimant would have performed had the victim or the claimant's child not been injured
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.52 (definitions)

params.item: stolen money, property loss, and pain and suffering

rules.summary: Pain and suffering, stolen money, and property loss are not covered.
rules.quote: Pain and suffering, stolen money and property loss are not covered.
rules.source_title: Financial Help for Victims of Violent Crime (brochure, 9/24)

rules.summary: Damaged or stolen property is not covered.
rules.quote: Expenses for damaged/stolen property are not covered.
rules.source_title: Minnesota Crime Victims Reimbursement Application Form (Rev. 5/24)

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list security systems as not covered.
rules.quote: Non-Covered Expenses Pain and suffering  Property Loss /stolen money Security systems
rules.source_title: Financial Assistance for Crime Victims (CVRB training slides, 10/4/2025)

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list clothing and bedding taken as evidence as not covered.
rules.quote: Non-Covered Expenses Pain and suffering  Property Loss /stolen money Security systems  Clothing /Bedding taken as evidence
rules.source_title: Financial Assistance for Crime Victims (CVRB training slides, 10/4/2025)

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list attorney's fees as not covered.
rules.quote: Non-Covered Expenses Pain and suffering  Property Loss /stolen money Security systems  Clothing /Bedding taken as evidence Attorney's fees
rules.source_title: Financial Assistance for Crime Victims (CVRB training slides, 10/4/2025)

params.item: moving expenses

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list moving expenses as not covered. Ask the program before you count on moving costs.
rules.quote: Non-Covered Expenses Pain and suffering  Property Loss /stolen money Security systems  Clothing /Bedding taken as evidence Attorney’s fees Tuition losses Expenses related to court proceedings  Replacement of offender’s income  Moving expenses
rules.source_title: Financial Assistance for Crime Victims (CVRB training slides, 10/4/2025)

rules.summary: The board does not reimburse lost tuition, scholarship, or student loan funds, or income lost from delayed schooling.
rules.quote: The board must not reimburse a claimant for loss of tuition, scholarship, or student loan funds or loss of income due to a delay in completion of schooling related to the crime.
rules.source_title: Minn. R. 3050.3200 (loss of income)

params.item: lost wages already covered by sick leave, vacation, compensatory time, or holiday pay

rules.summary: Wages already covered by the claimant's paid leave are not paid.
rules.quote: The board must not pay for lost wages covered by a claimant's accumulated sick leave, vacation leave, compensatory time, or holiday pay.
rules.source_title: Minn. R. 3050.3200 (loss of income)

params.extension: or later in some cases

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within three years of the victim's injury. If the claimant was unable to file in that time, the claim can be made within three years of when a claim could have been filed. If the injury could not reasonably be discovered within three years, the claim can be made within three years of when it could be.
rules.quote: no claim was filed with the board within three years of victim's injury or death; except that (i) if the claimant was unable to file a claim within that period, then the claim can be made within three years of the time when a claim could have been filed; and (ii) if the victim's injury or death was not reasonably discoverable within three years of the injury or death, then the claim can be made within three years of the time when the injury or death is reasonably discoverable.
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.53 (eligibility and limitations on awards)

rules.summary: These do not count as being unable to file: not knowing about the program, or police not giving you information or help. Being a minor does not count either, and neither does having a parent or guardian handle your affairs.
rules.quote: The following circumstances do not render a claimant unable to file a claim for the purposes of this clause: (A) lack of knowledge of the existence of the Minnesota Crime Victims Reimbursement Act, (B) the failure of a law enforcement agency to provide information or assistance to a potential claimant under section 611A.66 , (C) the incompetency of the claimant if the claimant's affairs were being managed during that period by a guardian, guardian ad litem, conservator, authorized agent, or parent, or (D) the fact that the claimant is not of the age of majority
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.53 (eligibility and limitations on awards)

rules.summary: For victims of child abuse, the police report time limit and the minimum claim amount do not apply, and the three-year filing period starts when the crime is reported to police.
rules.quote: The limitations contained in clauses (1) and (6) do not apply to victims of child abuse. In those cases the three-year limitation period commences running with the report of the crime to the police.
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.53 (eligibility and limitations on awards)

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to police within 30 days. If it could not reasonably be reported in that time, it must be reported within 30 days of when it could be. A victim of criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, third, or fourth degree who reports after 30 days is treated as having been unable to report within that time.
rules.quote: the crime was not reported to the police within 30 days of its occurrence or, if it could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within 30 days of the time when a report could reasonably have been made. A victim of criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, third, or fourth degree who does not report the crime within 30 days of its occurrence is deemed to have been unable to have reported it within that period
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.53 (eligibility and limitations on awards)

rules.summary: The program says there is no time limit to report for sexual assault victims, but the crime must still be reported to police.
rules.quote: Crime must have been reported to police within 30 days (no time limit for sexual assault and child abuse victims, but crime must be reported)
rules.source_title: Financial Help for Victims of Violent Crime (brochure, 9/24)

rules.summary: The victim must cooperate fully with police. Cooperation can be shown by police or prosecutor records, or by a signed document from a victim service, counseling, or medical professional involved in the case. This shows cooperation; it does not replace the police report.
rules.quote: Cooperation is determined through law enforcement reports, prosecutor records, or corroboration memorialized in a signed document submitted by a victim service, counseling, or medical professional involved in the case
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.53 (eligibility and limitations on awards)

rules.summary: No award is made if the claim is less than $50; this limit does not apply to child abuse victims.
rules.quote: or (6) the claim is less than $50. The limitations contained in clauses (1) and (6) do not apply to victims of child abuse.
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.53 (eligibility and limitations on awards)

rules.summary: Reimbursement is reduced by what collateral sources such as insurance pay, and the claimant must try those sources first.
rules.quote: reimbursement shall be reduced to the extent that economic loss is recouped from a collateral source or collateral sources. Where compensation is readily available to a claimant from a collateral source, the claimant must take reasonable steps to recoup from the collateral source before claiming reimbursement
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.54 (amount of reimbursement)

rules.summary: Life insurance and voluntary donations or gifts are not counted as collateral sources.
rules.quote: The term does not include a life insurance contract or benefits from any private source provided as a voluntary donation or gift.
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.52 (definitions)

rules.summary: The board may deny or reduce an award for contributory misconduct of the victim.

params.enroll: If you are eligible, you can enroll in the Safe at Home Program with the help of an Application Assistant.

rules.summary: Safe at Home, run by the Minnesota Secretary of State, gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, and others who fear for their safety a PO Box address and forwards their mail to their real address, so the home address stays confidential.
rules.quote: Safe at Home is a statewide address confidentiality program administered by the Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State. It is designed to help survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, or others who fear for their safety maintain a confidential address.
rules.pinpoint: Secretary of State, Safe at Home page, program description
rules.source_title: Minnesota Secretary of State: Safe at Home

rules.summary: While a claim is open, the claim and its supporting documents and reports are investigative data. After the claim is paid, denied, withdrawn, or abandoned, they are private data on individuals. The board may still send claim forms, supporting documents, and reports to local law enforcement to carry out section 611A.67.
rules.quote: Claims for reimbursement and supporting documents and reports are investigative data and subject to the provisions of section 13.39 until the claim is paid, denied, withdrawn, or abandoned. Following the payment, denial, withdrawal, or abandonment of a claim, the claim and supporting documents and reports are private data on individuals as defined in section 13.02, subdivision 12 ; provided that the board may forward any reimbursement claim forms, supporting documents, and reports to local law enforcement authorities for purposes of implementing section 611A.67
rules.source_title: Minn. Stat. 611A.57 (determination of claims)

rules.summary: The state SAFE program pays first for the sexual assault forensic exam and no forensic fees may be billed to the patient. The program says health insurance may be billed as a secondary payer. SAFE does not cover medical treatment.
rules.quote: While SAFE is the "payor of first resort" for these fees, health insurance carriers may be billed secondary. NO forensic fees may be billed to the patient. However, the SAFE program does not cover any medical treatment that may be required due to the sexual assault.
rules.pinpoint: Missouri DPS CVC page, Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Program (SAFE) section
rules.source_title: Missouri DPS, Crime Victims' Compensation and SAFE program page

params.payer: Missouri Department of Public Safety (SAFE Program), paid to the medical provider

rules.summary: By statute, provider charges for eligible forensic exams are billed to and paid by the Department of Public Safety, and the provider may not charge the victim for the forensic exam.
rules.quote: All appropriate medical provider charges for eligible forensic examinations shall be billed to and paid by the department of public safety. No appropriate medical provider conducting forensic examinations and providing medical treatment to victims of sexual offenses shall charge the victim for the forensic examination.
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.220 (forensic examinations)

params.payer: Missouri Department of Public Safety SAFE Program, for sexual crimes in Missouri
params.condition: if the crime was in Missouri

rules.summary: The SAFE program pays for collecting and keeping evidence during the forensic exam. It is for victims of sexual crimes that happened in Missouri.
rules.quote: The Sexual Assault Forensic Examination (SAFE) Program covers the cost of gathering, collecting and preserving evidence during the forensic examination for victims of sexual crimes that occurred in Missouri.
rules.pinpoint: Missouri DPS CVC page, Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Program (SAFE) section
rules.source_title: Missouri DPS, Crime Victims' Compensation and SAFE program page

rules.summary: Medical treatment after a sexual offense is not part of the free forensic exam; an eligible victim seeks payment for it through Crime Victims' Compensation.
rules.quote: For appropriate medical provider charges related to the medical treatment of victims of sexual offenses, if the victim is an eligible claimant under the crime victims' compensation fund, the victim shall seek compensation under sections 595.010 to 595.075
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.220 (forensic examinations)

rules.summary: No award may exceed $25,000.
rules.quote: no award pursuant to sections 595.010 to 595.075 shall exceed twenty-five thousand dollars
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.030 (when paid, maximum award)

rules.summary: Lost earnings are paid at the actual loss, up to $400 per week, inside the overall award cap.
rules.quote: Any compensation for loss of earnings or support from gainful employment shall be in an amount equal to the actual loss sustained not to exceed four hundred dollars per week
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.030 (when paid, maximum award)

rules.summary: Lost wages can be covered only if the victim was gainfully employed at the time of the crime.
rules.quote: If the victim was gainfully employed at the time of the crime, they may also be eligible for lost wages.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Fact Sheet (10/2021), p. 2, Crime Victim Compensation Program Overview
rules.source_title: Missouri DPS, CVC Program fact sheet (10/2021)

rules.summary: If the victim dies, burial and preparation expenses are capped at $5,000.
rules.quote: In the event of death of the victim, an award may be made for reasonable and necessary expenses actually incurred for preparation and burial not to exceed five thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.030 (when paid, maximum award)

rules.summary: Counseling is paid only when the provider is a licensed physician, psychologist, clinical social worker, professional counselor, or board-certified psychiatric-mental health nurse specialist or nurse practitioner. No dollar cap for counseling was found.
rules.quote: No compensation shall be paid for psychiatric treatment or other counseling services, including psychotherapy, unless the service provider is a:
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.030 (when paid, maximum award)

rules.summary: Crime-related medical, dental, and counseling costs may be covered if eligibility requirements are met.
rules.quote: If the eligibility requirements are met, potential benefits may include costs associated with the patient's crime-related medical, dental, and counseling.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Fact Sheet (10/2021), p. 2, Crime Victim Compensation Program Overview
rules.source_title: Missouri DPS, CVC Program fact sheet (10/2021)

rules.quote: Medical expenses, including prescriptions

params.extension: or within 2 years of when the crime was discovered

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within two years after the crime or after the crime was discovered.
rules.quote: A claim shall be filed not later than two years after the occurrence of the crime or the discovery of the crime upon which it is based.
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.025 (filing, time limit)

rules.summary: For a sexual offense, reporting the crime to the proper authorities can include several things. One is the medical provider sending the forensic exam report to the county prosecutor. Others are getting a forensic exam or getting an order of protection.
rules.quote: In the case of a sexual offense, filing a report of the offense to the proper authorities may include, but not be limited to, the filing of the report of the forensic examination by the appropriate medical provider, as defined in section 595.220 , with the prosecuting attorney of the county in which the alleged incident occurred, receiving a forensic examination, or securing an order of protection.
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.030 (when paid, maximum award)

rules.summary: In place of other records, the applicant may give a sworn statement under RSMo 589.663 that they have good reason to believe they are a victim of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault, human trafficking, or stalking and fear further violent acts from the assailant.
rules.quote: In lieu of other records the claimant may provide a sworn statement by the applicant under paragraph (c) of subdivision (2) of section 589.663 that the applicant has good reason to believe that he or she is a victim of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault, human trafficking, or stalking, and fears further violent acts from his or her assailant.
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.030 (when paid, maximum award)

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: To be eligible, you must cooperate with law enforcement in catching the offender, unless the department finds you had good cause not to.
rules.quote: The claimant, victim or dependent shall cooperate with law enforcement officials in the apprehension of the offender in order to be eligible, or the department has found that the failure to cooperate was for good cause.
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.015 (claims, application, cooperation)

rules.summary: An award is reduced by payments, benefits, or awards received or to be received because of the injury or death. Life insurance proceeds do not count.
rules.quote: any compensation paid pursuant to sections 595.010 to 595.075 shall be reduced by the amount of any payments, benefits or awards received or to be received as a result of the injury or death
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.035 (reductions, payor of last resort, contributory conduct)

rules.summary: If you have health insurance but still owe deductibles or co-payments, those out-of-pocket costs may be reimbursed.
rules.quote: However, if a claimant has a health insurance but still has out-of-pocket expenses because of deductibles or co-payments, those out-of-pocket costs may be eligible for reimbursement.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Program Guidelines, Costs Eligible for Reimbursement from the Fund
rules.source_title: Missouri DPS, Crime Victims' Compensation Program Guidelines

rules.summary: The department must consider whether the victim's consent, provocation, incitement or negligence contributed to the injury, and may reduce or deny the award on that basis.
rules.quote: the department of public safety shall determine whether, because of the victim's consent, provocation, incitement or negligence, the victim contributed to the infliction of the victim's injury or death, and shall reduce the amount of the compensation or deny the claim altogether, in accordance with such determination
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.035 (reductions, payor of last resort, contributory conduct)

rules.summary: Sexual assault victims are eligible, and a relative who needs counseling to help the victim recover can also be eligible.
rules.quote: In the case of a sexual assault victim, a relative of the victim requiring counseling in order to better assist the victim in his recovery
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.020 (eligibility)

params.rule: Crime must have occurred in Missouri; the brochure says victims of crimes in other states apply in that state, but the statute adds a narrow exception for Missouri residents (see the next residency rule).

rules.summary: The crime must have happened in Missouri. The brochure says that if it happened in another state, the application goes to that state's program; the statute makes a narrow exception for Missouri residents.
rules.quote: Crime Must Have Occurred In Missouri If the crime occurred in another state, application must be made in that state
rules.source_title: Missouri DPS, CVC brochure (Rev. 1/2024)

params.rule: A Missouri resident injured in another U.S. state or territory may apply in Missouri only if the conditions in RSMo 595.020.5 are met.

rules.summary: A Missouri resident injured by a crime in another state or U.S. territory may apply in Missouri, but only under the conditions the statute lists (such as the other place lacking a program that would cover them).
rules.quote: A Missouri resident who suffers personal injury or, in the case of death, a dependent of the victim or any member of the family who legally assumes the obligation, or who pays the medical or burial expenses incurred as a direct result thereof, in another state, possession or territory of the United States may make application for compensation in Missouri if
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.020 (eligibility)

params.rule: For CVC, a crime is an act committed in Missouri (plus terrorism abroad against a Missouri resident).

rules.summary: By statute, a covered crime is an act committed in Missouri involving force or violence or the threat of it, whether or not it is ever prosecuted.
rules.quote: an act committed in this state which, regardless of whether it is adjudicated, involves the application of force or violence or the threat of force or violence by the offender upon the victim
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.010 (definitions)

rules.quote:
Mailing Address: P.O. Box1589
Jefferson City, MO 65102-1589

params.enroll: An adult person, a parent or guardian acting on behalf of a minor, or a guardian acting on behalf of an incapacitated person may apply to the secretary to have a designated address assigned by the secretary to serve as the person's address or the address of the minor or incapacitated person; (2)  The secretary may approve an application if it is filed with the office of the secretary in the manner established by rule and on a form prescribed by the secretary.  A completed application shall contain: (a)  The date the application was prepared, the applicant's signature, and the signature and registration number of the application assistant who assisted the applicant in applying to be a program participant; (RSMo 589.663(1)-(2)(a). An application assistant is a trained, registered employee or volunteer of a government agency or nonprofit program serving victims of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault, human trafficking, stalking, or other crimes, RSMo 589.660(2).)

rules.summary: The Missouri Secretary of State runs an Address Confidentiality Program that gives victims of rape, sexual assault, and other listed crimes who fear for their safety a designated substitute address in place of their real address. Applicants apply to the Secretary with the help of a registered application assistant.
rules.quote: There is created in the office of the secretary of state a program to be known as the "Address Confidentiality Program" to protect victims of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault, human trafficking, stalking, or other crimes who fear for their safety, as well as the safety of individuals residing in the same household as the victim, by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims, their minor children, and individuals residing with them.
rules.source_title: RSMo 589.663 (Address Confidentiality Program created, application procedures)

rules.summary: CVC claim information and hearings are open to the public by default in Missouri. A claim for rape, sodomy, or sexual abuse is closed and confidential only when DPS decides that is in the best interest of the victim or dependents; claims involving a minor, or where the assailant has not been tried and disclosure would hurt the case, are also closed, and DPS may close any record in the interest of justice.
rules.quote: A claim in which the offense allegedly perpetrated against the victim is rape, sodomy or sexual abuse and it is determined by the department to be in the best interest of the victim or of the victim's dependents that the information be kept confidential or that the public be excluded from the hearing;
rules.source_title: RSMo 595.037 (CVC open records, exceptions, closed and confidential claims)

rules.summary: The bill for a sexual assault forensic exam goes to the state, and the survivor may not be billed or held responsible for it.
rules.quote: No bill for the examination will be submitted to the victim, nor shall the medical facility hold the victim responsible for payment.
rules.source_title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-37-25 (2025): Payment of costs of medical forensic examination and sexual assault evidence collection kit

rules.summary: The state's exam payment rules say the survivor's private insurance should not be billed for the forensic exam.
rules.quote: The victim’s private insurance should not be billed for the cost of the sexual assault medical forensic examination.
rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

params.payer: Division of Victim Compensation, Office of the Attorney General, paid directly to the health care provider

rules.summary: The Attorney General's Division of Victim Compensation pays for the forensic exam directly to the provider.
rules.quote: The Division of Victim Compensation shall pay for the medical examination conducted for the procurement of evidence to aid in the investigation and prosecution of the alleged offense.
rules.source_title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-37-25 (2025): Payment of costs of medical forensic examination and sexual assault evidence collection kit

params.payer: the victim may be billed for further medical services the investigation does not need

rules.summary: You may still be billed for other medical care that the investigation and prosecution do not need. If the assault caused harm that needs more care, you will be told about victim compensation and how to apply.
rules.quote: The victim may be billed for any further medical services not required for the investigation and prosecution of the alleged offense. In cases where the damage caused by the alleged sexual assault requires medical treatment or diagnosis in addition to the examination, the patient will be given information about the availability of victim compensation and the procedure for applying for such compensation.
rules.source_title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-37-25 (2025): Payment of costs of medical forensic examination and sexual assault evidence collection kit

params.payer: Office of the Attorney General, Victim Compensation Division; payment is payment in full

rules.summary: What the Attorney General pays the provider for the exam counts as payment in full.
rules.quote: Payment made to the provider by the Office of the Attorney General, Victim Compensation Division for the sexual assault medical forensic examination shall be considered by the provider as payment in full.

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $1,000.

rules.summary: Tuition loss is capped at $2,000.

rules.quote: Medical – reasonable charges incurred for reasonably needed and medically necessary products, services and accommodations

rules.quote: dental care and services may be eligible if treatment is directly related to the crime injury.

rules.quote: Mental Health Services – reasonable charges incurred for reasonably needed mental health counseling and care for the victim/claimant and the victim’s/claimant’s family members.
rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

rules.quote: Travel to a medical or mental health counseling facility is at least forty-five (45) miles, one way from the victim’s/claimant’s residence.

rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

rules.quote: Repair and/or Replacement Costs – reasonable costs for victim/claimant to repair and/or replace exterior broken windows, doors, locks or other security devices of a residential dwelling
rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

rules.summary: Cleaning the scene after a homicide or assault is covered.
rules.quote: Crime Scene Cleanup – reasonable and necessary cost of cleaning the crime scene after a homicide or assault.
rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

rules.summary: Damaged or stolen property is not reimbursed. Medical items such as eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures or prosthetics destroyed in the crime are handled separately as a medical expense.
rules.quote: Ineligible expenses include, but are not limited to, damaged or stolen property, pain and suffering, expenses not directly related to the crime injuries, attorney’s fees
rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

params.item: attorney's fees

rules.summary: Attorney's fees are not reimbursed.
rules.quote: Ineligible expenses include, but are not limited to, damaged or stolen property, pain and suffering, expenses not directly related to the crime injuries, attorney’s fees
rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

rules.summary: Pain and suffering is not compensated.
rules.quote: Ineligible expenses include, but are not limited to, damaged or stolen property, pain and suffering, expenses not directly related to the crime injuries, attorney’s fees
rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

params.extension: or up to 12 months later if the director extends it for good cause

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 36 months after the crime. For good cause the director may allow up to 12 more months.
rules.quote: Unless the claim has been filed with the director within thirty-six (36) months after the crime occurred, or in cases of child sexual abuse, within thirty-six (36) months after the crime was reported to law enforcement or the Department of Child Protection Services, but in no event later than the victim’s twenty-fifth birthday. For good cause, the director may extend the time period allowed for filing a claim for an additional period not to exceed twelve (12) months
rules.source_title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-41-17 (2025): Compensation awards; conditions; exceptions; reduction

params.applies_to: child sexual abuse
params.extension: No later than the victim's twenty-fifth birthday; the director may extend by up to 12 months for good cause.

rules.summary: For child sexual abuse, the claim must be filed within 36 months after the crime was reported to law enforcement or Child Protection Services, but no later than the victim's twenty-fifth birthday.
rules.quote: Unless the claim has been filed with the director within thirty-six (36) months after the crime occurred, or in cases of child sexual abuse, within thirty-six (36) months after the crime was reported to law enforcement or the Department of Child Protection Services, but in no event later than the victim’s twenty-fifth birthday. For good cause, the director may extend the time period allowed for filing a claim for an additional period not to exceed twelve (12) months
rules.source_title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-41-17 (2025): Compensation awards; conditions; exceptions; reduction

params.exception: or later if the program finds good cause for the delay

rules.summary: For compensation, the crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, unless there was good cause for not reporting in that time.
rules.quote: Unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence or unless it is found that there was good cause for the failure to report within such time
rules.source_title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-41-17 (2025): Compensation awards; conditions; exceptions; reduction

rules.summary: Good cause for a late report can include the victim's psychological state or compelling health or safety reasons.
rules.quote: The psychological state and any compelling health or safety reasons that would jeopardize the well-being of the victim/claimant.
rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

rules.summary: A police report is not needed for the state to pay for the forensic exam itself. This does not remove the reporting rule for a compensation claim.
rules.quote: It is not a requirement for the sexual assault to be reported to law enforcement for a medical provider to receive reimbursement for the cost of the sexual assault forensic exam.
rules.pinpoint: AG Sexual Assault Examination Payment Policy, Sec. II, Note
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Examination Payment Policy, Victim Compensation Division (2024)

rules.summary: Compensation is reduced by anything recovered from other sources such as insurance.
rules.quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be diminished to the extent: (a) That the economic loss is recouped from other sources, including collateral sources
rules.source_title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-41-17 (2025): Compensation awards; conditions; exceptions; reduction

rules.summary: The program is the payer of last resort: insurance, Medicaid, Medicare and Workers' Compensation must pay first.
rules.quote: All other sources of payment such as insurance, Medicaid, Medicare and Workers' Compensation must pay first.
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application (rev. 12.9.2025)

rules.summary: An award is reduced by the degree the victim is found responsible for the injury.
rules.quote: Of the degree of responsibility for the cause of injury or death attributable to the victim or claimant.
rules.source_title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-41-17 (2025): Compensation awards; conditions; exceptions; reduction

rules.summary: An award may be denied, withdrawn or reduced if the victim has not fully cooperated with law enforcement and prosecutors.
rules.quote: Upon a finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies and prosecuting attorneys, an award of compensation may be denied, withdrawn or reduced.
rules.source_title: Miss. Code Ann. 99-41-17 (2025): Compensation awards; conditions; exceptions; reduction

rules.summary: In sexual assault cases the program may consider the circumstances when judging cooperation, and may waive the cooperation requirement for compelling health or safety reasons.
rules.quote: Consideration of relevant circumstances may be given in cases of domestic violence, sexual assault and human trafficking. The Division may waive this requirement if there is compelling health or safety reasons that would jeopardize the well being of the victim/claimant.
rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

rules.summary: An advance award of up to $500 may be made when an award is probable and the claimant would face financial hardship without it.
rules.quote: determines that the claim is one with respect to which an award probably will be made; and b. the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless an advance award is made. 2. The advance award may not exceed Five Hundred Dollars ($500.00).
rules.source_title: Miss. Admin. Code Title 3, Part 1: Division of Victim Compensation rules

rules.summary: Sexual assault is listed as a covered crime.

rules.summary: The application lists sexual assault and child sexual abuse among covered crimes.
rules.quote: assault, burglary, child physical abuse, child sexual abuse, child pornography, domestic violence, DUI crashes, other vehicular crimes, homicide, human trafficking, kidnapping, robbery, sexual assault, stalking, and terrorism.

params.rule: Crimes committed in Mississippi qualify regardless of the victim's residence. A Mississippi resident hurt in another state or country qualifies only if that place has no compensation program for the injury.

params.enroll: Complete the Address Confidentiality Program application form(s); and submit the completed application form(s) to the Office of the Attorney General, Victim Compensation Division.

Applicants send the program application to the Attorney General's Victim Compensation Division; the assault does not have to have happened in Mississippi.
rules.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program helps victims keep their location confidential by providing them with a substitute address and a mail forwarding service for use when interacting with state and local agencies.

rules.quote: The records, papers, files and communications of the division, director, staff and agents must be regarded as confidential information and privileged and not subject to disclosure under any condition including the Mississippi Public Records Act of 1983.

rules.summary: Montana law lists it as a survivor's right not to be billed for the sexual assault forensic exam or the evidence kit collection. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.
rules.quote: a victim may not be billed for the cost of administering the sexual assault medical forensic examination or collecting evidence for the sexual assault evidence kit
rules.source_title: MCA 46-15-406, Notice of rights for victims of sexual assault

params.applies_to: exams paid by the state exam fund for cases not reported to police

rules.summary: When the state exam fund (FREPP) pays for an exam, the provider must accept its rate as payment in full for covered services. The provider cannot bill the survivor for the rest or sue the survivor to collect it. Treatment of any physical injuries from the assault may still be billed to the survivor.
rules.quote: A healthcare provider must accept FREPP’s reimbursement rate as payment in full for covered services and may not submit any remaining balance to the survivor or commence civil actions against the survivor to recover the balance. Treatment of any physical injuries that may have occurred at the time of the sexual assault may still be billed to the survivor.
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ: Forensic Rape Examination Payment Program (FREPP)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "exams paid by the state exam fund for cases not reported to police"

params.payer: local law enforcement agency where the offense occurred

rules.quote: The local law enforcement agency within whose jurisdiction an alleged incident of sexual intercourse without consent, sexual assault, or incest occurs shall pay for the sexual assault medical forensic examination of a victim of the alleged offense when the examination is directed by the agency or when evidence obtained by the examination is used for the investigation, prosecution, or resolution of an offense.
rules.source_title: MCA 46-15-411, Payment for medical evidence -- alleged sexual offenses

params.payer: Montana Department of Justice (Forensic Rape Examination Payment Program), subject to available funds

rules.summary: If the local police agency does not have to pay, the Montana Department of Justice pays for the exam, as long as money set aside for it is available.
rules.quote: The department of justice shall, as long as funds are available from an appropriation made for this purpose, pay for the sexual assault medical forensic examination of a victim of an alleged incident of sexual intercourse without consent, sexual assault, or incest if the cost is not the responsibility of a local law enforcement agency under subsection (1).
rules.source_title: MCA 46-15-411, Payment for medical evidence -- alleged sexual offenses

params.payer: FREPP, Montana Department of Justice

params.payer: FREPP, Montana Department of Justice

params.payer: FREPP, Montana Department of Justice

rules.summary: Crime Victim Compensation can pay up to $25,000 in benefits.

rules.quote: No, the CVC program cannot pay for stolen, damaged, or destroyed property.  CVC may pay for items such as eyeglasses, hearing aids, crutches, braces, and prosthetic devices.

rules.quote: Non-medical expenses, like clothing, motels , travel expenses, or legal fees

params.item: pain and suffering, inconvenience, physical impairment, nonbodily damage

rules.summary: No payment for pain and suffering, inconvenience, physical impairment, or nonbodily damage.
rules.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering, inconvenience, physical impairment, or nonbodily damage.
rules.source_title: MCA 53-9-128, Compensation benefits

params.item: missed work due to mental impairment

rules.summary: Lost wages are paid only for physical injury; missed work due to mental impairment is not covered.
rules.quote: CVC does not cover missed work due to mental impairment.
rules.pinpoint: Montana DOJ, Crime Victim Compensation page, Wage Loss
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ Office of Victim Services: Crime Victim Compensation

params.item: in-patient psychiatric care or chemical dependency counseling

rules.summary: In-patient psychiatric care and chemical dependency counseling are listed as ineligible.
rules.quote: In-patient psychiatric care or chemical dependency counseling
rules.pinpoint: Montana DOJ, Crime Victim Compensation page, Ineligible Benefits
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ Office of Victim Services: Crime Victim Compensation

rules.summary: File within 1 year of the crime.
rules.quote: compensation may not be awarded unless the claim is filed with the office within 1 year after the day the criminally injurious conduct occurred causing the injury or death upon which the claim is based.
rules.source_title: MCA 53-9-125, Limitations on awards

params.extension: Applies to sexual offenses against minors; the later of 1 year after the report or 1 year after age 18. Good cause extensions also apply.

rules.summary: For sexual offenses against minors, the deadline is 1 year after the report to police or child welfare, or 1 year after the victim turns 18, whichever is later.
rules.quote: Compensation in cases involving sexual offenses against minors may not be awarded unless the claim is filed with the office within 1 year after the day the criminally injurious conduct was reported to a law enforcement agency or an agency of the state responsible for provision of child welfare services, or within 1 year after the day the victim reaches 18 years of age, whichever occurs last.
rules.source_title: MCA 53-9-125, Limitations on awards

rules.summary: The office can give more time to file a claim for good cause.
rules.quote: The time for filing a claim may be extended by the office for good cause shown.
rules.source_title: MCA 53-9-125, Limitations on awards

rules.summary: A state rule says there is no good cause for more time if the claim is filed more than 2 years after the last day it could have been filed.
rules.quote: There is no good cause to extend the time limit if the claim is filed more than two years after the latest date the claim could have been filed in accordance with 53-9-125 , MCA.
rules.source_title: ARM 23.15.103, Good cause extensions to claim filing and reporting limits (via Cornell LII)

params.exception: or later if the office finds good cause or it was a sexual offense against a minor

rules.summary: A report to a law enforcement officer is required for any award. It must be made within 72 hours, unless the office finds good cause for the delay. The 72-hour limit does not apply to a sexual offense against a minor.
rules.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer. The report must be made within 72 hours after its occurrence, except in a case involving a sexual offense against a minor or when the office finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
rules.source_title: MCA 53-9-125, Limitations on awards

params.scope: what counts as good cause for a late report or claim

rules.summary: A state rule lists what can count as good cause for a late report or a late claim. It includes the victim's age when the crime happened and physical or mental incapacity. It also includes a delay that was reasonable given the crime and the injuries, or police or prosecutors not telling the victim about the program.
rules.quote: Factors considered when determining whether "good cause" exists for extending the one-year time limit for filing a claim, or for extending the 72 hour deadline to report criminally injurious conduct to law enforcement after its occurrence include, but are not limited to the following: (a) age of the victim when the crime occurred; (b) whether the delay in filing or reporting was reasonable, considering the circumstances of the crime and the resulting injuries to the victim; (c) physical or mental incapacity; or, (d) failure of law enforcement or prosecutors to notify the victim about the crime victim compensation.
rules.source_title: ARM 23.15.103, Good cause extensions to claim filing and reporting limits (via Cornell LII)

rules.summary: The program pays after insurance and other sources; payments are reduced by what those sources pay or could pay.
rules.quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant must be reduced or denied to the extent the compensation benefits payable are or can be recouped from collateral sources.
rules.source_title: MCA 53-9-125, Limitations on awards

rules.summary: The program is the payer of last resort, but it can pay deductibles and co-pays.
rules.quote: CVC is a payor of last resort. If you are covered by any kind of private or government benefit program, you must submit your expenses to that collateral source before you submit them to the CVC program. CVC benefits can be paid for your out-of-pocket expenses, including any required deductible or co-payment.
rules.pinpoint: Montana DOJ, Crime Victim Compensation page, Insurance and Collateral Sources
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ Office of Victim Services: Crime Victim Compensation

rules.summary: An award may be reduced or denied in proportion to the victim's contribution to the injury.
rules.quote: Compensation may be denied or reduced if the victim contributed to the infliction of death or injury with respect to which the claim is made. Any reduction in benefits under this subsection must be in proportion to what the office finds to be the victim's contribution to the infliction of death or injury.
rules.source_title: MCA 53-9-125, Limitations on awards

rules.summary: An award may be denied or reduced if the claimant or victim does not fully cooperate with police and prosecutors.
rules.quote: The office, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies or prosecuting attorneys, may deny or reconsider and reduce an award of compensation.
rules.source_title: MCA 53-9-125, Limitations on awards

rules.summary: A tentative award can be paid early when the claimant faces financial hardship and a final award looks likely. No set amount.
rules.quote: If the office determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant, to be deducted from the final award or repaid by and recoverable from the claimant to the extent that it exceeds the final award.
rules.source_title: MCA 53-9-126, Tentative award of compensation

rules.summary: Adult sexual assault is a listed crime type on the claim form.
rules.quote: [ ] Adult Sexual Assault
rules.pinpoint: Claim Form, Section C, Type of Crime
rules.source_title: Montana Crime Victim Compensation Claim Form (12-25)

params.rule: Crimes in Montana regardless of residency; Montana residents injured where the local program does not compensate non-residents

rules.summary: Anyone hurt by a crime in Montana can apply, including non-residents. Montana residents hurt elsewhere can apply only if that state or country's program does not cover non-residents.
rules.quote: Benefits may be awarded to: Non-residents injured in Montana. Montana residents injured in a state or country in which the victim compensation program does not compensate non-residents.
rules.pinpoint: Montana DOJ, Request a Claim Form page
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ: Request a Claim Form

params.target: Crime Victim Compensation Program P.O. Box 201410 Helena, MT 59620-1410

rules.summary: Mail the signed and dated claim form to the Crime Victim Compensation Program, P.O. Box 201410, Helena, MT 59620-1410.
rules.quote: Crime Victim Compensation Program P.O. Box 201410 Helena, MT 59620-1410 Please note: Be sure your claim form is signed and dated before you mail to the CVC program.
rules.pinpoint: Request a Claim Form, How to Request a Claim Form
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ: Request a Claim Form

rules.summary: Send copies of medical bills with the claim form.
rules.quote: Yes, please send copies of the bills with your claim form.
rules.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, Should I send in copies of medical bills along with the application?
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ: CVC Frequently Asked Questions

params.note: insurance explanation of benefits, if applicable

rules.summary: If insurance processed the bills, include a copy of the explanation of benefits.
rules.quote: If applicable, submit a copy of your insurance explanation of benefits.
rules.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, Should I send in copies of medical bills along with the application?
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ: CVC Frequently Asked Questions

params.note: only for wage loss claims

rules.summary: Wage loss claims need extra paperwork and verification.
rules.quote: Additional paperwork and verification are required to approve wage loss.
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ Office of Victim Services: Crime Victim Compensation

params.note: the claim form itself, signed and dated by the claimant

rules.summary: The claimant must sign and date the claim form or it will not be considered.
rules.quote: Claimant must sign and date here before the claim will be considered for benefits.
rules.pinpoint: Claim Form, Section G signature block
rules.source_title: Montana Crime Victim Compensation Claim Form (12-25)

rules.summary: The program aims to decide eligibility within 60 days; it can take longer if requested information is slow to arrive.
rules.quote: The goal of the CVC program is to determine eligibility on a claim within 60 days.
rules.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, How long will it take to receive a decision on compensation benefits?
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ: CVC Frequently Asked Questions

params.agency: Montana Department of Justice, Office of Victim Services
params.enroll: Download and complete the Address Confidentiality Program Application. Applicants must submit supporting documents with the application. Mail, email, or fax the application and supporting documentation to: Office of Victim Services ACP, P.O. Box 201410, Helena, MT 59620-1410; Fax: (406) 444-5335. An online application is also offered. For assistance in completing the ACP application, please contact a Crime Victim Advocate or contact the Office of Victim Services ACP Program.

rules.summary: Montana's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the DOJ Office of Victim Services, gives Montana residents who are victims of sexual assault, partner or family member assault, stalking, or human trafficking a substitute address and free confidential first-class mail forwarding. Survivors apply online or by mailing, emailing, or faxing the application with supporting documents, and a crime victim advocate can help.
rules.quote: Be a victim of partner or family member assault, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, or eligible to apply for an order of protection.
rules.pinpoint: Address Confidentiality Program page, eligibility list
rules.source_title: Montana DOJ Office of Victim Services: Address Confidentiality Program

rules.summary: The compensation office's records are generally open to public inspection, but personal, medical, or similar information is exempt from disclosure when releasing it would be an unreasonable invasion of privacy, and confidential criminal justice information stays protected under the Montana Criminal Justice Information Act.
rules.quote: the following public records of the office are exempt from disclosure: (a)	information of a personal nature, such as personal, medical, or similar information, if the public disclosure of the information would constitute an unreasonable invasion of privacy
rules.source_title: MCA 53-9-107: Public inspection and disclosure of office's records

rules.summary: A provider that performs a sexual assault forensic exam may not bill the survivor, the survivor's insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, or any other collateral source for it.
rules.quote: A medical facility or medical professional that performs a forensic medical examination shall not bill the victim, the victim's personal insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, or any other collateral source for the examination and other eligible expenses.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 143B-1200 (Assistance Program for Victims of Rape and Sex Offenses)

params.payer: Assistance Program for Victims of Rape and Sex Offenses (Rape Victim Assistance Program), NC Department of Public Safety

rules.summary: The state's Assistance Program for Victims of Rape and Sex Offenses (the Rape Victim Assistance Program at NC DPS) pays for forensic exams after a sexual assault or attempted sexual assault in North Carolina.
rules.quote: Whenever a forensic medical examination is conducted as a result of a sexual assault or an attempted sexual assault that occurred in this State, the Program shall pay for the cost of the examination.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 143B-1200 (Assistance Program for Victims of Rape and Sex Offenses)

params.payer: Rape Victim Assistance Program; the provider must accept its payment as payment in full

rules.summary: The provider must accept the program's payment as payment in full for the exam, so no balance can be passed to the survivor.
rules.quote: A medical facility or medical professional that performs a forensic medical examination shall accept payment made under this section as payment in full of the amount owed for the cost of the examination and other eligible expenses.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 143B-1200 (Assistance Program for Victims of Rape and Sex Offenses)

rules.summary: Total compensation for one victim's injury is capped at $45,000, not counting allowable funeral, cremation, and burial expenses.
rules.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to, or the death of, that victim may not exceed forty-five thousand dollars ($45,000) in the aggregate in addition to allowable funeral, cremation, and burial expenses.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

rules.summary: Lost wages are paid at no more than $400 per week for up to 26 weeks from the date of the injury.
rules.quote: Compensation for work loss will be limited to 26 weeks commencing from the date of the injury, and compensation shall not exceed four hundred dollars ($400.00) per week.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-2 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Lost wages are covered when the survivor was employed at the time of the crime and a physician certifies the survivor was unable to work.
rules.quote: A claim for work loss will be paid only upon proof that the injured person was gainfully employed at the time of the criminally injurious conduct and, by physician's certificate, that the injured person was unable to work.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-2 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Funeral, cremation, and burial expenses are covered up to $10,000.
rules.quote: Allowable expense includes a total charge not in excess of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) for expenses related to funeral, cremation, and burial, including transportation of a body, but excluding expenses for flowers, gravestone, and other items not directly related to the funeral service.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-2 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Allowable funeral, cremation, and burial expenses are paid on top of the total limit.
rules.quote: in addition to allowable funeral, cremation, and burial expenses.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

rules.summary: Medical care is a covered expense, paid at a set share (66 2/3%) of the provider's usual charge.
rules.quote: Allowable expense for medical care, counseling, rehabilitation, medically-related property, and other remedial treatment and care of a victim shall be limited to sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66 2/3%) of the amount usually charged by the provider for the treatment or care.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-2 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Counseling for the victim is a covered expense, paid at a set share (66 2/3%) of the provider's usual charge.
rules.quote: Allowable expense for medical care, counseling, rehabilitation, medically-related property, and other remedial treatment and care of a victim shall be limited to sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66 2/3%) of the amount usually charged by the provider for the treatment or care.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-2 (Definitions)

rules.summary: A provider that accepts the program's payment for treatment or care must treat it as payment in full and cannot bill the claimant for the rest.
rules.quote: By accepting the compensation paid as allowable expense pursuant to this subdivision, the provider agrees that the compensation is payment in full for the treatment or care and shall not charge or otherwise hold a claimant financially responsible for the cost of services in addition to the amount of allowable expense.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-2 (Definitions)

rules.summary: The program lists medical, counseling, dental or orthodontic, funeral, crime scene cleanup, and lost wages as accepted expenses.
rules.quote: Accepted Expenses ✓ Medical ✓ Counseling ✓ Dental or orthodontic ✓ Burial and funeral expenses ✓ Crime scene cleanup ✓ Lost wages
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, Accepted Expenses
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is an accepted expense when billed by a certified biohazard cleanup company; it may include repairing or replacing doors, locks, and windows as well as cleaning blood stains.
rules.quote: Crime scene cleanup Submit the itemized bill from a certified biohazard cleanup company. Services may include repair or replacement of doors, locks and windows, as well as cleanup of blood stains.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, FAQ: What paperwork do I need to submit? (Crime scene cleanup)
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.item: property damage or loss, lost or stolen money, replacement of property taken as evidence

rules.summary: Property damage or loss, lost or stolen money, and replacing property taken as evidence (for example a phone or clothing) are not accepted.
rules.quote: Not Accepted X Property damage or loss X Lost or stolen money X Replacement of property taken as evidence
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, Not Accepted
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.item: travel

rules.summary: Travel is listed as not accepted.
rules.quote: X Travel
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, Not Accepted
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.item: utilities, mortgage or rent

rules.summary: Utilities and mortgage or rent are not accepted.
rules.quote: X Utilities X Mortgage or rent
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, Not Accepted
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.item: pain and suffering (noneconomic detriment)

rules.summary: The program pays only economic loss, not pain and suffering or other noneconomic harm.
rules.quote: Compensation shall only be paid for economic loss and not for noneconomic detriment.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-4 (Award of compensation)

params.item: court fees and expenses

rules.summary: Court fees and expenses are not accepted.
rules.quote: X Court fees and expenses
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, Not Accepted
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.item: costs incurred more than one year after the crime

rules.summary: Costs that come more than one year after the crime are not paid. If the victim was 18 or younger when hurt, the limit is two years, but a minor's new medical or counseling costs from the crime can still be paid after that.
rules.quote: The economic loss is incurred after one year from the date of the criminally injurious conduct that caused the injury or death for which the victim seeks the award, except in the case where the victim for whom compensation is sought was 18 years old or younger at the time the injury occurred. In that case an award of compensation will be denied if the economic loss is incurred after two years from the date of the criminally injurious conduct that caused the injury or death for which the victim seeks the award, unless the minor victim has new medical or counseling expenses directly attributable to the crime.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

rules.summary: Replacement services loss (paying someone for ordinary household services the injured person would have done) is limited to $200 per week for up to 26 weeks from the date of the injury.
rules.quote: Replacement service loss will be limited to a 26-week period commencing from the date of the injury, and compensation may not exceed two hundred dollars ($200.00) per week.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-2 (Definitions)

rules.summary: An application must be filed within two years after the date of the crime.
rules.quote: The claimant fails to file an application for an award within two years after the date of the criminally injurious conduct that caused the injury or death for which the claimant seeks the award.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

rules.summary: The program's page says the two-year limit can be longer if the crime was an unreported sexual assault of a child.
rules.quote: In most cases, you are eligible for compensation if you apply no more than two years after the day the crime occurred. There are two exceptions that would extend this time period: the unreported sexual assault of a minor child.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, Am I eligible?
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.exception: or later with good cause

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within six months unless there was good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: The criminally injurious conduct was not reported to a law enforcement officer or agency within six months of its occurrence, and there was no good cause for the delay.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

rules.summary: An award is reduced by anything insurance or another collateral source pays or will pay for the same loss.
rules.quote: An award that has been approved shall nevertheless be denied or reduced to the extent that the economic loss upon which the claim is based is or will be recouped from a collateral source.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

rules.summary: The program pays last, after private or public insurance; deductibles and co-pays may be reimbursed.
rules.quote: Like other compensation programs, North Carolina is a payer of last resort, meaning victims should first submit expenses to private or public insurance companies. Deductibles and co-pays may be reimbursed.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, FAQ: Do I need to file a claim with my insurance?
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

rules.summary: A claim may be denied or reduced for the victim's contributory misconduct, with an exception for trafficking victims who were coerced or deceived.
rules.quote: The claimant or a victim through whom the claimant claims engaged in contributory misconduct, unless the claimant or victim through whom the claimant claims is a victim as defined by G.S. 14-43.10(a) and was coerced or deceived into participating in the contributory misconduct as a direct result of the person's status as a victim.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

rules.summary: A claim can be denied or an award cut if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with police or the prosecution, unless there was good cause. A claim already decided can also be looked at again for this.
rules.quote: A claim may be denied, an award of compensation may be reduced, and a claim that has already been decided may be reconsidered upon finding that the claimant or victim, without good cause, has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies or in the prosecution of criminal cases with regard to the criminally injurious conduct that is the basis for the award.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

rules.summary: Rape victims are eligible to apply.
rules.quote: Victims of rape, assault, domestic violence, drunk driving and pedestrian hit and run, as well as the families of homicide victims, are eligible to apply for financial help.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, FAQ: What financial support is available?
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.rule: Crimes in North Carolina; NC residents victimized in a state with no victim compensation program

rules.summary: The crime must have happened in North Carolina, except that a North Carolina resident hurt in a state with no compensation program may qualify.
rules.quote: Compensation shall only be awarded for criminally injurious conduct that occurs or is attempted in this State except that criminally injurious conduct that occurs or is attempted against a resident of this State while in another state which does not have a victims compensation program of any type may be a basis of compensation.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-4 (Award of compensation)

params.rule: Non-residents eligible for crimes in North Carolina

rules.summary: Survivors do not need to be North Carolina residents if the crime happened in North Carolina.
rules.quote: Victims do not need to be residents of North Carolina.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, FAQ: Am I eligible?
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.target: Office of Victim Compensation Services 4232 Mail Service Center Raleigh, NC 27699-4232

rules.summary: A paper application can be mailed to the Office of Victim Compensation Services, 4232 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-4232.
rules.quote: If you prefer to apply by mail, you may download and print a paper form . Mail your application to: Office of Victim Compensation Services 4232 Mail Service Center Raleigh, NC 27699-4232
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, How to Apply
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

rules.summary: Survivors can start an application online through ncdps.gov/4victims, which leads to the program's online portal.
rules.quote: To learn more about the program and start an application, visit ncdps.gov/4victims.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Rape Victim Assistance Program FAQ, 'Is financial help available for medical expenses beyond the cost of the forensic exam?'
rules.source_title: NC DPS Rape Victim Assistance Program page and FAQ

params.note: the application, completed, signed, and dated

rules.summary: The application must be completed, signed, and dated.
rules.quote: Complete, sign, and date the application.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'How can applicants avoid delays?'
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.note: law enforcement report or warrant that lists the victim's name

rules.summary: Include a copy of the law enforcement report or warrant that names the victim.
rules.quote: Include a copy of the law enforcement report or warrant that lists the victim’s name.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'How can applicants avoid delays?'
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.note: from medical or counseling providers

rules.summary: Medical and counseling expenses need itemized bills from the providers.
rules.quote: Submit itemized bills from certified providers of medical or counseling services.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Medical and counseling services)
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.note: proof of any payments by the victim, third parties, or insurance

rules.summary: Include proof of any payments already made toward the itemized bills, by the victim, third parties, or insurance.
rules.quote: Provide proof of payment made towards any of the itemized bills by the victim, third parties, or insurance companies.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'How can applicants avoid delays?'
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.note: employed: physician's letter with dates out of work, employer letter confirming the absence, last paystub before the crime

rules.summary: For lost wages, an employed survivor sends a physician's letter on letterhead, an employer letter confirming the absence, and the last paystub before the crime.
rules.quote: If you have an employer, you should submit a signed physician’s letter on the provider’s letterhead that details the dates and reasons you were advised to be out of work, an official employer letter on company letterhead that confirms your approved absence and your last paystub before the incident.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Lost wages)
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.note: self-employed or independent contractor: physician's letter plus signed federal tax return from the year before the crime
