rules.summary: For lost wages, a self-employed survivor sends a physician's letter on letterhead and a signed federal tax return from the year before the crime.
rules.quote: If you are self-employed or are an independent contractor, you’ll need a signed physician’s letter on the provider’s letterhead and a copy of your signed federal tax return from the year before the crime.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Lost wages)
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.note: dental claims: proposed treatment plan on the dentist's letterhead (optional)

rules.summary: For dental care, a survivor may send a proposed treatment plan on the dentist's letterhead.
rules.quote: You may submit a proposed treatment plan on your dentist’s letterhead.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Dental services)
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.note: funeral claims: death certificate, itemized funeral bill, law enforcement report

rules.summary: Funeral claims need a copy of the death certificate, the itemized funeral bill, and the law enforcement report.
rules.quote: Submit a copy of the death certificate, itemized funeral bill and the law enforcement report.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Funeral expenses)
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

rules.summary: The program says the average processing time is three to six months from when it receives the application.
rules.quote: From the time an application is received, the average processing time is between three to six months.
rules.pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What happens after I submit my application?'
rules.source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.agency: North Carolina Office of the Attorney General
params.enroll: File an application with the Attorney General with the assistance of an application assistant.

rules.summary: North Carolina's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Attorney General, gives relocated victims of domestic violence, sexual offense, or stalking a substitute address so assailants cannot find them through public records.
rules.quote: A program in the Office of the Attorney General to protect the confidentiality of the address of a relocated victim of domestic violence, sexual offense, or stalking to prevent the victim's assailants or potential assailants from finding the victim through public records.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15C-2 (Address Confidentiality Program definitions)

params.agency: North Carolina Office of the Attorney General
params.enroll: An individual who wants to participate in the Address Confidentiality Program shall file an application with the Attorney General with the assistance of an application assistant.

rules.summary: To enroll, the survivor files an application with the Attorney General with help from a designated application assistant (an advocate at a victim services agency or nonprofit).
rules.quote: An individual who wants to participate in the Address Confidentiality Program shall file an application with the Attorney General with the assistance of an application assistant.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15C-4 (Filing and certification of applications; authorization card)

rules.summary: Victims' and claimants' personal information and all information about how claims were decided (except the total amount awarded) are held confidential by the Commission and Director; medical and law enforcement records are also confidential.
rules.quote: All personal information, as that term is defined in 18 U.S.C. § 2725(3), of victims and claimants and all information concerning the disposition of claims for compensation, except for the total amount awarded a victim or claimant, shall be held confidential by the Commission and Director.
rules.source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-8.1 (Privilege and records of the Commission)

params.condition: if done within 120 hours of the assault

rules.summary: When an acute forensic medical exam is done for alleged criminal sexual conduct or domestic violence (within 120 hours unless good cause is shown for the delay), neither the exam nor any preliminary medical screening may be charged to the survivor, directly or through insurance or another third-party payer.
rules.quote: performed within one hundred twenty hours after the alleged crime unless good cause is shown for the delay in performing the examination. When an acute forensic medical examination is performed, the costs incurred by a health care facility or health care professional for performing the acute forensic medical examination or any preliminary medical screening examination may not be charged, either directly or through a third-party payer, to the alleged victim.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 12.1-34 (incl. 12.1-34-07, forensic medical examination costs)

rules.summary: When a child's forensic exam is done, neither the exam nor any medical screening before it may be charged to the child or to a parent, guardian, or custodian. This includes billing through insurance or another third-party payer.
rules.quote: When a child forensic medical examination is performed, the costs incurred by a health care facility or health care professional for performing the child forensic medical examination or any preliminary medical screening examination may not be charged, either directly or through a third-party payer, to the alleged child victim or the child's parent, guardian, or custodian.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 12.1-34 (incl. 12.1-34-07, forensic medical examination costs)

params.payer: North Dakota Attorney General, from the state general fund, reimburses the health care facility or professional

rules.summary: The Attorney General reimburses the hospital or provider for the reasonable cost of the medical screening and acute forensic exam, within the limits of legislative appropriations.
rules.quote: Upon submission of appropriate documentation, the attorney general, within the limits of legislative appropriations, shall reimburse from the general fund the health care facility or a health care professional for the reasonable costs incurred in performing the medical screening and acute forensic medical examination.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 12.1-34 (incl. 12.1-34-07, forensic medical examination costs)

rules.summary: The total award for one victim and all claimants together may not exceed $25,000.
rules.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of that victim may not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars in the aggregate.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: For adult victims, mental health counseling is limited to 30 sessions and $3,600 total.
rules.quote: For adult victims, no more than thirty sessions, and total compensation may not exceed three thousand six hundred dollars.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: For minor victims, mental health counseling is limited to 40 sessions and $4,800 total.
rules.quote: For minor victims, no more than forty sessions, and total compensation may not exceed four thousand eight hundred dollars.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: If the provider shows a need, up to 10 more counseling sessions and up to $1,200 more may be allowed.
rules.quote: If a provider substantiates the need for additional sessions, the division may allow up to ten additional sessions and up to one thousand two hundred dollars total compensation for the additional sessions.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: Counseling is paid for no longer than 2 years from the first session.
rules.quote: No longer than a two-year period beginning on the date of the first session
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: Work loss (and replacement services and dependent's losses) is paid at no more than $300 per week.
rules.quote: Compensation for work loss, replacement services loss, dependent's economic loss, and dependent's replacement services loss may not exceed three hundred dollars per week.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Work loss is capped at $300 per week and $4,800 in total.
rules.quote: Payment for work loss may not exceed more than three hundred dollars per week up to a maximum of four thousand eight hundred dollars.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: Reimbursement for crime-related lodging, meals, and mileage is capped at $1,000.
rules.quote: The maximum reimbursement for lodging, meals, and mileage is one thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: Travel is paid only when the trip is at least 150 miles round trip from home.
rules.quote: Travel distance must be at least one hundred fifty miles round trip from the claimant's residence in order for the claimant to be eligible for reimbursement of travel expenses.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: New prescription medications are covered up to $1,000.
rules.quote: The division may not pay more than one thousand dollars for new prescription medications.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: Dental services are covered up to $5,000.
rules.quote: The division may not pay more than five thousand dollars for dental services.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: Funeral, cremation, and burial expenses are covered up to $5,000.
rules.quote: The term includes a total charge not in excess of five thousand dollars for expenses in any way related to funeral, cremation, and burial.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Replacement services loss (paying someone for household services the victim can no longer do) is capped at $1,000.
rules.quote: The division may not pay more than one thousand dollars for replacement services loss.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: Reasonable charges for needed medical care, rehabilitation, and other remedial treatment caused by the injury are allowable expenses.
rules.quote: "Allowable expense" means reasonable charges incurred for reasonably needed products, services, and accommodations required due to the injury, including those for medical care, rehabilitation, rehabilitative occupational training, and other remedial treatment and care.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Mental health assessment, diagnosis, and treatment, including individual or group counseling, is covered.
rules.quote: Assessment, diagnosis, and treatment, including individual or group counseling sessions.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: Work loss (income the victim would have earned if not injured) is a compensable economic loss.
rules.quote: "Work loss" means loss of income from work the victim would have performed if the victim had not been injured
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: The program may reimburse meals, lodging, and travel directly related to the crime.
rules.quote: The division may reimburse a claimant for meals, lodging, and travel expenses for travel directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: Medical and dental expenses from the incident may be covered.
rules.quote: Medical/Dental benefits for the Victim – If the victim has medical or dental expenses from the incident, they may be eligible for medical/dental benefits.
rules.source_title: ND DOCR CVC Application Tips (PDF)

rules.summary: The program's application guide lists dependent care benefits when the victim was the primary caregiver.
rules.quote: Dependent Care – If the victim was the primary caregiver, the family may be eligible for dependent care benefits.
rules.source_title: ND DOCR CVC Application Tips (PDF)

params.item: property loss or damage

rules.summary: Claims for property loss or damage are not covered.
rules.quote: Claims for property loss or damage.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.item: noneconomic detriment (pain, suffering, inconvenience)

rules.summary: Noneconomic harm such as pain, suffering, and inconvenience is not a compensable loss by itself.
rules.quote: Noneconomic detriment is not loss.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params.item: interest, finance, or collection fees

rules.summary: The program does not pay interest, finance charges, or collection fees on bills.
rules.quote: The division may not pay compensation for interest, finance, or collection fees.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: Attorney's fees for help filing a claim are not paid.
rules.quote: Attorney's fees are not allowable for assisting a claimant in filing a claim.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params.item: travel for the victim to meet with law enforcement or to go to court

rules.summary: The program does not pay travel costs for the victim to meet with law enforcement, or for the victim or a homicide victim's immediate family to go to court.
rules.quote: The division may not pay reimbursement for travel expenses for the victim or immediate family of a homicide victim to attend court proceedings or for the victim to meet with law enforcement.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.extension: or later if the division finds the interests of justice require it

rules.summary: File within one year from the date the crime was reported to law enforcement; the program may extend this when the interests of justice require.
rules.quote: A claim for compensation must be filed within one year from the date the criminally injurious conduct was reported to a law enforcement officer. The division may extend the time for filing if it determines that the interests of justice so require.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params.exception: or later if the program finds good cause for the delay

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 96 hours, unless the program finds good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within ninety-six hours after its occurrence or the division finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params.scope: what counts as good cause for a late report

rules.summary: Good cause for a late report includes evidence, such as medical records or verifiable third-party reports, that reporting on time would have put the applicant's health or safety at risk.
rules.quote: Evidence, including medical records or verifiable reports from third parties, which substantiate the applicant's health or safety would have been jeopardized if the criminally injurious conduct had been reported in a timely manner.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.scope: what counts as good cause for a late report

rules.summary: Good cause for a late report also includes law enforcement confirming that the victim feared retaliation.
rules.quote: Law enforcement substantiates there was a fear of retaliation.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.exception: or, for abuse of a child, within 3 years after the child becomes an adult

rules.summary: For child abuse or sexual molestation of a child, the report to law enforcement must be made within three years after the child reaches the age of majority.
rules.quote: In the case of child abuse or sexual molestation of a child, the criminally injurious conduct must be reported to a law enforcement officer within three years after the child reaches the age of majority.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Awards are reduced or denied to the extent the loss is recouped from other sources, including insurance and other collateral sources.
rules.quote: To the extent the economic loss upon which the claim is based is recouped from other persons, including collateral sources;
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: The fund pays only for losses not paid by other sources such as health insurance, Medicaid, employer-paid leave, and online fundraising.
rules.quote: The crime victims compensation fund is a secondary source for payment for economic losses not paid by other collateral sources, including disability benefits; employer-paid leave, including sick leave or annual leave; health insurance, including medical, vision, and dental benefits; life insurance; Medicare; medical assistance or Medicaid; motor vehicle insurance; personal and charity fundraising, including online fundraising;
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: An award may be reduced or denied to the extent the program deems reasonable because of the victim's contributory misconduct.
rules.quote: To the extent the division deems reasonable because of the contributory misconduct of the claimant or of a victim on whose behalf compensation is claimed;
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: An award may be reduced or denied if the program finds the victim's intoxication was a factor causing the crime.
rules.quote: To the extent the division deems reasonable when it is determined that a victim was under the influence of an alcoholic beverage or a controlled substance at the time the criminally injurious conduct occurred and the victim's intoxication was a factor causing the criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: The program may deny, reconsider, or reduce an award if the claimant has not fully cooperated with law enforcement.
rules.quote: The division, upon finding that the claimant has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies, may deny, reconsider, or reduce an award of compensation.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: The admin rule requires denial when the claimant's conduct contributed substantially to the incident; the listed conduct includes intoxication that was a factor in the crime. Human trafficking victims are excluded from this rule.
rules.quote: The division shall deny compensation if the claimant's conduct contributed substantially to the incident.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

rules.summary: A tentative award may be paid if the claimant would otherwise suffer financial hardship and a final award appears likely; it is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: If the division determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made, and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant which must be deducted from the final award
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: Victims who suffered physical or emotional injuries from a violent crime can qualify. The sources do not list crimes by name; bodily injury is defined to include pregnancy and nervous shock.
rules.quote: The victim suffered physical or emotional injuries as a result of a violent crime, drunk driving, or hit and run.
rules.pinpoint: DOCR CVC page, What is Eligibility Criteria?
rules.source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

rules.summary: Bodily injury means harm that requires medical treatment and results in economic loss; it includes pregnancy and nervous shock.
rules.quote: "Bodily injury" means any harm that requires medical treatment and results in economic loss and includes pregnancy and nervous shock.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params.rule: Covers crimes in North Dakota. A North Dakota resident hurt outside the state has the same rights if the place where the crime happened has no compensation law covering the injury.

rules.summary: Crimes in North Dakota are covered. A North Dakota resident hurt by a crime somewhere else has the same rights as for a North Dakota crime if they show that place has no crime victims compensation law covering the injury.
rules.quote: If a resident of this state is a victim of criminally injurious conduct, but the criminally injurious conduct occurred outside the geographical boundaries of this state, the resident has the same rights under this chapter as if the criminally injurious conduct occurred within this state upon a showing that the state, territory, country, or political subdivision of the country in which the criminally injurious conduct occurred does not have a crime victims compensation law which covers the bodily injury or death of the victim.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params.note: The program page links to the online application; the portal itself could not be saved as a snapshot. No official source states a mail, email, or fax filing method for the application.

rules.summary: Apply online through the ND DOCR Crime Victim's Compensation Application portal linked from the program page.
rules.quote: Clicking the link below will take you to the online application for Crime Victim
rules.pinpoint: Program page, Crime Victims Compensation Application and Forms
rules.source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

params.note: The program page says to allow 2 to 4 weeks for an application or a reimbursement request.

rules.summary: Allow 2 to 4 weeks for the program to process an application or a reimbursement request.
rules.quote: Please allow 2-4 weeks for processing CVC application or claim reimbursement requests.
rules.source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

params.note: Completed application signed by the claimant or the claimant's parent, guardian, or legal representative, on the division's form.

rules.summary: Submit a completed application on the program's form, signed by the claimant or a parent, guardian, or legal representative; an employer, provider, or insurer cannot apply for you.
rules.quote: A claimant for benefits shall submit a completed application for compensation signed by the claimant or the claimant's parent, guardian, or legal representative on an application form prescribed by the division.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.note: Written explanation of the late report, only if the crime was not reported to law enforcement within the reporting window.

rules.summary: If the crime was not reported to law enforcement in time, explain the reason for the late report in the application.
rules.quote: There may be a justifiable reason for the late report. Please explain.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Application Tips, Section 3 (Incident Information, continued)
rules.source_title: ND DOCR CVC Application Tips (PDF)

params.note: Billing statement with the medical provider's name, business address, telephone number, and treatment plan.

rules.summary: For medical costs, include a billing statement showing the provider's name, business address, phone number, and treatment plan.
rules.quote: A request for compensation for medical services must include a billing statement containing the medical provider's name, business address, telephone number, treatment plan, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.note: Billing statement with the dental provider's name, business address, telephone number, and treatment plan.

rules.summary: For dental costs, include a billing statement showing the dentist's name, business address, phone number, and treatment plan.
rules.quote: A request for compensation for dental services must include a billing statement containing the dental provider's name, business address, telephone number, treatment plan, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.note: Billing statement of itemized transactions from the mental health provider.

rules.summary: For counseling, the provider's billing statement must list itemized transactions with the provider's name, business address, and phone number.
rules.quote: A billing statement of itemized transactions containing the provider's name, business address, and telephone number.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025), Verification Requirements
rules.source_title: ND CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025)

params.note: Provider Verification Form portion of the CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy form, returned with the billing invoice.

rules.summary: For counseling, the provider returns the CVC Provider Verification Form with the billing invoice.
rules.quote: The Provider Verification Form portion is to be returned with the billing invoice for reimbursement of services to the CVC program.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025), introduction
rules.source_title: ND CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025)

params.note: Written documentation from a medical or mental health provider and from the claimant's employer.

rules.summary: For lost wages, include written documentation from a medical or mental health provider and from your employer.
rules.quote: A claim for reimbursement for work loss must include written documentation from a medical or mental health provider, the claimant's employer, and information the division may request that supports payment for work loss.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.note: Work Loss - Employer's Report (SFN 12437), completed by the employer at the time of the crime.

rules.summary: For lost wages, the employer you worked for at the time of the crime completes the CVC Employer's Report.
rules.quote: FORM MUST BE COMPLETED BY EMPLOYER YOU WERE WORKING FOR AT THE TIME OF THE CRIME INCIDENT.
rules.source_title: ND CVC Work Loss - Employer's Report (SFN 12437, Rev. 06-2018)

params.note: Copy of the federal income tax return for the prior year, only if self-employed.

rules.summary: For lost wages, if you are self-employed, include a copy of your federal income tax return for the prior year.
rules.quote: Self-employed victims shall provide a copy of federal income tax return for one year prior and other substantial verification of work loss or profits the division determines is necessary to support payment for work loss.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.note: Work Loss - Physician's Report (SFN 60497), completed by a medical provider who treated the crime injuries.

rules.summary: For lost wages, a medical provider who treated your crime injuries completes the CVC Physician's Report.
rules.quote: FORM MUST BE COMPLETED BY A MEDICAL PROVIDER WHO TREATED YOU FOR YOUR CRIME INJURIES.
rules.source_title: ND CVC Work Loss - Physician's Report (SFN 60497, Rev. 06-2018)

params.note: Receipts for travel and lodging.

rules.summary: For travel and lodging, include your receipts.
rules.quote: The claimant shall submit receipts for travel and lodging expenses to the division.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.note: Itemized receipts for funeral and burial expenses.

rules.summary: For funeral and burial costs, include itemized receipts.
rules.quote: The claimant shall submit itemized receipts for reimbursement under this section.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.note: Receipts for replacement services showing the billed amount and type of service.

rules.summary: For replacement services, include receipts showing the billed amount and the type of service.
rules.quote: A claim for reimbursement for replacement services loss must include receipts for the billed amount, type of service provided, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.note: Proof of the support the victim provided to dependents, such as tax forms, benefits records, a certified death certificate, guardianship papers, birth certificates, or child support or spousal orders. Only for a loss of support claim.

rules.summary: For loss of support, include proof of the support the victim gave dependents before the crime, such as tax forms, a certified death certificate, or birth certificates.
rules.quote: A claim for loss of support must include verification of the amount of support the victim provided to dependents prior to the criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.note: Documentation of what insurance or another collateral source paid, or that it did not cover the service.

rules.summary: Before the program pays, you or the provider must show what insurance or another collateral source paid, or that it did not cover the service.
rules.quote: Before payment is made from the division, either the provider or the claimant shall provide documentation that: a. Verifies the amount paid by the collateral source; or b. Verifies the applicant or service was not covered by the collateral source.
rules.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params.note: Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information (SFN 61353), if the program asks for it.

rules.summary: The program may ask you to sign its Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information form so it can get records it needs to decide the claim.
rules.quote: The DOCR may, however, require that you authorize disclosure of your health information if needed to make a determination about your claim.
rules.pinpoint: Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information, SFN 61353, Privacy Statement
rules.source_title: ND CVC Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information (SFN 61353)

rules.summary: Program records about a compensation application or award are confidential and not open to the public. The law lists who may still see them.
rules.quote: All other records of the division concerning the application for or award of compensation under this chapter are confidential and are not open to public disclosure.
rules.source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

rules.summary: A sexual assault forensic medical exam may not be sent to the survivor or the survivor's insurance for payment.
rules.quote: A report of a forensic medical examination shall not be remitted to the patient or his or her insurance for payment.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1429.03 (Sexual Assault Payment Program)

params.payer: Sexual Assault Payment Program Cash Fund or the Victim's Compensation Fund (state)

rules.summary: The full out-of-pocket cost that could be charged to a survivor for a sexual assault forensic medical exam is paid from the state's Sexual Assault Payment Program Cash Fund or the Victim's Compensation Fund.
rules.quote: The full out-of-pocket cost or expense that may be charged to a sexual assault victim in connection with a forensic medical examination shall be paid from the Sexual Assault Payment Program Cash Fund or the Victim's Compensation Fund.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1429.03 (Sexual Assault Payment Program)

rules.summary: With the survivor's permission, a health care provider can apply to the program directly for treatment or exam costs from a sexual assault that insurance, Medicaid, the Sexual Assault Payment Program, or another source will not pay.
rules.quote: a health care provider may, with the permission of the victim, apply for reimbursement for health care costs incurred by the provider that are otherwise to be paid for by a victim of sexual assault, domestic assault, or child abuse and for which the provider will not otherwise receive reimbursement from private insurance, the medical assistance program established pursuant to the Medical Assistance Act, the Sexual Assault Payment Program, or any other entity, source, or fund, whether public or private.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1807

rules.summary: The most the program will award is $25,000 per applicant per incident.
rules.quote: no compensation shall be awarded under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act from the Victim's Compensation Fund in an amount in excess of twenty-five thousand dollars for each applicant per incident.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1823

params.exception: or more in some cases

rules.summary: Except as section 81-1813 provides, the program cannot award more than $25,000 for each applicant per incident.
rules.quote: Except as provided in section 81-1813 , no compensation shall be awarded under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act from the Victim's Compensation Fund in an amount in excess of twenty-five thousand dollars for each applicant per incident.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1823

rules.summary: Counseling or therapy is capped at $5,000, per the program's current web page.
rules.quote: Counseling | Therapy (Maximum of $5,000)
rules.pinpoint: NCC Crime Victim Reparations page, Types of Expenses
rules.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $5,000, per the program's current web page.
rules.quote: Crime-scene clean-up (Maximum of $5,000)
rules.pinpoint: NCC Crime Victim Reparations page, Types of Expenses
rules.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

rules.summary: Funeral expenses are capped at $10,000, per the program's current web page.
rules.quote: Funeral expenses (Maximum of $10,000)
rules.pinpoint: NCC Crime Victim Reparations page, Types of Expenses
rules.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

rules.summary: Medical expenses are covered, including hospital, doctor, dental, prescriptions, and x-rays.
rules.quote: Medical expenses (hospital, doctor, dental, prescriptions, x-rays, etc.)
rules.pinpoint: NCC Crime Victim Reparations page, Types of Expenses
rules.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

rules.summary: Expenses reasonably incurred because of the injury are covered, including mental health counseling and care.
rules.quote: Expenses actually and reasonably incurred as a result of the personal injury or death of the victim, including expenses for mental health counseling and care
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1819

rules.summary: Lost wages and lost future earning capacity from the victim's total or partial incapacity are covered, plus reasonable job retraining.
rules.quote: Loss of wages and future earning capacity as a result of total or partial incapacity of the victim and reasonable expenses of job retraining or similar employment-oriented rehabilitative services for the victim
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1819

rules.summary: Dental and prescription costs are listed as covered medical expenses.
rules.quote: Medical expenses (hospital, doctor, dental, prescriptions, x-rays, etc.)
rules.pinpoint: NCC Crime Victim Reparations page, Types of Expenses
rules.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

rules.summary: Prescriptions are listed as covered medical expenses.
rules.quote: Medical expenses (hospital, doctor, dental, prescriptions, x-rays, etc.)
rules.pinpoint: NCC Crime Victim Reparations page, Types of Expenses
rules.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

params.item: property crime, property loss, and property damage

rules.summary: Lost or damaged property is not covered.
rules.quote: The program does not cover property crime, property loss, property damage or pain and suffering.
rules.pinpoint: NCC Crime Victim Reparations page, Limitations
rules.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: Pain and suffering is not paid.
rules.quote: The program does not cover property crime, property loss, property damage or pain and suffering.
rules.pinpoint: NCC Crime Victim Reparations page, Limitations
rules.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

rules.summary: Lost wages are considered only when the victim missed more than 7 consecutive days of work. This applies to wage claims only, not to other expenses.
rules.quote: Loss of Wage will only be considered if more than seven (7) consecutive days are missed from work.
rules.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

params.condition: if you were 19 or older when it happened

rules.summary: A victim who was 19 or older at the time of the injury must apply within 2 years of the injury.
rules.quote: For a victim who was nineteen years of age or older at the time of the personal injury or death, within two years after the date of the personal injury or death
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

rules.summary: If you were under 19 when it happened, you can apply on or before your twenty-second birthday.
rules.quote: For a victim who was under nineteen years of age at the time of the personal injury, on or before the victim's twenty-second birthday
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

rules.summary: The committee may still look at a late application if it finds good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: The committee may evaluate applications submitted beyond the deadline established in this section if the committee finds that good cause existed for missing such deadline.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

params.exception: or, if you could not reasonably report that soon, within 5 days of when you could

rules.summary: Generally the crime must be reported to police within 5 days, or within 5 days of when a report could reasonably be made.
rules.quote: The personal injury or death was the result of an incident or offense which had been reported to the police within five days of its occurrence or, if the incident or offense could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within five days of the time when a report could reasonably have been made.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

rules.summary: For sexual assault, the 5-day police report rule does not apply if, before applying, the crime was reported to police at any time, a protection order was obtained, or the victim had a forensic medical exam.
rules.quote: An application submitted by or for a victim of sexual assault, domestic assault, child abuse, or sex trafficking is not subject to the five-day reporting requirement in subsection (1) of this section if, prior to submitting the application the: (a) Applicant or victim has reported such crime to the police; (b) Applicant or victim has obtained a protection order related to such incident or offense; or (c) Victim has presented for a forensic medical exam.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: The program's FAQ says you must cooperate with criminal justice officials in the investigation and prosecution of the crime.
rules.quote: You must cooperate with criminal justice officials in the investigation of the crime and the prosecution of the offender.
rules.pinpoint: CVR Frequently Asked Questions (4-5-2023), What must I do to be eligible?
rules.source_title: CVR Frequently Asked Questions (updated 4-5-2023)

rules.summary: The program pays last: awards are reduced by insurance and other payments, except life insurance and social security.
rules.quote: Any award will be reduced by the amounts of any payments received or to be received from any contract of insurance or any other source of compensation except life insurance proceeds or social security payments.
rules.source_title: 80 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 3, 004 (Reduction of Award and Exceptions), via Cornell LII

rules.summary: The program is the payor of last resort.
rules.quote: The Crime Victim's Reparations program is the payor of last resort.
rules.source_title: 80 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 3, 004 (Reduction of Award and Exceptions), via Cornell LII

rules.summary: The hearing officer considers whether the victim's own behavior contributed to the injury.
rules.quote: the committee or hearing officer shall consider all circumstances determined to be relevant, including, but not limited to, provocation, consent, or any other behavior of the victim which directly or indirectly contributed to his or her injury or death.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1816

rules.summary: The program says contributory conduct is never used when screening sexual assault, domestic violence, or human trafficking claims.
rules.quote: contributory conduct is never used in screening claims involving domestic violence, sexual assault, or human trafficking.
rules.source_title: CVR: Innocence and Contributory Conduct

rules.summary: No award is made if the victim broke a state criminal law and that violation caused or contributed to the injury.
rules.quote: If the victim violated a criminal law of the state, which violation caused or contributed to his or her injuries or death
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1822

rules.summary: An emergency award of up to $500 is possible when compensation is probable and waiting would cause undue hardship; it is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: The amount of the emergency compensation shall not exceed five hundred dollars
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1820

rules.summary: Compensation covers personal injury from a criminal act committed or attempted in Nebraska by someone else, which includes sexual assault.
rules.quote: The commission or attempt on the part of one other than the applicant of an unlawful criminal act committed or attempted in the State of Nebraska.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1818

rules.summary: The statute names sexual assault victims directly, including a special police-report rule for them.
rules.quote: An application submitted by or for a victim of sexual assault, domestic assault, child abuse, or sex trafficking
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

params.rule: Crimes committed in Nebraska; residents and nonresidents are treated the same.

rules.summary: Residents and nonresidents who are victims of crimes in Nebraska are treated the same.
rules.quote: Residents and nonresidents of Nebraska who are victims of crimes committed in Nebraska shall be treated similarly in determining compensation awards under the act.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1807

params.target: Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program PO Box 94946 Lincoln, NE 68509-4946

rules.summary: Mail the completed, signed application and documentation to the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program, PO Box 94946, Lincoln, NE 68509-4946.
rules.quote: Return the completed/signed application and documentation to the below address: Nebraska Crime Victim’s Reparations Program PO Box 94946 Lincoln, NE 68509-4946
rules.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

rules.summary: Email the claim application and the supporting documentation requested to ncc.cvr@nebraska.gov.
rules.quote: Submit, along with supporting documentation requested, by email or mailing to: CVR Claim → ncc.cvr@nebraska.gov
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victim Reparations program page, Apply
rules.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

rules.summary: The application's return-to block also lists the program's fax number, 402.471.2837.
rules.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

rules.summary: Include itemized copies of all medical bills related to the incident.
rules.quote: Submit itemized copies of all medical bills relating to the incident.
rules.pinpoint: FAQ, What must I do to apply for compensation?
rules.source_title: CVR Frequently Asked Questions (updated 4-5-2023)

params.note: Copies of crime-related bills plus any paid receipts.

rules.summary: Attach copies of crime-related bills and any receipts for bills you already paid.
rules.quote: Attach copies of crime related bills and any paid receipts.
rules.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

params.note: Signed and dated Authorization to Release Information (page 5 of the application).

rules.summary: Sign and date the Authorization to Release Information; no action is taken on the claim until it is signed.
rules.quote: This authorization is an integral part of your application and must be signed and dated by the victim or claimant before any action will be taken on your claim.
rules.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Authorization to Release Information
rules.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

params.note: Signed United States Citizenship Attestation; a qualified alien also provides a copy of USCIS documentation.

rules.summary: Complete the citizenship attestation; if you attest as a qualified alien, you agree to provide a copy of your USCIS documentation.
rules.quote: I am a qualified alien under the federal Immigration and Nationality Act and I agree to provide a copy of my USCIS documentation.
rules.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), United States Citizenship Attestation
rules.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

params.note: Pay stubs or an earning statement for the missed pay periods.

rules.summary: For lost wages, include pay stubs or an earning statement for the pay periods of work missed because of the incident.
rules.quote: Copy of pay stubs or an earning statement for the pay period(s) for missed work as a result of the incident.
rules.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
rules.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

params.note: If self-employed: most recent federal tax returns with Schedule C, plus estimates, bids, or contracts.

rules.summary: For lost wages when self-employed, include your most recent federal tax returns with Schedule C and copies of estimates, bids, or contracts.
rules.quote: If Self-Employed: submit the most recent federal tax returns including the schedule C form, Copies of Estimates, Bids, and/or Contracts.
rules.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
rules.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

params.note: A doctor's release back to work.

rules.summary: For lost wages, include a doctor's release back to work.
rules.quote: A Doctor’s release back to work.
rules.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
rules.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

params.note: Copy of the death certificate, for funeral or burial expenses.

rules.summary: For funeral or burial expenses, a copy of the death certificate is needed.
rules.quote: Funeral or Burial Expenses (A copy of the death certificate will need to be provided.)
rules.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

rules.summary: By statute, a hearing officer rules on an application within 180 days after receiving all required information; the clock does not start until the file is complete.
rules.quote: A hearing officer shall consider and rule upon any application made under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act within one hundred eighty days after receipt of all required information related to the crime.
rules.pinpoint: Claims Process, quoting Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1809(1)
rules.source_title: CVR Claims Process

params.note: typically 6 to 9 months to be fully processed

rules.summary: The program says claims are typically fully processed within 6 to 9 months.
rules.quote: CVR program applications take time, typically claims are fully processed within 6-9 months.
rules.source_title: Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program pamphlet (English)

params.enroll: Application for ACP is made in person at one of the designated victim assistance centers located throughout the state. Applications will not be accepted at the Secretary of State’s Office.

rules.summary: Nebraska's Address Confidentiality Program is for victims of abuse, sexual assault or stalking who fear for their safety, among other conditions.
rules.quote: To be eligible for ACP, an individual must be (1) a victim of abuse, sexual assault or stalking who fears for his or her safety
rules.source_title: Nebraska Secretary of State: Address Confidentiality Program page

rules.summary: By statute, the name of a sexual assault victim in the reparations committee's records when applying for compensation may not be made public. The statute protects the name; it does not say the whole claim file is confidential.
rules.quote: The name of any victim of a sexual assault appearing in information or records of the Crime Victim's Reparations Committee when the victim is applying for compensation under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act shall not be made public.
rules.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1842 (sexual assault victim; records; confidential)

rules.summary: A physician or hospital that examines a survivor of an alleged sexual offense to gather evidence must provide the exam without charge to the survivor.
rules.quote: If a physician or a hospital provides any physical examination of a victim of an alleged sexual offense to gather information and evidence of the alleged crime, these services shall be provided without charge to the individual.
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-c, Victim of Alleged Sexual Offense

rules.summary: The bill for a sexual assault medical exam may not be sent or given to the survivor or the survivor's family.
rules.quote: The bill for the medical examination of a sexual assault victim shall not be sent or given to the victim or the family of the victim.
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-c, Victim of Alleged Sexual Offense

rules.summary: If a survivor with insurance chooses to bill it, the provider bills the insurer, and neither the survivor nor the department may be billed for anything above the coverage limit. A separate rule says that for survivors on Medicaid or Medicare whose kit is not anonymous, the provider bills Medicaid or Medicare.
rules.quote: If the victim of a felonious sexual assault has insurance, and chooses to bill their healthcare insurance, the health provider shall seek payment from the patient's healthcare insurer. Neither the patient nor the department shall be billed for anything above the coverage limit
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.payer: New Hampshire Department of Justice (or the provider writes off the charges)

rules.summary: If a survivor chooses to remain anonymous, the provider bills the Department of Justice or writes off the charges, even when the survivor has insurance.
rules.quote: If the victim of a felonious sexual assault chooses to remain anonymous, even if they have healthcare insurance, the health provider shall seek payment directly from the department or shall write off such charges
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.payer: New Hampshire Department of Justice

rules.summary: The Department of Justice reimburses the physician or hospital for the exam to the extent the cost is not covered by health insurance or a similar third party.
rules.quote: Upon submission of appropriate documentation, the physician or hospital shall be reimbursed for the cost of such examination by the department of justice to the extent such costs are not the responsibility of a third party under a health insurance policy or similar third party obligation.
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-c, Victim of Alleged Sexual Offense

params.payer: New Hampshire Department of Justice (deductibles and co-payments)

rules.summary: If a survivor uses insurance for the exam, the Department of Justice pays or reimburses any deductible or co-payment.
rules.quote: If a person who claims to be a victim of a felonious sexual assault has health insurance, and opts to use their insurance, which requires the payment of a deductible or a co-payment for such services or examination, the department shall either reimburse the victim for such payment made or pay such deductible or co-payment directly.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: A person examined by a physician or hospital after a felonious sexual assault, for treatment or to gather evidence, may not be charged for services related to the assault or other crime-related injuries. Payments are at the fee for service Medicaid rate.
rules.quote: a person who claims to be a victim of a felonious sexual assault who is examined by a physician or hospital for the purpose of treatment, gathering information or evidence shall not be charged for such services or examination that relate to the sexual assault and any other crime-related injuries
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.payer: Medicaid or Medicare (survivor enrolled and kit not anonymous)

rules.summary: If the survivor is covered by Medicaid or Medicare and the kit is not anonymous, the provider bills Medicaid or Medicare directly. This is an exception to billing insurance only by choice.
rules.quote: If the victim of a felonious sexual assault is covered by Medicaid or Medicare and the reporting kit is not anonymous, the health provider shall seek payment directly from Medicaid or Medicare.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.payer: New Hampshire Department of Justice (follow-up care)

rules.summary: The Department of Justice also pays for follow-up services and exams related to the sexual assault, but not for other crime-related injuries under this rule.
rules.quote: The department shall also pay for follow-up services and examination related to the sexual assault only and shall not pay for such services or examinations for other crime-related injuries or expenses.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: The statute caps recovery at $50,000 per claimant per incident. The program web page states a lower figure; the statute controls.
rules.quote: There shall be a $50,000 maximum recovery per claimant per incident.
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

rules.summary: Counseling is covered up to $4,000 or 40 visits, whichever comes first.
rules.quote: The commission shall award compensation up to $4,000 in total expenses, or 40 visits, whichever comes first
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Therapists who sign the program's treatment plan form agree to accept $75 per individual session and $35 per group session as payment in full.
rules.quote: I will accept the NH Victims' Compensation Program's reimbursement of $75 for an individual, crime-related, therapy session and $35 for a group, crime-related, therapy session as payment in full
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Relocation expenses are capped at $5,000, as a one-time benefit per claim.
rules.quote: Relocation expenses shall be capped at $5,000
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Safety and security expenses are capped at $3,000.
rules.quote: Safety and security expenses shall be capped at $3,000.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Mileage for crime-related interviews, court proceedings, protective order hearings and parole is capped at $500.
rules.quote: A $500 cap for mileage reimbursement for travel to crime-related interviews, pre-trial, trial, sentencing, hearings for securing protective orders and parole.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Reasonable and necessary medical treatment by licensed providers is covered after insurance and other sources are applied.
rules.quote: The actual cost of reasonable and necessary medical treatment provided by licensed health-care personnel, after first applying any available insurance or other available collateral financial source
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: The program lists medical and dental care among the costs it can pay.
rules.quote: Medical and dental care;
rules.pinpoint: NH DOJ Victims' Compensation Program page, What Costs May Be Paid?
rules.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

rules.summary: Prescription medications for the survivor's physical and mental health injuries are covered.
rules.quote: The portion of the cost of all prescription medications prescribed to treat the victim's physical and mental health injuries
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Individual or group therapy by licensed mental health providers is covered for issues directly caused by the crime, after insurance.
rules.quote: The actual cost of treatment, whether individual, group, or both, provided by licensed mental health personnel, after first applying any available insurance or other available collateral financial source, for mental health issues that were directly caused by the crime
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Lost wages are covered at up to 75% of pre-crime wages for up to 3 months, counting any workers' compensation or disability benefits.
rules.quote: The total compensation paid for lost wages shall not exceed 75% of the claimant's pre-crime wages, not to exceed 3 months, including any workers' compensation or disability benefits received.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Lost wages can be paid even if the survivor used paid leave to cover the time off, including time for medical, counseling, police and court appointments.
rules.quote: Wages lost for any of the reasons listed under (c) above shall be compensable even if the claimant had leave time available from his or her employer and was paid by using such leave time.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Relocation is paid only if the offender is a continuing, credible threat to your safety. You also need a police report and a temporary restraining order or other court order. A final restraining order also counts. If you have no restraining order, a letter from a victim's advocate explaining why can count instead.
rules.quote: The offender poses a continuing credible threat to the safety of the claimant; (2) There is either: a. A police report and a temporary restraining order or other court order have been issued against the claimant’s abuser or potential abuser or a final restraining order has been issued against the claimant’s abuser or potential abuser; or b. If the claimant does not have a restraining order against the abuser, the claimant shall present a letter from a victim’s advocate setting forth the basis for not obtaining a protective order, which may include, among other reasons, safety concerns for the claimant
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Security costs are covered, including installing a home monitoring system, up to one year of monitoring, and locks for windows and doors.
rules.quote: Installation costs of a residential monitoring system; (2) Up to one year of residential monitoring; (3) Installation of locks and other devices to secure windows and doors in the residence
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Mileage to medical appointments is paid at the Medicaid rate for trips over 10 miles round trip, capped at 100 miles round trip.
rules.quote: Mileage to and from appointments with licensed health care providers, at the rate used by Medicaid to compensate mileage. Mileage shall be paid for trips over 10 miles round trip and is capped at 100 miles round trip
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Shelter for the survivor and family is one of the goods a crisis center can pay for from emergency funds, which the commission then reimburses to the crisis center.
rules.quote: The cost of shelter for the victim and the victim's family
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: As part of a relocation award, the cost of changing a cell phone number is covered.
rules.quote: The cost, as billed by the cellular provider, for changing a cell phone number.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: If the examining provider finds the survivor may have been exposed to HIV, the survivor is given a voucher for preventive medication.
rules.quote: If it is determined by the examining health care provider that the victim may have been exposed to HIV/AIDS as a result of the assault, a voucher for prophylactic medication(s) shall be given to the victim.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Under medical expenses, the program can replace lost or badly damaged assistive devices the survivor already had, such as hearing aids, dentures, wheelchairs, and prescription glasses or contact lenses.
rules.quote: Replacement of lost or badly damaged existing physically assistive devices such as: a. Hearing aids; b. Dentures; c. Prosthetic and other devices; d. Wheelchairs; e. Prescription eyeglasses and other corrective lenses, including contact lenses
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.item: property loss; pain and suffering

rules.summary: The program cannot pay for property loss or for pain and suffering.
rules.quote: The program does not have authority to award money for property loss or pain and suffering.
rules.pinpoint: NH DOJ Victims' Compensation Program page, What Costs May Be Paid?
rules.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.item: cable television, long-distance telephone and internet service after relocation

rules.summary: Relocation awards do not pay for cable television, long-distance phone service or internet service.
rules.quote: No compensation shall be awarded for cable television, long-distance telephone, internet service
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.item: hospital care for an insured victim unless the hospital denied free or reduced-fee care

rules.summary: Hospital care is not paid if the victim had health insurance and the hospital has not denied free or reduced-fee care.
rules.quote: The commission shall not award compensation for hospital care if: a. The victim had health insurance at the time of treatment for injuries sustained as a direct result of the crime; and b. Free or reduced fee care has not been denied by the hospital
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.extension: You can apply later with good cause, and some sexual abuse survivors have no deadline.

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 2 years of the crime unless good cause is shown. A survivor of sexual abuse that happened when they were a minor may file at any time.
rules.quote: The claimant, guardian ad litem or child advocate, or parent may file a claim for compensation within 2 years of the crime, unless good cause is shown. A claimant who was the victim of sexual abuse or human trafficking under subparagraph I(a)(3), or a guardian ad litem, child advocate, or parent on behalf of such claimant, may file a claim at any time.
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

rules.summary: A claim is denied if the crime was not reported within 5 days, unless good cause is shown, such as a medical condition, fear for safety, fear of retribution, or the survivor's emotional state or mental health.
rules.quote: The crime was not reported within 5 days of the crime unless good cause, which shall include but not be limited to the following, is shown
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor who sought a medical exam or treatment is treated as having reported to law enforcement and as having shown credible evidence of the crime.
rules.quote: A victim who has sought medical treatment pursuant to (a) and (d) above shall be deemed to: (1) Have made a report to law enforcement in compliance with Jus 605.02(c); and (2) Have presented credible evidence that an eligible crime has occurred
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: A claim is denied if the victim did not cooperate in a meaningful way with law enforcement, unless there was good cause, such as fear of retaliation.
rules.quote: The primary victim failed to cooperate materially with law enforcement agencies without good cause such as fear of retaliation by or on behalf of the offender
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: No reimbursement is paid unless the claimant has at least $100 in reimbursable expenses.
rules.quote: No reimbursement shall be paid unless the claimant has incurred reimbursable expenses of at least $100.
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

rules.summary: The program is a payer of last resort: insurance and other sources are applied first.
rules.quote: help eligible victims of eligible crimes with the expenses that have been incurred as a direct result of the crime by acting as a payer of last resort
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: If expenses the fund paid are later covered by insurance, a civil settlement, restitution or another source, the claimant must pay the fund back for the amount recovered.
rules.quote: If expenses paid through the victims' assistance program fund are later covered by insurance settlements, civil suit settlements, or restitution, or through any other source, the claimant shall reimburse the fund for the amount of expenses recovered.
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

rules.summary: The commission considers the victim's contributory fault when deciding eligibility and the award amount.
rules.quote: In determining eligibility and the amount of compensation to be awarded, the commission shall consider the contributory fault of the victim in causing his injury.
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

rules.summary: Contributory fault is not considered in setting the award for a survivor of sexual abuse or human trafficking that happened when they were a minor.
rules.quote: The commission shall not consider contributory fault in determining the amount of compensation to be awarded if the claimant was a victim of sexual abuse or human trafficking under subparagraph I(a)(3).
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

rules.summary: A crisis center can give a domestic violence or sexual assault victim 10-day emergency funds (food, clothing, shelter, transportation, locks, medications), and the commission reimburses the crisis center, not the victim. The crisis center must send a police report or a restraining order with its request.
rules.quote: the commission shall award compensation to a crisis center for payment of 10-day emergency funds by the crisis center to a victim of domestic violence or sexual assault
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Emergency funds through a crisis center are limited to $1,000 per adult, not counting clothing.
rules.quote: The per-adult limit for the provision of all goods and services, except the purchase of clothing pursuant to (d)(2) and (e)(1) above, shall be $1,000
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Anyone who suffers personal injury from a felony or misdemeanor, including sexual assault, is an eligible victim.
rules.quote: Any person who sustains personal injury as a result of a felony or misdemeanor
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

rules.summary: Personal injury includes mental health harm, not only physical injury.
rules.quote: means death or corporeal or mental health damage suffered as a result of an eligible crime
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: A person who was a victim of sexual abuse while under 18 is an eligible victim.
rules.quote: Any person who is a victim of sexual abuse or human trafficking and is under the age of 18 at the time of the offense
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

params.rule: Crime in New Hampshire (any victim), or crime elsewhere with no qualifying compensation program if the victim lived in New Hampshire

rules.summary: Victims of crimes in New Hampshire are eligible regardless of where they live. New Hampshire residents hurt in a place without a qualifying compensation program are also covered.
rules.quote: Any person who suffered personal injury or death as a direct result of an eligible crime occurring in either: (1) New Hampshire; or (2) Any other state or jurisdiction that does not have a crime compensation program meeting the requirements of 34 U.S.C. 20102(b), and such person was domiciled in New Hampshire at the time of the crime
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.rule: Citizenship and immigration status are not required

rules.summary: Immigration status does not bar eligibility: non-citizens, with or without legal status, are eligible.
rules.quote: an individual who is not a citizen of the United States or who is not a legal alien shall be considered victims eligible for compensation under this section.
rules.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

params.target: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 33 Capitol Street Concord, N.H. 03301-6397

rules.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Victims' Compensation Program at the Department of Justice in Concord. This is the return address printed on the application form.
rules.quote: Please return completed application to: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 33 Capitol Street Concord, N.H. 03301-6397
rules.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params.target: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 1 Granite Place South Concord, NH 03301

rules.summary: The program page lists a newer office address in Concord (Granite Place South). The form still prints the Capitol Street address, so a survivor may want to call the program to confirm which address to use.
rules.quote: How To Contact Our Office New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 1 Granite Place South Concord, NH 03301
rules.pinpoint: Program page, How To Contact Our Office
rules.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

params.note: Copies of bills from every provider listed (hospital, doctors, dentists, counselors, ambulance, radiology, prescriptions), if available.

rules.summary: For medical, dental, or counseling costs, list every provider and enclose copies of their bills if you have them.
rules.quote: If applicable, list all providers that provided treatment, including hospital, doctors, dentists, mental health counselors, ambulance, radiology and prescriptions (drugs and eyeglasses). Attach additional sheets if necessary. If available, please enclose copies of bills.
rules.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params.note: Photocopies of all crime-related mental health counseling bills.

rules.summary: After the application arrives, the program may ask for photocopies of all crime-related counseling bills.
rules.quote: Photocopies of all crime-related mental health counseling bills
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.note: A signed HIPAA-compliant hospital and/or medical release so the program can request records and itemized statements from providers.

rules.summary: To claim medical or hospital costs, sign a HIPAA-compliant medical release so the program can get itemized statements and records from your providers.
rules.quote: If a claimant seeks compensation for medical expenses, the victim or victim's parent or guardian shall complete and submit a HIPAA- compliant hospital and/or medical release.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.note: Copies of pay stubs if employed when the crime happened.

rules.summary: To claim lost wages, fill in the employment section and send copies of your pay stubs.
rules.quote: If yes, complete the following section, and submit copies of your pay stubs.
rules.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params.note: If self-employed, a copy of the tax return for the year before the crime.

rules.summary: If you were self-employed, send a copy of your tax return for the year before the crime instead of pay stubs.
rules.quote: If you were self-employed at the time of the crime, please submit a copy of your tax return documentation for the year before the crime.
rules.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params.note: A doctor's statement verifying how long you could not work, if you missed more than two weeks.

rules.summary: If you missed more than two weeks of work, include a doctor's statement saying how long you were unable to work.
rules.quote: If you have missed more than two weeks of work, please provide a doctor's statement verifying length of time you were unable to work.
rules.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params.note: Copies of written appointment confirmations (medical, mental health, police, and other crime-related appointments).

rules.summary: For lost wages, keep and send copies of written confirmations of crime-related appointments such as medical, counseling, and police meetings.
rules.quote: Copies of all written confirmations of appointments with medical providers, mental health providers, police and other law-enforcement officials, and any other appointments necessitated as a direct result of the crime.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.note: Automobile insurance policy declarations page, only if the crime involved a motor vehicle.

rules.summary: If the crime involved a motor vehicle, include your auto insurance policy declarations page.
rules.quote: Did the crime involve motor vehicles? (If yes, please provide your automobile insurance policy declarations page.)
rules.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params.note: A separate sheet explaining any insurance, benefits, or other resources that may cover the expenses, with names, addresses, and phone numbers.

rules.summary: If insurance, leave, benefits, restitution, or any other resource might cover part of the costs, explain it on a separate sheet and attach it.
rules.quote: please explain in full on a separate piece of paper and attach it to this application.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
rules.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params.note: Copies of documents showing you were found ineligible for Medicaid, Medicare, hospital free care, or other public assistance, if you applied.

rules.summary: If you applied for Medicaid, Medicare, hospital free care, or public assistance and were turned down, attach copies of the denial documents.
rules.quote: attach copies of the documents that show your ineligibility for public assistance.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
rules.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

rules.summary: After the program receives the application, staff will contact the applicant by mail or email within 2 weeks. This is first contact, not a decision.
rules.quote: Once the program receives your application, you will be contacted by mail or email within 2 weeks.
rules.pinpoint: Program page FAQ, How Long Will It Take?
rules.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

rules.summary: Once an application is complete, the rules say no more than 60 days should pass before the commission can decide. The program page warns the whole process may take several months or longer while police reports are gathered.
rules.quote: In no case shall placement on the agenda result in the passage of more than 60 days after the claimant submitted a completed application before a decision can be made by the commission.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.agency: New Hampshire Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General
