params.enroll: Contact a New Hampshire crisis center first for consultation and assistance, which the law requires; the application is then filed with the attorney general on the form the attorney general prescribes, with a sworn statement that the applicant is a victim of domestic violence, stalking, or sexual assault and fears for their safety. A restraining order, pending charges, or a police report are not required.

rules.summary: Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking can apply to New Hampshire's Address Confidentiality Program if they meet its eligibility guidelines.
rules.quote: Any adult person, a parent or guardian acting on behalf of a minor or guardian acting on behalf of an incapacitated person, may apply to the program if they are a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking and meet the eligibility guidelines.
rules.pinpoint: DOJ ACP page, FAQ: What are the eligibility guidelines?
rules.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Address Confidentiality Program page and FAQ

params.agency: New Hampshire Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General

rules.summary: You do not need a restraining order, pending criminal charges, or a police report to take part in the program.
rules.quote: Having a restraining order, criminal charges pending or even reporting the abuse to law enforcement are not required in order to participate in the ACP.
rules.pinpoint: DOJ ACP page, FAQ: What are the eligibility guidelines?
rules.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Address Confidentiality Program page and FAQ

rules.summary: Everything the compensation program receives or keeps about a claim is confidential and may not be released to anyone unless the claimant authorizes it or another law allows it.
rules.quote: All information received, obtained, or maintained by the program in connection with any claim for victims' compensation shall be maintained as confidential material, and shall not be released or disclosed to any person or entity whatsoever, except as authorized by the claimant or as otherwise provided by law.
rules.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rules.summary: Each county Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner program must make sure survivors are not charged any fee for services directly tied to the forensic exam, including screening, STI prophylaxis, pregnancy tests and emergency contraception.
rules.quote: Develop and implement procedures to ensure that victims of sexual assault are not charged any fee for services that are directly associated with forensic sexual assault examinations, including routine medical screening, medications for prophylaxis of sexually transmitted infections, pregnancy tests, emergency contraception, supplies, equipment and use of space.

rules.summary: The Attorney General's office says the medical-forensic exam is free, and a survivor does not have to report to police to get one.
rules.quote: The medical-forensic exam is free and a victim of sexual assault does not need to report the assault to the police to have an exam.
rules.pinpoint: NJ OAG, Sexual Assault Victims page (Forensic Nurse Examiner section)
rules.source_title: NJ OAG Sexual Assault Victims page

rules.summary: Under the Attorney General's SART standards, survivors are not charged for the forensic exam, preventive medication or the evidence kits, but emergency care beyond the exam itself can be billed under hospital policy.
rules.quote: Victims shall not be charged for the medical forensic exam, prophylactic medication, or the SAFE Kit and/or DFSA/Tox Kit. (N.J.S.A 52:4B-52(k)). However, the victim shall be charged pursuant to hospital policy for any services provided beyond this scope.
rules.pinpoint: AG Standards for Providing Services to Victims of Sexual Assault (2018), Standard on the medical forensic exam, Non-Participating Examination Facilities
rules.source_title: Attorney General Standards for Providing Services to Victims of Sexual Assault (2018)

rules.summary: Except as the statute otherwise provides, the most the program can award is $25,000.
rules.quote: compensation shall not be awarded under P.L.1971, c.317 (C.52:4B-1 et seq.) in an amount in excess of $25,000

params.exception: or more in cases the program finds catastrophic

rules.summary: Except in cases the program finds catastrophic, no award can be more than $25,000.
rules.quote: Except for cases determined to be catastrophic in nature, no compensation shall be awarded in an amount in excess of $ 25,000.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Counseling is capped at $20,000 per claim, no matter how many sessions, except in catastrophic cases.
rules.quote: (b) Except for cases determined to be catastrophic in nature, the maximum award for unreimbursed and unreimbursable counseling expenses shall be $ 20,000, notwithstanding the number of counseling sessions attended.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Lost earnings are paid at no more than $600 a week.
rules.quote: (h) The weekly maximum reimbursement for loss of earnings or support shall not exceed $ 600.00.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Lost earnings are limited to 104 weeks, or 260 weeks (five years) for a victim who is permanently disabled.
rules.quote: (e) The maximum reimbursement for loss of earnings shall not exceed a total of 104 weeks, unless a victim has been rendered permanently disabled as defined by 42 U.S.C. §§ 1381. et seq., in which case loss of earnings may be awarded for a total period of 260 weeks (five years).
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Moving expenses are capped at $3,000, when the Office finds relocation is needed for the victim's health and safety.
rules.quote: (d) Maximum reimbursement for moving expenses shall be $ 3,000.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: If the victim cannot move, the same $3,000 relocation allotment can go toward an alarm system, new locks, or other home security devices. It is not an extra $3,000 on top of relocation.
rules.quote: In the event a victim is unable to relocate due to home ownership or other personal circumstances, the Office may apply the $ 3,000 allotted for moving expenses towards the victim's purchase of a security alarm system, new door locks, or any other reasonable home security device(s), needed for the purpose of protecting the health and safety of the victim and the victim's family.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Crime-related transportation is reimbursed at up to $10 a day, figured at 31 cents per mile.
rules.quote: (a) Maximum reimbursement for transportation expenses incurred as a direct result of the incident giving rise to the claim shall not exceed $ 10.00 a day, calculated at the rate of.31 cents per mile up to the daily maximum allowance.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

params.item: non-medical transportation other than court attendance

rules.summary: Transportation that is not medical is not covered, except travel to court proceedings related to the crime.
rules.quote: All non-medically related transportation costs are excluded other than attendance at any court proceeding related to the crime.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Child care or day care is capped at $6,500 in total, except in catastrophic cases.
rules.quote: 2. Except for cases determined to be catastrophic in nature, reimbursement for child care and/or day care services shall not exceed $ 6,500 in the aggregate.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Crime scene clean-up is capped at $4,000 in total.
rules.quote: (f) An award of compensation for crime scene clean-up shall not exceed $ 4,000 in the aggregate.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: The Office can pay up to $10,000 to a lawyer who helps the victim with a legal matter arising from the crime (other than the compensation claim itself).
rules.quote: (b) The Office may allow payment of an attorney fee, including costs, up to a maximum of $ 10,000, to an attorney who provides legal assistance to a victim in any legal matter, other than a decision of the Office, arising from, or related to, having been the victim of the offense that forms the basis of the victim's or claimant's application for compensation.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: When the victim dies, funeral costs are capped at $7,500.
rules.quote: In claims involving the death of a victim, the maximum reimbursement for funeral expenses shall be $ 7,500.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Domestic help needed because of the crime (housecleaning, laundry, cooking and similar day-to-day support) is capped at $6,500 in total, except in catastrophic cases.
rules.quote: Except for cases determined to be catastrophic in nature, the total amount of reimbursement for domestic help shall not exceed $ 6,500 in the aggregate.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Unreimbursed out-of-pocket medical care and other necessary services caused by the crime are reimbursable.
rules.quote: Reimbursable expenses include those unreimbursed and unreimbursable out-of-pocket expenses or indebtedness for medical care or other necessary services, loss of earnings, loss of support, pecuniary loss to the dependents of deceased victims, and other reasonable pecuniary loss resulting from the personal injury or death of the victim.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Lost earnings caused by the crime are reimbursable.
rules.quote: Reimbursable expenses include those unreimbursed and unreimbursable out-of-pocket expenses or indebtedness for medical care or other necessary services, loss of earnings, loss of support, pecuniary loss to the dependents of deceased victims, and other reasonable pecuniary loss resulting from the personal injury or death of the victim.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Mental health counseling related to the crime and not covered by insurance can be paid.
rules.quote: Counseling: Mental health counseling expenses related to the incident and not covered by insurance.
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

rules.summary: Dental costs from a crime-related injury that insurance does not fully cover can be paid.
rules.quote: Dental: Dental expenses directly related to a crime related injury and not totally covered by insurance.
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

rules.summary: Prescription costs from a crime-related injury that insurance does not fully cover can be paid.
rules.quote: Prescription: Prescription expenses directly related to a crime related injury and not totally covered by insurance.
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

rules.summary: As part of crime scene clean-up, the Office may pay the reasonable replacement value of bedding and clothing.
rules.quote: The Office may award compensation for the reasonable replacement value of bedding and clothing;
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

params.item: personal property loss or damage (for example, a phone)

rules.summary: Lost or damaged personal property, such as a phone, is not reimbursed unless the rules specifically allow it (for example, some crime scene items).
rules.quote: (f) Except as otherwise permitted by this chapter, no compensation shall be awarded for loss of personal property or property damage.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: The program does not pay for pain and suffering.
rules.quote: (e) In making its award, the Office shall make no allowance for pain and suffering.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

params.extension: or later if the program finds good cause for the delay

rules.summary: Apply within 5 years of the injury, or later if the Office finds good cause for the delay.
rules.quote: unless the application has been made within five years after the date of the personal injury or death or after that date upon determination by the office that good cause exists for the delayed filing

rules.summary: If the victim was under 18, the 5-year clock starts on their 18th birthday.
rules.quote: If the victim is under 18 years of age, the five-year limit on filing shall commence on the day the victim turns 18 years old.

params.extension: good cause

rules.summary: For child sexual abuse, the application is due within 5 years after reasonable discovery of the injury and its link to the abuse, unless good cause is shown.
rules.quote: In the case of child sexual abuse, defined as an act of sexual contact or sexual penetration between a child under the age of 18 and an adult, an application for compensation shall be filed within five years after reasonable discovery of the injury and its causal relationship to an act of child sexual abuse, unless good cause is shown, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 2A:61B-1.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

params.exception: counted from the crime or from when it was reasonably discovered

rules.summary: The crime must have been reported to police or another law enforcement agency within 9 months of when it happened or was reasonably discovered.
rules.quote: which had been reported to the police or other appropriate law enforcement agency within nine months after its occurrence or reasonable discovery

params.exception: or later for good cause

rules.summary: The Office can excuse a late police report for good cause.
rules.quote: The Office reserves the right to, upon determination that good cause exists for the delayed filing, make an exception to the requirement that the incident be reported to the police within the stated time period.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: The Attorney General's SART standards tell hospitals to inform survivors that compensation is only available to those who report the crime to law enforcement, even though the exam itself does not require a report.
rules.quote: Victims shall be informed that VCCO benefits are only eligible to those victims who report the crime to law enforcement.
rules.pinpoint: AG Standards for Providing Services to Victims of Sexual Assault (2018), Standard on the medical forensic exam
rules.source_title: Attorney General Standards for Providing Services to Victims of Sexual Assault (2018)

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: The program will not pay if the victim did not cooperate with reasonable requests from law enforcement. A compelling health or safety reason for not cooperating is the exception.
rules.quote: No compensation shall be awarded if: a. Compensation to the victim proves to be substantial unjust enrichment to the offender or if the victim did not cooperate with the reasonable requests of law enforcement authorities unless the victim demonstrates a compelling health or safety reason for not cooperating

rules.summary: There is no minimum loss requirement for crimes on or after June 26, 1995.
rules.quote: There are no minimum loss requirements for incidents occurring on or after June 26, 1995.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Eligibility page, Preconditions for Eligibility
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Eligibility page

rules.summary: The program pays last, after insurance and other sources.
rules.quote: The Victims of Crime Compensation Office (VCCO) is the payer of last resort.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Eligibility page, Moneys from other Sources
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Eligibility page

rules.summary: Money received or receivable from other sources because of the crime is taken into account when setting the award.
rules.quote: (a) In determining the amount of compensation to be awarded, the Office shall take into consideration amounts received or receivable from other sources by the victim, claimant, and/or his or her dependents as a result of the offense or occurrence giving rise to the application.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: The Office must consider whether the victim's conduct contributed to the injury and may reduce or deny the award on that basis.
rules.quote: In determining the amount of an award, the office shall determine whether, because of the victim's conduct, the victim of such crime contributed to the infliction of the victim's injury, and the office shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the application altogether, in accordance with the determination

rules.summary: When an award is reduced for the victim's conduct, it cannot exceed $12,500 in total.
rules.quote: Where an award is to be limited or reduced due to contribution or other circumstances relating to the victim's behavior or action, said award shall not exceed $ 12,500 in the aggregate.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Emergency awards can be made before a final decision when compensation is likely and the applicant would face undue hardship without funds right away.
rules.quote: The Victims of Crime Compensation Office may make one or more emergency awards to any applicant for compensation pending final determination of a case, when it determines that compensation is likely to be provided and that the applicant will suffer undue hardship if funds are not made immediately available.
rules.source_title: Criminal Injuries Compensation Act, N.J.S.A. 52:4B (OAG compilation effective 8/1/2020)

rules.summary: A single emergency award can be up to $7,500.
rules.quote: (c) The maximum amount of any emergency award shall not exceed $ 7,500.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: Aggravated sexual assault, sexual assault, aggravated criminal sexual contact and criminal sexual contact are covered crimes.
rules.quote: (9) aggravated sexual assault, sexual assault, aggravated criminal sexual contact, criminal sexual contact;

params.rule: Crime in New Jersey (residency not required), or a New Jersey resident victimized in a state with no compensation program or one that did not fully compensate the losses.

rules.summary: Anyone hurt by a crime in New Jersey can apply regardless of residence; New Jersey residents hurt elsewhere can apply if that state has no program or did not fully compensate them.
rules.quote: The crime must occur in New Jersey, although you need not be a New Jersey resident; or you must be a New Jersey resident who became a victim in another state or jurisdiction that does not have a crime victim compensation program or has a program which has not provided full compensation for your crime-related losses.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Eligibility page, Preconditions for Eligibility
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Eligibility page

rules.summary: Applications can be filed online through the VCCO claims system.
rules.quote: For applications and submission of documents, you may: File online @ www.njvictims.org
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Contact page, applications and submission of documents
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Contact page

params.target: VCCO, 50 Park Place, 5th floor, Newark, NJ 07102

rules.summary: Paper applications go by mail to the VCCO office in Newark.
rules.quote:
Mail all applications
to Newark office at:
VCCO
50 Park Place, 5th floor
Newark, NJ 07102
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions page II sidebar
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

rules.summary: Applications and documents can be faxed to the VCCO.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Contact page, applications and submission of documents
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Contact page

params.note: Attach if available; the VCCO will request it from police or the prosecutor if you do not have one.

rules.summary: Attach a copy of the police incident report if you have one; otherwise the VCCO requests it.
rules.quote:
Attach a copy
of the incident report. If you don't have one, the
VCCO will request one from the police and/or
prosecutor.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions, Section 4
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

params.note: Copies of itemized receipts, as many as you have; more can be sent later.

rules.summary: Include copies of itemized receipts with the application.
rules.quote:
Include
copies of as much related information (i.e. copies of itemized receipts,
bills, insurance statements) as you have.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions page II
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

params.note: Copies of itemized bills from doctors, hospitals and counselors, if you already have them.

rules.summary: Send copies of any itemized medical or counseling bills you already have.
rules.quote:
If you already
have itemized bills, please send copies with
your application.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions, Section 7
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

params.note: Copies of insurance statements, as many as you have.

rules.summary: Include copies of insurance statements with the application.
rules.quote:
Include
copies of as much related information (i.e. copies of itemized receipts,
bills, insurance statements) as you have.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions page II
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

params.note: For lost wages, if available: pay stubs from the week before the crime and the week you returned to work.

rules.summary: For lost wages, supply pay stubs from before the crime and from your return to work.
rules.quote:
If available, please supply your pay stubs from the week before the crime, the week you returned to work
and a letter from your doctor stating your period of disability.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Section 8 (Lost Wages/Support Information)
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

params.note: For lost wages: a letter from your doctor stating your period of disability.

rules.summary: For lost wages, supply a doctor's letter stating the period of disability.
rules.quote:
If available, please supply your pay stubs from the week before the crime, the week you returned to work
and a letter from your doctor stating your period of disability.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Section 8 (Lost Wages/Support Information)
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

params.note: Self-employed lost wages: income and business tax returns for the 2 years before the crime.

rules.summary: Self-employed applicants claiming lost wages must supply income and business tax returns for the 2 years before the crime.
rules.quote: If you are self-employed, you must supply copies of your income tax returns and business tax returns for the last 2 years before the crime.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Section 8 (Lost Wages/Support Information)
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

params.note: Signed HIPAA authorization (application Section 15) so the VCCO can get records from health care providers.

rules.summary: The HIPAA release in the application must be completed, signed and dated before the claim can be processed.
rules.quote:
This authorization is necessary to obtain information
from your health care providers under federal law.
It must be completed, signed and dated in order
for the VCCO to process your claim.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions, Section 15
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

rules.summary: The VCCO decides on an application within 90 days after it acknowledges receiving the completed application and all supporting information; this can be extended for good cause.
rules.quote:
The Office will make its determination regarding the application within 90 days of acknowledgment by the
Office of receipt of the completed application and any and all necessary supplemental information
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rules.summary: The application instructions say claims take 3 months to process once all documentation is received.
rules.quote:
the turn around time for processing a claim is 3 months of receipt of
all documentation.
rules.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions page II
rules.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

params.agency: Division on Women, New Jersey Department of Children and Families
params.enroll: Each applicant shall complete an application, which may be obtained from a local domestic violence program, sexual violence agency, or other agencies, as designated by the Division on Women. Information about how to contact the aforementioned programs can be obtained by contacting the New Jersey Address Confidentiality Program at 1-877-218-9133.

rules.summary: New Jersey's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Division on Women in the Department of Children and Families, is meant to keep the addresses of victims of domestic violence, stalking and sexual assault confidential. The law lets public agencies accept a program participant's substitute mailing address.
rules.quote: to enable interagency cooperation with the Director of the Division on Women in the Department of Children and Families in providing address confidentiality for victims of domestic violence, stalking, and sexual assault, and reproductive health service patients and providers, and to enable public agencies to accept a program participant's use of an address designated by the director as a substitute mailing address.
rules.source_title: N.J.S.A. 47:4-2 Address confidentiality for certain individuals (Justia 2025)

rules.summary: VCCO claim files are confidential and are not government records open under the Open Public Records Act; nobody may inspect a victim's or claimant's file unless the law or a court order allows it.
rules.quote: The files maintained by the Office that relate directly to the handling of any claim for compensation filed by a victim or claimant are not government records subject to disclosure under the Open Public Records Act and shall be considered confidential.
rules.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

params.scope: collecting the evidence kit

rules.summary: A health care provider may not charge the survivor, directly or indirectly, for the costs of collecting a sexual assault examination kit. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.
rules.quote: No costs incurred by a health care provider for the collection of a sexual assault examination kit shall be charged directly or indirectly to the survivor of the sexual assault.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 30-9-21 (Sexual assault survivor's bill of rights)

params.payer: The administrator under the Sexual Crimes Prosecution and Treatment Act (NMSA 29-11-3 defines this as the director of the mental health division of the Department of Health, or a designee)

rules.summary: Under the Sexual Crimes Prosecution and Treatment Act, the state administrator must provide free forensic medical exams to victims of sexual crimes, arrange free exams, or reimburse victims for the exam cost.
rules.quote: The administrator shall: A. provide free forensic medical exams to victims of sexual crimes; B. arrange for victims of sexual crimes to obtain free forensic medical exams; or C. reimburse victims of sexual crimes for the cost of forensic medical exams
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 29-11-7 (Free forensic medical exams for victims of sexual crimes)

params.payer: The administrator under the Sexual Crimes Prosecution and Treatment Act, by reimbursement

rules.summary: If the victim is reimbursed for the exam instead of getting it free, reimbursement covers the full cost with no deductible or limit, and the victim can apply for reimbursement for one year from the exam date.
rules.quote: the reimbursement covers the full cost of the forensic medical exam, without any deductible requirement or limit on the amount of the reimbursement; (2) the victim of a sexual crime is entitled to apply for reimbursement for a period of one year from the date of the forensic medical exam
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 29-11-7 (Free forensic medical exams for victims of sexual crimes)

params.exception: or up to $30,000 more if an injury leaves you fully disabled for life

rules.summary: The maximum award is $20,000 per victim. The commission may add up to $30,000 more for extraordinary losses when the injury is catastrophic and causes permanent total disability.
rules.quote: No award of reparation shall be in excess of twenty thousand dollars ($20,000) per victim, except that the commission may award up to an additional thirty thousand dollars ($30,000) for extraordinary pecuniary losses, if the personal injury to a victim is catastrophic and results in a permanent total disability.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-14 (Limitations on award; collateral recovery; preliminary award)

rules.summary: Mental health counseling is approved for up to 30 sessions per eligible person unless the commission approves more therapy.
rules.quote: The commission shall approve up to thirty sessions per person deemed eligible under the application submitted unless approval for additional therapy has been granted by the commission.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rules.summary: Funeral expenses are capped at $6,000.
rules.quote: Awards for funeral expenses shall not exceed six thousand dollars ($6,000.00).
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

params.item: eyeglasses or contact lenses

rules.summary: Replacement of eyeglasses or contact lenses damaged in the crime is capped at $350.
rules.quote: Awards for eyeglasses or contact lenses shall not exceed three hundred fifty dollars ($350.00).
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

params.item: Native American medicine man treatment

rules.summary: Native American medicine man treatment fees can be considered, up to $3,000 per application unless the board approves more in advance.
rules.quote: In all cases of medicine man care, the commission board shall only approve up to $3,000.00 per application unless prior approval has been granted by the commission board for additional treatment.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rules.summary: The commission may pay expenses actually and reasonably incurred because of the victim's injury.
rules.quote: The commission may order payment of reparation for: A. expenses actually and reasonably incurred as a result of the victim's injury or death;
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-9 (Award of reparation)

rules.summary: The program lists medical and dental care and mental health counseling (30 session maximum) as types of reparation.
rules.quote: Medical and dental care; Mental health counseling; (30 session maximum)
rules.pinpoint: CVRC Compensation FAQ, What are the types of reparation?
rules.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

rules.summary: The commission may pay for the victim's lost earning power from total or partial incapacity.
rules.quote: B. loss to the victim of earning power as a result of total or partial incapacity;
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-9 (Award of reparation)

rules.summary: Lost wages can be paid for a recovery period of up to 14 calendar days after the crime without a physician's certification. The person must have been employed at the time of the incident.
rules.quote: Loss of wages may be paid to the victim, claimant, and/or, in the case of a minor victim, guardian, for up to fourteen calendar days after the crime for a recovery period.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

params.scope: gas for trips over 30 miles one way to a health provider

rules.summary: Gas to get to a health provider can be reimbursed at 20 cents per mile when the trip is over 30 miles one way from home.
rules.quote: Gas expenses to transport the victim to a health provider may be considered if the travel is over thirty miles one way from the victim's residence. This travel shall be verified by the health provider's billing and reports for the travel requested. The gas will be reimbursed at the rate of twenty cents per mile.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rules.summary: The program lists medical and dental care among the expenses it can pay.
rules.quote: can be made for the following: Medical and dental care;
rules.pinpoint: CVRC Compensation FAQ, What are the types of reparation?
rules.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

rules.summary: The application lists crime scene cleanup as a potentially eligible expense.
rules.quote: Crime Scene Cleanup
rules.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

rules.summary: The application lists prescriptions as a potentially eligible expense.
rules.quote: Prescriptions
rules.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

params.scope: gas for trips over 30 miles one way from home, at 20 cents a mile

rules.summary: Gas to travel to a law enforcement agency on official business about the incident can be reimbursed at 20 cents per mile when the trip is more than 30 miles one way.
rules.quote: The distance traveled shall be more than thirty miles one way from the victim's residence and the gas will be reimbursed at the rate of twenty cents per mile.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rules.summary: No award is made for any loss of or damage to property.
rules.quote: B. No award shall be made for any loss or damage to property.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-8 (Crimes enumerated)

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: The program does not pay for property loss, pain and suffering, or attorney's fees.
rules.quote: No awards are made for property loss, pain and suffering, or attorney
rules.pinpoint: CVRC Compensation FAQ, What are the types of reparation?
rules.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

rules.summary: Attorney fees are not paid as part of or on top of a reparation award.
rules.quote: None of the appropriation in this act [31-22-1 to 31-22-21 NMSA 1978] shall be used to pay attorney fees either as part of or in addition to awards of reparation.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-6 (Medical examination; attorneys' fees; penalty)

params.item: phone bills, copying fees, postage

rules.summary: Phone bills, copying fees, and postage are not reimbursed.
rules.quote: The following expenses shall not be considered for reimbursement: (1) phone bills; (2) copying fees; (3) postage costs.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

params.extension: The statute makes an exception for minors hurt by child abuse or some sex crimes, but does not say what deadline applies to them.

rules.summary: Apply within two years after the injury. The statute makes an exception for minors who were victims of child abuse or abandonment, criminal sexual penetration, or criminal sexual contact of a minor. It does not say what deadline applies to them instead.
rules.quote: An application for reparation shall be made within two years after the injury or death, except for minors who are victims of criminal activity under the provisions of Section 30-6-1 NMSA 1978, regarding abandonment or abuse of a child, Section 30-9-11 NMSA 1978, regarding criminal sexual penetration, or Section 30-9-13 NMSA 1978, regarding criminal sexual contact of a minor.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-14 (Limitations on award; collateral recovery; preliminary award)

rules.summary: A police report is not the only option. The crime must have led to an arrest, been reported to police in a reasonable time, or been reported to a licensed medical, mental health or counseling provider, or a tribal health provider.
rules.quote: provided an arrest has been made or the act or omission constituting a crime has been reported to the police in a reasonable time or the act or omission constituting a crime has been reported to a licensed medical, mental health or counseling provider, or tribal health provider.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-7 (Eligibility for reparation)

rules.summary: The victim or claimant must have fully cooperated with law enforcement, unless the commission finds they acted reasonably under the circumstances.
rules.quote: the claimant or victim fully cooperated with the appropriate law enforcement agencies or the commission finds that the claimant or victim acted reasonably under the circumstances.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-7 (Eligibility for reparation)

rules.summary: Payments from collateral sources such as insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, or government benefits are deducted from the award.
rules.quote: the commission shall deduct from any reparation awarded any payments received from a collateral source or from the United States or the state or any of its political subdivisions for injury or death subject to reparation under the Crime Victims Reparation Act.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-14 (Limitations on award; collateral recovery; preliminary award)

rules.summary: Expenses covered by insurance or another collateral source must be submitted there first. Only what those sources do not cover is considered.
rules.quote: shall submit covered expenses to the source(s) for payment. Only those expenses not covered by the collateral source(s) will be considered for reparation.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rules.summary: The commission considers the victim's behavior and reduces the award by the degree of responsibility it attributes to the victim. Shown for information only.
rules.quote: The commission shall consider the behavior of the victim and whether, because of provocation or otherwise, the victim bears responsibility for the act or omission constituting a crime that caused the victim's injury or death and shall reduce the amount of reparation in accordance with its assessment of the degree of responsibility attributable to the victim.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-7 (Eligibility for reparation)

rules.summary: If a final award looks likely, the director can authorize a preliminary award with the commission chair's agreement. It is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: If it appears that a final award of reparation will be made by the commission, a preliminary award may be authorized by the director of the commission or the commission's designee when the commission chair concurs.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-14 (Limitations on award; collateral recovery; preliminary award)

rules.summary: Criminal sexual penetration and criminal sexual contact of a minor are covered crimes.
rules.quote: (9) criminal sexual penetration; (10) criminal sexual contact of a minor;
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-8 (Crimes enumerated)

rules.summary: Injury includes bodily harm, pregnancy, and extreme mental distress, so a victim does not need a physical injury to qualify.
rules.quote: "injury" means actual bodily harm or disfigurement and includes pregnancy and extreme mental distress.
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-3 (Definitions)

params.rule: Crimes in New Mexico (any victim); New Mexico residents victimized in a state without an eligible compensation program

rules.summary: Covers anyone injured by a covered crime in New Mexico, regardless of residency, and New Mexico residents hurt in another state that has no eligible compensation program.
rules.quote: a person in New Mexico who is injured or killed by any act or omission of any other person that is a crime enumerated in Section 31-22-8 NMSA 1978; (2) a resident of New Mexico who is injured or killed by such a crime occurring in a state other than New Mexico if that state does not have an eligible crime victims compensation program
rules.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-3 (Definitions)

rules.summary: You can file online through the CVRC application portal, where you sign in or create an account and submit the application.
rules.quote: To begin Please choose one of the following options: Sign In OR Create an Account
rules.pinpoint: CVRC online application portal, home page
rules.source_title: CVRC online compensation application portal (home page)

params.target: Crime Victims Reparation Commission 6200 Uptown Blvd., Suite 210 Albuquerque, NM 87110
params.note: 10.40.2.8(B) NMAC (NM-S12) counts a paper application as received when it is postmarked, delivered or faxed to the commission's offices.

rules.summary: A paper application goes to the Crime Victims Reparation Commission office in Albuquerque; the rules count it as filed on the postmark date.
rules.quote: Crime Victims Reparation Commission 6200 Uptown Blvd., Suite 210 Albuquerque, NM 87110
rules.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, How do I apply?
rules.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

params.note: 10.40.2.8(B) NMAC (NM-S12) counts a paper application as received when it is postmarked, delivered or faxed to the commission's offices.

rules.summary: A paper application can be faxed to the commission's office.
rules.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, How do I apply?
rules.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

params.note: Only if one exists; the commission also accepts a provider incident verification form (see NM-DOC-2).

rules.summary: The application asks for a copy of the police report if one is available.
rules.quote: CRIME INFORMATION (Provide copy of police report if available)
rules.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

params.note: A complete offense report or a provider incident verification form; the commission requests it itself.

rules.summary: The commission reviews the application with a complete offense report or a provider incident verification form, which its office requests.
rules.quote: The application and related documentation received, including a complete offense report or provider incident verification form (which this office requests), will then be reviewed to determine if the victim and/or claimant are eligible for compensation.
rules.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, What happens after I send my application?
rules.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

params.note: Invoices, receipts or canceled checks showing payee, payer, amount paid, date of service and the service; affidavits and letters are not accepted.

rules.summary: Expenses must be documented with invoices, receipts or canceled checks that show who was paid, who paid, the amount, the date and the service.
rules.quote: This documentation must provide the name of payee, the name of payer, the amount paid, date of services, and indicate what service was provided. This documentation may include invoices, receipts and canceled checks. Affidavits and letters shall not be considered proper documentation.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

params.note: Only when lost wages are claimed: an employer statement of dates missed, hourly wage, average weekly hours and any leave or other pay received.

rules.summary: For lost wages, the employer must give a statement of the work dates missed, hourly wage and average weekly hours.
rules.quote: a statement from the employer providing: (a) the dates of work missed due to the incident; (b) hourly wage; (c) the average number of hours worked weekly; and (d) any type of compensation received, such as sick leave, annual leave, unemployment, etc.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

params.note: Only when lost wages are claimed: a doctor's statement or medical documentation that the victim cannot work.

rules.summary: For lost wages, a doctor's statement or medical documentation must show the victim is unable to work.
rules.quote: a copy of a doctor's statement certifying that the victim is unable to work; or a doctor's statement included in a medical document, or medical documentation showing the inability of the victim to work.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

params.note: Provided by the counselor to commission staff, including a patient evaluation and an itemized statement for services.

rules.summary: Counselors must give commission staff a detailed patient evaluation describing the effect of the victimization.
rules.quote: All counselors shall provide the commission staff with the following: (a) detailed patient evaluation describing the effect of the victimization
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

params.note: Death certificate, only if the victim died.

rules.summary: If the victim is deceased, the application asks for a copy of the death certificate.
rules.quote: DECEASED (Submit copy of death certificate)
rules.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

params.note: Power of attorney, only if the victim is incapacitated.

rules.summary: If the victim is incapacitated, the application asks for a power of attorney.
rules.quote: INCAPACITATED (Submit a power of attorney)
rules.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

params.note: Signed Acknowledgement and Authorization page (release of information and subrogation agreement).

rules.summary: The signed Acknowledgement and Authorization page is required for the application to be processed.
rules.quote: This authorization is part of your application and must be completed and signed in order to process this application.
rules.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

rules.summary: An eligibility decision is usually made within 120 days.
rules.quote: A decision about whether the victim/claimant is eligible is usually made within 120 days.
rules.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, What happens after I send my application?
rules.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

params.program_name: Safe at Home (formerly the Confidential Address Program)
params.enroll: Survivors who wish to enroll in the Safe at Home Program, must apply to the program by filling out the forms included in the Safe at Home Application Packet while in the presence of an application assistant. An application assistant is a person who works or volunteers for a domestic violence or sexual assault program in New Mexico. The forms must then be notarized by a Notary Public in the presence of the applicant and application assistant. The application assistant will then submit the forms to the Secretary of State’s Office.

rules.summary: New Mexico's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, lets survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, attempted sexual assault or stalking use the Secretary of State's address as a substitute address with state and local agencies, with mail forwarded to their real address. Applicants fill out the application packet with an application assistant from a domestic violence or sexual assault program, and the forms are notarized.
rules.quote: The Secretary of State’s Safe at Home program (formerly known as the Confidential Address Program) allows survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking to receive mail using the Secretary of State’s address as a substitute for their own, while keeping their actual address confidential.
rules.pinpoint: Safe at Home program page, program description; enrollment steps from the Eligibility, FAQs & Resources page (NM-S16), How to Apply
rules.source_title: Secretary of State: Safe at Home program page

rules.summary: Crime Victims Reparation Commission application files that contain confidential medical and police records are confidential, and the information in them may not be publicly disclosed.
rules.quote: Application files which contain confidential medical and police records shall be considered confidential. No public disclosure of the information contained within shall be made.
rules.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rules.summary: The costs of a sexual assault forensic medical exam must not be charged directly to the survivor. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.
rules.quote: Any costs incurred pursuant to subsection 2 must not be charged directly to the victim of sexual assault.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

params.payer: State Fund for the Compensation of Victims of Crime; the county where the offense happened pays any remainder if the Fund is short

rules.summary: A medical provider's costs for the forensic exam are paid from the state Fund for the Compensation of Victims of Crime. If the Fund does not have enough money, the county where the assault happened pays the rest.
rules.quote: any costs incurred by a medical provider for the forensic medical examination of the victim must be paid out of the Fund for the Compensation of Victims of Crime, unless there is not sufficient money in the Fund to pay such costs. If there is not sufficient money in the Fund to pay such costs, the county in whose jurisdiction the offense was committed shall pay any remaining costs.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

params.payer: County where the sexual assault was committed (medical care for physical injuries within 72 hours)

rules.summary: The county where the assault happened pays for medical care for physical injuries from the assault that is given within 72 hours after the survivor first arrives for treatment.
rules.quote: The county in whose jurisdiction a sexual assault is committed shall pay any costs incurred for medical care for any physical injuries resulting from the sexual assault which is provided to the victim not later than 72 hours after the victim first arrives for treatment.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

rules.summary: The costs of the county-paid medical care for physical injuries from the assault must not be charged directly to the survivor.
rules.quote: Any costs incurred pursuant to subsection 1: (a) Must not be charged directly to the victim of sexual assault.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

rules.summary: You do not have to report to police to qualify for the forensic medical exam that this part of Nevada law pays for.
rules.quote: The filing of a report with the appropriate law enforcement agency must not be a prerequisite to qualify for a forensic medical examination pursuant to this section.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

rules.summary: The program says each individual benefit has its own limit and no claim may exceed $35,000.
rules.quote: There are limits on individual benefits and no claim may exceed $35,000.
rules.pinpoint: VOCP Benefits and Covered Expenses page
rules.source_title: Nevada VOCP Benefits and Covered Expenses page

params.exception: or more for a catastrophic injury

rules.summary: Program policy sets the claim limit at $35,000 per approved claim. For catastrophic injuries, the VOCP Coordinator may approve a higher limit.
rules.quote: The claim limit established by these policies is $35,000 per approved claim except in cases of catastrophic injuries, where limits may be extended upon approval of the VOCP Coordinator.
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 500.12(A)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: The program's current application instructions say that in general the total award cannot go over $35,000, but some services, such as counseling and crime scene cleanup, may be paid beyond that amount.
rules.quote: In general, the total award cannot exceed $35,000, although some services— such as counseling and crime-scene cleanup—may be covered beyond that amount.
rules.pinpoint: Application Instructions, Expenses That May Be Covered
rules.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation Instructions and form (2026)

rules.summary: Medical and medically related expenses caused by the crime can be paid up to $35,000 (inside the same $35,000 claim limit).
rules.quote: The Victims of Crime Program may pay up to $35,000 for medical and medically related expenses caused by a crime
rules.pinpoint: Coverage Limits for Service Providers: Medical Service Providers
rules.source_title: Nevada VOCP Coverage Limits for Service Providers page

rules.summary: Dental treatment for crime injuries can be paid up to $35,000 (inside the same $35,000 claim limit).
rules.quote: The VOCP may pay up to $35,000 for treatment of dental, myofacial, temporomandibular, and other conditions and injuries caused by a crime
rules.pinpoint: Coverage Limits for Service Providers: Dental Service Providers
rules.source_title: Nevada VOCP Coverage Limits for Service Providers page

rules.summary: Mental health counseling is paid up to $5,000.
rules.quote: The VOCP pays up to $5,000 in mental health counseling for qualified victims.
rules.pinpoint: Coverage Limits for Service Providers: Mental Health Providers
rules.source_title: Nevada VOCP Coverage Limits for Service Providers page

rules.summary: Lost earnings can be paid at up to 100 percent of gross pay, capped at $350 per week for up to 52 weeks.
rules.quote: Loss of earnings may be paid at up to 100 percent of the victim's gross pay, up to a maximum of $350 per week, not to exceed 52 weeks, or up to a maximum of $18,200.
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 400.8(B)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: Total lost earnings are capped at $18,200.
rules.quote: Loss of earnings may be paid at up to 100 percent of the victim's gross pay, up to a maximum of $350 per week, not to exceed 52 weeks, or up to a maximum of $18,200.
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 400.8(B)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: Short work absences (up to 10 working days) can be paid at $70 a day, up to $700.
rules.quote: A Compensation Officer may approve lost wage or income reimbursement claims for temporary crime disabilities or work interruptions lasting up to ten (10) working days, or up to $700 at the rate of $70/day.
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 400.7(A)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: All relocation expenses together are capped at $2,500 per claim.
rules.quote: The total amount for all relocation expenses cannot exceed $2,500 per claim
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 400.9(E)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: Within the relocation limit, temporary lodging is capped at $500.
rules.quote: Temporary lodging expenses of no more than $500
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 400.9(E)(3)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: Repairing or improving home security for the survivor's safety can be reimbursed up to $1,500.
rules.quote: A victim may be eligible to receive reimbursement of up to $1,500 for repairing or improving residential security when necessary for the victim's personal safety and related to the crime for which the victim is approved.
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 400.11(A)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: Childcare caused by the crime is capped at $2,500 per crime for all children together.
rules.quote: The total benefit available for all affected children, per crime, may not exceed $2,500.
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 400.12(A)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: Prescriptions prescribed for up to 6 months after the crime can be paid back, up to $6,000. More time can be approved 90 days at a time, with medical records showing the medicine is needed.
rules.quote: The VOCP may reimburse applicant for prescription medications prescribed for up to 6 months after the crime. Additional time limits may be authorized for 90-day intervals with accompanying medical documentation provided to indicate that prescriptions are medically necessary. The VOCP may reimburse up to a maximum of $6,000 for prescription medication during this time.
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 400.5(A)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is paid up to $5,000.

rules.quote: Funeral expenses that are actually and reasonably incurred as a result of the death of the victim

Narrow exceptions appear elsewhere in program text: medically necessary items such as eyeglasses or dentures lost, stolen or broken in the crime can be paid as medical expenses, and the current application instructions list limited property damage for qualifying hate crimes.

rules.summary: Apply no later than 60 months after the injury. The Director or a designee may waive the deadline for good cause.
rules.quote: (a) Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b), not later than 60 months after the injury or death for which compensation is claimed
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

params.extension: good_cause

rules.summary: If the survivor was a minor when injured, the deadline is 60 months after turning 21.
rules.quote: (b) If the applicant was a minor at the time of the injury, not later than 60 months after the applicant reaches 21 years of age.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

params.extension: good_cause

rules.summary: The filing deadline can be waived for good cause.
rules.quote: The Director or a person designated by the Director may waive the limitation on time described in subsection 1 for good cause shown.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

rules.summary: Eligibility can be shown with documents other than a police report, such as a protective order, court testimony, a government record, a record from a victim services organization, or an affidavit from a qualified third party (the statute lists licensed clinicians and victim advocates).
rules.quote: (b) A police report, investigative report or complaint which the victim filed with a law enforcement agency; (c) A copy of an order for protection; (d) A transcript of testimony given under oath or affirmation in a civil or criminal proceeding; (e) A record of a governmental entity; (f) A record from an organization which provides services to victims of crime; (g) An affidavit of a qualified third party; or (h) Other documentary evidence deemed sufficient by the Director.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

rules.summary: The program's current application instructions say law enforcement reports are not required for eligibility. The same document's eligibility list still says the crime was reported to law enforcement or another appropriate authority, and its form accepts advocate statements, medical or counseling records, protective orders, professional statements and other official records as proof.
rules.quote: I understand that law enforcement reports are not required for eligibility.
rules.pinpoint: Application Instructions, Authorization 1: Law Enforcement Reports
rules.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation Instructions and form (2026)

rules.summary: Program policy lets a claim be approved without a police report when a sexual assault survivor had a forensic exam, as long as there is enough documentation that a crime happened.
rules.quote: when a sexual assault victim submits to a forensic examination but does not file a law enforcement report, the Compensation Officer may approve the claim without a crime report as long as there is sufficient documentation that a crime was committed against the applicant.
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 300.12(C)(1)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: Money received or likely to be received from the offender, insurance, an employer, or public programs is subtracted from the survivor's total expenses.
rules.quote: The compensation officer shall deduct the amounts that the applicant has received or is likely to receive from those sources from the applicant's total expenses.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

rules.summary: The program is the payer of last resort and considers insurance, restitution, and other payments before deciding an award.
rules.quote: The Victims Compensation Program is the payer of last resort. This means we must consider payments from other sources, such as insurance or restitution, before determining your award.
rules.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation Instructions and form (2026)

rules.summary: In general, compensation is awarded unless the injury was substantially caused or provoked by the victim's own wrongful act.
rules.quote: the compensation officer shall award compensation unless the injury or death of the victim was substantially attributable to a wrongful act of the victim or substantially provoked by the victim.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

rules.summary: In sexual assault cases the compensation officer may not consider the victim's behavior at all when deciding the claim.
rules.quote: If the case involves a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, facilitating sex trafficking or sex trafficking, the compensation officer shall not consider the wrongful act, provocation or any other behavior of the victim that directly or indirectly contributed to the injury or death of the victim.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

rules.summary: Sexual assault (including spousal rape) is a qualifying crime under program policy.
rules.quote: Sexual Assault or Spousal Rape: NRS 200.366
rules.pinpoint: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime 200.2(A)
rules.source_title: Nevada State Plan for Services for Victims of Crime (VOCP policies, July 1, 2020)

rules.summary: The program's eligibility page lists sexual assault among the crimes it can help with.
rules.quote: The VOCP can help victims for crimes such as: Assault/Battery Child abuse Domestic violence Drunk driving Elder abuse Homicide Physical abuse Sexual assault
rules.source_title: Nevada VOCP Eligibility Criteria page

params.rule: Crime in Nevada: residents and nonresidents may apply on the same terms.

rules.summary: A victim of a crime in Nevada who does not live in Nevada can apply the same way a resident can.
rules.quote: A victim of a crime that occurred in this State who is not a resident of this State may apply to the Director for compensation in the same manner as a resident of this State.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

params.rule: Nevada residents hurt in another state may apply only if that state has no program or they are ineligible there.

rules.summary: A Nevada resident victimized in another state can apply to Nevada if that state has no compensation program or the resident is not eligible under it.
rules.quote: A resident who is a victim of a crime that occurred in a state other than the State of Nevada may apply to the Director for compensation if: (a) The state in which the crime occurred does not have a program for compensating victims of crime for their injuries; or (b) The resident is ineligible to receive compensation under the program of the other state.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

params.rule: Citizenship and immigration status do not matter.

rules.summary: A person harmed by a covered act counts as a victim whether or not they are a Nevada resident, a U.S. citizen, or lawfully in the U.S.
rules.quote: The term includes any person who was harmed by an act listed in subsection 1, regardless of whether: (a) The person is a resident of this State, a citizen of the United States or is lawfully entitled to reside in the United States;
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026
