rules.quote: We need documentation that a crime occurred. Check all that you have or can provide.
rules.pinpoint: 2026 application, Section 2: How can we verify the crime occurred?
rules.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation Instructions and form (2026)

rules.summary: Unless the claim is denied at first review, the compensation officer must decide it within 60 days after receiving the application.
rules.quote: the compensation officer shall conduct an investigation and, except as otherwise provided in subsection 6, render a decision within 60 days after receipt of the application or order.
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

params.agency: Nevada Division of Child and Family Services
params.enroll: Applicants do not enroll or apply directly with the Nevada Confidential Address Program. Any person interested in applying to the program must meet in person with a CAP Certified Advocate. Certified Advocates are located throughout the state in agencies and non-profit programs that provide counseling, referral, shelter, or assistance to victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking and stalking.

rules.summary: Nevada's Confidential Address Program, run by the Division of Child and Family Services, helps victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, human trafficking, or stalking keep the person who hurt them from finding them through public records. If your application is approved, you get a fictitious address to use instead of your home, work, or school address, and the program forwards your mail at no cost. To apply, you need specific evidence that you were a victim, and you apply in person through a CAP Certified Advocate, not directly with the program.
rules.quote: The Nevada Confidential Address Program (CAP) is a program that helps victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking and/or stalking from being located by the perpetrator through public records. The program provides a fictitious address and confidential mail forwarding services to individuals and families across Nevada.
rules.pinpoint: DCFS Confidential Address Program page, 'About the Confidential Address Program'
rules.source_title: Nevada DCFS Confidential Address Program page

rules.summary: Information a compensation officer gathers while investigating a claim, and information submitted with an application, is confidential. It may be disclosed only at the applicant's or their attorney's request, as needed to run the program, or under a court order.
rules.quote: Any information which a compensation officer obtains in the investigation of a claim for compensation pursuant to NRS 217.090 or which is submitted pursuant to NRS 217.100 is confidential and must not be disclosed except
rules.source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

rules.summary: The provider must accept the OVS exam fee as payment in full and may not bill the survivor for the forensic exam services.
rules.quote: The hospital, sexual assault examiner program, or licensed health care provider must accept this fee as payment in full for these specified services. No additional billing of the survivor for said services is permissible.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: Private insurance can be used for the exam only if the survivor chooses to assign it, and then the survivor owes no deductible, coinsurance, or balance bill.
rules.quote: A sexual assault survivor may voluntarily assign any private insurance benefits to which they are entitled for the healthcare forensic examination, in which case the hospital or healthcare provider may not charge the office; provided, however, in the event the sexual assault survivor assigns any private health insurance benefit, such coverage shall not be subject to annual deductibles or coinsurance or balance billing by the hospital, sexual assault examiner program or licensed health care provider.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: Hospitals must make sure survivors are not billed for forensic exams and must tell them, orally and in writing, they can decline to give insurance information and have OVS pay instead.
rules.quote: ensuring sexual assault survivors are not billed for sexual assault forensic exams and are notified orally and in writing of the option to decline to provide private health insurance information and have the office of victim services reimburse the hospital for the exam
rules.source_title: N.Y. Public Health Law 2805-i (Treatment of sexual offense victims)

rules.summary: A provider that accepts OVS payment for the exam takes it as payment in full and may not bill the survivor for the difference between its charges and what OVS paid.
rules.quote: The billing provider may not bill victims/survivors or their guardians for the difference between charged amounts and the amount reimbursed by OVS.
rules.pinpoint: OVS FRE Provider Billing Manual (March 2026), III.c Reimbursement Rates
rules.source_title: OVS Forensic Rape Exam Direct Reimbursement Program Provider Billing Manual (March 2026, Version 2.0)

params.payer: New York State Office of Victim Services (direct reimbursement to the provider)

rules.summary: The hospital or provider gives sexual assault survivors exam services free of charge and bills the Office of Victim Services directly.
rules.quote: such hospital, sexual assault examiner program, or licensed healthcare provider shall provide such services to the person without charge and shall bill the office directly.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

params.payer: New York State Office of Victim Services

rules.summary: OVS pays the medical provider directly for the exam when the survivor has no private insurance or chooses not to use it.
rules.quote: OVS can directly reimburse medical providers for forensic rape exams when sexual assault survivors do not have private health insurance or choose not to use their insurance.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Forensic Rape Exam Direct Reimbursement Program page
rules.source_title: OVS Forensic Rape Exam (FRE) Direct Reimbursement Program

params.payer: OVS pays only for exam-related services and medicines under the exam claim

rules.summary: OVS direct payment covers only services and medicines related to the forensic exam.
rules.quote: Only services and pharmaceuticals that are related to the forensic rape exam may be reimbursed under an FRE claim.
rules.pinpoint: OVS FRE Provider Billing Manual (March 2026), III Reimbursement
rules.source_title: OVS Forensic Rape Exam Direct Reimbursement Program Provider Billing Manual (March 2026, Version 2.0)

rules.summary: Out-of-pocket costs a sex offense victim (Penal Law article 130) incurs for a hospital or medical exam tied to the investigation or prosecution are covered.
rules.quote: an award shall include out-of-pocket expenses, including indebtedness reasonably incurred by the victim of a sex offense or the person responsible for the victim of such sex offense, as such sex offense is defined in article one hundred thirty of the penal law, for a hospital or medical examination in connection with the investigation or prosecution of any such offense.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: Unreimbursed medical care and other necessary services caused by the injury count as out-of-pocket loss.
rules.quote: Out-of-pocket loss shall mean unreimbursed and unreimbursable expenses or indebtedness reasonably incurred for medical care or other services necessary as a result of the injury upon which such claim is based
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 626 (Out-of-pocket loss; definition)

rules.summary: Counseling is covered for physically injured crime victims and their spouse, children, or stepchildren (sex offense victims are presumed physically injured).
rules.quote: Such expenses or indebtedness shall include the cost of counseling for the eligible spouse, domestic partner, grandparents, parents, stepparents, guardians, brothers, sisters, stepbrothers, stepsisters, children, stepchildren or grandchildren of a homicide victim, and crime victims who have sustained a personal physical injury as the direct result of a crime and the spouse, children or stepchildren of such physically injured victim.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 626 (Out-of-pocket loss; definition)

params.scope: trips to necessary medical care caused by the crime

rules.summary: Reasonable travel to crime-related medical care is covered, with receipts for fares or the federal mileage rate for driving yourself.
rules.quote: medical expenses shall also include the reasonable transportation expenses incurred for necessary, causally related medical care which may include, but are not limited to, reasonable airplane, cab, bus or train fare, with receipts, or if a claimant has provided his or her own transportation, the federally recognized mileage reimbursement rate at the time the expense was incurred
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.3 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

params.scope: trips to court for the prosecution

rules.summary: Reasonable transportation to necessary court appearances in the prosecution is covered.
rules.quote: an award shall include reasonable transportation expenses incurred for necessary court appearances in connection with the prosecution of such crimes upon which the claim is based.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

params.scope: new or better security devices, if a doctor, counselor, or the district attorney says your health is in imminent danger without them

rules.summary: New or enhanced security devices can be covered when a physician, counselor, or the district attorney states the claimant's health is in imminent danger without the device.
rules.quote: In order for the costs associated with new or enhanced security devices, beyond those which, pursuant to the Executive Law are repaired or replaced under subdivision 2 of section 631, or are awarded under subdivision 12 of section 631 , to be compensable, the office shall require a statement from the claimant's physician or counselor, or the district attorney handling the victim's case, indicating that without the aid of such a device the claimant's health is in imminent danger.
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.scope: moving when it is necessary for your health or safety

rules.summary: Relocation costs are covered when moving is necessary for the victim's health or safety.
rules.quote: "Relocation expenses" shall mean the cost of relocating a crime victim, when relocation is necessary for the health or safety of the victim.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

params.scope: belongings needed for your health, welfare, or safety

rules.summary: Only essential personal property counts: belongings needed for the victim's health, welfare, or safety.
rules.quote: "Essential personal property" shall mean articles of personal property necessary and essential to the health, welfare or safety of the victim.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Lost earnings or support are capped at $30,000.
rules.quote: loss of earnings or support resulting from such injury not to exceed thirty thousand dollars
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: Lost earnings or support are paid at no more than $600 per week.
rules.quote: no such award shall exceed six hundred dollars for each week of lost earnings or support.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: Relocation expenses are capped at $2,500.
rules.quote: reasonable relocation expenses not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

params.scope: employment_related_only

rules.summary: Employment-related transportation (extra cost of getting to work because of crime injuries) is capped at $2,500. Medical and court travel are not under this cap.
rules.quote: reasonable employment-related transportation expenses, not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup and securing a crime scene (for example repairing doors, windows, and locks) are capped at $2,500.
rules.quote: the costs of crime scene cleanup and securing of a crime scene not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: Repair or replacement of essential personal property is capped at $2,500, with cash losses limited to $100.
rules.quote: Any award made for the cost of repair or replacement of essential personal property, including cash losses of essential personal property, shall be limited to an amount of twenty-five hundred dollars, except that all cash losses of essential personal property shall be limited to the amount of one hundred dollars.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

params.item: items related to the victim's ability to communicate

rules.summary: Essential property related to the victim's ability to communicate is paid at the receipted amount, up to $1,500 per item.
rules.quote: All awards made pursuant to Executive Law article 22 and this Part related to a victim's ability to communicate shall be limited to the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding one-thousand five-hundred dollars per item.
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.item: items for the safe operation of the victim's personal means of transportation

rules.summary: Essential property related to safely operating the victim's own means of transportation is paid at the receipted amount, up to $2,500 per item.
rules.quote: All awards made pursuant to Executive Law article 22 and this Part related to a victim's safe operation of their personal means of transportation shall be limited to the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding two-thousand five-hundred dollars per item.
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.item: medically necessary life-sustaining equipment

rules.summary: Medically necessary life-sustaining equipment lost or damaged in the crime has its own cap of $10,000 instead of the general essential property cap.
rules.quote: In the case of medically necessary life-sustaining equipment which was lost or damaged as the direct result of a crime, the award shall be limited to the amount of ten thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

params.item: outerwear, suits and footwear

rules.summary: Outerwear, suits, and footwear are paid at the receipted amount, up to $500 per item.
rules.quote: Items of outerwear, suits and footwear shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding five-hundred dollars per item.
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.item: clothing other than outerwear, suits and footwear

rules.summary: Other clothing is paid at the receipted amount, up to $100 per item.
rules.quote: All other items of clothing shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding one-hundred dollars per item.
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.item: mattress and platform or box spring

rules.summary: A mattress and platform or box spring are paid at the receipted amount, up to $2,000.
rules.quote: Mattress and platform or box spring shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding two-thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.item: bedding other than mattress and box spring

rules.summary: Other bedding is paid at the receipted amount, up to $500 in total.
rules.quote: All other items of bedding shall be the receipted amount, in a cumulative amount not exceeding five-hundred dollars.
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

rules.summary: Attorney fees for representation before OVS or on judicial review are capped at $1,000.
rules.quote: the cost of reasonable attorneys' fees for representation before the office and/or before the appellate division upon judicial review not to exceed one thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 626 (Out-of-pocket loss; definition)

params.item: periodic monitoring or maintenance charges for security devices

rules.summary: For security devices, only the device and installation are covered; monitoring and maintenance fees are not.
rules.quote: Compensable costs shall be limited to the devices themselves and their installation, and shall not include the periodic service charges for monitoring or maintaining any such devices.
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.item: meals during travel

rules.summary: Meals during travel for medical care are not reimbursed as transportation.
rules.quote: Meals shall not be considered a related transportation expense.
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.3 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

params.item: purchase, lease or rental of a vehicle

rules.summary: Employment-related transportation does not cover buying, leasing, or renting a vehicle.
rules.quote: Such costs shall not include the purchase, lease or rental of a vehicle.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

params.extension: or of when the crime was discovered, or later if OVS finds good cause

rules.summary: File within 3 years of the crime or its discovery; OVS may extend this for good cause.
rules.quote: A claim must be filed by the claimant not later than three years after the occurrence or discovery of the crime upon which such claim is based, three years after a court finds a lawsuit to be frivolous, or not later than three years after the death of the victim, provided, however, that upon good cause shown, the office may extend the time for filing.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 625 (Filing of claims)

params.extension: good reasons, including not knowing compensation existed or not knowing you may be eligible

rules.summary: Even after 3 years, OVS can waive the deadline for good reasons, such as not knowing the program existed or not knowing you were eligible.
rules.quote: Please keep in mind that even if it has been more than three years, OVS has the ability to waive this requirement if the claimant or victim/survivor can show they had good reasons for not filing a claim within that timeframe. Good reasons can include, but are not limited to not knowing that victim compensation existed, or not knowing that they may be eligible for compensation.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Compensation Program Updates for Victims and Survivors, Timely Filing
rules.source_title: OVS Compensation Program Updates for Victims and Survivors

rules.summary: A police report is not required. The crime must have been reported, but records of a support agency for survivors of crime can show this instead of police records.
rules.quote: the records of a support agency for survivors of crime or the records of a criminal justice agency show that such crime was reported.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: A medical facility that provides forensic exams for rape and sexual assault counts as a support agency, so its records can stand in for a police report.
rules.quote: any medical facility established under the laws of the state that provides a forensic physical examination for victims of rape and sexual assault
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: For sex offenses, a family court also counts as a support agency.
rules.quote: in cases involving any sex offense or family offense a support agency for survivors of crime shall also include a family court
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: Since December 31, 2025, a victim service provider or a medical or mental health professional can fill out a Crime Verification Form instead of a police report.
rules.quote: Starting December 31, 2025, instead of filing a report with law enforcement, you can go to a local victim service provider , or a medical or mental health professional, and tell them that you or a loved one experienced a crime. The provider can fill out a short form to tell OVS about the crime.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Compensation Program Updates for Victims and Survivors, Reporting a Crime
rules.source_title: OVS Compensation Program Updates for Victims and Survivors

rules.summary: Under the statute, when the victim cannot report to or cooperate with police because of age, physical or psychological state, cultural or language barriers, or another health or safety concern, a court that issued a restraining or protective order, a contracted victim services provider, or a licensed medical or mental health provider also counts as a support agency.
rules.quote: in cases where a physically injured claimant and/or victim is unable to report to or otherwise cooperate with a criminal justice agency because of the victim's age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or linguistic barriers, or any other health or safety concern that jeopardizes the victim's wellbeing, a support agency for survivors of crime shall also include: (A) a court which issued a temporary or permanent restraining order or protective order against the party or parties alleged to have committed the crime against the victim, or (B) a "victim services provider"
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by payments from the offender, mandated insurance, public funds, the claimant's own insurance, and any emergency award.
rules.quote: Any award made pursuant to this article shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received by the claimant as a result of the injury (a) from or on behalf of the person who committed the crime, (b) under insurance programs mandated by law, (c) from public funds, (d) under any contract of insurance wherein the claimant is the insured or beneficiary, (e) as an emergency award pursuant to section six hundred thirty of this article.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: OVS pays last: insurance or benefit plans must be billed first. The forensic exam has its own billing rules, shown in the exam section.
rules.quote: OVS is the payer of last resort and can only consider your out-of-pocket loss. OVS can only process payments for crime-related expenses. You must bill your insurance company or benefits plan before OVS can pay.
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

rules.summary: OVS considers whether the victim's own conduct contributed to the injury and can reduce or deny the award on that basis.
rules.quote: the office shall determine whether, because of such victim's conduct, the victim of such crime contributed to the infliction of such victim's injury, and the office shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether, in accordance with such determination.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rules.summary: Being a victim of sexual assault is a mitigating factor, and OVS may then make the award with no conduct reduction.
rules.quote: However, when considering conduct contributing the office shall examine the following mitigating factors: the victim was a minor, a victim of human trafficking, a sex worker, or a victim of sexual assault. If any such mitigating factors are found in the investigation of the claim pursuant to subdivision (b) of section 525.5 of this part, the office may make an award without reduction for conduct contributing.
rules.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

rules.summary: When an award is likely and waiting would cause undue hardship, OVS can make emergency awards totaling up to $2,500, which are later deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: the office may make one or more emergency awards to the claimant pending a final decision of the office or payment of an award in the case, provided, however, that the total amount of such emergency awards shall not exceed twenty-five hundred dollars.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 630 (Emergency awards)

rules.summary: Victims of sex offenses under Penal Law article 130 are presumed to have suffered physical injury, which is the usual gateway to compensation.
rules.quote: For the purposes of this subdivision, the victim of a sex offense as defined in article one hundred thirty of the penal law is presumed to have suffered physical injury.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 626 (Out-of-pocket loss; definition)

params.rule: Crime committed in New York State

rules.summary: Acts committed in New York count as crimes for compensation whether or not anyone was arrested, charged, or prosecuted, and whether or not the claimant dealt with police.
rules.quote: an act committed in New York state which would, if committed by a mentally competent criminally responsible adult, who has no legal exemption or defense, constitute a crime as defined in and proscribed by law, regardless of whether any suspect was arrested, charged, apprehended or prosecuted for the commission of the act or whether the claimant has interacted with a criminal justice agency investigating such act
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

params.rule: New York residents victimized in a state without an eligible compensation program

rules.summary: A New York resident hurt by a crime in another state can apply only if that state has no eligible compensation program.
rules.quote: an act committed outside the state of New York against a resident of the state of New York which would be compensable had it occurred within the state of New York and which occurred in a state which does not have an eligible crime victim compensation program
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

params.target: NYS Office of Victim Services, AE Smith Building, 80 S. Swan Street, Albany, NY 12210-8002

rules.summary: A paper application and documents can be mailed to the OVS office in Albany.
rules.quote: Mailing Address: NYS Office of Victim Services AE Smith Building 80 S. Swan Street Albany, NY 12210-8002
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, OVS Contact Information
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

rules.summary: The application and supporting documents can be emailed to the OVS intake address.
rules.quote: Email applications and documents to: OVSIntake@ovs.ny.gov
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, OVS Contact Information
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

rules.summary: A claim can be filed online through the OVS Compass Applicant Portal, as a guest or with a NY.gov account.
rules.quote: Yes, you can visit https://ovs.ny.gov/ to access the secure OVS Compass Applicant Portal, or Victim Advocate Portal, and file an application online.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 1, FAQ: Is there another way to apply?
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params.note: all bills and receipts for the crime-related goods and services claimed

rules.summary: Include all bills and receipts for the expenses described in the application.
rules.quote: All bills and receipts for expenses related to goods and services you described in this application.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params.note: the same instruction asks for all bills, not only receipts

rules.summary: Include the bills for the crime-related goods and services claimed.
rules.quote: All bills and receipts for expenses related to goods and services you described in this application.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params.note: HIPAA release form, one per medical or mental health provider; a blank copy is at the end of the application

rules.summary: Include one completed HIPAA authorization for each medical and mental health provider seen for crime-related care.
rules.quote: One completed HIPAA form for each medical and mental health provider you saw for services related to this crime.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params.note: letters from insurers or government agencies denying or approving payment

rules.summary: Include any letters from insurance companies or government agencies that denied or authorized payment for the claimed expenses.
rules.quote: Letters from any insurance or government agencies denying or authorizing payments related to goods and services you described in this application.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params.note: crime verification: one third-party document, such as a Crime Verification Form from a victim service provider or a medical or mental health professional

rules.summary: Only one third-party document confirming the crime is needed, and a Crime Verification Form from a victim service provider or medical or mental health professional works.
rules.quote: You only need to submit one document showing OVS that a third-party has confirmed that you or the victim/survivor experienced a crime. You can speak to a victim service provider or medical or mental health professional, and they can fill out a Crime Verification Form.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 9, Supporting Documentation for Crime Verification
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params.note: optional; a police or other criminal justice agency report is one way to verify the crime, not the only way

rules.summary: A police or other criminal justice agency report can be submitted as the crime verification document, but it is a choice.
rules.quote: You may also choose to report the crime to law enforcement and submit a criminal justice agency report, like a police report, as part of this application.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 9, Supporting Documentation for Crime Verification
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params.note: optional; the applicant can choose to use the forensic rape exam report as part of the application

rules.summary: If a forensic rape exam was done, the survivor can choose to use the exam report in the application.
rules.quote: If an FRE was performed, do you want to use the report as part of your application?
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 10, Medical Care
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params.note: Workers' Compensation or disability insurance decision letter, only if the victim has that coverage

rules.summary: If the victim has Workers' Compensation or disability insurance coverage, OVS needs that provider's decision letter.
rules.quote: If the victim has coverage through either Worker's Compensation or a Disability Insurance provider, OVS will need the decision letter from either Worker's Compensation or the Disability Insurance provider to help determine eligibility for compensation.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 16, Workers Compensation/Disability
rules.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params.agency: New York Department of State (Secretary of State)
params.enroll: You may apply online or by completing a pdf application. Completed applications may either be mailed or faxed. Filing instructions are on the form. (DOS ACP: (518) 474-7306, toll-free (855) 350-4595, Address Confidentiality Program, P.O. Box 1110, Albany, NY 12201-1110, fax (518) 474-0709.)

rules.summary: The Department of State runs an Address Confidentiality Program that gives eligible victims, including victims of a sexual offense, a designated substitute address to use instead of their real address, with free mail forwarding.
rules.quote: There is created in the office of the secretary of state a program to be known as the "address confidentiality program" to protect victims of domestic violence, victims of human trafficking, victims of kidnapping, victims of a sexual offense, victims of stalking, and reproductive health care services providers, employees, volunteers, patients, or immediate family members of reproductive health care services providers by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims and their minor children.
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 108 (Address confidentiality program)

rules.summary: OVS records and proceedings on a victim's or claimant's compensation claim are confidential and are not shared with government or private entities, except for listed purposes such as criminal justice requests, judicial subpoenas, the claimant's own requests, and program administration.
rules.quote: Records maintained by the office and proceedings by the office based thereon regarding a claim submitted by a victim or a claimant shall be deemed confidential and shall not be shared with any government or private entity, with the following exceptions:
rules.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 633 (Confidentiality of records)

params.scope: the exam and tests done to gather evidence
params.condition: if the crime was in Ohio

rules.summary: Hospitals may not bill a survivor of a sex crime under Ohio law, or the survivor's insurance, for the medical exam and tests done to gather evidence. The rule covers only that evidence exam, not other care at the same visit.
rules.quote: No costs incurred by a hospital or emergency facility in conducting a medical examination and test of any victim of an offense under any provision of sections 2907.02 to 2907.06 of the Revised Code for the purpose of gathering physical evidence for a possible prosecution of a person shall be billed or charged directly or indirectly to the victim or the victim's insurer.
rules.source_title: ORC 2907.28 (payment for sexual assault medical examination)

params.payer: Ohio reparations fund, paid by the Attorney General (SAFE Program) directly to the hospital or facility

rules.summary: The state reparations fund pays the hospital for the forensic exam, including antibiotics and HIV post-exposure prophylaxis given as part of the exam.
rules.quote: Any cost incurred by a hospital or emergency medical facility in conducting a medical examination of a victim of an offense under any provision of sections 2907.02 to 2907.06 of the Revised Code for the purpose of gathering physical evidence for a possible prosecution, including the cost of any antibiotics administered as part of the examination and the cost of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis provided as part of the examination, shall be paid out of the reparations fund established pursuant to section 2743.191 of the Revised Code
rules.source_title: ORC 2907.28 (payment for sexual assault medical examination)

params.payer: Ohio Attorney General SAFE Program (flat fee to the facility)

rules.summary: The hospital must accept a flat fee of $632 from the state as payment in full for the forensic exam, including antibiotics given during it.
rules.quote: A hospital, children's advocacy center, or other emergency medical facility shall accept a flat fee payment of: (A) Six hundred thirty-two dollars as payment in full for any cost incurred in conducting a medical examination and test of a victim of an offense under any provision of sections 2907.02 to 2907.06 of the Revised Code for the purpose of gathering physical evidence for a possible prosecution of a person, including the cost of any antibiotics administered as part of the examination.
rules.source_title: OAC 109:7-1-02 (sexual assault examination payment amount)

params.payer: Ohio Attorney General SAFE Program

rules.summary: Payment for the forensic exam does not depend on the survivor cooperating with police.
rules.quote: The sexual assault forensic exam and reimbursement is not dependent on the patient cooperating with law enforcement.
rules.pinpoint: SAFE Reimbursement Instructions, item 12 (Law enforcement reporting)
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

params.payer: Ohio Attorney General SAFE Program

rules.summary: If an adult patient does not report to police and asks to stay fully anonymous, the provider can send the exam's payment form as Jane or John Doe.
rules.quote: If the adult patient chooses not to report to law enforcement and asks that their identity be kept completely confidential, a reimbursement form submitted on behalf of “Jane/John Doe” is an acceptable submission.
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

params.payer: Patient, when an adult's last incident was more than 96 hours before the exam

rules.summary: For an adult, the Attorney General's billing instructions list the exam procedures as billable to the patient when the last incident was more than 96 hours before the exam.
rules.quote: Last incident(s) greater than 96 hours**** - procedures billable to patient
rules.pinpoint: SAFE Reimbursement Instructions, mandated examination components table (18 and over); see item 9
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

params.payer: Ohio Attorney General SAFE Program, for evidence collected after 96 hours when justified; payment not guaranteed

rules.summary: The instructions say evidence should sometimes be collected more than 96 hours after the assault, for example when the patient was unconscious. The provider must explain why, and that does not guarantee the SAFE Program will pay.
rules.quote: There are cases in which evidence should be collected beyond 96 hours. Examples include where the patient was unconscious or sedentary or where an exam may corroborate chronic injury or excessive force related to the sexual assault. Documentation must clearly justify the reasoning for the forensic collection as it relates to the sexual assault. Documentation does not guarantee payment by the SAFE Program.
rules.pinpoint: SAFE Reimbursement Instructions, item 9 (Date/Time of Abuse/Assault)
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

params.payer: Patient or insurer (emergency contraception given at the exam)

rules.summary: Emergency contraception given to an adult or adolescent at the sexual assault exam is not part of the state-paid exam and can be billed to the patient or the patient's insurer.
rules.quote: If an adult/adolescent patient presenting in the emergency department as a victim of sexual assault is provided emergency contraception those costs are billable to the patient/insurer
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

params.payer: Ohio Attorney General SAFE Program (HIV post-exposure prophylaxis, actual amount billed up to the cap)

rules.summary: The facility is paid the actual amount billed for HIV post-exposure prophylaxis, up to $2,500, as payment in full.
rules.quote: (B) A hospital, children's advocacy center, or other emergency medical facility shall accept payment of the actual amount billed; not to exceed twenty-five hundred dollars, as payment in full for any cost incurred in administration of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis protocol in rule 109:7-1-01 of the Administrative Code.
rules.source_title: OAC 109:7-1-02 (sexual assault examination payment amount)

rules.summary: Total compensation for an injured victim, together with everyone else claiming for that victim's injury, is capped at $50,000.
rules.quote: Reparations payable to a victim described in division (L)(1) of section 2743.51 of the Revised Code and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to or the death of that victim shall not exceed fifty thousand dollars in the aggregate.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

params.applies_to: an immediate family member who lived with a sexual assault victim and needs counseling, not the victim

rules.summary: An immediate family member living with a sexual assault victim can claim counseling on their own, capped at $5,000; for this kind of claimant counseling is the only payable expense.
rules.quote: Reparations payable to a victim described in division (L)(2) of section 2743.51 of the Revised Code shall not exceed five thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "an immediate family member who lived with a sexual assault victim and needs counseling, not the victim"

rules.summary: Cleanup of the crime scene and repairs to damaged property for personal security (for example doors and windows) are capped at $750 per claim.
rules.quote: (2) Reasonable and necessary costs of cleaning the scene and repairing, for the purpose of personal security, property damaged at the scene where the criminally injurious conduct occurred, not to exceed seven hundred fifty dollars in the aggregate per claim.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params.item: replacing property police took as evidence

rules.summary: Replacing property that police took as evidence (such as a phone or clothing) is capped at $750 per claim.
rules.quote: (U) "Cost of evidence replacement" means costs for replacement of property confiscated for evidentiary purposes related to the criminally injurious conduct, not to exceed seven hundred fifty dollars in the aggregate per claim.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params.item: lawyer's fees for an order that separates you from the offender

rules.summary: Attorney's fees for successfully getting a restraining order, custody order, or other order that physically separates the victim from the offender are covered up to $1,000, at no more than $100 an hour.
rules.quote: (b) Attorney's fees not exceeding one thousand dollars, at a rate not exceeding one hundred dollars per hour, incurred to successfully obtain a restraining order, custody order, or other order to physically separate a victim from an offender.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params.applies_to: a family member with trauma so severe it keeps them from normal daily activities, such as an immediate family member who cares for a dependent sexual assault victim, not the victim

rules.summary: A family member with trauma so severe it keeps them from normal daily activities, including an immediate family member who is the caretaker of a dependent sexual assault victim, can claim only work loss and counseling, capped at $15,000.
rules.quote: Reparations payable to a victim described in division (L)(3) of section 2743.51 of the Revised Code shall not exceed fifteen thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "a family member with trauma so severe it keeps them from normal daily activities, such as an immediate family member who cares for a dependent sexual assault victim, not the victim"

rules.summary: Medical care, rehabilitation, and other remedial treatment are allowable expenses for an injured victim.
rules.quote: "allowable expense" means reasonable charges incurred for reasonably needed products, services, and accommodations, including those for medical care, rehabilitation, rehabilitative occupational training, and other remedial treatment and care
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params.scope: replacing dentures, hearing aids, eyeglasses, and mobility aids

rules.summary: Replacement of dentures, retainers, and other dental appliances is an allowable expense, along with hearing aids, mobility aids, and eyeglasses.
rules.quote: including replacement costs for hearing aids; dentures, retainers, and other dental appliances; canes, walkers, and other mobility tools; and eyeglasses and other corrective lenses
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

rules.summary: The application lets the victim request counseling expenses for themselves.
rules.quote: Counseling expenses for victim
rules.pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Section 4
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

rules.summary: Lost income from work the victim could not do because of the injury is covered as work loss.
rules.quote: (G) "Work loss" means loss of income from work that the injured person would have performed if the person had not been injured
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params.scope: replacing clothing removed to check for or treat injuries

rules.summary: Clothing removed from the victim so injuries could be assessed or treated can be replaced.
rules.quote: (1) The replacement cost for items of clothing removed from a victim in order to make an assessment of possible physical harm or to treat physical harm;
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params.scope: paying someone for child care, housecleaning, or errands the victim would normally do

rules.summary: Replacement services, meaning paying someone to do what the victim would normally do such as child care, housecleaning, or errands, can be claimed.
rules.quote: Replacement services (paying someone to do what the victim would normally do such as housecleaning, child care, errands, etc.)
rules.pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Section 4; see ORC 2743.51(H)
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

params.item: stolen, damaged, or lost property; pain and suffering

rules.summary: The program does not pay for stolen, damaged, or lost property (for example a broken or stolen phone), or for pain and suffering. Property police kept as evidence is handled separately as evidence replacement.
rules.quote: Yes. Compensation cannot be paid for pain and suffering, stolen, damaged, or lost property.
rules.pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, program overview (Are there limits on compensation?)
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

params.item: pain and suffering (noneconomic detriment)

rules.summary: Pain, suffering, and other noneconomic harm are not compensable economic loss.
rules.quote: Noneconomic detriment is not economic loss
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params.extension: or later in some cases

rules.summary: Apply within three years of the crime. Other parts of the law allow more time in some cases.
rules.quote: All applications for an award of reparations may be filed at any time within three years after the occurrence of the criminally injurious conduct, except as provided in divisions (A)(2)(b) to (d) of section 2743.60 of the Revised Code.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.56 (application for award)

rules.summary: If the claimant was under twenty-one when the crime happened, the claim is not time-barred until after the claimant's twenty-fourth birthday.
rules.quote: If the claimant was under twenty-one years of age at the time of the criminally injurious conduct, the claim is not barred under division (A)(2)(a) of this section until after the claimant's twenty-fourth birthday.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

rules.summary: Even after these deadlines, the Attorney General may still make an award at any time for good cause.
rules.quote: (d) Notwithstanding divisions (A)(2)(a), (b), and (c) of this section, the attorney general is permitted to make an award of reparations at any time for good cause shown.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

rules.summary: The crime must have been reported to a law enforcement officer or agency at some point. Without a report, no award can be made.
rules.quote: The attorney general or the court of claims shall not make or order an award of reparations to a claimant if the criminally injurious conduct upon which the claimant bases a claim never was reported to a law enforcement officer or agency.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

rules.summary: The Court of Claims confirms the old 72-hour police report deadline is gone, but a police report is still required.
rules.quote: Although the former 72-hour deadline for filing a police report has been eliminated, the victim must File a police report.
rules.pinpoint: Court of Claims FAQ: Do I need to File a police report in order to qualify for the program?
rules.source_title: Ohio Court of Claims, Crime Victims Compensation page and FAQ

params.scope: what the exam provider must tell police

rules.summary: The Attorney General's billing instructions say Ohio law has health care providers report a sexual assault to police even when the patient does not want to talk to police. If an adult patient stays unnamed, the provider gives police the date, time, and general location of the assault, but not the patient's name or other identifying details.
rules.quote: Law enforcement reporting – Ohio Revised Code (ORC) 2921.22 (A) & (B) (see page 7) requires health care providers report a sexual assault to law enforcement whether a patient chooses to speak with law enforcement or not. If the adult patient chooses to remain unnamed, the provider is mandated to provide the date, time, and general location the assault took place, but not the patient’s name or other identifiers.
rules.pinpoint: SAFE Reimbursement Instructions, item 12 (Law enforcement reporting)
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

rules.summary: The state only pays an award that comes to $50 or more.
rules.quote: The attorney general shall provide for payment of the claimant or providers in the amount of the award only if the amount of the award is fifty dollars or more.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.191 (reparations fund; minimum award payment)

rules.summary: The award is reduced by anything recovered from other sources, such as insurance, so the program pays after those sources.
rules.quote: The attorney general or the court of claims shall reduce an award of reparations or deny a claim for an award of reparations that is otherwise payable to a claimant to the extent that the economic loss upon which the claim is based is recouped from other persons, including collateral sources.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

rules.summary: If a claimant unreasonably fails to file a timely claim with insurance or another source that would have paid, the award can be reduced or denied to that extent.
rules.quote: If a claimant unreasonably fails to present a claim timely to a source of benefits or advantages that would have been a collateral source and that would have reimbursed the claimant for all or a portion of a particular expense, the attorney general or the court of claims may reduce an award of reparations or deny a claim for an award of reparations to the extent that it is reasonable to do so.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

rules.summary: An award can be reduced or denied for contributory misconduct, which the statute defines narrowly as unlawful or intentionally tortious conduct at the time of the crime that caused or threatened serious harm and provoked the crime.
rules.quote: The attorney general or the court of claims shall reduce an award of reparations or deny a claim for an award of reparations to the extent it is determined to be reasonable because of the contributory misconduct of the claimant or the victim.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

rules.summary: An award can be denied or reduced if the victim or claimant did not fully cooperate with law enforcement.
rules.quote: The attorney general or the court of claims, upon a finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies, may deny a claim or reconsider and reduce an award of reparations.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

rules.summary: If a final award looks likely and waiting would cause undue hardship, the Attorney General can make an emergency award of up to $2,000, which is taken out of the final award.
rules.quote: An emergency award shall not exceed two thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.67 (emergency awards)

rules.summary: Ohio covers criminally injurious conduct: conduct in Ohio that poses a substantial threat of personal injury or death and is punishable as a crime. The same statute names sexual assault among the crimes whose family members can claim counseling.
rules.quote: any conduct that occurs or is attempted in this state; poses a substantial threat of personal injury or death; and is punishable by fine, imprisonment, or death
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params.rule: Crime in Ohio: victim must have been a U.S. resident (or a resident of a reciprocal foreign country) at the time of the crime.

rules.summary: For a crime in Ohio, a victim who was a resident of the United States can apply (or a resident of a foreign country that gives Ohio residents reciprocal compensation).
rules.quote: (i) A resident of the United States; (ii) A resident of a foreign country the laws of which permit residents of this state to recover compensation as victims of offenses committed in that country.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params.rule: Crime outside Ohio: Ohio residents who meet one of the conditions in ORC 2743.51(A)(2)(a)(i) to (ix).

rules.summary: An Ohio resident hurt by a crime in another state or country can apply if they also met one listed condition, such as working in Ohio, being a full-time student at a school in another state, or being temporarily out of state for treatment or work.
rules.quote: A victim who had a permanent place of residence within this state at the time of the criminally injurious conduct and who, at the time of the criminally injurious conduct, complied with any one of the following:
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

rules.summary: Register on the Attorney General's Crime Victim's Compensation Portal and file the claim application online.
rules.quote: Register and file a claim application online.
rules.pinpoint: AG Apply for Victims Compensation, Two options for filing a claim
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Apply for Victims Compensation page

params.target: Crime Victim Services Section 30 E. Broad Street, 26th Floor Columbus, OH 43215

rules.summary: Print the paper application, fill it out, and mail it to the Attorney General's Crime Victim Services Section in Columbus.
rules.quote: Download and print an application , fill it out and mail it to Crime Victim Services Section 30 E. Broad Street, 26th Floor Columbus, OH 43215
rules.pinpoint: AG Apply for Victims Compensation, Two options for filing a claim
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Apply for Victims Compensation page

rules.summary: The completed paper application can be faxed to either of the Attorney General's fax numbers.
rules.pinpoint: AG Apply for Victims Compensation, Two options for filing a claim
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Apply for Victims Compensation page

params.note: Attach the application as a PDF or Word document; photos or screenshots of the pages are not accepted.

rules.summary: New applications can be emailed, but only as a PDF or Word attachment; photos or screenshots of the pages are rejected.
rules.quote: New applications can also be emailed to CrimeVictimsCompensationApplications@OhioAGO.gov but they must be attached as a PDF or Word document . No photos or screenshots of the pages will be accepted.
rules.pinpoint: AG Apply for Victims Compensation, Two options for filing a claim
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Apply for Victims Compensation page

params.note: Only when claiming lost wages: copies of the 6 paychecks before the crime.

rules.summary: If claiming lost wages, include copies of the 6 paychecks from before the crime.
rules.quote: Complete if filing for loss of earnings. Provide copies of 6 paychecks prior to crime.
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

params.note: Front and back copy of each insurance or benefit card listed in Section 6.

rules.summary: Send a front and back copy of each insurance or benefit plan card listed on the application.
rules.quote: Please send front and back copy of card
rules.pinpoint: Application, Section 6: Insurance and Benefit Information
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

params.note: The signed and dated release in Section 12 of the application; the two medical record authorizations follow it in the PDF.

rules.summary: The release in the application must be signed and dated, or the application will not be processed.
rules.quote: This release must be signed and dated for the application to be processed.
rules.pinpoint: Application, Section 12: Subrogation, Authorization, and Signature
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

params.note: Only for funeral expense claims: a copy of the death certificate if the applicant has one.

rules.summary: For funeral expense claims, include a copy of the death certificate if you have one.
rules.quote: If you have a copy of the death certificate, please include a copy with your application.
rules.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

rules.summary: The Attorney General must issue a written decision within 120 days after receiving the application, but may extend that limit with written reasons.
rules.quote: The attorney general shall make a written finding of fact and decision in accordance with sections 2743.51 to 2743.72 of the Revised Code within one hundred twenty days after receiving the claim application.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.59 (investigating claim; decision deadline)

params.program_name: Safe at Home (Ohio address confidentiality program)
params.enroll: Participants must apply through a certified Application Assistant. The statute adds that the application is on a form prescribed by the secretary of state, with a notarized statement and the Application Assistant's recommendation.

rules.summary: Ohio's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, gives a substitute address to use on government records. To apply, you must fear for your safety, or a household member's, because one of you is a victim of rape, sexual battery, domestic violence, stalking, or human trafficking. You apply with a certified Application Assistant at a survivor services organization.
rules.quote: The applicant fears for the safety of the applicant, a member of the applicant's household, or the minor, incompetent, or ward on whose behalf the application is made because the applicant, household member, minor, incompetent, or ward is a victim of domestic violence, menacing by stalking, human trafficking, trafficking in persons, rape, or sexual battery.
rules.source_title: ORC 111.42 (address confidentiality program; application to secretary of state)

rules.summary: Records the Attorney General or Court of Claims gets for a compensation claim (such as medical or counseling records) that were confidential or exempt from public records law in the hands of whoever created them stay confidential once the program has them. This does not make the whole claim file confidential, and the records can still be used in hearings and written decisions on the claim.
rules.quote: any record or report that the court of claims or the  attorney general has obtained prior to, or obtains on or after,  June 30, 1998, under the provisions of sections 2743.51 to 2743.72 of the Revised Code and that is confidential or otherwise exempt  from public disclosure under section 149.43 of the Revised Code  while in the possession of the creator of the record or report  shall remain confidential or exempt from public disclosure under  section 149.43 of the Revised Code while in the possession of the  court of claims or the attorney general.
rules.source_title: ORC 2743.62 (privilege; confidentiality of records obtained for reparations claims)

rules.summary: Oklahoma's written notice of rights for sexual assault victims lists the right to a free forensic medical examination. In this law, sexual assault means rape, rape by instrumentation, or forcible sodomy.
rules.quote: The right to a free forensic medical examination
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142A-3 Notice of rights to victims of sexual assault

rules.summary: The exam fund pays whether or not the survivor has health insurance, and the survivor does not have to give insurance or employment information or file with a private insurer.
rules.quote: The payment of a sexual assault examination will be made, regardless of whether the victim is medically insured. (b) In order to provide anonymity to the sexual assault victim and maintain confidentiality, any victim who has obtained a forensic sexual assault examination, will not be required to provide information to the Board relative to employment or insurance; and, shall not be required to file a claim with any private insurance company for the payment of a forensic sexual assault examination.
rules.source_title: Okla. Admin. Code 185:15-1-6 Insurance (Sexual Assault Examination Fund)

params.payer: Sexual Assault Examination Fund, administered by the Crime Victims Compensation Board (Oklahoma District Attorneys Council)

rules.summary: Once the victim applies, the Crime Victims Compensation Board can pay for the forensic exam and the medicine the health care professional orders. The money comes from the Sexual Assault Examination Fund.
rules.quote: The Crime Victims Compensation Board is authorized to pay for this examination and the medications directed by the qualified licensed health care professional upon application submitted by the victim of a sexual assault.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.20 Sexual Assault Examination Fund

rules.summary: The exam fund pays at most $800 for a sexual assault examination.
rules.quote: in no event shall the Crime Victims Compensation Board pay an amount to exceed: 1. Eight Hundred Dollars ($800.00) for a sexual assault examination
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.20 Sexual Assault Examination Fund

params.scope: medicine ordered at the forensic exam, paid by the exam fund

rules.summary: The exam fund pays at most $100 for medications related to the sexual assault that the health care professional directs.
rules.quote: One Hundred Dollars ($100.00) for medications which are related to the sexual assault and directed and deemed necessary by the health care professional
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.20 Sexual Assault Examination Fund

params.payer: Sexual Assault Examination Fund, paid directly to the service provider

rules.summary: For sexual assaults on or after November 1, 2023, up to $800 can be paid straight to the exam providers for exam and facility fees.
rules.quote: For sexual assaults occurring on or after November 1, 2023, the law allows payment of up to $800 which may be paid directly to the service provider(s) for expenses incurred for the forensic examination (such as an examination fee or a facility fee).
rules.pinpoint: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page
rules.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

params.exception: or up to $25,000 more, but only for lost pay or lost support

rules.summary: Total compensation for one victim is capped at $25,000. After that, the Board may add up to $25,000 more only for the victim's lost wages or a dependent's loss of support.
rules.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of that victim may not exceed Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00) in the aggregate. The Board may, after approval of an initial award of Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00), grant an additional sum not to exceed Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00), specifically for loss of wages for the victim or loss of support for dependents of a deceased victim, provided there is verifiable economic loss after deducting payments from other sources.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

rules.summary: Outpatient counseling for the victim is capped at $3,000 in total. The same subsection lets the Board waive this limit in extreme cases.
rules.quote: A total not to exceed Three Thousand Dollars ($3,000.00) may be awarded for individual counseling sessions for victims of criminally injurious conduct.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

params.item: inpatient mental health treatment
params.scope: inpatient mental health treatment

rules.summary: Inpatient mental health treatment is reviewed case by case and may be paid up to $20,000.
rules.quote: Inpatient mental health treatment will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis and may be compensated, at the discretion of the Board, in an amount not to exceed Twenty Thousand Dollars ($20,000.00).
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

params.item: caregiver lost income
params.applies_to: a caregiver who missed work

rules.summary: Lost income of a caregiver who missed work to care for the injured victim is capped at $3,000. This cap is for the caregiver, not the victim's own lost wages.
rules.quote: Loss of income of a caregiver shall not exceed Three Thousand Dollars ($3,000.00).
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

rules.summary: Funeral, cremation, or burial expenses are capped at $7,500.
rules.quote: Reasonable funeral, cremation or burial expenses shall not exceed Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($7,500.00).
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $2,000.
rules.quote: Reasonable costs associated with crime scene cleanup shall not exceed Two Thousand Dollars ($2,000.00).
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

rules.summary: Medical services are covered at up to 80% of the cost of the service.
rules.quote: Awards for all medical services shall not exceed eighty percent (80%) of the total cost of the service less any other reduction for contributory conduct, as determined by the Board.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.9 Limits of compensation, provider payment, debt collection

rules.summary: A medical, dental, or psychological provider that accepts the program's payment must treat it as payment in full and cannot bill the claimant for the rest of those services.
rules.quote: Any medical provider that receives payment from the Crime Victims Compensation Revolving Fund for medical, dental or psychological services, or any provider that supplies equipment pursuant to an award under the Oklahoma Crime Victims Compensation Act shall, as a condition of the receipt of such payment, accept such payment as discharging in full any and all obligations of the claimant to pay, reimburse or compensate the provider
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.9 Limits of compensation, provider payment, debt collection

rules.summary: If the survivor already paid a medical bill, the program reimburses the out-of-pocket amount, less any conduct reduction.
rules.quote: In the event the claimant has paid for a medical service, the claimant will be reimbursed for the out-of-pocket loss, less any reductions for contributory conduct, as determined by the Board.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.9 Limits of compensation, provider payment, debt collection

rules.summary: The Board may pay for the victim's lost income from work (work loss).
rules.quote: The Crime Victims Compensation Board may compensate for work loss, replacement services loss, dependent
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

rules.summary: The Board may consider outpatient counseling costs when the counseling focuses on the crime and the counselor is a qualified mental health care provider.
rules.quote: Outpatient counseling expenses for a victim of criminally injurious conduct may be considered by the Board provided the counseling is focused on the crime and the counselor is a qualified mental health care provider.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

params.scope: mileage to the victim's medical, dental, and counseling appointments

rules.summary: The program lists mileage to the victim's medical, dental, and counseling appointments as a covered expense.
rules.quote: Mileage reimbursement for medical, dental, and counseling appointments for the victim
rules.source_title: Oklahoma Crime Victims Compensation home page

rules.summary: The program lists dental care and prescriptions among covered expenses.
rules.quote: Medical, dental, and prescriptions
rules.source_title: Oklahoma Crime Victims Compensation home page

rules.summary: The program lists prescriptions among the crime-related costs it may pay.
rules.quote: Medical, dental, and prescriptions
rules.source_title: Oklahoma Crime Victims Compensation home page

params.item: personal property and pain and suffering

rules.summary: Personal property (for example a damaged or stolen phone) and pain and suffering are not reimbursed.
rules.quote: Pain and suffering and personal property are NOT allowable expenses under the Crime Victims Compensation Act
rules.source_title: OCVC Fund Eligibility page

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 30 months after the injury or death it is based on.
rules.quote: Unless the claim has been filed with the Crime Victims Compensation Board within thirty (30) months after the injury or death upon which the claim is based.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

params.extension: kit-tested date may be used for adult sexual assault; Board may extend for good cause or in all sexual assault cases

rules.summary: For an adult (18 or older) sexual assault, the Board may measure timeliness from the date the evidence kit was tested, and it may extend the filing period for good cause or in any sexual assault case.
rules.quote: In cases involving sexual assault of an adult eighteen (18) years of age or older, the Board may use the date the sexual assault forensic evidence kit was tested when establishing whether the claim was timely filed. The Board may, at its discretion, extend the filing period beyond one (1) year upon a showing of good cause or in all cases of sexual assault
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

rules.summary: If the victim is under 18 or has a mental or cognitive disability, the Board may start the clock later. It can count from the day a responsible adult was told about the crime.
rules.quote: If the victim is under a mental or cognitive disability or is a child under eighteen (18) years of age, the Board may use the date the criminal incident was disclosed to a responsible adult when establishing whether or not the claim was timely filed.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to police within 72 hours, but a sexual assault survivor can instead meet this by having a forensic medical exam within 120 hours, and the Board can excuse either for good cause.
rules.quote: such conduct was reported to a law enforcement officer within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence, b. in the case of sexual assault, the victim undergoes a forensic medical examination within one hundred twenty (120) hours after its occurrence, or c. the Board finds there was good cause for the failure to report the crime or obtain a forensic medical examination within the time specified in subparagraph a or b of this paragraph.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor who has a forensic medical exam within 120 hours after the assault is found to have fully cooperated.
rules.quote: Victims of sexual assault who undergo a forensic medical examination within one hundred twenty (120) hours after the sexual assault shall be found to have fully cooperated.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by anything insurance or other collateral sources pay for the same loss.
rules.quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be diminished to the extent: 1. That the economic loss is recouped from collateral sources
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

rules.summary: The Board may reduce an award by the degree of responsibility it attributes to the victim. Tend shows this only as information.
rules.quote: Of the degree of responsibility for the cause of the injury or death attributable to the victim as determined by the Board.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

rules.summary: If the claimant would face financial hardship otherwise, the Board can pay an advance that comes out of the final award.
rules.quote: If the Board determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless an advance award is made, an amount may be paid to the claimant and shall be deducted from the final award
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.14 Advancement on award

rules.summary: Victims who suffered physical or psychological harm or death from a violent crime can qualify.
rules.quote: A primary requirement is that the crime be one in which the victim suffered physical or psychological harm or death as a result of a violent crime.
rules.source_title: OCVC Fund Eligibility page

params.rule: Crimes in Oklahoma (any victim), or crimes against Oklahoma residents in a state without an eligible VOCA compensation program.

rules.summary: The crime must have happened in Oklahoma, or be against an Oklahoma resident in a state without an eligible compensation program.
rules.quote: a misdemeanor or felony which occurs or is attempted in this state, or against a resident of this state in a state that does not have an eligible crime victims compensation program
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.3 Definitions

rules.summary: For the exam fund, Medicaid or another federally funded program counts as a collateral source, so the fund pays only after that program denies the exam.
rules.quote: For sexual assault exams performed on adults and children, Medicaid or any other federally funded program is considered a collateral source and payment will not be made unless the denial of benefits is provided.
rules.source_title: Okla. Admin. Code 185:15-1-6 Insurance (Sexual Assault Examination Fund)

params.payer: Sexual Assault Examination Fund; examiner and facility fees share the $800 limit pro rata

rules.summary: Only charges directly tied to the forensic exam are paid, and when the examiner fee and the facility fee together exceed $800 the fund splits the $800 between the providers by percentage.
rules.quote: Any charges not directly related to the forensic exam are not compensable. In cases where there is both an examiner fee and a facility fee exceeding $800, we prorate, allowing a percentage to each provider.
rules.pinpoint: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page
rules.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

rules.summary: For the exam fund and the sexual assault rights notice, sexual assault means rape, rape by instrumentation, or forcible sodomy as defined in the criminal code.
rules.quote: rape, or rape by instrumentation, as defined in Sections 1111 , 1111.1 and 1114 of this title, or b. forcible sodomy, as defined in Section 888 of this title
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.20 Sexual Assault Examination Fund

rules.summary: Apply online through the OCVC online application portal.
rules.quote: Use our online application to apply for compensation benefits.
rules.pinpoint: VCP Online Access home page, How to Apply
rules.source_title: OCVC VCP Online Access claim portal

params.target: 421 N.W. 13TH STREET, SUITE 290 • OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA 73103
