rules.summary: Fax the printed and signed claim form to 405/264-5097.
rules.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), page 1 header
rules.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

rules.summary: The claim form says it can be emailed once printed and signed; the program email is victimsservices@dac.state.ok.us.
rules.quote: Website: www.okvictimscomp.com E-mail: victimsservices@dac.state.ok.us
rules.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), instructions header
rules.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

params.note: Complete every section and sign all three signature areas on page four; the form must be printed and signed.

rules.summary: Fill out every section of the paper form and sign all three signature areas on page four.
rules.quote: Please thoroughly complete ALL sections and sign all three areas of page four.
rules.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

params.note: All itemized medical statements for the injuries listed in Section I.

rules.summary: List the injuries from the crime and attach all itemized medical statements.
rules.quote: List the injuries suffered as a result of the crime and attach all itemized medical statements.
rules.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions, Section I
rules.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

params.note: Send every bill received so far; later bills can be added.

rules.summary: Send all the bills you have received with the application; bills that arrive later can be added.
rules.quote: Please submit all the bills that you have received. If more come in, they can always be added later.
rules.pinpoint: FAQ, Do I need to submit all bills with the application?
rules.source_title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions

params.note: Proof of payment for medical, dental, or counseling costs you paid yourself.

rules.summary: Out-of-pocket medical, dental, and counseling costs are reimbursed at 100% only with documentation of payment.
rules.quote: Medical, dental, and counseling expenses that the victim is out-of-pocket will be reimbursed at 100%, provided there is documentation of payment and no collateral sources exist.
rules.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

params.note: Requested by the District Attorney's Victim-Witness Coordinator during documentation, not attached by the survivor.

rules.summary: The DA's Victim-Witness Coordinator requests the police report while documenting the claim.
rules.quote: A police report is requested, along with any other forms and reports that may be needed to determine out-of-pocket expenses.
rules.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

params.note: Work loss verified by the employer and the attending physician.

rules.summary: Lost income must be verified by both your employer and your attending physician.
rules.quote: Work loss must be verified by the employer and the attending physician.
rules.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Income Loss / Economic Loss
rules.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

params.note: Disability verification from a physician or mental health professional covering the time off work.

rules.summary: For lost wages, a physician or mental health professional and your employer must verify the disability time.
rules.quote: provided the crime prevented the person from working and the disability can be verified by a physician or mental health professional and by the victim’s employer.
rules.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions, Section G
rules.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

params.note: Tax returns for the last three years, if self-employed.

rules.summary: If you are self-employed, tax returns for the last 3 years are required for lost wages.

params.note: Provider documentation verifying the dates of medical or counseling appointments, for mileage.

params.note: Future economic loss: itemized list of expected expenses with an explanation.

rules.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

params.note: Written estimate from the attending physician for future dental work or surgery, stating the work and cost.

rules.summary: For future dental work or surgery, ask the attending physician for a written estimate of the work and the cost.
rules.quote: For future dental work or surgery necessary to repair damage from the criminal incident, ask the attending physician to write an accurate estimate which clearly states the work to be performed and the cost.
rules.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Future Economic Loss
rules.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

params.note: Traditional American Indian healing or burial services: receipts with each item's purpose noted.

rules.summary: For traditional American Indian healing or burial services, receipts must note each item's purpose.
rules.quote: In order for reimbursement of these expenses, receipts must be provided with the item’s purpose clearly noted on the receipt.
rules.pinpoint: Eligible Expenses, Traditional American Indian Services
rules.source_title: OCVC Fund Eligibility page

params.note: Social Security number, only if you paid the exam bill yourself and want reimbursement.

rules.quote: If the victim/guardian paid the bill out of their own pocket, we will need a Social Security number in order to reimburse them.
rules.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

params.note: Varies by area where the crime occurred.

rules.quote: Claims are generally placed on a docket for decision within 30 days of receipt of all documentation from the Victim-Witness Coordinator.

rules.summary: Payments are generally made within 3 weeks of approval.
rules.quote: PAYMENTS are generally made within three weeks of approval.

rules.summary: Sexual Assault Examination Fund payments are usually made within 30 days of receiving the application.

params.agency: Oklahoma Office of the Attorney General
params.enroll: Victims do not apply directly to the Oklahoma Address Confidentiality Program. Application is made in person at one of the designated victim assistance programs located throughout the state. Designated programs are state or local agencies or nonprofit agencies that provide counseling and shelter services to victims of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking and have ACP trained staff.

rules.summary: Oklahoma's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of the Attorney General, gives victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, and child abduction who have moved somewhere unknown to their abuser a substitute address to use with state and local agencies, plus free mail forwarding. Applicants apply in person through a designated victim assistance program with an ACP-trained application assistant.
rules.quote: The ACP aids in protecting the physical address of victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, and child abduction from disclosure. ACP contributes to the safety of victims by denying abusers the opportunity to use public records to violate the rights of others. Victims who have moved to a new location unknown to their abuser are provided with a substitute address when interacting with state and local agencies.
rules.source_title: Oklahoma Attorney General Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) page

rules.summary: All records and information given to the Crime Victims Compensation Board to process a claim are confidential and generally cannot be obtained through discovery in a civil or criminal case, with narrow exceptions for an appeal of a Board decision or a strict showing to a court.
rules.quote: All records and information given to the Board to process a claim on behalf of a crime victim shall be confidential.
rules.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.9 Limits of compensation, provider payment, debt collection

params.condition: if Oregon's SAVE Fund pays for it

rules.summary: A provider that bills the SAVE Fund for a sexual assault medical assessment may not bill the survivor for it, unless the Fund lacks money or declines to pay. The statute does not address billing the survivor's insurance; the SAVE Fund rule does, and it bars billing insurance too.
rules.quote: A provider who submits a bill under this subsection may not bill the victim for the medical assessment except to the extent that the department is unable to pay the bill due to lack of funds or declines to pay the bill.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.condition: if Oregon's SAVE Fund pays for it

rules.summary: A provider that bills the SAVE Fund may not bill the survivor or the survivor's insurance for the exam, evidence collection, or other services given with the exam (exceptions: the Fund lacks money or declines to pay for reasons other than a late or incomplete bill).
rules.quote: An eligible medical services provider (including subcontractor or other designee) who submits a bill to the Fund under these rules may not bill the victim or the victim's insurance carrier for a medical examination, collection of forensic evidence using the Oregon State Police SAFE Kit, or other services provided in conjunction with the sexual assault exam
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 84 (SAVE Fund)

params.payer: Oregon Department of Justice, Sexual Assault Victims' Emergency Medical Response (SAVE) Fund

rules.summary: The Oregon Department of Justice pays for a sexual assault medical assessment through the SAVE Fund, subject to available funds and the time frame set by rule.
rules.quote: Subject to the availability of funds from gifts, grants and donations in the Sexual Assault Victims' Emergency Medical Response Fund, the Department of Justice shall pay the costs of a medical assessment obtained by a victim if the victim obtains the medical assessment within the time frame established in rules adopted by the department.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: The SAVE Fund law counts you as a victim only if the sexual assault happened in Oregon.
rules.quote: “Victim” means a person who has experienced an incident of sexual assault as defined in ORS 181A.323 that occurred in this state.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.payer: Oregon Department of Justice, SAVE Fund

rules.summary: You can get the exam and fill out the SAVE Fund form whether or not you report the assault to police.
rules.quote: A victim may obtain a medical assessment and complete and submit a form under this section regardless of whether the victim reports the sexual assault to a law enforcement agency.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: The SAVE Fund also covers 5 counseling sessions, which must be used within 18 months of the exam.
rules.quote: Five (5) counseling sessions; counseling sessions expire 18 months from the date of the sexual assault exam.
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 84 (SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: The most compensation that can be awarded in total is $47,000.
rules.quote: The maximum amount of compensation that may be awarded, in aggregate, to the victim and the survivors and dependents of a deceased victim is $47,000.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: Medical and hospital expenses, including counseling and medications, are covered up to $20,000 combined.
rules.quote: The victim's reasonable medical and hospital expenses, including counseling expenses and the cost of any medications, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: The victim's counseling counts toward the same $20,000 limit as medical and hospital expenses.
rules.quote: The victim's reasonable medical and hospital expenses, including counseling expenses and the cost of any medications, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: An applicant who does not meet the eligibility requirements (for example, the reporting requirement) may still get a limited counseling award of up to $5,000.
rules.quote: If the applicant files an application for a compensable crime and does not meet the eligibility requirements set forth in ORS 147.015, the Department may grant a limited counseling award of up to $5,000.00.
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: On an approved claim, CVC pays for 30 counseling sessions and needs a treatment plan from the provider for more.
rules.quote: If CVC approves the claim, we can pay for 30 counseling sessions. We require a treatment plan from the provider for any further sessions.
rules.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, How much do compensation benefits cover?
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

rules.summary: Lost earnings are paid at up to $600 per week.
rules.quote: Loss of the victim's earnings, at a maximum rate of $600 per week, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: Lost earnings are capped at $20,000 in total.
rules.quote: Loss of the victim's earnings, at a maximum rate of $600 per week, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: Lost earnings are figured at 75% of the victim's documented gross earnings on the date of the crime.
rules.quote: Compensation for lost earnings under ORS 147.035(2)(b) shall be computed on the basis of 75% of the victim's documented gross earnings on the date of the compensable crime.
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: Missing more than 10 working days requires confirmation from a health provider, or a licensed therapist for an emotional injury.
rules.quote: Lost earnings compensation for periods of disability in excess of 10 working days may be paid only if the period of disability is confirmed by a health provider , or a licensed therapist when the victim has missed work due to an emotional injury.
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: A parent or guardian who misses work to care for a minor victim can get up to $5,000 in lost earnings.
rules.quote: Loss of earnings for the parent or guardian are compensable up to a maximum of $5,000.00 under the child victim's claim under ORS 147.035 (2)(f).
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: Travel for the victim's covered medical care or counseling is paid up to $3,000, only when the care is more than 30 miles from home and adequate care is not available closer.
rules.quote: Expenses related to transportation for the victim's medical care or counseling, at a rate determined by the Department of Justice, up to a maximum amount of $3,000, when: (A) The medical care or counseling is compensable under this section; (B) The medical care or counseling is provided more than 30 miles away from the victim's residence; and (C) Adequate medical care or counseling is not available in closer proximity to the victim's residence.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.scope: mileage to medical and mental health treatment

rules.summary: Mileage to medical and mental health treatment is reimbursed at 50 cents per mile, up to $3,000.
rules.quote: Reimbursement of mileage (50¢ per mile) for travel to medical and mental health treatment, up to $3,000.
rules.pinpoint: CVC brochure (2024), What Does CVC Pay For?
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

rules.summary: Rehabilitation expenses, such as physical therapy, are covered up to $4,000.
rules.quote: The victim's rehabilitation expenses, up to a maximum amount of $4,000
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: Crime scene cleaning is covered up to $2,500.
rules.quote: Reasonable cleaning expenses, up to a maximum of $2,500
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: Damaged eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures and other medically necessary devices can be replaced if mentioned in the police report or medical chart notes.
rules.quote: Replacement of damaged eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures and other medically necessary devices and expenses (must be mentioned in the police report or medical chart notes)
rules.pinpoint: Compensation for Victims of Crime page, benefits list
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Compensation for Victims of Crime

rules.summary: Crime-related dental work is covered; without insurance, CVC must first approve a treatment plan from a licensed dental provider.
rules.quote: If you do not have insurance, CVC must review and approve a treatment plan provided by a licensed dental provider. All treatment needs to be directly related to the crime.
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

rules.summary: Compensation is not paid for property damage or for noneconomic damages.
rules.quote: Compensation may not be awarded under ORS 147.005 to 147.367 for property damage or noneconomic damages as defined in ORS 31.705.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.item: lost items or property damage

rules.summary: CVC cannot pay for lost items or property damage.
rules.quote: The CVC Program cannot pay for lost items or property damage.
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

rules.summary: CVC does not pay relocation costs.
rules.quote: CVC can not reimburse damages for property crimes, or pay for relocation costs.
rules.pinpoint: Compensation for Victims of Crime page
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Compensation for Victims of Crime

params.item: SAVE Fund exclusions: DNA testing, off-site prescriptions, follow-up services, anesthesia, transportation

rules.summary: The SAVE Fund does not pay for DNA testing, prescriptions filled off-site, follow-up services, anesthesia, or transportation; the provider may bill these to the survivor or insurance, and CVC may cover them on an accepted claim.
rules.quote: Examples of services not covered by the Fund include, but are not limited to: DNA testing; prescriptions filled off-site of the location of a medical examination; follow-up services; anesthesia services; and transportation.
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 84 (SAVE Fund)

params.extension: or later if the department gives you more time for good cause

rules.summary: The application must be filed within one year of the injury, or later if the department allows an extension for good cause.
rules.quote: Within one year of the date of the injury to the victim; or (B) Within such further extension of time as the department, for good cause shown, allows.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.extension: good cause includes lack of knowledge of the program, police failure to inform, or emotional or physical trauma

rules.summary: Good cause for filing after one year includes not knowing about the program, police not giving the required information, or trauma that got in the way of filing on time.
rules.quote: "Good cause" for failure to file an application for compensation within one year of the date of the crime as required by ORS 147.015(1)(e) includes but is not limited to the victim's lack of knowledge of the Crime Victims' Compensation Program, failure of a law enforcement official to provide information to the victim as required by ORS 147.365(1), or emotional or physical trauma sustained by the victim that was a barrier to timely filing the application for compensation.
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement, unless the department finds the applicant acted reasonably in not reporting. No fixed number of days is set.
rules.quote: The appropriate law enforcement officials were notified of the perpetration of the crime allegedly causing the death or injury to the victim, unless the Department of Justice finds that, notwithstanding the failure of notification, the applicant acted reasonably under the circumstances
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: The report rule can also be met in other ways. A sexual assault medical assessment or any other forensic exam counts. So does a health, tribal health, student health, or community mental health provider certifying that the victim reported the crime to them. So does other documentation that counts as notice under the department's rules.
rules.quote: (E) A medical assessment, as defined in ORS 147.395, for sexual assault, or any other forensic exam or medical assessment; (b) A health provider, tribal health provider, student health provider or community mental health provider certifies that the victim reported the crime to the provider; or (c) The victim provides to the department documentation that qualifies as law enforcement notification under the rules of the department.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: Getting a sexual abuse restraining order (or a stalking, abuse prevention or no contact order) because of the crime also meets the reporting requirement.
rules.quote: A sexual abuse restraining order under ORS 163.760 to 163.777
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: Survivors can meet the reporting requirement by reporting to police, telling a medical or mental health provider, getting a protective order, or getting a forensic exam.
rules.quote: You may report your crime in one of the following ways: • Report to law enforcement • Report to a medical or mental health provider • Obtain a protective order • Obtain a forensic medical exam due to sexual assault or strangulation
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

rules.summary: The report (or alternative) must happen before the department receives the application.
rules.quote: Notification of the perpetration of the crime as required by ORS 147.015 must have been done prior to the application being received by the Department in order for a person to be eligible for an award of compensation.
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: The award is reduced by benefits from workers' compensation, government funds, or any other source that the victim received or is entitled to because of the injury.
rules.quote: shall deduct the amount of benefits, payments or awards that are payable under the Workers' Compensation Law, from local governmental, state or federal funds or from any source, and that the victim or survivors or dependents of the victim have received or to which the victim or survivors or dependents of the victim are entitled as a result of the death or injury of the victim
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: Health insurance (including OHP), auto, workers' comp, disability, homeowner's, Paid Leave Oregon, unemployment, restitution and settlements must be used first; Indian Health Services is not a prior resource.
rules.quote: A prior resource may include but is not limited to: private or public health insurance, automobile insurance, workers' compensation, disability insurance, homeowner's insurance, Paid Leave Oregon or equivalent plan, unemployment benefits, restitution, civil settlements, and tribal per capita payments. Indian Health Services insurance is not considered a prior resource.
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: After insurance pays, CVC can cover copays, deductibles, and crime-related treatment insurance does not cover.
rules.quote: CVC will pay for copays, deductibles, and crime-related treatment that insurance does not cover within the scope of this program.
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

rules.summary: Eligibility depends on the department finding the victim acted reasonably given the victim's specific situation. Shown for information only.
rules.quote: The department determines that the victim acted reasonably with respect to the incident causing the death or injury to the victim, taking into account the specific situation of the victim and what a reasonable action would be for a person in the victim's circumstances
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: The department may make an emergency award of up to $1,000 before a final decision when an award is likely and waiting would cause undue hardship.
rules.quote: The amount of such emergency award shall not exceed $1,000.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: Sexual assault is an eligible crime.
rules.quote: Eligible crimes include domestic violence, sexual assault, child abuse, assault, homicide, hate/bias crimes, and other crimes resulting in physical or psychological injury.
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

rules.summary: Injury includes mental or emotional harm and pregnancy, not only physical harm.
rules.quote: "Injury" means abuse of a corpse, actual bodily harm, mental or emotional harm and, with respect to a victim, includes pregnancy and mental or nervous shock.
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.rule: crime must occur in Oregon; victim residency not required

rules.summary: Victims of crimes committed in Oregon can apply, regardless of where they live.
rules.quote: Killed or injured in this state as a result of a compensable crime perpetrated or attempted against that person
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.rule: Oregon residents injured in a U.S. state without a reciprocal program

rules.summary: An Oregon resident hurt in another U.S. state that has no reciprocal crime victims' compensation program can apply in Oregon.
rules.quote: Who is an Oregon resident killed or injured as a result of a compensable crime perpetrated or attempted against the person in a state, within the United States, without a reciprocal crime victims' compensation program
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.rule: immigration status not considered

rules.summary: Immigration status is not asked about or considered.
rules.quote: CVC does not request or consider immigration status when determining eligibility for compensation.
rules.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

rules.summary: Apply online through the CVC Portal, which also lets you upload documents and check claim status.
rules.quote:
You can apply electronically through the Crime Victims’ Compensation Portal at
doj.state.or.us/cvcportal.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, How do I apply?
rules.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

rules.summary: Email the completed, signed application to the program.
rules.quote: You can also submit your application by email: cvssd@doj.oregon.gov
rules.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, How do I apply?
rules.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

params.target: Oregon Department of Justice Crime Victims’ Compensation Program 1162 Court Street NE Salem, OR 97301–4096

rules.summary: Mail the signed paper application to the DOJ Crime Victims' Compensation Program in Salem.
rules.quote:
You can mail a paper application to:
Oregon Department of Justice
Crime Victims’ Compensation Program
1162 Court Street NE
Salem, OR 97301–4096
rules.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, How do I apply?
rules.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

params.target: your local District Attorney’s Office Victim Assistance Program or local community-based victim services agency

rules.summary: You can also apply in person through a county District Attorney's victim assistance program or a community-based victim services agency.
rules.quote: Apply at your local District Attorney’s Office Victim Assistance Program or local community-based victim services agency.
rules.pinpoint: CVC brochure (2024), How Do I Submit an Application?
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

params.note: Signed release on page 4 of the application; unsigned applications are returned.

rules.summary: Sign the release in the application so CVC can verify your information; unsigned applications are returned.
rules.quote: You must sign this form to allow CVC to verify the information in your application. We will return any unsigned applications.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page 4, Required Release to Process Your Application
rules.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

params.note: Only for lost earnings: employer documentation of employment and time lost, plus the paystub just before the crime.

rules.summary: For lost earnings, provide employer documentation of employment and time lost and your last paystub before the crime.
rules.quote: The following information must be provided to CVC: Documentation from your employer to verify employment and time loss. Your paystub just prior to the crime.
rules.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, loss of earnings benefit
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

params.note: Only for lost earnings if self-employed: the previous year's tax records.

rules.summary: If you are self-employed and claim lost earnings, submit the previous year's tax records.
rules.quote: If you are self-employed, please submit the previous year tax records.
rules.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, loss of earnings benefit
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

params.note: Work release from a doctor or mental health therapist, only if more than 2 weeks of work were missed.

rules.summary: If you missed more than 2 weeks of work, a work release from your doctor is required.
rules.quote: A work release from a doctor is required beyond 2 weeks of missed work.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, Answers to Commonly Asked Questions
rules.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

params.note: Itemized billing statements showing services, provider name, and date of service; submitted after the claim is accepted.

rules.summary: Payment requests must be itemized billing statements listing the services, the provider's name, and the date of service.
rules.quote: Requests for payment of crime related expenses shall be submitted in the form of an itemized billing statement detailing the services provided, the provider’s name, the date of service
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

params.note: Insurance EOBs, combined with chart notes and bills in one portal upload.

rules.summary: Insurance EOBs, chart notes, and bills can be combined into one upload in the CVC Portal.
rules.quote: EOB’s, chart notes, and bills can all be combined to one document and select bill as the category.
rules.pinpoint: Applying for CVC, Crime Victims Portal FAQs, How do I upload documents?
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Applying for Crime Victims' Compensation

params.note: Valid receipts for car rental, bus, train, or air fare used instead of mileage.

rules.summary: If CVC pays for a car rental or bus, train, or air fare instead of mileage, it needs a valid receipt.
rules.quote: the Department may, at its discretion, reimburse reasonable and necessary round-trip car rental or bus, train, or air fare, upon submission of a valid receipt.
rules.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: CVC confirms receipt by mail or email and issues a claim number within 2 business days.
rules.quote:
We will notify you by mail or email when we receive your application. You will receive a
claim number within 2 business days.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, What happens next?
rules.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

rules.summary: CVC says it will contact you in 60 to 90 days to tell you whether the application was accepted.
rules.quote:
We will contact you again in 60 to 90 days to tell you if we have accepted your
application.
rules.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, What happens next?
rules.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

params.agency: Oregon Department of Justice, Crime Victim and Survivor Services Division
params.enroll: To apply to the Address Confidentiality Program, you must work with a victim advocate who has been designated as an Application Assistant by the Attorney General.

rules.summary: Oregon DOJ's Address Confidentiality Program is a free mail forwarding service that gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, and bias crimes a substitute address to use instead of their real one.
rules.quote: It helps survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, bias crimes or bias incidents shield their physical address. Health care providers who provide physical and behavioral reproductive and gender-affirming health care also can participate in ACP. Program participants are provided with a substitute address to use instead of their real address.
rules.pinpoint: Oregon DOJ ACP page, 'Protecting Addresses for Victims'; program established by ORS 192.822
rules.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

rules.summary: Information an applicant gives the DOJ is open to the public by default, but the department may keep it confidential when the crime is rape, sodomy, sexual abuse, trafficking, or domestic violence and the victim's interests require it. The statute does not make the whole claim file confidential.
rules.quote:
All information submitted to the Department of Justice by an applicant and
all hearings of the Workers’ Compensation Board under ORS 147.005 to 147.367
shall be open to the public unless the department or board determines that the
information shall be kept confidential or that a closed hearing shall be held
because: (a) The alleged
assailant has not been brought to trial and disclosure of the information or a
public hearing would adversely affect either the apprehension or the trial of
the alleged assailant; (b) The offense
allegedly perpetrated against the victim is rape, sodomy, sexual abuse,
trafficking in persons or a crime involving domestic violence as defined in ORS
135.230, and the interests of the victim or of the victim’s dependents require
that the information be kept confidential or that the public be excluded from
the hearing;
rules.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rules.summary: The cost of a forensic rape exam and the medications prescribed to the survivor may not be charged to the survivor.
rules.quote: The cost of a forensic rape examination and the cost of medications prescribed to the direct victim shall not be charged to the victim.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params.payer: Office of Victims' Services (VCAP), after insurance unless the survivor asks that insurance not be billed

rules.summary: The hospital or provider bills the state compensation program (Office of Victims' Services) for the exam when insurance does not cover it, or when the survivor asks that their insurance not be billed.
rules.quote: A hospital or other licensed health care provider may submit a claim for reimbursement for the cost of a forensic rape examination if the cost is not covered by insurance or if the victim requests that the insurance carrier not be billed.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params.payer: Victims Compensation Assistance Program (VCAP)

rules.summary: The survivor does not have to report to police or talk to law enforcement for the program to pay for the exam.
rules.quote: The victim of a sexual offense does not need to 'report' the sexual offense or 'talk' to law enforcement in order for the costs to be paid by the Victims Compensation Assistance Program (VCAP).
rules.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
rules.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

params.payer: Victims Compensation Assistance Program (VCAP)

rules.summary: For the program to pay for the exam, the hospital must notify the local police where the assault happened within 12 hours of collecting the evidence.
rules.quote: In order for payments to be considered, hospitals or licensed health care providers requesting reimbursement of costs associated with a forensic rape examination are required to notify the local law enforcement agency where the reported sexual assault occurred within 12 hours of collection of the sexual assault evidence as per the Sexual Assault Testing and Evidence Collection Act (Act 165 of 2006).
rules.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
rules.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

params.payer: Victims Compensation Assistance Program (VCAP)

rules.summary: Adults 18 or older can choose an anonymous report when evidence is collected, if they are worried about the kit going to police. A minor's exam cannot be done anonymously.
rules.quote: Adult victims (age 18 or older) have the option of anonymous reporting and gathering of evidence and may consider this option if they have concerns about the kit being provided to police. An exam cannot be completed anonymously for a minor.
rules.source_title: VCAP Forensic Rape Examination Frequently Asked Questions (September 2024)

rules.summary: If the program pays the maximum and a balance remains, the provider still may not bill the survivor; the program payment is payment in full.
rules.quote: No. A health care provider must accept the payment in full for the costs of the forensic rape examination.
rules.source_title: VCAP Forensic Rape Examination Frequently Asked Questions (September 2024)

rules.summary: The provider must file the exam claim within one year of the crime or its discovery; if the provider misses that deadline, the survivor still cannot be billed.
rules.quote: The claim must be filed by a hospital or other licensed health care provider, within one year of the date of the crime or discovery of the crime. Failure to file within the prescribed time frame will result in non-payment of the claim and the victim cannot be billed for those costs.
rules.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, A.4
rules.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

rules.summary: A survivor who was billed by mistake and paid for the forensic rape exam or related medications can be reimbursed, up to $1,000.
rules.quote: OVS will reimburse a direct victim who is erroneously billed and subsequently pays the cost of the forensic rape examination or medications directly related to the sexual offense. The reimbursement will be subject to the $1,000 monetary limitation.
rules.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

rules.summary: Payment for a forensic rape exam and related medications is capped at $1,000, and this sits outside the $35,000 total award cap.
rules.quote: In no case shall the total amount of an award exceed $35,000 except for payment of the following: (i) counseling, the maximum amount of which shall be in accordance with paragraph (4.1); (ii) forensic rape examination and medications directly related to the sexual assault or rape, the amount of which shall not exceed $1,000
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params.payer: Survivor or insurance for care beyond the forensic rape exam (for example x-rays or other treatment); a standard VCAP claim can be filed for it

rules.summary: The no-bill rule covers only the forensic rape exam costs and related medications. Providers must tell the survivor they may be billed for other care, such as x-rays or other medical treatment, which can be submitted on a standard VCAP claim.
rules.quote: They must inform the victim that they may be billed for services in instances where they have additional expenses beyond the forensic rape examination costs, such as x-rays or other medical treatment not associated with a forensic rape examination.
rules.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
rules.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

params.exception: not counting some costs that are paid on top

rules.summary: The total award is capped at $35,000, except that counseling, forensic rape exam costs, and crime scene cleanup are paid on top of that cap.
rules.quote: In no case shall the total amount of an award exceed $35,000 except for payment of the following
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: Counseling for an adult direct victim is capped at $5,000, and a minor direct victim at $10,000; counseling is paid on top of the total award cap.
rules.quote: The amount of an award under paragraph (4)(i) shall not exceed $5,000 where the direct victim is an adult and shall not exceed $10,000 where the direct victim is a minor.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: Counseling for a direct victim who was a minor is capped at $10,000.
rules.quote: The amount of an award under paragraph (4)(i) shall not exceed $5,000 where the direct victim is an adult and shall not exceed $10,000 where the direct victim is a minor.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: The program pays for counseling, and for the transportation to get to counseling, when done by or under a psychiatrist, psychologist, licensed professional counselor, or licensed social worker.
rules.quote: An award for counseling performed by or under the supervision of a psychiatrist, psychologist, licensed professional counselor or licensed social worker and reimbursement of associated transportation costs
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: A direct victim of sexual abuse in Pennsylvania can get counseling paid through a separate sexual assault counseling claim, paid directly to the provider.
rules.quote: The Office of Victims' Services shall provide funding for counseling services related to sexual abuse for an individual who is a direct victim of sexual abuse. Payment shall be made directly to the health care provider that provides the services from funding provided for the implementation of this section.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: Sexual assault counseling claims are capped at $5,000 if the survivor was 18 or older at the time of the abuse, and $10,000 if under 18.
rules.quote: (1) Five thousand dollars if the individual was, at the time of the abuse, 18 years of age or older. (2) Ten thousand dollars if the individual was, at the time of the abuse, under 18 years of age.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: Lost earnings are capped at $15,000 in total, and this counts toward the overall award cap.
rules.quote: Except as set forth in subparagraph (iii), the aggregate award for the loss shall not exceed $15,000.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: Lost earnings caused by the injury are covered, up to the state average weekly wage for each week, if not otherwise reimbursed.
rules.quote: OVS may make an award within the monetary limitations of the act to compensate a direct victim, intervenor or claimant for loss of earnings attributable to the injury not to exceed the average weekly wage if the claimant was not otherwise reimbursed for the loss.
rules.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

rules.summary: Relocation for safety is capped at $1,000 per household for each direct victim.
rules.quote: This reimbursement will not exceed $1,000 per household for each direct victim for the following:
rules.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

rules.summary: Temporary or permanent relocation is covered when there is an immediate need to protect the safety and health of the victim and household, verified by a medical provider, human services provider, or law enforcement.
rules.quote: expenses resulting from the temporary or permanent relocation of a direct victim and individuals residing in the household of the direct victim due to the incident forming the basis of the victim's claim when there is an immediate need to protect the safety and health of the victim and individuals residing in the household, as verified by a medical provider, human services provider or law enforcement
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 1: Definitions (18 P.S. 11.103)

rules.summary: The move must happen within 120 days of the crime, or within 120 days of a new threat or sign of danger.
rules.quote: Relocation must occur within 120 days from the date of crime, or 120 days from the date the victim is threatened by any change of circumstance or indicator of danger.
rules.source_title: VCAP flyer: Relocation Expenses (11/2023)

rules.summary: Lodging while relocating for safety is reimbursed up to $75 per day, inside the $1,000 relocation limit.
rules.quote: This reimbursement will not exceed $1,000 per household for each direct victim for the following: (1)  Relocation expenses to be reimbursed are as follows: (i)   Lodging to a daily maximum of $75.
rules.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

rules.summary: Travel to medical care or counseling, and to criminal justice or protection from abuse proceedings, is reimbursed.
rules.quote: OVS will reimburse expenses associated with travel necessary and reasonable as determined by OVS to obtain medical care or counseling, attend or participate in criminal justice or protection from abuse proceedings, and other circumstances when good cause is shown by the claimant.
rules.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

rules.summary: Car rental for crime-related travel (medical care, counseling, court) is reimbursed up to $30 per day.
rules.quote: Car rental, up to $30 a day.
rules.source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

rules.summary: Meals are reimbursed up to $28 per day ($6 breakfast, $6 lunch, $16 dinner), but only when travel to a provider is 50 miles or more one way.
rules.quote:
Additionally, if travel to a provider is 50 miles or more (one way) from the eligible person’s
home, the following is eligible for reimbursement:
• Meals. Up to $28 a day, with no more than $6 for breakfast, $6 for lunch and $16 for
dinner.
rules.source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

rules.summary: Unreimbursed medical care and treatment caused by the crime are covered.
rules.quote: expenses for unreimbursed and unreimbursable expenses or indebtedness incurred for medical care, nonmedical remedial care and treatment as approved by the Office of Victims' Services or other services
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 1: Definitions (18 P.S. 11.103)

rules.summary: Once the program accepts a claim, the hospital or provider must take the program's payment as payment in full and may not collect more from the survivor.
rules.quote: If the Office of Victims' Services accepts a claim, the hospital or other licensed health care provider shall accept such payment as payment in full and may not attempt to collect from the victim any amount exceeding the amount of reimbursement made by the Office of Victims' Services.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params.item: replacing medical devices, eyeglasses, and prescription medicine

rules.summary: Replacing eyeglasses, hearing aids, dental devices, prescription medications and similar health items stolen or damaged in the crime is capped at $1,000, with eyeglass frames limited to $200. This is not a cap on ordinary medical bills.
rules.quote: OVS will reimburse a claimant for costs for the replacement of each prosthetic device, wheelchair, cane, walker, hearing aid, eyeglasses or other corrective lenses, dental device or prescription medications. Reimbursement will not exceed $1,000 and will be subject to the following limitations: (1)  Two hundred dollars for eyeglass frames.
rules.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

params.scope: services needed because of the crime, such as child care, cleaning, or laundry

rules.summary: Services needed because of the crime, such as child care, cleaning, laundry, and meal preparation, can be reimbursed.
rules.quote: The cost of obtaining services needed as a result of the crime such as laundering, cleaning, child care, administration of medication, food shopping and meal preparation.
rules.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

params.scope: helpers who are not family members

rules.summary: A helper who is not a family member is paid at most $8 an hour. A family member who does the work is paid their own lost earnings, up to the average weekly wage.
rules.quote: The cost of obtaining services needed as a result of the crime such as laundering, cleaning, child care, administration of medication, food shopping and meal preparation. (i) Members of the family of the direct victim or intervenor engaged to perform the services will be paid their net loss of earnings not to exceed the average weekly wage and if not otherwise reimbursed for the loss of earnings. (ii) Individuals engaged to perform services who are not family members will be paid a maximum hourly rate of $8.
rules.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

rules.summary: Cleaning a crime scene at a private residence or privately owned vehicle is capped at $500, paid on top of the total award cap.
rules.quote: reasonable and necessary costs of cleaning the crime scene of a private residence or privately owned motor vehicle, the amount of which shall not exceed $500.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params.item: property damage; pain and suffering

rules.summary: Property damage and pain and suffering are not covered.
rules.quote: Except as otherwise provided, the term does not include property damage or pain and suffering.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 1: Definitions (18 P.S. 11.103)

params.item: property loss or damage (only certain medical equipment and supplies and, case by case, official documents are excepted; phones are not named)

rules.summary: Lost or damaged property is not paid, except certain medical equipment and supplies and, case by case, certain official documents such as a driver's license or passport.
rules.quote: Property - A claim cannot be paid for property loss or damage (except certain medical equipment and supplies; or certain official documents, i.e., driver's license, passport, etc. on case by case basis).
rules.pinpoint: VCAP Manual 2025, Miscellaneous Eligibility Information (p. 10 to 11)
rules.source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

params.extension: or later in some cases, such as sexual abuse counseling claims, some survivors who were children, or when the program finds good cause

rules.summary: Under the current law, a claim must be filed within five years after the crime is discovered.
rules.quote: a claim must be filed not later than five years after the discovery of the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: The program's page says the 5-year limit is for crimes on or after 9/8/2022. For an older crime, it asks you to contact the program to find out the filing rules.
rules.quote: For crimes occurring on or after 9/8/2022, the claim must be filed within 5 years of the crime. For crimes occurring prior to 9/8/2022, please contact the Program to determine filing requirements.
rules.pinpoint: PA.gov Apply for Victims' Compensation page, Who is eligible?
rules.source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

rules.summary: Claims for counseling related to sexual abuse are an exception to the filing deadline.
rules.quote: (2) Exceptions shall be as follows: (i) ((i) deleted by amendment). (i.1) Claims for counseling services related to sexual abuse under section 701.1.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: If the survivor was under 18 and the abuser was a parent, a caretaker, someone living in the same home, or a parent's partner, the deadline does not start until the survivor turns 21. It then runs until the later of the criminal time limit for the crime or the usual deadline.
rules.quote: If a direct victim is under 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence of the crime and the alleged offender is the direct victim's parent or a person responsible for the direct victim's welfare, an individual residing in the same home as the direct victim or a paramour of the direct victim's parent, all of the following shall apply: (A) The limitation period under this subsection is tolled until the direct victim reaches 21 years of age. (B) The limitation period shall run until the later of: (I) the end of the limitation period for the offense as set forth in 42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 55 Subch. C (relating to criminal proceedings); or (II) the end of the limitation period under paragraph (1).
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: If the survivor was under 18 and the claim is only for counseling, the deadline does not start until the survivor turns 21.
rules.quote: (ii.1) If a direct victim is under 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence of the crime and the direct victim is seeking reimbursement for counseling services only, all of the following shall apply: (A) The limitation period under this subsection is tolled until the direct victim reaches 21 years of age.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: The Office of Victims' Services may accept a late claim for good cause, such as when the victim was incapacitated or a minor, feared retaliation, or the crime was not readily apparent.
rules.quote: (iii.1) The Office of Victims' Services may find good cause to accept a claim beyond the limitation period under paragraph (1) if one of the following circumstances existed at the time of the occurrence of the crime or the discovery of the occurrence of the crime: (A) The direct victim, intervenor or claimant was mentally or physically incapacitated. (B) The victim was a minor. (C) There was a fear of retaliation. (D) The occurrence of the crime was not readily apparent. (E) Other circumstances when good cause is shown by the claimant.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: Under the current law, the crime must have been promptly reported to the proper authorities. The law sets no fixed number of hours.
rules.quote: The crime was promptly reported to the proper authorities.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params.scope: crimes before 9/8/2022

rules.summary: The program's manual says the filing, reporting, and minimum loss rules are different for a crime before 9/8/2022, and asks you to contact the program about them.
rules.quote: For eligibility requirements for crime occurring prior to 9/8/2022, please contact the program as there are different filing requirement, reporting requirement, and minimum loss requirements.
rules.pinpoint: VCAP Manual for Compensation Assistance, Eligibility
rules.source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

rules.summary: Starting a court case for a sexual violence or intimidation protection order can meet the reporting requirement without a police report.
rules.quote: may satisfy the eligibility requirement under subsection (a)(3) for reporting a crime to the proper authorities by commencing an action brought in accordance with 42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 62A (relating to protection of victims of sexual violence or intimidation)
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params.scope: a protection order case that is later withdrawn

rules.summary: If you start a protection order case to meet the report rule and then drop it, you cannot get an award unless the program finds you had good reason to drop it.
rules.quote: An award may not be made if the record shows that the petition was withdrawn, except if the Office of Victims' Services finds the withdrawal to have been justified, consistent with regulations of the Office of Victims' Services.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params.exam_condition: for a crime on or after September 8, 2022

rules.summary: For crimes on or after 9/8/2022, having a forensic rape exam counts as reporting to the proper authorities, so a survivor who had the exam can file a standard claim without reporting the crime to police.
rules.quote: Effective for crimes occurring on or after 9/8/2022, a forensic rape exam is considered acceptable for reporting to proper authorities. This change allows victims who have the FRE completed to be eligible for a standard claim without having to report the crime to law enforcement.
rules.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
rules.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

rules.summary: A survivor of sexual abuse in Pennsylvania who did not or does not want to report can still file a counseling-only claim.
rules.quote: A direct victim of sexual abuse which occurred in Pennsylvania, who did not report or does not want to report the crime to authorities, is eligible to submit a claim for counseling services related to their abuse.
rules.pinpoint: PA.gov VCAP page, Sexual Assault Counseling Claims
rules.source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: For a standard claim, the survivor must also have fully cooperated with law enforcement and the program, unless the program finds there was a good reason not to.
rules.quote: The direct victim, intervenor or claimant has fully cooperated with all law enforcement agencies and the Office of Victims' Services, unless the Office of Victims' Services finds the noncompliance to have been justified consistent with the Office of Victims' Services regulations.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: The program may excuse not cooperating if the survivor was incapacitated, feared retaliation, was a minor, or shows other good cause.
rules.quote: OVS may consider a failure to cooperate with law enforcement and OVS to be justified when one of the following circumstances exist: (1) The direct victim, intervenor or the claimant is mentally or physically incapacitated. (2) There is a fear of retaliation. (3) The victim is a minor. (4) Other circumstances when good cause is shown by the claimant.
rules.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

waived_for: victim or claimant age 60 or older

rules.summary: The claimant must have at least $50 in out-of-pocket loss or lost earnings, unless the victim or claimant was 60 or older.
rules.quote: no award shall be made on a claim unless the claimant has incurred an aggregate minimum out-of-pocket loss, loss of earnings or loss of support of $50. (b) Exception.--Subsection (a) shall not apply if the direct victim or claimant was 60 years of age or older at the time the crime occurred.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: The award is reduced by insurance, public funds, offender payments, settlements and similar payments; the program pays last.
rules.quote: an award made under this chapter shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received by the claimant as a result of the injury
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: In general, the program may reduce or deny an award if the victim's conduct contributed to the injury.
rules.quote: The Office of Victims' Services may reduce the amount or deny the claim altogether in accordance with the determination.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: If the crime is rape or sexual assault, the victim's conduct may not be considered at all.
rules.quote: If the crime involved is rape or sexual assault, the conduct of the direct victim shall not be considered.
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rules.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $5,000 per claim.
rules.quote: The total amount of an emergency award will not exceed $5,000 per claim.
rules.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

rules.summary: Sexual offenses under Chapter 31 of the Pennsylvania Crimes Code (including rape and sexual assault) are personal injury crimes covered by the program.
rules.quote: 18 Pa.C.S. Ch. 31 (relating to sexual offenses).
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 1: Definitions (18 P.S. 11.103)

params.rule: Crime in Pennsylvania, regardless of the victim's residence; or a Pennsylvania resident injured or killed in a foreign country that has no compensation program; or an act of international terrorism. Exam claims have a wider rule (PA-RES-2).

rules.summary: The crime must have occurred in Pennsylvania, or be against a Pennsylvania resident in a foreign country with no compensation program, or be international terrorism.
rules.quote: The crime occurred in Pennsylvania, or to a Pennsylvania resident who is injured or killed in a foreign country that does not have a compensation program, or by an act of international terrorism.
rules.pinpoint: VCAP Manual 2025, Requirements for receiving compensation, 1
rules.source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

params.rule: Exam claims: crime in Pennsylvania, or a Pennsylvania resident assaulted in another state who returns to Pennsylvania for the exam.

rules.summary: A Pennsylvania resident sexually assaulted in another state who comes back to Pennsylvania for the exam can have the exam paid by the Pennsylvania program.
rules.quote: Any provider performing a forensic rape examination on a sexual assault victim may file a claim with VCAP if the crime occurred in Pennsylvania, OR if a Pennsylvania resident that is sexually assaulted in another state returns to Pennsylvania to have the exam done by a hospital or licensed health care provider as defined by the Crime Victims Act.
rules.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, A.5
rules.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

rules.summary: Mail the completed claim form to VCAP's mailing address, PO Box 1167, Harrisburg, PA 17108-1167.
rules.quote: Mailing Address PO Box 1167 Harrisburg, PA 17108-1167
rules.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), back page contact block; PA.gov apply page step 4: 'Mail or email your claim'
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

rules.summary: File the claim online through the DAVE portal (the Crime Victims App also files online).
rules.quote: File online at https://www.dave.pa.gov
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

rules.summary: Email the completed claim form to VCAP at ra-davesupport@pa.gov.
rules.quote: Email ra-davesupport@pa.gov
rules.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), back page contact block; PA.gov apply page step 4: 'Mail or email your claim'
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

params.note: medical bills, in the victim's name

rules.summary: Include itemized medical bills related to the crime, in the victim's name.
rules.quote: Provide all itemized medical bills related to the crime. Medical bills must be in the name of the victim.
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

params.note: counseling bills

rules.summary: Include itemized counseling bills related to the crime.
rules.quote: Provide all itemized counseling bills related to the crime.
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

params.note: cancelled checks or receipts for bills already paid

rules.summary: Include copies of cancelled checks or receipts for any bills the victim or claimant already paid.
rules.quote: Provide copies of cancelled checks and/or receipts for any bills paid by the victim/claimant.
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

params.note: insurance payments or rejections for each bill

rules.summary: If insured, submit bills to insurance first and include the insurance statements showing payments or rejections.
rules.quote: Provide insurance statements of all payments and/or rejections for corresponding bills.
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

params.note: for loss of earnings: two pay stubs before the crime, W-2s, or latest tax return

rules.summary: For lost wages, include two pay stubs from right before the crime, W-2 statements, or the most recent tax return with all schedules.
rules.quote: Provide two pay stubs immediately prior to the crime incident, W-2 statements, or most recently filed IRS tax returns including all schedules.
rules.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

params.note: provider certification of disability, for lost wages from crime injuries

rules.summary: For lost wages from crime injuries, a doctor, psychologist, or other listed provider must certify the disability.
rules.quote: If filing for loss of earnings due to crime-related injuries a physician verification certifying disability is needed.
rules.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

params.note: proof of other pay received (sick, vacation, disability, unemployment, workers comp)

rules.summary: For lost wages, include proof of any sick, vacation, personal, or disability pay or other benefits received.
rules.quote: Provide documentation of any reimbursements received, such as sick, vacation, personal, or disability pay
rules.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

params.note: relocation verification letter from a human service agency, police, or medical provider

rules.summary: For relocation, include a letter from a human service agency, law enforcement, or a medical provider saying the move is needed for safety and health.
rules.quote: Please provide a verification letter explaining that the immediate need for relocation is necessary to protect the safety and health of the victim and individuals residing in the same household
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

params.note: signed acknowledgement, authorization, and HIPAA release on the back of the form

rules.summary: Sign the Acknowledgement and Reimbursement Agreement and Authorization to Obtain Information (and the HIPAA release for medical or counseling expenses) before the claim can be processed.
rules.quote: The Acknowledgement and Reimbursement Agreement and Authorization to Obtain Information must be signed before a claim can be verified and processed for payment.
rules.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Acknowledgement & Reimbursement Agreements section
rules.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

rules.summary: The program says most claims are processed in 12 weeks or less, though each claim differs.
rules.quote: Most organizations process claims in 12 weeks or less.
rules.pinpoint: PA.gov apply page, FAQ: How long does it take the Program to make a decision?
rules.source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

params.note: payment release after approval, for amounts owed to the victim/claimant up to $5,000; the rest in 2 to 4 weeks

rules.summary: Once approved, payments owed to the victim or claimant of $5,000 or less are released within 2 business days.
rules.quote: Payments owed to the victim/claimant that total $5,000.00 or less are released within 2 business days of being approved.
rules.source_title: VCAP flyer: Claim Process (11/2023)

params.enroll: Complete an online ACP application; Visit your local Victim Service Program to complete an ACP Application; Call OVA at 800-563-6399. Online applications are returned to OVA by email (RA-PMOVA-ACPPROGRAM@pa.gov) or mail (Office of Victim Advocate, 1101 S. Front St, Suite 5200, Harrisburg, PA 17112).

rules.summary: Pennsylvania's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of Victim Advocate, can give survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, or child abduction an alternate mailing address to keep their address out of public records, once the office approves their application.
rules.quote: The ACP can provide you with an alternate mailing address to keep your address out of public records if you are a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, or child abduction.
rules.pinpoint: OVA Address Confidentiality Program page; statute: 23 Pa.C.S. 6703(a), 6704(2)
rules.source_title: PA Office of Victim Advocate: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

rules.summary: Everything VCAP obtains or produces while processing a claim is confidential and privileged, is not subject to subpoena or discovery, and may be used only to process the claim; disclosure needs the victim's written consent except as the law provides.
rules.quote:
All reports, records or other information
obtained or produced by the Office of Victims' Services during
the processing or investigation of a claim shall be confidential
and privileged, shall not be subject to subpoena or discovery,
shall be used for no purpose other than the processing of a
claim
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params.payer: Crime Victim Compensation Program (reimburses the exam cost)

rules.summary: The Attorney General's bill of rights says survivors can be compensated for the cost of the forensic exam even if they do not report to police or cooperate with an investigation. It does not say the hospital cannot bill the survivor first.
rules.quote: Victims are eligible to receive compensation for the cost of their forensic sexual assault examination, regardless of whether or not they report the assault to law enforcement and/or cooperate with any investigation or prosecution.
rules.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights (R.I. Gen. Laws § 23-98-5), "Your right to obtain a medical examination"
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights, Rhode Island Attorney General

params.payer: Crime Victim Compensation Program

rules.summary: The Attorney General's bill of rights page also warns that choosing not to take part in the criminal justice system will likely limit your eligibility for compensation benefits.
rules.quote: However, your decision not to participate in the criminal justice system will likely limit your eligibility for benefits under the crime victim compensation program.
rules.pinpoint: Attorney General's Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights page, Your right to choose whether to report
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights, Rhode Island Attorney General

rules.summary: First or second degree sexual assault is one of the offenses the program covers.
rules.quote: First or second degree sexual assault;
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-20 (Offenses to which chapter applies)

rules.summary: A covered injury includes physical harm, mental or nervous shock, and a pregnancy resulting from a sexual attack.
rules.quote: “Personal injury” means actual bodily harm, mental or nervous shock, and a pregnancy resulting from sexual attack.
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-17 (Definitions)

rules.summary: The total award to a victim cannot exceed $25,000 (plus any attorney fees awarded on appeal).
rules.quote: No compensation shall be awarded under this chapter to the victim, or in the case of death to dependent relatives or to the legal representative, in a total amount in excess of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000)
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-22 (Limitations upon awarding compensation)

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 3 years of the injury.
rules.quote: Actions for compensation under this chapter shall be commenced within three (3) years after the date of the injury or death
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-22 (Limitations upon awarding compensation)

rules.summary: For a victim who was a minor, the application is due within three years after turning eighteen.
rules.quote: If the personal injury to the minor victim or secondary victim occurred on or after September 1, 1999, then the application must be filed within three years after the date on which the minor victim or secondary victim reaches the age of eighteen.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: If you found out about the crime more than 1 year after it happened, the time to apply starts when you found out, or should have. This applies only if the crime led to a criminal complaint, an indictment or criminal information, or another court finding of probable cause.
rules.quote: If the Applicant did not discover the act which constitutes a crime until more than one year after the crime was committed, the filing period shall not commence until the Applicant discovered or, in exercise of reasonable diligence, should have discovered, the act which constitutes a crime, provided, however, that in such cases, the crime for which the Applicant seeks compensation must have resulted in the issuance of a criminal complaint, indictment or criminal information, or other judicial determination of probable cause that an act constituting a crime occurred
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.extension: unsound mind or good cause shown

rules.summary: The office may accept a late application if the victim was of unsound mind or shows good cause.
rules.quote: office may allow an application for compensation to be filed with the office after the expiration of the statute of limitations if the victim or secondary victim was of unsound mind or for good cause shown.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: Not knowing the filing rules does not count as good cause for a late application.
rules.quote: Delay resulting from the lack of knowledge of the filing requirements of R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 12-25-1, et seq. shall not constitute good cause.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to police within 15 days, but the office may allow a claim without a police report when a sexual assault survivor had a medical forensic exam within 15 days of the crime.
rules.quote: no compensation shall be awarded for an injury or death resulting from a crime that was not reported to the appropriate law enforcement authority within fifteen (15) days of its occurrence; provided, that the office shall have the authority to allow a claim that was not reported pursuant to this section when a victim of a sexual assault receives a medical forensic examination within fifteen (15) days of the crime
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-22 (Limitations upon awarding compensation)

rules.summary: Applying to a court for a restraining order under R.I. Gen. Laws 15-15-3 with a supporting affidavit, or applying for a criminal complaint, counts as a report to law enforcement.
rules.quote: The reporting of a crime to a court through a citizen application for a restraining order under R.I. Gen. Laws § 15-15-3 accompanied by an affidavit in support of the application for protection, or through a citizen application for a criminal complaint, shall constitute a report to law enforcement authorities.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: Telling a rape crisis center, private security, rescue personnel, or the compensation program does not count as a police report.
rules.quote: Reports to private security personnel, rape crisis centers, rescue personnel, or the Crime Victim Compensation Program do not constitute reports to law enforcement authorities.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: A late police report can be excused for good cause, such as being physically or psychologically unable to make a report, or a reasonable fear of retaliation by the offender or others.
