rules.quote: Good cause for delay shall include, but not be limited to, delay caused by physical or psychological incapacity which prevented the making of a report; or by reasonable fear of retaliation by the offender or others.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.scope: what counts as good cause for a late report

rules.summary: Believing police will not investigate, or not knowing that an award depends on reporting the crime, is not good cause for a late report. The program's rule also says good cause excuses only the delay, not the reporting requirement itself.
rules.quote: Delay resulting from a belief that law enforcement authorities will not investigate the crime, or delay resulting from lack of knowledge that an award under R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-1 et. seq. is contingent upon reporting the crime to law enforcement authorities, does not constitute good cause for delay. d. A finding of good cause for delay does not excuse the reporting requirement which must be satisfied as a condition of receiving compensation.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: A crime against a minor can be reported to the Department of Children, Youth and Families instead of the police.
rules.quote: Crimes involving minor victims may be reported to the Department of Children, Youth and Families pursuant to the reporting requirements of R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 40-11-3 and 40-11-3.1.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.scope: cooperation with law enforcement

rules.summary: The program's rule says a victim must cooperate with reasonable requests from law enforcement in the investigation and prosecution of the crime. It says this includes reporting the crime, helping identify the suspect, and following reasonable requests for information and help.
rules.quote: A victim must cooperate with the reasonable requests of law enforcement agencies and personnel in the investigation and prosecution of the crime. a. Victim’s obligations: Cooperation with law enforcement agencies and personnel includes reporting the crime to law enforcement authorities; assisting in identifying the suspect; and complying with all reasonable requests of law enforcement agencies and personnel for information and assistance.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: The program pays only after insurance, government benefits, and payments from the offender.
rules.quote: The Criminal Injuries Compensation Act shall be regarded as a fund of last resort.
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-23 (Terms of the award)

rules.summary: The office may reduce or deny an award if the victim's own behavior, including past behavior, directly or indirectly contributed to the injury, unless the victim was lawfully trying to stop a crime or catch an offender.
rules.quote: The behavior of the victim, including past behavior, that directly or indirectly contributed to his or her injury or death, unless the injury or death resulted from the victim’s lawful attempt to prevent the commission of a crime or to apprehend an offender. The office may reduce or deny an award based on these circumstances.
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-19 (Awarding compensation)

rules.summary: Emergency awards can cover relocation, safety modifications to the home, crime scene cleanup, and burial; they are at the administrator's discretion and are deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: The office may award emergency compensation under this chapter for the: (1) Burial expenses of a victim who dies as a direct result of a violent crime as defined in this chapter; (2) Cost of the crime scene clean up; (3) Relocation expenses; and (4) Compensation for modifications to a victim’s residence necessary to ensure safety.
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-21.1 (Emergency fund for victims)

rules.summary: Medical expenses, including psychiatric care, that no other source pays are covered.
rules.quote: Medical expenses (including psychiatric care) for which the victim is not compensated by any other source;
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-17 (Definitions)

rules.summary: When the program pays a medical provider, the provider must accept that as full payment and cannot charge the victim more.
rules.quote: Medical service providers shall be required to accept these awards as full payment for services rendered and shall be prohibited from assessing any additional charges against the victim or secondary victim.
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-19 (Awarding compensation)

rules.summary: Dental expenses are among the covered expense types.
rules.quote: Medical, dental and counseling expenses
rules.pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, "What expenses are eligible for reimbursement?"
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ, Office of the General Treasurer

rules.summary: Mental health counseling and psychiatric care caused by the crime are covered.
rules.quote: A victim shall be eligible for compensation for reasonable and necessary mental health counseling and psychiatric care expenses that have been actually and reasonably incurred as a direct result of the crime.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: Individual sessions with a licensed psychiatrist are paid at up to $130 per hour.
rules.quote: $130 per hour is reimbursed for individual services provided by a licensed psychiatrist;
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: Individual sessions with a licensed clinical psychologist are paid at up to $110 per hour.
rules.quote: $110 per hour is reimbursed for individual services provided by a licensed clinical psychologist;
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: Individual sessions with a licensed clinical social worker, mental health nurse, marriage and family therapist, or psychiatric clinical nurse specialist are paid at up to $90 per hour.
rules.quote: $90 per hour is reimbursed for individual services provided by a licensed clinical social worker, mental health nurse, marriage and family therapist (MFT), or clinical nurse specialist with a specialty in psychiatric mental health nursing;
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: Lost earnings that no other source replaces are covered.
rules.quote: Loss of past earnings for which the victim is not compensated by any other source;
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-17 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Lost earnings for injuries on or after January 1, 2022 are figured at 62% of gross earnings.
rules.quote: All net earnings for injuries occurring on or after January 1, 2022 are calculated based on 62% of the victim’s gross earnings.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: Travel and overnight stays to get medical care or counseling or to attend court are capped at $1,000 per claim (the administrator may waive the cap for good cause).
rules.quote: An award for reasonable and necessary travel expenses and overnight accommodation shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) per claim.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: Temporary or permanent relocation costs of a victim can be covered.
rules.quote: The Administrator may issue an award for expenses resulting from the temporary or permanent relocation of a victim
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: Emergency relocation is capped at $5,000. Any relocation award is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: Compensation awarded for emergency relocation expenses shall not exceed the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00). Any award for emergency relocation expenses shall be deducted from the final award.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: To be paid for a move, the crime must have happened in your home. If it did not, you must show the crime makes you reasonably afraid to stay there. You must also need to move right away, reasonably fear living as you did before the crime, or be unable to afford your documented housing costs right after the crime.
rules.quote: The crime must have occurred in the victim’s primary place of residence or the Applicant must demonstrate that, as a result of the crime, he or she reasonably fears for his or her continued safety in his or her primary place of residence. (2) An Applicant must have an immediate need to relocate, a reasonable fear to continue to live within the arrangements as established prior to the crime, or, alternatively, immediately following the crime, the Applicant must be unable to afford the documented housing costs.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rules.summary: Safety modifications to the home are capped at $1,000 and cannot be paid on top of an emergency relocation award.
rules.quote: An award for expenses associated with reasonable modifications to the victim’s residence necessary to ensure victim safety shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) and shall not be awarded in addition to an award for emergency compensation for relocation costs.
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-21.1 (Emergency fund for victims)

params.item: property losses

rules.summary: Property losses are not covered.
rules.quote: Property losses are not compensable expenses.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: Pain and suffering is not paid for crimes on or after September 1, 1999.
rules.quote: any claims involving crimes resulting in personal injury or death which occurred on or after September 1, 1999 would not be eligible for an award for pain and suffering.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.rule: Crimes in Rhode Island (including its maritime jurisdiction) are covered regardless of the victim's residence.

rules.summary: Crimes that happen in Rhode Island are covered; the statute does not limit this to Rhode Island residents.
rules.quote: Within the physical confines of the state of Rhode Island;
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-19 (Awarding compensation)

params.rule: Rhode Island residents injured out of state, only if not entitled to compensation where the crime occurred.

rules.summary: A Rhode Island resident hurt in another state can apply here only if they also lived in Rhode Island when it happened and are not entitled to any compensation from the state where it happened.
rules.quote: Outside the state of Rhode Island to any victim who has his or her residence in the state of Rhode Island and had the residence in the state at the time that the offense occurred, and is not entitled to compensation of any kind from the state, possession, or territory or district of the United States in which the offense occurred
rules.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-19 (Awarding compensation)

params.target: CRIME VICTIM COMPENSATION PROGRAM, Office of the General Treasurer, 50 Service Avenue, 2nd Floor, Warwick, RI 02886

rules.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Crime Victim Compensation Program at the Office of the General Treasurer in Warwick.
rules.quote: Return completed Application to: CRIME VICTIM COMPENSATION PROGRAM Office of the General Treasurer 50 Service Avenue, 2nd Floor Warwick, RI 02886
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (English)

rules.summary: A printed application can be faxed to the program.
rules.quote: You can also print out an application below, either in English or Spanish, and fax it to 401-462-7694
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Program page, how to apply
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ, Office of the General Treasurer

rules.summary: Applications can be filed online through the Treasury's CVCP portal; registration is required.
rules.quote: Applications can be submitted online here . (registration required)
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Program page, how to apply (link target http://cvcapp.treasury.ri.gov/)
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ, Office of the General Treasurer

rules.summary: Include a copy of a valid photo ID with the application.
rules.quote: MUST SUBMIT A COPY OF A VALID PHOTO ID
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (English)

params.note: copies of bills for each expense checked on the form

rules.summary: Include copies of the bills for the expenses being claimed.
rules.quote: PLEASE SUBMIT COPIES OF BILLS
rules.source_title: CVCP Application (English)

params.note: signed application with release of information; the form's consent section must be signed and dated

rules.summary: The application must be signed under penalty of perjury and include a release of information.
rules.quote: The application must be signed by the Applicant under the pains and penalties of perjury;
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.note: where appropriate: lost wage verifications, W-2 forms, tax returns

rules.summary: Where they apply, the applicant must provide lost wage verifications, W-2 forms, and tax returns.
rules.quote: Such documentation shall include, where appropriate, all expenses, lost wage verifications, W-2 forms, tax returns, death and birth certificates, and the incident report from the appropriate law enforcement authorities.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.note: incident report from law enforcement, where appropriate; the form also asks for the police department and report number

rules.summary: Where appropriate, the applicant provides the incident report from law enforcement.
rules.quote: Such documentation shall include, where appropriate, all expenses, lost wage verifications, W-2 forms, tax returns, death and birth certificates, and the incident report from the appropriate law enforcement authorities.
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.note: optional for sexual assault victims: evidence of a SANE or qualifying medical forensic exam, used in place of or alongside a police report

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor may submit evidence of a Sexual Assault Nurse Examination or other qualifying medical forensic exam.
rules.quote: Victims of sexual assault may submit documentary evidence of their Sexual Assault Nurse Examination or other qualifying Medical Forensic Examination consistent with the requirements of R.I. Gen. Laws
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.note: on request, when claiming lost earnings: a disability letter from a treating physician or mental health provider

rules.summary: If the office asks, a victim claiming lost earnings must send a disability letter from a treating physician or mental health provider.
rules.quote: Upon request by the office, the victim must submit a disability letter from a treating physician or mental health provider demonstrating that the victim is disabled from working as a direct result of the crime
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.agency: Rhode Island Department of State (Secretary of State)
params.enroll: Click here to download the application. Applications should be sent to: Department of State Attention: ACP PO Box 6888 Providence, RI 02940. Applicants can contact the Department by email, phone, or in-person for help filling out the application.

rules.summary: Rhode Island's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of State, helps victims of domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, trafficking, or abuse who have moved or are about to move. To qualify, you must live in Rhode Island, fear for your own or your children's safety, live or plan to live at an address the person who harmed you does not know, and agree not to give that person the address. You apply by mailing a sworn application to the Department, which can help you fill it out.
rules.quote: The goal of the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP/Program) is to help victims of domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, and trafficking and/or abuse as defined by RI Gen. Laws §42-164-2 who have relocated or are about to relocate
rules.source_title: Address Confidentiality Program page, Rhode Island Department of State

rules.summary: Medical, counseling, psychiatric, employment, financial, and investigative records the compensation office gets with a claim are confidential and cannot be released without the applicant's permission unless law allows it. The application itself and the notice of award or denial are treated as public records unless another law says otherwise.
rules.quote: All medical records, mental health counseling records, psychiatric records, employment information, personal financial information and investigative records received, obtained or maintained by the office in connection with any application for compensation shall be maintained as confidential investigative material
rules.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params.scope: the routine forensic exam

rules.summary: State law says a victim of criminal sexual conduct or child sexual abuse must not bear the cost of the routine medicolegal (forensic) exam.
rules.quote: The State must ensure that a victim of criminal sexual conduct in any degree, criminal sexual conduct with a minor in any degree, or child sexual abuse must not bear the cost of his or her routine medicolegal exam following the assault.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

params.scope: the routine forensic exam

rules.summary: The program's hospital billing instructions say neither the victim nor the victim's insurance, including Medicaid and Medicare, may be billed for the medicolegal exam.
rules.quote: Neither the victim nor their insurance, including Medicaid and Medicare, may be billed for the medicolegal examination.
rules.pinpoint: DCVC Sexual Assault Program provider instructions, Sexual Assault Forensic Medical Examination
rules.source_title: DCVC Sexual Assault Program: Instructions for Reimbursement of Hospital Billing by DCVC (Feb 2018 provider guide)

params.payer: South Carolina Department of Crime Victim Compensation (Victim Compensation Fund), billed directly by the health care facility
params.condition: if the crime was in South Carolina

rules.summary: The hospital or health care facility may file the exam claim directly with the Department of Crime Victim Compensation if the offense happened in South Carolina.
rules.quote: may file a claim for reimbursement directly to the Office of the Attorney General, South Carolina Crime Victim Services Division, Department of Crime Victim Compensation if the offense occurred in South Carolina.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

params.payer: South Carolina Department of Crime Victim Compensation (DCVC)

rules.summary: The program says it is the only payer for forensic medical exams in South Carolina; providers bill it directly and its fee-schedule payment is payment in full.
rules.quote: Sexual Assault Program: DCVC is the Sole Reimbursement Provider for Forensic Medical Examinations in S.C. Health Care Providers will bill DCVC directly; all reimbursements are from a fee schedule and are considered payment in full.
rules.pinpoint: DCVC sexual assault brochure, Sexual Assault Program
rules.source_title: DCVC brochure: Compensation Benefits for Victims of Sexual Assault

rules.summary: The program's sexual assault brochure says victims of an assault in South Carolina can ask for a forensic exam at no cost. This holds whether or not they involve police.
rules.quote: victims of assault in the State of South Carolina may request, at no cost to them, a forensic examination for sexual assault, regardless of their involvement with law enforcement.
rules.source_title: DCVC brochure: Compensation Benefits for Victims of Sexual Assault

params.payer: South Carolina Department of Crime Victim Compensation (DCVC), Sexual Assault Program

rules.summary: The program's provider guide says an exam with no evidence kit collected (NKC) is also paid. It covers victims who decline the rape kit.
rules.quote: This expense covers victims who decline the rape kit.
rules.pinpoint: DCVC Sexual Assault Program provider instructions, Sexual Assault Program Eligibility Criteria (NKC)
rules.source_title: DCVC Sexual Assault Program: Instructions for Reimbursement of Hospital Billing by DCVC (Feb 2018 provider guide)

params.payer: South Carolina Department of Crime Victim Compensation (DCVC), Sexual Assault Program

rules.summary: For a victim who declines the kit, the nurse offers the same exam without collecting evidence, within the program's set time of 72-120 hours after the assault.
rules.quote: The SANE will offer the medical forensic exam without evidence collection and will follow the same procedures including a thorough examination of the victim within the set time parameters which is 72 -120 hours post assault.
rules.pinpoint: DCVC Sexual Assault Program provider instructions, Sexual Assault Program Eligibility Criteria (NKC)
rules.source_title: DCVC Sexual Assault Program: Instructions for Reimbursement of Hospital Billing by DCVC (Feb 2018 provider guide)

params.payer: South Carolina Department of Crime Victim Compensation (DCVC), Sexual Assault Program

rules.summary: The program's brochure says its exam for adults 18 and older is for evidence collected within 120 hours of the assault.
rules.quote: Evidence collected within 120 hours of the assault for victims 18 and older
rules.pinpoint: DCVC sexual assault brochure, Sexual Assault (ACUTE) Protocol
rules.source_title: DCVC brochure: Compensation Benefits for Victims of Sexual Assault

params.payer: South Carolina Department of Crime Victim Compensation (DCVC), Sexual Assault Program

rules.summary: The program's brochure lists reasons it may delay or deny exam payments. One is that police did not order the exam or interview for a victim 17 or younger.
rules.quote: Law enforcement did not order the exam/interview for victim 17 and younger
rules.pinpoint: DCVC sexual assault brochure, Reasons Payments Are Delayed or Denied
rules.source_title: DCVC brochure: Compensation Benefits for Victims of Sexual Assault

params.item: charges beyond evidence collection during the forensic exam, such as follow-up care (the victim can claim them through a compensation application)

rules.summary: The Sexual Assault Program pays for the evidence collection exam on its fee schedule. Fees beyond evidence collection, such as follow-up care, are the victim's responsibility, but the victim can file a regular compensation application to ask the fund to pay them.
rules.quote: Any fees beyond the actual collection of evidence during a forensic examination are the responsibility of the victim. A Victim may submit a Compensation application for payment consideration to the Victims' Compensation Fund for these additional costs.
rules.pinpoint: DCVC Sexual Assault Program provider instructions, Sexual Assault Forensic Medical Examination
rules.source_title: DCVC Sexual Assault Program: Instructions for Reimbursement of Hospital Billing by DCVC (Feb 2018 provider guide)

params.exception: or up to $25,000 in extraordinary cases

rules.summary: Total awards for a victim are capped at $15,000, or up to $25,000 if the advisory board (by a two-thirds vote) and the director agree extraordinary circumstances exist.
rules.quote: The aggregate of award to and on behalf of victims may not exceed fifteen thousand dollars unless the Crime Victim Advisory Board, by two-thirds vote, and the director concur that extraordinary circumstances exist. In this case, the award may not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

rules.summary: Payment for counseling is limited to 20 sessions or to the sessions in the 180 days after the first one, whichever is more. The board may let victims who use up 20 sessions ask for up to 20 more, 40 in all, if the director recommends it.
rules.quote: Payment for mental health counseling is limited to the number of sessions during a one hundred eighty-day period beginning on the date of the first counseling session or twenty sessions, whichever is greater. Upon recommendation of the director, the board may allow victims who max out the current benefit of twenty mental health counseling sessions to request up to an additional twenty sessions for a total of forty sessions;
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

rules.summary: Reasonable and customary charges for medical services, including mental health counseling, needed because of the crime injury are covered when a licensed professional provides them.
rules.quote: reasonable and customary charges as periodically determined by the board for medical services, including mental health counseling, required and rendered as a direct result of the injury on which the claim is based, as long as these services are rendered by a licensed professional.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

rules.summary: An award can pay for mental health counseling needed because of the crime. A licensed professional must provide it.
rules.quote: An award may be made for: (1) reasonable and customary charges as periodically determined by the board for medical services, including mental health counseling, required and rendered as a direct result of the injury on which the claim is based, as long as these services are rendered by a licensed professional.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

rules.summary: The program lists dental and orthodontic services as expenses it may consider.
rules.quote: Dental or Orthodontic Services
rules.pinpoint: DCVC compensation brochure, Services DCVC May Consider For Payment
rules.source_title: DCVC brochure: What is Crime Victim Compensation?

rules.summary: Funeral and burial costs of a deceased victim can be paid to the claimant who took on the debt.
rules.quote: Funeral/burial of a deceased victim. The claimant must incur the debt for the funeral/burial
rules.pinpoint: SC Attorney General, Crime Victim Compensation program page
rules.source_title: SC Attorney General, Crime Victim Compensation (program page)

rules.summary: The program lists doctor-ordered medicine, equipment, and supplies as expenses it may consider.
rules.quote: Doctor ordered medicine, equipment, supplies

params.extension: or of a later date in some cases, such as when police learned it was a crime. With good cause, the program can allow up to 4 years after the crime

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 180 days. The days count from the latest of these: the crime, the victim's death, the day police learned it was a crime, or, for a crime against a minor, the day a resulting injury was diagnosed. With good cause, the time can be extended, but not past 4 years after the crime, the diagnosis, or the death.
rules.quote: A claim must be filed by the claimant not later than one hundred eighty days after the latest of the following events: (1) the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based; (2) the death of the victim; (3) the discovery by the law enforcement agency that the occurrence was the result of crime; or (4) the manifestation of a mental or physical injury is diagnosed as a result of a crime committed against a minor. (C) Upon good cause shown, the time for filing may be extended for a period not to exceed four years after the occurrence, diagnosed manifestation, or death.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

params.exception: or later if special circumstances justify it

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to the proper authority promptly; a report more than 48 hours after the crime is not prompt unless special circumstances justify the delay.
rules.quote: For the purposes of subsection (A)(3), a crime reported more than forty-eight hours after its occurrence is not "promptly reported", absent a showing of special circumstances or causes which justify the delay.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

rules.summary: No award can be made unless the crime was promptly reported and recorded in police records. The crime must have directly caused the victim physical or mental harm. The claimant must also have fully cooperated with all law enforcement agencies and with the program.
rules.quote: No award may be made unless: (1) a crime was committed; (2) the crime directly resulted in physical or psychic trauma to the victim; (3) the crime was promptly reported to the proper authority and recorded in police records; and (4) the claimant or other award recipient has fully cooperated with all law enforcement agencies and with the Office of the Attorney General, South Carolina Crime Victim Services Division, Department of Crime Victim Compensation.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

rules.summary: For sexual assault, the program says law enforcement is involved in processing a compensation application unless the victim files anonymously.
rules.quote: Please Note: Law enforcement will be involved as the crime victim compensation application is processed, unless the victim files anonymously.
rules.pinpoint: DCVC sexual assault brochure, Sexual Assault Program
rules.source_title: DCVC brochure: Compensation Benefits for Victims of Sexual Assault

rules.summary: The program's provider guide lists what the anonymous route needs. An eligible sexual assault claim is on file with the program. The crime happened in South Carolina. The hospital recorded the victim's physical or psychological injuries. The program got a compensation application with "Anonymous" written in section 4 within 180 days of the forensic exam.
rules.quote: Anonymous Waiver Reporting Criteria: • An eligible Sexual Assault claim is on file with DCVC. • The crime must have occurred in SC. • The victim sustained physical or psychological injuries recorded by the hospital. • DCVC received a Compensation Application with “Anonymous” written in section 4, within 180 days from the date of forensic medical examination.
rules.pinpoint: DCVC Sexual Assault Program provider instructions, Anonymous Reporting: Sexual Assault (Acute) Protocols (Victims 18 and older), Anonymous Waiver Reporting Criteria
rules.source_title: DCVC Sexual Assault Program: Instructions for Reimbursement of Hospital Billing by DCVC (Feb 2018 provider guide)

rules.summary: An award is made only for compensable loss over $100; this can be waived in the interest of justice and must be waived for claimants 65 or older.
rules.quote: An award may be made only if and to the extent that the amount of compensable loss exceeds one hundred dollars; however, this limitation may be waived in the interest of justice and must be waived upon a showing that the claimant is at least sixty-five years old.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

rules.summary: The $100 deductible is waived for the sexual assault exam.
rules.quote: For the purpose of this particular exam, the one hundred dollar deductible is waived for award eligibility under the fund.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

rules.summary: An award can be reduced by payments from the offender or any other private or public source, such as workers' compensation, but not by gifts from family or charitable donations.
rules.quote: Any award made pursuant to this article may be reduced by or set off by the amount of any payments received or to be received as a result of the injury (a) from or on behalf of the person who committed the crime, (b) from any other private or public source, including an award of workers' compensation pursuant to the laws of this State or (c) as an emergency award pursuant to Section 16-3-1150; provided, that private sources shall not include contributions received from family members, or persons or private organizations making charitable donations to a victim.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

rules.summary: In a compensation claim, insurance must be billed first. If the victim has insurance and chooses not to use it, the program will not cover the cost.
rules.quote: Payer of Last Resort: Insurance must be filed first if a victim has private or public insurance. DCVC is the payer of last resort. If the victim has insurance, and the victim elects not to use his/her insurance, DCVC will not cover the cost.
rules.pinpoint: DCVC Payments and Reimbursements At A Glance, Payer of Last Resort
rules.source_title: DCVC Payments and Reimbursements At A Glance (Rev 8/2021)

rules.summary: In a compensation claim, private or public insurance is used first, and the program can pay deductibles and co-pays if otherwise eligible.
rules.quote: DCVC is the payer of last resort (Victims' private/public insurance must be used first. DCVC can pay deductibles and co-pays if otherwise eligible)
rules.pinpoint: DCVC compensation brochure, Services DCVC May Consider For Payment
rules.source_title: DCVC brochure: What is Crime Victim Compensation?

rules.summary: The program may reduce or reject an award if it finds the victim's own conduct contributed to the injury.
rules.quote: In determining the amount of an award, the Deputy Director, the Board, or its panel shall determine whether because of his conduct the victim or intervenor of such crime contributed to the infliction of his injury, and the Deputy Director, the Board, or its panel may reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether in accordance with such determination;
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

rules.summary: If an award is likely and waiting would cause undue hardship, emergency awards of up to $500 each, and $1,000 total, can be paid before the final decision and are deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: (1) the amount of each emergency award shall not exceed five hundred dollars; (2) the total amount of such emergency awards shall not exceed one thousand dollars; (3) the amount of such emergency awards must be deducted from any final award made to the claimant;
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

params.enroll: If you are interested in enrolling in the Address Confidentiality Program, please contact the ACP at [email address obfuscated in saved page] or 803-734-4517 to be connected with an Application Assistant in your area. (Statute: Upon the recommendation of an application assistant, an individual, or a parent, guardian, or other appropriate adult for a minor, may apply to the Attorney General for assignation of a designated address.)

rules.summary: South Carolina's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Attorney General, lets victims of domestic violence, human trafficking, stalking, harassment, or sexual offenses apply, with an application assistant's help, for a designated substitute address that state and local agencies and courts must use, plus forwarding of first-class, certified, and registered mail. The program's page says participants must live in South Carolina or plan to move there, and must be adults or a parent or guardian applying for a minor; there is no fee.
rules.quote: The address confidentiality program is established to protect victims of domestic violence, human trafficking, stalking, harassment, or sexual offenses by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims. The program is administered by the Attorney General
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 25 (incl. 16-25-130, Victim address confidentiality program)

rules.summary: Information about people applying for or receiving compensation may not be disclosed except to run the fund or with the applicant's written consent, and the program's records and files are confidential and exempt from the Freedom of Information Act.
rules.quote: The records, papers, files, and communications of the board, its panel, and the director and his staff must be regarded as confidential information and privileged and not subject to disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act as contained in Chapter 4, Title 30.
rules.source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

params.payer: the county where the alleged rape or sexual offense occurred

rules.summary: The county where the sexual assault happened pays for the forensic medical exam.
rules.quote: The county where an alleged rape or sexual offense occurred shall pay the cost of any forensic medical examination performed on the victim of the alleged rape or sexual offense.
rules.source_title: SDCL 22-22-26, Forensic medical examination, costs to county

params.payer: the county where the alleged rape or sexual offense occurred

rules.summary: The exam cost the county pays includes the provider and facility services for the exam, forensic supplies, scope procedures, lab tests such as STI, HIV, and pregnancy screening, any medication given during the exam, and radiology tied to the exam.
rules.quote: The cost of a forensic medical examination includes: (1) Provider, hospital, or clinic services directly related to the examination; (2) Necessary forensic supplies; (3) Scope procedures directly related to the examination, including anoscopy and colposcopy; (4) Laboratory testing directly related to the examination, including drug screening, urinalysis, pregnancy screening, syphilis screening, chlamydia culture, gonorrhea coverage culture, HIV screening, hepatitis B and C screening, herpes culture, and any other sexually transmitted disease testing directly related to the examination; (5) Any medication provided during the examination; and (6) Any radiology service directly related to the examination.
rules.source_title: SDCL 22-22-26, Forensic medical examination, costs to county

params.condition: if the crime was in South Dakota

rules.summary: For an exam under section 22-22-26, which has the county where the assault happened pay, hospitals and clinics must tell survivors the exam is available at no cost to them. A survivor does not have to take part in the criminal case or cooperate with police to get the exam. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.
rules.quote: Each hospital and clinic that provides a forensic medical examination under § 22-22-26 shall coordinate with the county to establish a payment process by which the county shall pay for the cost of the examination, and to notify any victim of rape or sexual offense of the availability of an examination at no cost to the victim. A victim of rape or sexual offense is not required to participate in the criminal justice system or to cooperate with law enforcement to be provided with a forensic medical examination.
rules.source_title: SDCL 22-22-26.2, Forensic medical examinations, payment, notice to victim

rules.summary: The compensation program does not reimburse rape or sexual offense exams that are provided under the county-pay exam statute.
rules.quote: Reimbursement is not allowed for rape or sexual offense examinations provided under the provisions of SDCL
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

rules.summary: Total compensation for one victim's injury or death may not exceed $15,000.
rules.quote: Compensation granted to any claimant suffering economic loss as the result of injury to or death of any one victim may not exceed fifteen thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: Except for an emergency award, the commission may go above the limits on single costs when the claimant shows evidence of need. In no case can payments go above the program's overall limit.
rules.quote: With the exception of an emergency award, the commission may deviate from the limits established in this chapter. The claimant must submit evidence to the commission that substantiates the need for the deviation. Based on the evidence submitted, the commission shall determine whether the deviation is warranted. Within 15 days of the commission's decision, the department shall notify the individual in writing. Under no circumstances may payments exceed the program limits established in SDCL 23A-28B-21.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

rules.summary: Security devices are covered up to $500, including materials and labor.
rules.quote: Payment for security devices may not exceed $500, including materials and labor.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

rules.summary: Basic funeral and burial expenses are capped at $8,000.
rules.quote: Payment for basic funeral and burial expenses may not exceed $8,000.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

params.applies_to: homicide scene cleanup

rules.summary: Homicide scene cleanup is capped at $1,500.
rules.quote: Payment for homicide scene cleanup may not exceed one thousand five hundred dollars.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

rules.summary: Lost earnings are paid based on the victim's average monthly earnings for the 6 months before the injury or the monthly minimum wage, whichever is less. The monthly minimum wage is the federal hourly minimum wage times 173.2 hours.
rules.quote: Loss of earnings, loss of future earnings, and loss of support shall be determined on the basis of the victim's average monthly earnings for the six months immediately preceding the date of injury, or the monthly minimum wage as of the date of the crime underlying the claim, whichever is less. The monthly minimum wage shall be based upon the federal hourly minimum wage in effect as of the date of the crime multiplied by 173.2 hours per month.
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: When the victim is the claimant, lost earnings are paid only for the 12 months right after the crime.
rules.quote: Payment for lost earnings or loss of future earnings is limited to the following: (1) If the claimant is the victim, the 12-month period immediately following the date of the crime;
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

rules.summary: Mental health services are covered, including individual or group counseling by a qualified mental health professional, for a limited number of months after the crime.
rules.quote: Payment for mental health services is limited to assessment, diagnosis, and treatment, including individual or group counseling sessions provided by a mental health professional
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

rules.summary: If the victim was a juvenile at the time of the crime and the late-filing deadline is waived for good cause, mental health services can be paid for up to 24 months from the date of the application.
rules.quote: If the victim is a juvenile, or was a juvenile at the time of victimization, and there is good cause to waive the one-year requirement under SDCL 23A-28B-25 , payment for mental health services may be made for up to 24 months from the date of the application.
rules.source_title: ARSD 67:55:04:03, Mental health services

rules.summary: Covered medical expense includes medical and dental services, mental health counseling, dental and prosthetic devices, and eyeglasses or other corrective lenses.
rules.quote: "Medical expense," the cost of all medical and dental services, mental health counseling, dental and prosthetic devices, eyeglasses or other corrective lenses
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: Payment for medical expenses is limited to medical services provided in the 12 months right after the crime. The department may extend this 12-month period for good cause.
rules.quote: payment for medical expenses is limited to those medical services provided during the 12-month period immediately following the date the crime occurred. The department may extend this 12-month period if good cause is shown.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

rules.summary: Medical services are paid only if given in the 12 months after the crime. The department may extend this for good cause. This 12-month limit does not apply to mental health care or to medicine for a mental condition.
rules.quote: Except for mental health expenses covered under § 67:55:04:03 and the costs of medications related to the treatment of a mental condition, payment for medical expenses is limited to those medical services provided during the 12-month period immediately following the date the crime occurred. The department may extend this 12-month period if good cause is shown.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

params.scope: mileage to treatment, court, or meetings with police

rules.summary: Mileage is covered for the victim's trips to treatment and therapy, to court proceedings, and to meet with law enforcement.
rules.quote: Mileage accrued for the victim to obtain treatment and therapy; (3) Mileage accrued for the victim to attend court proceedings; (4) Mileage accrued for the victim to meet with law enforcement
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

params.scope: mileage to a hospital or medical facility for a sexual assault exam

rules.summary: Mileage is covered for getting the victim to a hospital or medical facility for a sexual assault exam.
rules.quote: Mileage accrued for transporting the victim to a hospital or medical facility for a sexual assault examination
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

params.scope: mileage in a private car, paid at the state employee rate

rules.summary: Mileage is reimbursed at the state employee rate for a privately owned car.
rules.quote: Mileage is reimbursed at the rate established for state employees in SDCL 3-9-1 , as applicable, for the use of a privately owned automobile.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

rules.summary: Security devices such as locks, door eyeholes, and security lights needed for the victim's safety are a covered loss.
rules.quote: "Security devices," the cost to repair or install locks, door eyeholes, security lights, or other similar security and safety measures necessary to ensure the safety of the victim.
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: Security devices can be paid for. This includes digital security cameras.
rules.quote: Expenses for security devices , including digital security cameras, are payable.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

params.item: monthly service cost of a security device

rules.quote: monthly service cost , if any, of a security device installed for the benefit of a victim is the victim's responsibility.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

params.scope: replacing clothing, bedding, and other property used as evidence

rules.summary: The replacement value of property taken as evidence, including clothing and bedding, is covered if it is not returned.
rules.quote: "Personal property losses," the replacement value of property, including clothing and bedding, used for evidentiary purposes
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: Child care is covered when the parent cannot care for the child because of crime-related impairment, court, police meetings, or a medical appointment.
rules.quote: Child care expenses are payable if the parent is unable to care for the child because the parent has sustained physical or emotional impairment as a direct result of a crime, if the parent is required to attend court proceedings or meet with law enforcement, or the parent has a medical appointment.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

params.item: cell phones, guns, guard dogs

rules.summary: The program does not pay for cell phones, guns, or guard dogs.
rules.quote: No payment may be made for cell phones, guns, or guard dogs.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

params.item: property losses, attorney's fees, pain and suffering

rules.summary: The program does not pay for property losses (other than items kept as evidence), attorney's fees, or pain and suffering.
rules.quote: Compensation cannot be paid for property losses, attorney's fees, or pain and suffering.
