params.item: property damaged in the incident

rules.summary: Property damaged in the incident is not covered.
rules.quote: Only clothing and bedding that was collected as evidence, and will not be returned to the claimant, is compensable through the CVC Program. Property damaged in the incident is not eligible for compensation.
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Primary Application Instructions

params.extension: or later if the department waives the deadline for good cause

rules.summary: The application must be filed within one year after the date of the injury, but the department may waive that for good cause.
rules.quote: Unless an application for compensation is filed with the department within one year after the date of the personal injury or death and the personal injury or death was the result of a crime which had been reported to a law enforcement officer or agency within five days of its occurrence or, if the crime could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within five days of the date when a report could reasonably have been made. The department may waive the one year application requirement for good cause shown
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

params.exception: or, if you could not reasonably report that soon, within 5 days of when you could

rules.summary: The crime must have been reported to law enforcement within 5 days. If that was not reasonably possible, it must have been reported within 5 days of when it could have been.
rules.quote: the personal injury or death was the result of a crime which had been reported to a law enforcement officer or agency within five days of its occurrence or, if the crime could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within five days of the date when a report could reasonably have been made
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: If the crime was not reported within 5 days of when it happened, or the victim did not cooperate, the application asks for a letter explaining the late report or the decision not to cooperate.
rules.quote: If the crime was not reported within 5 days of the date that it occurred or if the victim did not cooperate, please submit a letter explaining the reason for the delay in reporting or decision not to cooperate.
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

rules.summary: No award may be made if the victim fails or refuses to cooperate fully with law enforcement or with the department.
rules.quote: Fails or refuses to cooperate fully with any appropriate law enforcement officer or agency or with the department in the administration of this chapter.
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: Any award is reduced by money the victim gets, or will get, because of the crime from the sources the law lists. These include the offender, insurance, Medicaid or Medicare, workers compensation, and an employer's wage continuation.
rules.quote: Any award of victims' compensation made pursuant to this chapter shall be reduced by the amount of any payment received, or to be received, by the victim from any collateral source as a result of the conduct giving rise to the application for compensation.
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: Before the compensation program pays a bill for a rape exam or related care, the bill must first go to insurance and other sources, including health insurance.
rules.quote: Bills for rape exams and related expenses must be submitted to collateral sources, including health insurance, before payment may be made under the provisions of this article.
rules.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

rules.summary: An award may be denied if the victim's conduct substantially contributed to the injury, but by statute this does not apply to victims of a sex offense under chapter 22-22, human trafficking, domestic abuse, or child abuse.
rules.quote: Engaged in conduct which substantially contributed to the infliction of the victim's injury or death or engaged in conduct which the victim should reasonably have foreseen could lead to the injury or death. However, this subsection does not apply to any victim defined in subsections 23A-28B-1(12)(b) and (c) or to any victim of: a sex offense under chapter 22-22 ; human trafficking under chapter 22-49 ; domestic abuse under § 25-10-1 ; child abuse, neglect, or exploitation under § 26-8A-2
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $1,000.
rules.quote: The amount of an emergency award may not exceed one thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: A covered crime is conduct in South Dakota that is punishable as a felony or misdemeanor and causes personal injury or death.
rules.quote: "Crime," conduct that occurs or is attempted in this state, including that arising from domestic violence, human trafficking, and acts of terrorism, as defined in 18 USC § 2331 as of January 1, 1997, which conduct results in personal injury or death and is punishable as a felony or misdemeanor
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: Personal injury includes emotional distress, not only bodily harm.
rules.quote: "Personal injury," actual bodily harm or emotional distress
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: An award can be made whether or not anyone is prosecuted or convicted for the crime.
rules.quote: An award of compensation may be made without regard to whether any person is prosecuted or convicted for the criminal conduct that is the basis of the award.
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

params.rule: Crimes in South Dakota are covered. A South Dakota resident hurt by a crime outside the state may apply only if that place has no compensation law covering the injury (or, per ARSD 67:55:01:09, the person applied there and was found ineligible).

rules.summary: South Dakota residents hurt by a crime in another state have the same rights as if it happened in South Dakota, but only if that state has no compensation law that covers the injury.
rules.quote: If a resident of South Dakota is a victim of a crime as defined in § 23A-28B-1 , but the crime occurred outside the boundaries of this state, the resident has the same rights under the provisions of this chapter as if the crime had occurred within this state upon a showing that the state, territory, country, or political subdivision of a country in which the crime occurred does not have a crime victims' compensation law which covers the injury or death suffered by the resident.
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

params.target: Department of Public Safety Crime Victims' Compensation Program 118 West Capitol Avenue Pierre SD 57501

rules.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Department of Public Safety, Crime Victims' Compensation Program, 118 West Capitol Avenue, Pierre SD 57501.
rules.quote:
Please return completed application to:
Department of Public Safety
Crime Victims’ Compensation Program
118 West Capitol Avenue
Pierre SD 57501
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

rules.summary: The application can be emailed as a digital copy to VictimsServices@state.sd.us; the program's apply page says to mail the form or email a digital copy.
rules.quote: Email address: VictimsServices@state.sd.us
rules.pinpoint: Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17), page 2, program contact block
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.note: The word MAVIS in the quote links to this URL on the program's apply page.

rules.summary: A survivor can apply online through the state's MAVIS portal instead of filing the paper form.
rules.quote: You may apply online for Crime Victims' Compensation through MAVIS.
rules.pinpoint: SD DPS Eligibility and Apply page, Apply section
rules.source_title: SD DPS, Crime Victims' Compensation Eligibility and Apply

params.note: Copies of all medical bills related to the crime.

rules.summary: Attach copies of all medical bills that apply to the request.
rules.quote: Attach copies of all bills, receipts, and insurance benefits statements received that apply to this request.
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

rules.summary: Attach copies of insurance benefits statements received for the claimed medical bills.
rules.quote: Attach copies of all bills, receipts, and insurance benefits statements received that apply to this request.
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.note: Receipts or estimates for other expenses such as transportation, clothing, security, and child care.

rules.summary: Attach receipts or estimates for non-medical expenses claimed in Section IX.
rules.quote:
SECTION IX. Other Expenses or Losses as a result of the Crime
Attach receipts or estimates.
rules.pinpoint: Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17), Section IX (Other Expenses or Losses)
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.note: Self-employed applicants claiming lost wages include their most recent federal income tax return.

rules.summary: A self-employed victim claiming lost wages includes a copy of the most recent federal income tax return.
rules.quote:
Self-employed individuals need to include
a copy of most recent Federal Income Tax Return.
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.note: Physician's disability statement when more than 40 hours of lost work are claimed.

rules.summary: A physician's disability statement is required when more than 40 hours of lost work are requested.
rules.quote: A physician’s disability statement is required if over 40 hours are requested.
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.note: Letter explaining a late police report (more than 5 days) or a decision not to cooperate.

rules.summary: If the crime was not reported within 5 days or the victim did not cooperate, include a letter explaining why.
rules.quote:
If the crime was not reported within 5 days of the
date that it occurred or if the victim did not cooperate, please submit a letter explaining the reason for the delay in
reporting or decision not to cooperate.
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.note: Letter explaining the delay when filing more than 12 months after the crime.

rules.summary: If filing more than 12 months after the crime, include a letter stating the reason for the delay.
rules.quote:
If you are filing past 12 months, please
submit a letter stating the reason for the delay.
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.note: Signed and dated Declaration and Authorization (page 10).

rules.summary: Include the signed and dated Declaration and Authorization on page 10 of the application.
rules.quote: Signed and dated Declaration and Authorization, page 10.
rules.pinpoint: Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17), page 9, Completed applications include
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.note: Signed, dated, and witnessed Authorization for the Use or Disclosure of Protected Health Information (pages 11 to 12).

rules.summary: Include the health information release on pages 11 to 12, signed, dated, and with a witness signature.
rules.quote:
Signed, dated and witness signature on the Authorization for the Use or Disclosure of Protected Health Information,
page 11-12.
rules.pinpoint: Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17), page 9, Completed applications include
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.note: W-9; required only if the final award is over $5,000, but the program recommends filling it out when applying.

rules.summary: A W-9 must be filled out if the final award totals over $5,000, so the program suggests including it with the application.
rules.quote:
The W-9 is not required but must be filled out if the final award totals over $5,000; therefore, it is best practice to fill out the
W-9 when applying to avoid any unnecessary delays in receiving the final award.
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Primary Application Instructions

params.note: Guardianship papers if a legal guardian files for the victim.

rules.summary: A legal guardian filing for the victim attaches the guardianship documentation.
rules.quote: If you have been appointed legal guardian of the victim, please attach documentation.
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.note: Copy of the death certificate when the victim died as a result of the crime.

rules.summary: If the victim died as a result of the crime, attach a copy of the death certificate.
rules.quote: Attach a copy of Certificate of Death.
rules.pinpoint: Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17), Section X (Death as a result of the Crime)
rules.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

params.enroll: A person eligible to vote under 12-4-1 may apply to the secretary of state to be listed in the master registration file with a secured active designation.

rules.summary: South Dakota's only address confidentiality program is voter-only: a person with an active protection order or living in a victims' services shelter can ask the Secretary of State to keep their voter record out of public inspection. It does not give a substitute mailing address.
rules.quote: A voter record with a secured active designation shall be excluded from public inspection or copying, except if requested by a law enforcement agency, if directed by a court order, or if a secured active designation has been cancelled at the request of the secured active designee.
rules.pinpoint: SDCL 12-4-9.2, as quoted on the Secretary of State Secure Active Designation page
rules.source_title: SD Secretary of State, Address Confidentiality - Secure Active Designation (quotes SDCL 12-4-9.2)

rules.summary: Records and reports the department or commission obtains stay confidential if another law or rule already makes them confidential. The statute does not make the whole claim file confidential.
rules.quote: Any record or report obtained by the department or commission, the confidentiality of which is protected by any law or administrative rule, shall remain confidential.
rules.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rules.summary: A victim of a covered sexually-oriented crime gets the forensic medical exam free. No bill may be sent to the victim and the facility may not hold the victim responsible for payment. The statute does not say whether the victim's insurance may be billed.
rules.quote: shall be entitled to forensic medical examinations without charge to the victim. No bill for the examination shall be submitted to the victim, nor shall the medical facility hold the victim responsible for payment.
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: A provider paid by the fund for a forensic exam may not bill the victim for any additional cost of the exam.
rules.quote: No provider receiving compensation pursuant to this section shall bill the victim for any additional cost related to the forensic medical examination.
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

params.payer: Tennessee Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund (claim filed by the health care provider)

rules.summary: Forensic exam claims are paid from the state Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund.
rules.quote: All claims for forensic medical examinations are eligible for payment from the criminal injuries compensation fund, created under § 40-24-107.
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: A victim does not have to report to police or cooperate with prosecution for the forensic exam to be paid.
rules.quote: the victims shall not be required to report the incident to law enforcement officers or to cooperate in the prosecution of the crime in order to be eligible for payment of forensic medical examinations
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

params.payer: Tennessee Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund pays the health care provider directly; the payment is full compensation to the provider

rules.summary: The fund pays the provider up to $1,000 for a forensic exam, and that payment counts as full payment, so the provider cannot bill the victim for the rest.
rules.quote: The amount of compensation that may be awarded under this section shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000), and shall constitute full compensation to the health care provider that provided the service.
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

params.condition: for a crime on or after July 1, 2025

rules.summary: For crimes on or after July 1, 2025, the Treasury lists an overall maximum of $34,100 for all expenses on claims from the crime. The cap depends on the crime date.
rules.quote: For crimes occurring on or after July 1, 2025: $34,100
rules.pinpoint: Treasury Maximum Expense Amounts (June 2025); set under T.C.A. 29-13-106(h)
rules.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund Maximum Expense Amounts (June 2025)

params.item: pain and suffering
params.scope: for victims of rape, human trafficking, or another sexual crime

rules.summary: Pain and suffering is not paid for most crimes, but it can be paid to victims of rape, human trafficking, and crimes involving sexual deviancy.
rules.quote: Compensation must not be awarded for any personal injury or loss alleged to have been incurred as a result of pain and suffering, except for victims of the crime of rape, victims of a human trafficking offense, and victims of a crime involving sexual deviancy
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: A pain and suffering award for a victim of a sexually-oriented crime may not exceed $3,000.
rules.quote: Any award based on the pain and suffering experienced by a claimant victimized by a sexually-oriented crime is to be made in an amount deemed necessary and appropriate, not to exceed three thousand dollars ($3,000)
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

params.applies_to: family members and others listed in 29-13-105(a)(3), (a)(6), (a)(7), not the victim

rules.summary: Counseling for certain family members (for example a sibling or non-offending parent of a child victim of a sexually-oriented crime) is capped at $3,500. This sub-cap is for those family members, not for the victim.
rules.quote: Any award made for mental health counseling or treatment pursuant to § 29-13-105(a)(3), (a)(6) or (a)(7) shall be made in an amount deemed necessary and appropriate, not to exceed three thousand five hundred dollars ($3,500)
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "family members and others listed in 29-13-105(a)(3), (a)(6), (a)(7), not the victim"

params.applies_to: sibling or non-offending custodial parent of a victim under 18

rules.summary: When a sexually-oriented crime is committed against someone under 18, the victim's sibling or non-offending custodial parent can be paid for counseling made necessary by the crime.
rules.quote: In the case of a sexually-oriented crime committed against a victim who is under eighteen (18) years of age, where the compensation is for unreimbursed or unreimbursable mental health counseling or treatment made necessary by the sexually-oriented crime, any sibling or non-offending custodial parent of the victim, or both
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-105 (persons eligible), 2025 via Justia
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "sibling or non-offending custodial parent of a victim under 18"

params.scope: counseling you need because of the injury

rules.summary: The program says it may consider paying for counseling the victim needs because of the injury. The most it can pay is the overall limit.
rules.quote: Any counseling services must be necessary due to the injury and may be considered for the victim up to the maximum award.
rules.pinpoint: Program page, Eligible (Covered) Expenses Explained: Medical Bills/Mental Health Counseling
rules.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation program page (eligibility, Apply for Compensation, FAQ)

rules.summary: Expenses actually and reasonably incurred because of the injury, including medical and hospital services, are covered.
rules.quote: Expenses actually and reasonably incurred as a result of the personal injury or death of the victim, including, but not limited to, actual expenditures of moneys for or indebtedness resulting from medical services, hospital services, funeral and burial expenses
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: Lost wages caused by the crime are paid on the workers' compensation temporary total disability schedule, but at 85 percent of the claimant's average weekly wage.
rules.quote: Any award made for lost wages proximately caused by a violent crime is to be based upon those schedules of compensation for temporary total disability allowable by the workers' compensation statutes, found in § 50-6-207, in effect at the time of the commission of the crime giving rise to such claim; provided, however, that the sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) rate prescribed in the workers' compensation statutes shall not be used in determining the amount of any award hereunder. Instead, such rate shall be eighty-five percent (85%) of the claimant's average weekly wage.
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

params.scope: moving costs, if the assault happened at your home, for up to 2 moves

rules.summary: If you move because of an assault at your home, reasonable moving costs, storage fees, and fees to move your utilities are covered. This is for no more than 2 moves.
rules.quote: The victim's reasonable moving expenses, storage fees and fees for transfer of utility service if the move is a direct result of an assault committed upon such victim at the victim's residence, provided that the victim shall not receive compensation for more than two (2) moves resulting from the assault
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.scope: cleaning the scene, if it was your home or a relative's home

rules.summary: Reasonable costs to clean the scene of a sexual assault are covered when the scene was the home of the victim or a relative.
rules.quote: Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred for cleaning supplies, equipment rental and labor needed to clean the scene of a homicide, sexual assault or aggravated assault, if the scene was the residence of the victim or a relative of the victim
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $3,000.
rules.quote: Any award made for expenses under § 29-13-106(a)(4) shall not exceed three thousand dollars ($3,000)
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

params.item: travel to and from the trial and later appellate or post-conviction proceedings

rules.summary: Travel to and from the offender's trial and later appeals is paid up to a cumulative $1,250 for each claimant.
rules.quote: Any award made under the preceding sentence to a claimant shall not exceed a cumulative total of one thousand two hundred fifty dollars ($1,250) for all such travel.
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.item: travel to doctor appointments

rules.summary: The Treasury lists travel to doctor appointments as not covered.
rules.quote: Travel to Doctor Appointments
rules.pinpoint: Treasury CIC resource guide, Eligible versus Ineligible
rules.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation resource guide (brochure)

rules.summary: Funeral and burial expenses are capped at $6,000.
rules.quote: Any award made for funeral and burial expenses shall not exceed six thousand dollars ($6,000)
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

params.item: damage to real or personal property (lost, stolen or damaged items such as a phone), other than the eyeglasses, hearing aids and scene-processing damage covered by subdivision (a)(8)

rules.summary: Damage to real or personal property is not paid. The narrow exception covers eyeglasses and hearing aids damaged in the crime and property damaged while police processed a sexual assault scene at the victim's or a relative's home. A phone taken or broken in the assault is not covered.
rules.quote: In no case will any compensation be awarded for any damage to real or personal property, except as provided in subdivision (a)(8).
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.item: eyeglasses and hearing aids; property damaged in processing a sexual assault scene at the residence
params.scope: cleaning, fixing, or replacing the victim's eyeglasses and hearing aids damaged by the crime or the crime scene work

rules.summary: Reasonable costs to clean, fix, or replace the victim's eyeglasses and hearing aids are covered when the crime or the crime scene work damaged them.
rules.quote: Reasonable costs of cleaning, repairing or replacing eyeglasses and hearing aids owned by the victim that were damaged or destroyed by the crime or the processing of the crime scene
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.scope: repairing or replacing things damaged when police processed the scene at your home or a relative's home

rules.summary: The program covers reasonable costs to repair or replace property of the victim or a relative that was damaged when police processed the scene. This is for a sexual assault, homicide, or aggravated assault at the home of the victim or of the relative who owned the property.
rules.quote: the reasonable costs of repairing or replacing personal property owned by the victim or a relative of the victim as defined in § 29-13-102 that was damaged or destroyed in processing the scene of a homicide, sexual assault or aggravated assault if the scene was the residence of the victim or the relative of the victim who owned the property.
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.item: deposits, rent and utility bills

rules.summary: The Treasury lists deposits, rent, and utility bills as not covered.
rules.quote: Deposits, Rent and Utility Bills
rules.pinpoint: Treasury CIC resource guide, Eligible versus Ineligible
rules.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation resource guide (brochure)

params.item: costs from identity theft or fraud

rules.summary: The Treasury lists costs from identity theft or fraud as not covered.
rules.quote: Cost from Identity Theft or Fraud
rules.pinpoint: Treasury CIC resource guide, Eligible versus Ineligible
rules.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation resource guide (brochure)

params.extension: or later if the program extends it for good cause

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 2 years after the crime. For listed sexual offenses against a minor, it can also be filed within 2 years after a resulting injury is diagnosed, and good cause can extend the time.
rules.quote: A claim for compensation must be filed not later than two (2) years after the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based, two (2) years after the death of the victim, or two (2) years after any mental or physical manifestation or injury is diagnosed as a result of an act committed against a minor that would constitute a criminal offense under §§ 39-13-502 – 39-13-505, § 39-13-522, § 39-15-302, § 39-17-902, or §§ 39-17-1003 – 39-17-1005, or an attempt, conspiracy, or solicitation to commit such offenses; provided, that upon good cause shown, the time period for filing such claim may be extended either before or after the expiration of the filing period.
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: Some sex crimes against a minor allow more time. A claim can also be filed within 2 years after a mental or physical injury from the crime is diagnosed.
rules.quote: two (2) years after any mental or physical manifestation or injury is diagnosed as a result of an act committed against a minor that would constitute a criminal offense under §§ 39-13-502 – 39-13-505, § 39-13-522, § 39-15-302, § 39-17-902, or §§ 39-17-1003 – 39-17-1005, or an attempt, conspiracy, or solicitation to commit such offenses
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

params.exception: or later if there is good cause, which can include sexual assault

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to the proper authorities within 15 days, but a late report can be excused for good cause, and being a victim of sexual assault is a listed reason for good cause.
rules.quote: A claim cannot be filed until the crime upon which the claim is based has been reported by the victim, or a member of the victim's family, to the proper authorities within fifteen (15) days after the occurrence of such crime unless, for good cause shown, it is found that the delay was justified. Good cause for the failure of a victim or a member of the victim's family to report a crime may be found if the victim is: (1) Physically unable; (2) A victim of sexual assault;
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: Proof that the crime happened can come from documents other than a police report, such as medical records from a health care provider or a restraining order issued by a court. This is proof of the offense only; it does not replace the timely report to law enforcement that a compensation claim still needs.
rules.quote: (vii) Medical records from a healthcare provider, as those terms are defined in § 9-8-408; (viii) A written communication from a prosecuting attorney or investigating law enforcement officer who has personal involvement in the prosecution or investigation of any criminal case relative to the claim filed; (ix) A report from child protective services or another government agency; (x) A restraining order issued by a court;
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-103 (burden of proof; documentation; proof of offense), 2025 via Justia

params.waived_for: interest of justice; not applied to trial travel

rules.summary: To qualify, the claimant needs at least $100 in out-of-pocket loss or at least 2 continuous weeks of lost earnings or support, unless the limit would not serve the interest of justice.
rules.quote: no award shall be made unless the claimant has incurred a minimum out of pocket loss of one hundred dollars ($100) or has lost at least two (2) continuous weeks earnings or support, unless it is determined that the interest of justice would not be served by such a limitation
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by money received or legally owed from the offender or any other public or private source, such as insurance.
rules.quote: Any award shall be reduced by the amounts of payment already received or any amounts which claimant is legally entitled to receive as a result of the injury: (A) From or on behalf of the offender; (B) From any other public or private source;
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: In deciding whether to award, or how much, the program may consider the victim's behavior that directly or indirectly contributed to the injury.
rules.quote: In determining whether to make an award under this section, or the amount of the award, any circumstances reasonably relevant to the criminal act may be considered, including the behavior of the victim which directly or indirectly contributed to the victim's injury or death
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-109 (claims requirements; awards; victim conduct; cooperation), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $500.
rules.quote: The amount of such emergency award shall not exceed five hundred dollars ($500).
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-114 (emergency award), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: Compensation covers personal injury from an act in Tennessee that would be a crime under state or federal law, which includes sexual assault.

rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-104 (offenses to which compensation applies), 2025 via Justia

params.rule: Crimes committed in Tennessee are covered. A Tennessee resident hurt by a crime in another state may claim only if that state does not honor the claim.

rules.summary: Covers crimes in Tennessee. A Tennessee resident victimized in another state can claim here only if that state's program does not honor the claim.
rules.quote: Any of the foregoing acts committed or taken in another state if the victim was a resident of this state at the time the crime or act occurred and the claimant's request for compensation from the state in which the crime or act occurred is not honored.
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-104 (offenses to which compensation applies), 2025 via Justia

rules.summary: The division must make every effort to approve or deny a claim within 90 days of receiving it.
rules.quote: the division shall investigate every claim for compensation and shall make every effort to honor or deny each claim within ninety (90) days of receipt of the claim
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

params.program_name: Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program
params.enroll: an adult person, or a parent or fiduciary acting on behalf of a minor or person with a disability, may apply to the secretary of state with the assistance of an application assistant to have an address designated by the secretary of state serve as the person's substitute address, or the substitute address of the minor or person with a disability on whose behalf the application is filed, where the applicant, or the individual on whose behalf the application is filed, resides at an address not previously identified in any public record as the person's address, or has relocated to a new residence within the preceding thirty (30) calendar days or presently intends to relocate to a new residence within ninety (90) calendar days from the date of the application. The application shall be made on a form prescribed by the secretary of state and filed in the office of the secretary of state in the manner prescribed by the secretary of state.

rules.summary: Safe at Home is a free program run by the Tennessee Secretary of State. It is open to survivors of rape, sexual battery, or another sex crime, and of domestic abuse, stalking, or human trafficking, who meet its eligibility and application rules. Once approved, you get a substitute address to use as your official mailing address for state and local government.
rules.quote: The Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program is a statewide address confidentiality program administered by the Office of the Tennessee Secretary of State. It is open to all victims of domestic abuse, stalking, human trafficking, rape, sexual battery, or any other sexual offense who satisfy eligibility and application requirements at no cost. Once a participant has been approved, they are provided with a 'substitute' address that can be used by them and their children as their official mailing address for all state and local government purposes
rules.pinpoint: Secretary of State, Safe at Home FAQ 'What is the Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program?'; statute T.C.A. 40-38-601 to 40-38-604 (enroll text from 40-38-604(a))
rules.source_title: Tennessee Secretary of State, Safe at Home FAQ: What is the Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program?

rules.summary: For victims who apply for compensation, Tennessee law makes the home address, home and personal cell phone numbers, Social Security number, and the crime the victim is being compensated for confidential and closed to public inspection. The statute does not list the victim's name or the rest of the claim file.
rules.quote: The following information regarding victims who apply for compensation under the Criminal Injuries Compensation Act, compiled in title 29, chapter 13, shall be treated as confidential and shall not be open for inspection by members of the public: (1) Residential information, including the street address, city, state and zip code; (2) Home telephone and personal cell phone numbers; (3) Social security number; and (4) The criminal offense from which the victim is receiving compensation.
rules.source_title: T.C.A. 10-7-504 (confidential records; (k) Criminal Injuries Compensation Act applicants), 2025 via Justia

params.scope: the forensic part of an exam or the evidence kit

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor cannot be made to pay for the forensic part of the exam or the evidence kit. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed for it.
rules.quote: A victim of a sexual assault may not be required to pay for: (1) the forensic portion of the forensic medical examination; or (2) the evidence collection kit.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56A (Subchapter G, forensic medical examination)

params.payer: Texas Office of the Attorney General, reimbursing the health care provider or sexual assault examiner on application

rules.summary: The Attorney General reimburses the provider or examiner for the forensic portion of the exam, the evidence kit, and medical care given during the exam.
rules.quote: a health care provider that provides a forensic medical examination to a sexual assault survivor in accordance with this subchapter, or the sexual assault examiner or sexual assault nurse examiner who conducts that examination in accordance with this subchapter, as applicable, is entitled to be reimbursed in an amount set by attorney general rule for: (1) the reasonable costs of the forensic portion of that examination; (2) the evidence collection kit;
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56A (Subchapter G, forensic medical examination)

rules.summary: Emergency Medical Care (EMC): the Attorney General pays for medical care given during a sexual assault forensic exam, at medical fee guideline rates, up to $25,000. The program's medical care page treats this as separate from the general award cap.
rules.quote: The attorney general shall make a payment under Subsection (a) in accordance with the medical fee guidelines prescribed by Subtitle A, Title 5, Labor Code. A payment made under Subsection (a) may not exceed $25,000.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56A (Subchapter G, forensic medical examination)

params.scope: the forensic part of an exam or the evidence kit

rules.summary: The program's emergency medical care page says victims cannot be billed for the forensic costs of a sexual assault exam.
rules.quote: Note: Victims cannot be billed for forensic costs of the exam.
rules.pinpoint: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation page
rules.source_title: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation (sexual assault exam)

params.exception: or more in some cases

rules.summary: Awards for one victim and everyone claiming because of that victim's injury may not exceed $50,000 in total.
rules.quote: Except as otherwise provided by this article, awards payable to a victim and any other claimant sustaining pecuniary loss because of injury or death of that victim may not exceed $50,000 in the aggregate.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: For crimes after September 1, 2014, counseling is limited to 60 sessions per victim or claimant; more may be approved in unusual circumstances.
rules.quote: for criminally injurious conduct after September 1, 2014, 60 sessions per victim or claimant.
rules.source_title: 1 Tex. Admin. Code 61.503 (Psychiatric Care or Counseling Expenses)

rules.summary: For crimes on or after July 15, 2016, lost earnings are paid up to $700 per week.
rules.quote: On or after July 15, 2016, the maximum amount of an award for loss of earnings is $700 per week.
rules.source_title: 1 Tex. Admin. Code 61.402 (Loss of Earnings)

params.scope: moving costs and rent, if the assault happened in your home

rules.summary: A victim of sexual assault who was assaulted at home can be paid relocation costs and housing rent.
rules.quote: A victim of stalking, family violence, or trafficking of persons, a victim of sexual assault who is assaulted in the victim's place of residence, or a child who is a victim of a murder attempt in the child's place of residence may receive compensation for the following expenses: (1) relocation expenses, including expenses for rental deposit, utility connections, expenses relating to moving belongings, motor vehicle mileage expenses, temporary or emergency lodging, and for an out-of-state move, expenses for transportation, lodging, and meals; and (2) housing rental expenses.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

params.scope: moving costs and rent, if a move is needed for your health or safety

rules.summary: Other victims can be paid moving costs and rent when a move is needed to protect their health or safety.
rules.quote: A victim other than a victim described by Subsection (c), a dependent of any victim, a family member of any victim if that family member has previously resided with the victim for a period of not less than two years, or a household member of any victim may receive compensation for the following expenses, if the expenses are necessary to protect the health or safety of the victim, dependent, or family or household member: (1) relocation expenses, including expenses for rental deposit, utility connections, expenses relating to moving belongings, motor vehicle mileage expenses, temporary or emergency lodging, and for an out-of-state move, expenses for transportation, lodging, and meals; and (2) housing rental expenses.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: Relocation and housing rental expenses together are capped at $5,000 per victim or claimant.
rules.quote: A victim or claimant may not receive more than $5,000 in the aggregate for relocation expenses and housing rental expenses under Subsection (c) or (c-1).
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

params.scope: emergency or temporary lodging for up to 14 days

rules.summary: Emergency or temporary lodging can be paid for up to 14 days, as part of help with moving.
rules.quote: Emergency or temporary lodging (up to 14 days)
rules.pinpoint: OAG Rent and Relocation Reimbursement page
rules.source_title: OAG Rent and Relocation Reimbursement

params.scope: trips over 20 miles one way to medical or mental health care, court, or a victim's funeral

rules.summary: Travel is reimbursed when the one-way trip to medical or mental health care, court, or a victim's funeral is over 20 miles.
rules.quote: Travel over 20 miles one way for medical or mental health care, court proceedings, or a victim's funeral
rules.source_title: OAG Travel Cost Reimbursement

rules.summary: If you were subpoenaed to appear in court, the program does not pay for those trips. Its page says to ask the prosecutor's office instead.
rules.quote: Note: Victims or claimants subpoenaed to appear in court cannot receive reimbursement through the CVC program for those appearances. If subpoenaed, please seek reimbursement from the prosecutor’s office.
rules.pinpoint: OAG Travel Cost Reimbursement page, Note
rules.source_title: OAG Travel Cost Reimbursement

rules.summary: Reasonable and necessary medical, hospital, nursing, and physical therapy costs from the injury are covered.
rules.quote: "Pecuniary loss" means the amount of the expense reasonably and necessarily incurred as a result of personal injury or death for: (A) medical, hospital, nursing, or psychiatric care or counseling, or physical therapy;
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: For care sought after August 31, 2025, Emergency Medical Care also pays for prescribed care tied to the assault in the 30 days after the exam.
rules.quote: For medical care sought after August 31, 2025, EMC also covers any prescribed continuing medical care that is related to the sexual assault and provided to the victim during the 30-day period following the exam.
rules.pinpoint: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation page
rules.source_title: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation (sexual assault exam)

rules.summary: Prescriptions and dental work for crime-related injuries are among the medical costs the program lists as covered.
rules.quote: Examples of expenses that can be covered include: Hospitalization Doctor's services Ambulance services Prescriptions Dental work
rules.source_title: OAG Medical Care Expenses

rules.summary: Psychiatric care and counseling are covered losses.
rules.quote: "Pecuniary loss" means the amount of the expense reasonably and necessarily incurred as a result of personal injury or death for: (A) medical, hospital, nursing, or psychiatric care or counseling, or physical therapy;
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: Lost past and future earnings are covered when caused by the injury, by getting care for it, or by taking part in the investigation or court process.
rules.quote: actual loss of past earnings and anticipated loss of future earnings and necessary travel expenses because of: (i) a disability resulting from the personal injury; (ii) the receipt of medically indicated services related to the disability; or (iii) participation in or attendance at investigative, prosecutorial, or judicial processes
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: For crimes on or after July 15, 2016, new child or dependent care costs are paid up to $300 per week for each child or dependent.
rules.quote: On or after July 15, 2016, $300 per week for each child or dependent.
rules.source_title: 1 Tex. Admin. Code 61.405 (Other Limits on Compensation)

rules.summary: For crimes on or after July 15, 2016, crime scene cleaning is capped at $2250 per victim.
rules.quote: for criminally injurious conduct that occurs on or after July 15, 2016, compensation may not exceed $2250 per victim.
rules.source_title: 1 Tex. Admin. Code 61.405 (Other Limits on Compensation)

params.scope: replacing clothing, bedding, or property taken as evidence or ruined by the investigation

rules.summary: Clothing, bedding, or other property of the victim that police took as evidence or that the investigation made unusable can be replaced.
rules.quote: reasonable replacement costs for clothing, bedding, or property of the victim seized as evidence or rendered unusable as a result of the criminal investigation;
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: For crimes on or after July 15, 2016, replacement of seized or unusable clothing, bedding, or property is capped at $1000 per victim.
rules.quote: Under Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 56.32(a)(9)(G), the OAG may pay for the reasonable replacement costs as follows: (1) for criminally injurious conduct that occurs between September 1, 1995 and July 14, 2016, compensation may not exceed $750; and (2) for criminally injurious conduct that occurs on or after July 15, 2016, compensation may not exceed $1000 per victim.
rules.source_title: 1 Tex. Admin. Code 61.405 (Other Limits on Compensation)

params.item: property theft, damage, or loss

rules.summary: The program does not pay for property theft, damage, or loss. Replacing clothing, bedding, or property seized as evidence or made unusable by the investigation is a separate covered cost.
rules.quote: The CVC Program cannot make payments for the following: Property theft, damage, or loss Identity theft costs Pain, suffering, or emotional distress Any cost not a direct result of the crime
rules.pinpoint: OAG CVC Covered Costs page, Costs Not Covered
rules.source_title: OAG CVC Covered Costs

params.item: pain, suffering, or emotional distress

rules.summary: Pain, suffering, or emotional distress damages are not paid.
rules.quote: The CVC Program cannot make payments for the following: Property theft, damage, or loss Identity theft costs Pain, suffering, or emotional distress Any cost not a direct result of the crime
rules.pinpoint: OAG CVC Covered Costs page, Costs Not Covered
rules.source_title: OAG CVC Covered Costs

params.item: missed counseling appointments and pre-existing psychological conditions

rules.summary: Missed counseling appointments and pre-existing psychological conditions are not paid.
rules.quote: The CVC Program will not pay for: Pre-existing psychological conditions Missed appointments Therapist court appearances for testimony
rules.pinpoint: OAG Mental Health Care Expenses page
rules.source_title: OAG Mental Health Care Expenses

params.extension: or later if you show good cause for the delay

rules.summary: Apply within 3 years of the crime; the program can accept a late application for good cause.
rules.quote: You're applying within 3 years of the crime (unless good cause can be shown for the delay).
rules.source_title: OAG CVC Eligibility

rules.summary: If the victim is a child, the time to apply counts from the day the victim or claimant learns of the crime. It ends on the third anniversary of that day, and no later than the child's 21st birthday.
rules.quote: If the victim is a child, the application must be filed not later than the third anniversary of the date the claimant or victim is made aware of the offense, but not after the child attains 21 years of age.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: If medical records show the crime left you unable to apply, that time does not count toward the deadline.
rules.quote: If a claimant or victim presents medically documented evidence of a physical or mental incapacity that was incurred by the claimant or victim as a result of the criminally injurious conduct and that reasonably prevented the claimant or victim from filing the application within the limitations period under Subsection (a), the period of the incapacity is not included.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: You may not apply unless the crime was reported to police or another public safety agency in a reasonable time. The report cannot be so late that it gets in the way of the investigation and prosecution.
rules.quote: a claimant or victim may not file an application unless the victim reports the criminally injurious conduct to the appropriate state or local public safety or law enforcement agency within a reasonable period, but not so late as to interfere with or hamper the investigation and prosecution of the offense after the criminally injurious conduct is committed.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

params.exception: unless the victim is a child

rules.summary: The attorney general may give more time to report in extraordinary circumstances. The report rule does not apply if the victim is a child.
rules.quote: The attorney general may extend the time for reporting the criminally injurious conduct if the attorney general determines that the extension is justified by extraordinary circumstances. (c) Subsection (a) does not apply if the victim is a child.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

params.scope: Emergency Medical Care only (medical care at a sexual assault exam), not the full compensation claim

rules.summary: For Emergency Medical Care compensation (medical care given during a sexual assault exam), no police report is needed. This exception does not cover the full compensation claim.
rules.quote: Special rules apply for sexual assault Emergency Medical Care (EMC): reporting to law enforcement is not required.
rules.pinpoint: OAG CVC Eligibility page, Basic requirements
rules.source_title: OAG CVC Eligibility

rules.summary: The program pays only for losses not covered by a collateral source such as insurance, Medicaid, or restitution.
rules.quote: a claimant or victim suffered personal injury or death that resulted in a pecuniary loss for which the claimant or victim is not compensated from a collateral source.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: An award can be denied or reduced if the victim's behavior shares responsibility for the crime, or if the victim did not substantially cooperate with law enforcement.
rules.quote: the attorney general may deny or reduce an award otherwise payable: (1) if the claimant or victim has not substantially cooperated with an appropriate law enforcement agency; (2) if, as a result of the claimant's or victim's behavior, the claimant or victim bears a share of the responsibility for the act or omission giving rise to the claim;
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: Getting a forensic medical exam is enough to show a sexual assault victim cooperated with the investigation.
rules.quote: a victim receiving a forensic medical examination constitutes sufficient evidence that a victim has substantially cooperated with an investigation of a sexual assault or other sex offense.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: An emergency award for urgent costs is possible when a final award is likely and the victim faces undue hardship; it may not exceed $1,500.
rules.quote: An emergency award may not exceed $1,500.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: Sexual assault is one of the violent crimes the program covers.
rules.quote: We can help victims of violent crimes or attempted crimes including: Arson (when present in the building) Assault Burglary (when present in the building) Child abuse Criminally negligent homicide DWI crashes Elder abuse Family violence Harassment Hit and run Homicide Human trafficking Kidnapping Manslaughter Robbery Sexual assault
rules.pinpoint: OAG CVC Eligibility page, Covered crimes
rules.source_title: OAG CVC Eligibility

params.rule: Crime occurred in Texas and the victim is a resident of Texas or another US state; Texas residents injured in a state or country without a VOCA-qualifying program are also covered (art. 56B.003(14)(B)).

rules.summary: Covers people injured by a crime in Texas who live in Texas or another US state; Texas residents hurt in a state or country without a qualifying compensation program can also apply.
rules.quote: suffers personal injury or death as a result of criminally injurious conduct or as a result of actions taken by the individual as an intervenor, if the conduct or actions occurred in this state; and (ii) is a resident of this state or another state of the United States;
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)
