params.agency: Office of the Attorney General of Texas
params.enroll: Connect with an advocate (recommended), who helps gather documents and submits the application. On your own, download the application and, with ONE of a protection order, temporary restraining order or injunction, or documentation of the crime, upload it through the Submit Documents Online form link or mail it to Texas Address Confidentiality Program, P.O. Box 12199, Austin, Texas 78711-2199. Questions: (888) 832-2322.

rules.summary: The Attorney General runs an address confidentiality program for survivors of sexual assault and other listed crimes. It gives each participant a substitute P.O. box address to use instead of their real home, work, or school address, and forwards their mail.
rules.quote: (a)  The attorney general shall establish an address confidentiality program, as provided by this subchapter, to assist a victim of family violence, sexual assault or abuse, stalking, child abduction, or trafficking of persons in maintaining a confidential address. (b)  The attorney general shall: (1)  designate a substitute post office box address that a participant may use in place of the participant's true residential, business, or school address;
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 58 (Confidentiality of Identifying Information; Address Confidentiality Program, Subch. B)

rules.summary: Texas law keeps your compensation application and the Attorney General's records on it private, with some exceptions. Once compensation is awarded, the name of the victim or claimant and the amount are public under Gov. Code 552.132(c). A court order, your consent, or a subpoena in a criminal case can also open some records.
rules.quote: An application for compensation under this chapter and any information, document, summary, or other record provided to or received, maintained, or created by the attorney general under this chapter, including a report released to the attorney general under Article 56B.054 (f), is: (1)  except as provided by Section 552.132 (c), Government Code, not subject to disclosure under Chapter 552 of that code; and (2)  except as provided by Subsection (c), not subject to disclosure, discovery, subpoena, or other means of legal compulsion for release.
rules.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rules.summary: A survivor may not be charged for a medical forensic sexual assault exam, and does not have to take part in the criminal justice system or cooperate with police or prosecutors to get one.
rules.quote: A victim may not be: (a) charged for a medical forensic sexual assault examination; or (b) required to participate in the criminal justice system or cooperate with law enforcement or prosecuting attorneys as a condition of being provided a medical forensic sexual assault examination.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: An exam provider that accepts payment from the Utah Office for Victims of Crime must take it as payment in full and may not try to collect more from the patient.
rules.quote: A sexual assault exam service provider who accepts payment from UOVC agrees to accept that payment as payment in full on behalf of the patient and may not attempt to collect additional payment from the patient.
rules.pinpoint: UOVC Sexual Assault Services Providers billing page, Payment in Full Requirement
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Sexual Assault Services Providers billing page

params.payer: Utah Office for Victims of Crime

rules.summary: The Utah Office for Victims of Crime may pay the examiner up to $1,250 for a complete medical forensic sexual assault exam with photo documentation; this limit covers the examiner's fee only, and the exam room, lab tests, and medications are paid separately.
rules.quote: The office may pay a medical service provider who performs a medical forensic sexual assault examination: (a) up to $1,250 for a complete medical forensic sexual assault examination with photo documentation
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: The office may pay the full cost of medications the exam provider gives the survivor during the exam, such as emergency contraception and medication to treat or prevent sexually transmitted infections.
rules.quote: the full cost of any medications the medical service provider gives directly to a victim during a medical forensic sexual assault examination such as: (i) the morning after pill or high dose oral contraceptives for the prevention of pregnancy; and (ii) medication for the treatment and prevention of sexually transmitted diseases.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: Sexual assault service providers must bill all available insurance or other payment sources before submitting claims to the Utah Office for Victims of Crime.
rules.quote: Providers must bill all available insurance or other payment sources before submitting claims to UOVC.
rules.pinpoint: UOVC Sexual Assault Services Providers billing page, Reminder
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Sexual Assault Services Providers billing page

params.payer: Utah Office for Victims of Crime (exam facility fees)

rules.summary: The office may also pay the facility where the exam is done 50% of the exam room fee, up to $350, plus the PEHP rate or 50% of the fee for the history and physical, specimen collection, STD and pregnancy testing, and STD treatment.
rules.quote: 50% of the fee for the use of an examination room to perform a medical forensic sexual assault examination up to a maximum payment of $350
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

params.payer: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, if the exam provider reports the exam to law enforcement

rules.summary: For the office to pay for the exam, the provider who did it must report the exam to law enforcement, and may collect evidence only with the permission of the victim or the victim's legal guardian.
rules.quote: To be eligible for reimbursement of a medical forensic sexual assault examination, the medical service provider who performed the sexual assault forensic examination shall: (a) report the medical forensic sexual assault examination to law enforcement; and (b) only collect evidence with the permission of the victim or the legal guardian of the victim.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

params.item: over-the-counter at-home sexual assault evidence kits and testing of them

rules.summary: The office does not reimburse any cost of an over-the-counter at-home sexual assault evidence kit, including the kit and any testing of it.
rules.quote: The office may not provide any reimbursement for any costs associated with an over-the-counter sexual assault evidence kit that is available to the public for at home collection of evidence, including the cost of the kit and the cost of any testing performed on the kit.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

params.exception: or more in some cases

rules.summary: A compensation award may not exceed $25,000, including any award for a secondary victim, except for medical expenses from serious or substantial bodily injury.
rules.quote: Except as provided in Subsection (4)(b), a compensation award may not exceed $25,000 including any compensation award for a secondary victim.
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: An award for medical expenses from serious bodily injury or substantial bodily injury may not exceed $50,000.
rules.quote: A compensation award for medical expenses resulting from serious bodily injury or substantial bodily injury may not exceed $50,000.
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: A primary victim can get up to 25 outpatient mental health counseling sessions, individual or group. The reparations officer can approve more if the counselor sends enough documentation to justify them and extenuating circumstances call for them.
rules.quote: a primary victim of a crime is eligible for a total of 25 outpatient mental health counseling sessions, including either individual or group counseling session;
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: Lost earnings can be reimbursed for up to 12 weeks of work loss, not exceeding the weekly workers' compensation maximum in effect at the time.
rules.quote: The office may reimburse victims for a loss of earnings for up to a maximum of 12 weeks work loss, at an amount not to exceed the maximum allowed per week by Worker's Compensation guidelines in effect at the time of work loss.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: The office may pay up to $2,000 for reasonable and necessary costs to secure a safe living situation after the crime, such as moving or keeping up rent.
rules.quote: the office may pay up to $2,000 for any reasonable and necessary cost for a victim to secure a safe living situation after a crime has occurred.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: The office may pay up to $1,000 for reasonable and necessary travel to court, meetings with police or prosecutors, and medical, mental health, or other crime-related appointments.
rules.quote: the office may pay up to $1,000 for the reasonable and necessary costs for a victim to travel to and from:
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: Up to $1,500 may be allowed for other essential personal property such as burglar alarms, door locks, crime scene cleanup, and repair of walls and broken windows.
rules.quote: The reparations officer may allow up to $1,500 for other essential personal property such as burglar alarms, door locks, crime scene cleanup, repair of walls and broken windows.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: Up to $5,000 may be allowed for medically necessary items such as eyeglasses, hearing aids, and wheelchairs.
rules.quote: The reparations officer may allow up to $5,000 for medically necessary items such as eyeglasses, hearing aids, and wheelchairs.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: The office may pay up to $14,000 for reasonable and necessary funeral and burial expenses of a victim.
rules.quote: up to $14,000 for any reasonable and necessary expense related to the funeral and burial of a victim;
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: Inpatient and outpatient medical treatment and physical therapy are allowable expenses, subject to the office's rules.
rules.quote: inpatient and outpatient medical treatment and physical therapy, subject to rules made by the office
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: When there is no other payment source, the office may pay medical services at the PEHP fee schedule rate, or 50% of billed charges if PEHP has no fee schedule for that service.
rules.quote: if the victim does not have any collateral source to pay for medical services the office may pay: (1) the rate established by the PEHP fee schedule for medical services; or (2) 50% of the billed charges for medical services if PEHP does not have a fee schedule established for a medical service.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: Medical services under the rule include dental services.
rules.quote: medical services include dental services
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: Mental health counseling can be covered, but a compensation specialist must approve a mental health treatment plan for it before any payment is made.
rules.quote: mental health counseling that: (A) is set forth in a mental health treatment plan that is approved before any payment is made by a compensation specialist
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: Lost past and future earnings from death or disability caused by the injury are covered at up to 66-2/3% of gross weekly wages or the state workers' compensation maximum.
rules.quote: actual loss of past earnings and anticipated loss of future earnings because of a death or disability resulting from the personal injury at a rate not to exceed 66-2/3% of the individual's weekly gross salary or wages or the maximum amount allowed under the state workers' compensation statute;
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

params.scope: child care so you or your spouse can keep working

rules.summary: Care of minor children so the victim or the victim's spouse (not both) can keep working is covered, at a weekly per-child rate set by rule.
rules.quote: care of minor children enabling a victim or spouse of a victim, but not both, to continue gainful employment at a rate per child per week as determined under rules established by the office
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

params.scope: personal property needed for your health or safety

rules.summary: Personal property necessary and essential to the victim's health or safety is covered, as defined by the office's rules.
rules.quote: personal property necessary and essential to the health or safety of the victim as defined by rules made by the office
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: A survivor who becomes pregnant from the sexual assault can be covered for related health care during the pregnancy, and for the survivor and the child for one year after the child is born.
rules.quote: for a victim of sexual assault who becomes pregnant from the sexual assault, health care: (A) for the victim during the duration of the victim's pregnancy if the health care is related to or resulting from the sexual assault or the pregnancy; and (B) for the victim and the victim's child for one year after the day on which the victim's child is born.
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: Prescription or over-the-counter medications used with medical treatment are considered while the victim is being treated by the physician.
rules.quote: The office shall only consider reimbursement of prescription or over-the-counter medications used in conjunction with medical treatment while the victim is being treated by the physician.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: As part of an award, the office pays for an abortion that is permitted under Utah's abortion law (Title 76, Chapter 7, Part 3) when the award requirements are met.
rules.quote: As part of a reparations award, the office shall pay expenses for an abortion that is permitted pursuant to Title 76, Chapter 7, Part 3 if the requirements of Section 63M-7-511 have been met.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

params.item: pain, suffering, and other noneconomic harm

rules.summary: The program does not pay for harm that is not a money loss, such as pain and suffering.
rules.quote: "Economic loss" does not include noneconomic detriment.
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

params.item: interest, finance, or collection fees

rules.summary: The office does not pay interest, finance, or collection fees.
rules.quote: The office may not pay: (a) interest, finance, or collection fees
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

params.item: wilderness programs

rules.summary: The office does not pay for wilderness programs.
rules.quote: The office may not pay for wilderness programs.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: In general the crime must be reported to a law enforcement officer or another federal or state investigative agency; sexual assault survivors have an advocate questionnaire alternative.
rules.quote: the criminally injurious conduct is reported to a law enforcement officer, in the law enforcement officer's capacity as a law enforcement officer, or another federal or state investigative agency;
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor does not have to report to police or cooperate with police and prosecutors to be eligible if the survivor gets help from a victim advocate or advocacy services provider who completes the office's questionnaire about the assault.
rules.quote: a victim of sexual assault is not required to report the sexual assault to a law enforcement officer or another federal or state investigative agency or cooperate with the appropriate law enforcement agencies and prosecuting attorneys to be eligible for a compensation award under this section if: (i) the victim seeks assistance from an advocacy services provider, a criminal justice system victim advocate, or a nongovernment organization victim advocate; and (ii) the advocacy services provider, the criminal justice system victim advocate, or the nongovernment organization victim advocate completes a questionnaire, provided by the office, regarding the sexual assault.
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: The program says that in sexual assault cases a sexual assault victim service provider can complete a questionnaire in place of a police report.
rules.quote: In cases of sexual assault, a questionnaire can be completed by a sexual assault victim service provider in place of a police report.
rules.pinpoint: UOVC Apply for Compensation page, Eligibility
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Apply for Compensation (application process and eligibility)

rules.summary: If the victim has medical insurance or another collateral source, the office pays only the remaining portion the victim owes after every other source has paid.
rules.quote: If a victim has medical insurance or another collateral source to pay for services, the office may only pay up to the remaining portion of the bill that the victim is obligated to pay after each other collateral source has paid.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: A reparations officer may waive the insurance-first requirement if using the other source would likely compromise the victim's safety, quality or continuation of care, or access to services.
rules.quote: A reparations officer may waive the requirement in Subsection (5)(a) if: (i) it appears likely that compliance would compromise a victim's; (A) safety; (B) quality or continuation of care; or (C) access to services due to distance, lack or transportation or other relevant circumstances;
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: The office may reduce or deny an award if the loss could be recouped from other sources, including collateral sources, or if the claim is unreasonable because of the claimant's misconduct.
rules.quote: The office may reduce or deny a compensation award otherwise payable to a claimant if: (i) the economic loss upon which the claim is based has been or could be recouped from other persons, including collateral sources; (ii) the compensation specialist considers the compensation claim unreasonable because of the misconduct of the claimant;
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: In deciding misconduct, reparations officers may not consider any behavior committed, or perceived to have been committed, by the victim of any sex crime, or behavior under duress, threat, exploitation, or coercion.
rules.quote: When determining whether the victim engaged in misconduct, reparations officers shall not consider: (a) any behavior or action of any victim that is committed by the victim while under the duress or experience of threat, exploitation, coercion or any circumstance absent the victim's own willful desire to participate; or (b) any behavior or action committed or perceived to have been committed by the victim of any sex crime.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: If a claimant will suffer financial hardship without an emergency award and a final award appears likely, the office may pay an amount that is later deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: If a compensation specialist determines that a claimant will suffer financial hardship unless an emergency compensation award is made, and a final compensation award appears likely, the office may pay an amount to the claimant, to be deducted from the final compensation award
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: The office may make emergency awards of up to $1,000.
rules.quote: the office may make emergency reparations awards up to $1,000.
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rules.summary: A victim is someone who suffers bodily or psychological injury or death as a direct result of criminally injurious conduct.
rules.quote: "Victim" means an individual who suffers bodily or psychological injury or death as a direct result of: (i) criminally injurious conduct
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: The program lists sex crimes and child physical or sexual abuse among the crimes eligible for compensation.
rules.quote: Crimes that are eligible for compensation include: Aggravated Robbery Assault Domestic Violence Bigamy Child Physical or Sexual Abuse DUI with Injury or Death Elder Abuse Home Invasion Homicide Human Trafficking (Sex or Labor) Kidnapping and Unlawful Detention Protective Order Violations Sex Crimes Stalking
rules.pinpoint: UOVC Apply for Compensation page, Eligibility
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Apply for Compensation (application process and eligibility)

rules.summary: An award can be made whether or not anyone is arrested, prosecuted, or convicted.
rules.quote: A compensation award may be made to a victim regardless of whether any individual is arrested, prosecuted, or convicted of the criminally injurious conduct giving rise to a compensation claim.
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

params.rule: Crimes that occurred in Utah; Utah residents injured in a state, territory, or country with no crime victims' compensation program.

rules.summary: The crime must have occurred in Utah, or the victim must be a Utah resident hurt in a place that has no crime victims' compensation program.
rules.quote: the criminally injurious conduct occurred in Utah; or (ii) the victim is a Utah resident who suffers injury or death as a result of criminally injurious conduct inflicted in a state, territory, or country that does not provide a crime victims' compensation program;
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rules.summary: The application can be completed through UOVC's online portal (the page's Online Application link goes to newclaim.crimevictim.utah.gov).
rules.quote: The application can be completed either through the online portal or by filling out the PDF and submitting it via email, mail, or fax.
rules.pinpoint: Apply for Compensation, Victim Compensation Application Process
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Apply for Compensation (application process and eligibility)

rules.summary: The PDF application can be emailed to UOVC at crimevictims@utah.gov, the email printed at the top of the application.
rules.quote: Email: crimevictims@utah.gov
rules.source_title: Application for the Crime Victim Reparations Program (English)

params.target: 420 East South Temple, Suite 500, Salt Lake City, UT 84111

rules.summary: The PDF application can be mailed to UOVC at its current mailing address on East South Temple in Salt Lake City.
rules.quote: Mailing & Physical Address: 420 East South Temple, Suite 500, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Contact Us (mailing address, email, fax)

rules.summary: The PDF application can be faxed to UOVC.
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Contact Us (mailing address, email, fax)

params.note: You do not send it. List the law enforcement agency and case number on the application; UOVC requests the investigative report from the agency.

rules.summary: UOVC staff request the investigative report directly from law enforcement, so you list the agency and case number rather than attaching the report.
rules.quote: The Utah Office for Victims of Crime staff must request the investigative report directly from the law enforcement agency.
rules.pinpoint: Apply for Compensation, Victim Compensation Application Process
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Apply for Compensation (application process and eligibility)

params.note: Sexual assault: a questionnaire completed by a sexual assault victim service provider can stand in for a police report.

rules.summary: In sexual assault cases, a questionnaire completed by a sexual assault victim service provider can take the place of a police report.
rules.quote: In cases of sexual assault, a questionnaire can be completed by a sexual assault victim service provider in place of a police report.
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Apply for Compensation (application process and eligibility)

params.note: Insurance details on the application (health insurance, Medicaid, or workers compensation; provider name and policy number; auto insurer if a vehicle was involved). Leaving them out delays processing.

rules.summary: Fill in the insurance section of the application; leaving it blank delays processing.
rules.quote: INSURANCE (Failure to provide this information will delay processing of the application)
rules.source_title: Application for the Crime Victim Reparations Program (English)

params.note: A parent or legal guardian must complete and sign the application for a child victim.

rules.summary: For a child victim, the application must be completed and signed by the child's parent or legal guardian.
rules.quote: APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED FOR CHILD VICTIMS UNDER THE AGE OF EIGHTEEN MUST BE COMPLETED AND SIGNED BY THE CHILD'S PARENT OR LEGAL GUARDIAN
rules.source_title: Application for the Crime Victim Reparations Program (English)

params.note: Bills go from the provider to UOVC. Give the provider your claim number and ask them to send the bills directly.

rules.summary: For crime-related medical bills, give your provider your claim number and ask them to send the bills directly to UOVC.
rules.quote: Contact your medical provider, provide them with your claim number, and ask them to send the bills directly to UOVC.
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Victim FAQs

params.note: Your counselor submits a Mental Health Treatment Plan, and the reparations officer approves it before UOVC pays.

rules.summary: Before UOVC pays for outpatient counseling, your counselor must submit a Mental Health Treatment Plan for approval.
rules.quote: a qualified mental health professional who intends to provide outpatient mental health counseling to a victim shall submit a Mental Health Treatment Plan to the office
rules.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

params.note: Funeral or relocation costs can be paid to the provider or reimbursed to you once you submit the necessary documentation.

rules.summary: Funeral or relocation costs can be paid directly to providers, or reimbursed to you when you submit the necessary documentation.
rules.quote: Payment for these services may be made directly to the providers, or the claimant/victim can be reimbursed upon submission of the necessary documentation.
rules.pinpoint: What Happens After a Decision, Funeral or Relocation Costs
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, What Happens After a Decision

rules.summary: Applications are reviewed in the order received, and processing takes about 60 to 90 days.
rules.quote: Processing time is approximately 60-90 days.
rules.pinpoint: Apply for Compensation, Victim Compensation Application Process
rules.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Apply for Compensation (application process and eligibility)

params.enroll: In order to apply for the Safe at Home Program, a victim must meet with a Certified Safe at Home Program Assistant. Safe at Home Program Assistants are victim advocates and others who work with victims that have gone through a certification training. They will complete the application with the victim and submit it to Safe at Home on behalf of the victim. Safe at Home cannot accept applications directly from an individual. That individual must work with a Program Assistant.

rules.summary: Utah's Safe at Home Program is for survivors of sexual assault, abuse, child abuse, domestic violence, stalking, or human trafficking who live in Utah and are afraid they will be in physical danger if the perpetrator knows where they live. It gives them a substitute address and mail forwarding. You apply through a certified program assistant, not on your own.
rules.quote: Utah’s Safe at Home Program is available to survivors of abuse, child abuse, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, and sexual assault who are afraid that they will be in physical danger if their perpetrator knows where they live. The program will provide a substitute address and mail forwarding for survivors living in Utah.
rules.pinpoint: Safe at Home homepage, program description; Utah Code 75E-11-102 and 75E-11-302 (UT-S16)
rules.source_title: Utah Safe at Home, program homepage (Utah's address confidentiality program)

rules.summary: Records the Utah Office for Victims of Crime keeps about a claim, including restitution records, can be shared only as this law allows, whatever the state open records law says.
rules.quote: Notwithstanding Title 63G, Chapter 2, Government Records Access and Management Act, a confidential record, a public restitution record, and a nonpublic restitution record may only be disclosed as provided in this section.
rules.pinpoint: Utah Code 75E-5-205(1)-(3); definition of confidential record at 75E-5-101(10)
rules.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

params.payer: Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund (Virginia Victims Fund SAFE Payment Program)

rules.summary: The state's Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund pays for physical evidence recovery kit (PERK) exams for sexual assault victims.
rules.quote: the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund shall pay for physical evidence recovery kit examinations conducted on victims of sexual assault
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

params.payer: the Commonwealth, through the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund

rules.summary: Exam evidence-gathering fees are paid by the Commonwealth, and the survivor does not have to cooperate with police or the criminal case to get the exam.
rules.quote: shall be paid by the Commonwealth pursuant to subsection F of § 19.2-368.11:1 . Such victims shall not be required to participate in the criminal justice system or cooperate with law-enforcement authorities in order to be provided with such medical exams.
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-165.1 (Payment of medical fees in certain criminal cases)

params.scope: evidence collection

rules.summary: Survivors have the right to seek evidence collection at no cost to them.
rules.quote: You have the right to seek evidence collection at no cost to you;
rules.pinpoint: VVF Notice to Sexual Assault Patients
rules.source_title: Notice to Sexual Assault Patients (SAFE Payment Program)

rules.summary: Patients should be billed only for expenses the SAFE Payment Program does not cover; a patient billed by mistake for the exam can seek reimbursement from the program.
rules.quote: Patients should only receive bills from providers for expenses considered ineligible for payment by the SAFE Payment Program.
rules.pinpoint: SAFE Payment Program Procedures and Guidelines, Eligibility Criteria 3(b)
rules.source_title: SAFE Payment Program Procedures and Guidelines (2026)

params.payer: SAFE Payment Program, after any federally funded insurance such as Medicaid, Medicare or Tricare; billing private insurance first is not required unless the patient asks

rules.summary: If you have Medicaid, Medicare, Tricare or other federally funded insurance, it must be billed first. Your private health insurance does not have to be billed first unless you ask for that. The program pays any eligible amount still owed.
rules.quote: If the patient is covered by a federally funded insurance such as Medicaid, Medicare, Tricare, etc., insurance must be billed primary. Billing private health insurance primary is not required unless requested by the patient. The SAFE Payment Program will pay any eligible remaining patient responsibility.
rules.pinpoint: VVF SAFE Payment Program page, Submit a SAFE claim
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: SAFE Payment Program page

params.payer: SAFE Payment Program, for crimes in Virginia when evidence is collected
params.condition: if done within 120 hours of a Virginia crime

rules.summary: The SAFE Payment Program pays only if the crime was in Virginia and evidence is collected.
rules.quote: The crime occurred within the Commonwealth of Virginia . Collection of evidence took place as outlined in §19.2-165.1 of the Code of Virginia. Patients are not required to report the crime to law enforcement, nor cooperate with an investigation in order to request a Physical Evidence Recovery Kit (PERK) exam or for that exam to be paid per §19.2-165.1 (B). If the patient declines evidence collection, the claim is not eligible for reimbursement. The SAFE Payment Program does not reimburse for consults, only for collection of medical forensic evidence. Medical forensic examinations for non-acute (more than 120 hours after the crime) and/or chronic sexual abuse cases require authorization by law enforcement officer or prosecutor for payment per §19.2-165.1 (A).
rules.pinpoint: VVF SAFE Payment Program page, Eligibility Requirements
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: SAFE Payment Program page

params.payer: SAFE Payment Program, with law enforcement or prosecutor authorization for non-acute exams

rules.summary: Non-acute exams (more than 120 hours after the crime) and chronic sexual abuse cases need authorization from a law enforcement officer or prosecutor to be paid.
rules.quote: Medical forensic examinations for non-acute (more than 120 hours after the crime) and/or chronic sexual abuse cases require authorization by law enforcement officer or prosecutor for payment per §19.2-165.1 (A).
rules.pinpoint: VVF SAFE Payment Program page, Eligibility Requirements
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: SAFE Payment Program page

params.payer: Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund

rules.summary: What the Fund pays for a PERK exam does not count against the survivor's maximum award.
rules.quote: Funds paid for physical evidence recovery kit or anonymous trace evidence collection kit collection shall not be offset against the Fund's maximum allowable award as provided in subsection H.
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

rules.summary: Total payments on a claim, after collateral sources are subtracted, cannot exceed $35,000.
rules.quote: payments for injury or death to a victim of crime, to the victim's dependents or to others entitled to payment for covered expenses, after being reduced as provided in subsection G, shall not exceed $35,000 in the aggregate.
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

rules.summary: A claim must have a minimum value of $100 to qualify for an award.
rules.quote: To qualify for an award under this chapter, a claim must have a minimum value of $100
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

rules.summary: The weekly rate is 66-2/3 percent of the victim's average weekly wages.
rules.quote: at a weekly compensation rate equal to 66-2 /3 percent of the victim's average weekly wages
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

rules.summary: If the crime leaves the victim totally unable to work, lost pay is paid weekly while that lasts. The rate is 66-2/3 percent of the victim's average weekly wages.
rules.quote: An award made pursuant to this chapter for total loss of earnings that results directly from incapacity incurred by a crime victim shall be payable during total incapacity to the victim or to such other eligible person, at a weekly compensation rate equal to 66-2 /3 percent of the victim's average weekly wages
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

rules.summary: Reasonable and necessary moving expenses are covered up to $2,000.
rules.quote: reasonable and necessary moving expenses, not to exceed $2,000, incurred by a victim or survivors
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

rules.summary: Home security purchase and installation is covered up to $1,000, and the system should be installed within 30 days after the crime.
rules.quote: Home Security: Reimbursement of the purchase and installation of home security measures. This expense is based on an immediate need for safety; therefore, the system should be installed within thirty (30) days after the crime. (up to $1,000)
rules.pinpoint: VVF Eligibility page, Requirement #4: Expense Stipulations
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Eligibility page

params.scope: temporary lodging, only if staying in the home where the crime happened is not safe, starting right after the crime, for up to 30 days

rules.summary: Temporary lodging is covered only in limited situations, when staying in the home where the crime happened would put the victim's safety at risk. Receipts must be in the victim's name. The stay must start right after the crime and cannot be longer than 30 days.
rules.quote: Temporary Lodging: Limited situations only, when the physical safety of the victim would be risked by staying in the dwelling where the crime occurred. Receipts must be in the victim’s name. Temporary lodging must begin immediately following the crime and must not exceed 30 days.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Eligibility page, Requirement #4: Expense Stipulations
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Eligibility page

rules.summary: Unreimbursed medical expenses, or debt reasonably incurred for medical expenses, are covered.
rules.quote: unreimbursed medical expenses or indebtedness reasonably incurred for medical expenses
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

rules.summary: Expenses attributable to a pregnancy resulting from forcible rape are covered.
rules.quote: expenses attributable to pregnancy resulting from forcible rape
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

rules.summary: Prescriptions for crime-related injuries or conditions may be reimbursed with receipts.
rules.quote: Prescriptions for treatment of injuries/conditions caused by the crime may be reimbursed.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Eligibility page, Requirement #4: Expense Stipulations
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Eligibility page

rules.summary: When a provider decides HIV prevention medication is needed, the SAFE Payment Program pays for the full 28-day course.
rules.quote: The full course (28-day supply) of HIV preventative medication
rules.pinpoint: VVF SAFE Payment Program page, HIV Prevention
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: SAFE Payment Program page

rules.summary: Counseling is an eligible expense for direct victims.
rules.quote: Counseling For direct victims
rules.pinpoint: VVF How Compensation Works, Eligible Expenses
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: How Compensation Works

params.scope: mileage to and from medical care, police, and court, for minor victims only

rules.summary: Mileage to and from medical treatment, investigations and court is reimbursed for minor victims only.
rules.quote: Mileage - Minor Victims Only: Reimbursement for mileage to/from medical treatment, criminal investigations and court proceedings. (Minor victims only.)
rules.pinpoint: VVF Eligibility page, Requirement #4: Expense Stipulations
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Eligibility page

params.scope: replacing clothing or bedding taken as evidence

rules.summary: When clothing or bedding is taken as evidence, the fund may pay for replacements.
rules.quote: When clothing or bedding are taken as evidence, VVF may pay for the purchase of a replacement.
rules.pinpoint: VVF How Compensation Works, Non-Eligible Expenses
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: How Compensation Works

params.item: replacement of stolen vehicles, cellphones, money, or other personal property

rules.summary: The fund does not replace stolen vehicles, cellphones, money, or other personal property.
rules.quote: Replacement of stolen vehicles, cellphones, money, or other personal property
rules.pinpoint: VVF How Compensation Works, Non-Eligible Expenses
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: How Compensation Works

params.item: attorneys' fees

rules.summary: The program cannot award attorneys' fees.
rules.quote: The Commission lacks authority to award attorneys’ fees.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Policies, Criteria for an Award (E)
rules.source_title: Policies of the Virginia Victims Fund (revised September 2025)

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: The fund cannot pay for pain and suffering.
rules.quote: The Fund cannot consider payment for pain and suffering and non-eligible property damage.
rules.pinpoint: VVF How Compensation Works, Payer of Last Resort
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: How Compensation Works

params.condition: for a crime on or after July 1, 2025

rules.summary: The program applies the three-year deadline to crimes committed on or after July 1, 2025.
rules.quote: Crimes committed on and after July 1, 2025 The deadline to file a claim is three years from the crime.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Eligibility page, Requirement #5: Filing Timeline Stipulations
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Eligibility page

rules.summary: The date of the crime decides how long you have to file, based on the law in effect at that time.
rules.quote: The date of the crime will determine how long the victim has to file a claim with VVF based on the law in effect at the time.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Eligibility page, Requirement #5: Filing Timeline Stipulations
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Eligibility page

rules.summary: The current statute says a claim must be filed within three years after the crime.
rules.quote: A claim shall be filed by the claimant not later than three years after the occurrence of the crime upon which such claim is based
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.5 (Filing of claims)

params.extension: good cause shown, with a written explanation of the delayed filing

rules.summary: For crimes committed July 1, 2001 through June 30, 2025, the deadline is one year from the crime, extendable for good cause with a written explanation.
rules.quote: Crimes committed on July 1, 2001 through June 30, 2025 The deadline to file a claim is one year from the crime. This deadline may be extended for good cause shown if the the claimants file a written explanation of the delayed filing.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Eligibility page, Requirement #5: Filing Timeline Stipulations
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Eligibility page

params.extension: No time limit where the sexual abuse of a minor was a felony.

rules.summary: For sexual abuse of a minor, the claim may be filed up to 10 years after the victim's eighteenth birthday; where the conduct was a felony, there is no time bar.
rules.quote: in cases involving claims of sexual abuse of a minor, the claim shall be filed within 10 years after the minor's eighteenth birthday, except for in cases involving claims of sexual abuse of a minor where the conduct constitutes a felony, the passage of time shall not be a barrier to when the victim can file a claim.
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.5 (Filing of claims)

rules.summary: For a crime on or after July 1, 2001, the Commission may give more time to file for good cause.
rules.quote: For good cause shown, the Commission may extend the time for filing for a crime committed on or after July 1, 2001.
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.5 (Filing of claims)

rules.summary: The requirement that police or court records show the crime was promptly reported does not apply to claims of sexual abuse (which the statute defines to include rape, sodomy, object sexual penetration and sexual battery).
rules.quote: The provisions of this subdivision shall not apply to claims of sexual abuse.
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.10 (When awards to be made; reporting crime to law enforcement)

rules.summary: Anyone who submits to and completes a PERK exam is considered to have met the program's reporting requirements.
rules.quote: Any individual that submits to and completes any such examination shall be considered to have met the reporting requirements of this chapter.
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by payments from the offender or any other public or private source, such as insurance.
rules.quote: Any claim made pursuant to this chapter shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received as a result of the injury from or on behalf of the person who committed the crime or from any other public or private source
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

rules.summary: The award may be reduced or denied if the victim's conduct contributed to the injury.
rules.quote: the Commission shall determine whether, because of his conduct, the victim of such crime contributed to the infliction of his injury, and the Commission shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether, in accordance with such determination
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.12 (Awards; apportionment; reductions)

rules.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $3,000.
rules.quote: the amount of such emergency award shall not exceed $3,000
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.9 (Emergency awards)

rules.summary: Sexual abuse covers rape, sodomy, object sexual penetration and sexual battery.
rules.quote: "Sexual abuse" means sexual abuse as defined in subdivision 6 of § 18.2-67.10 and acts constituting rape, sodomy, object sexual penetration or sexual battery as defined in Article 7 (§ 18.2-61 et seq.) of Chapter 4 of Title 18.2.
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.2 (Definitions)

rules.summary: The program lists sexual abuse of minors and adults as an eligible crime, requiring physical injury for misdemeanors or emotional injury for felonies.
rules.quote: Sexual Abuse (minors and adults) (must result in physical injury for misdemeanors or emotional injury for felonies) Rape, sodomy, object sexual penetration Sexual battery
rules.pinpoint: VVF Eligibility page, Requirement #1: Crime Stipulations
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Eligibility page

params.rule: Crime must occur in Virginia; Virginia residency or U.S. citizenship is not required for crimes in Virginia.

rules.summary: For a crime committed in Virginia, the victim does not need to be a Virginia resident or a U.S. citizen.
rules.quote: As long as the crime was committed in Virginia, there is no requirement that the victim be a Virginia resident or United States citizen to be eligible for an award under the Act.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Policies, Criteria for an Award (H)
rules.source_title: Policies of the Virginia Victims Fund (revised September 2025)

params.rule: Virginia residents hurt by a crime outside Virginia can apply only if that place has no eligible VOCA compensation program and does not compensate nonresidents.

rules.summary: A Virginia resident hurt by a crime outside Virginia can qualify only if they would be eligible had it happened in Virginia and the place where it happened has no eligible compensation program that pays nonresidents.
rules.quote: A resident of Virginia who is the victim of a crime occurring outside Virginia and any other person as defined in subsection A who is injured as a result of a crime occurring outside Virginia shall be eligible for an award pursuant to this chapter if (i) the person would be eligible for benefits had the crime occurred in Virginia and (ii) the state, country or territory in which the crime occurred does not have a crime victims' compensation program deemed eligible pursuant to the provisions of the federal Victims of Crime Act and does not compensate nonresidents.
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.4 (Persons eligible for awards)

rules.summary: Mail the completed application to the Virginia Victims Fund at P.O. Box 26927, Richmond, VA 23261.
rules.quote: Submit application to P.O. Box 26927, Richmond, VA 23261 or (fax) 804-823-6905.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 2 (Returning the Application)
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

rules.summary: The application can be faxed to the Virginia Victims Fund at 804-823-6905.
rules.quote: Submit application to P.O. Box 26927, Richmond, VA 23261 or (fax) 804-823-6905.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 2 (Returning the Application)
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

rules.summary: Claims can be filed in person at the office of the Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission, which runs the Fund; the contact page says in-person help is by appointment only.
rules.quote: Claims shall be filed in the office of the Commission in person, by mail, or by electronic means in accordance with standards approved by the Commission.
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.5 (Filing of claims)

params.note: Only trained Victim/Witness advocates (and medical providers) can use WebFile; a survivor files online by working with a local Victim/Witness program.
params.condition: for victim advocates with special training

rules.summary: WebFile, the program's online claim system, is for victim advocates with special training.
rules.quote: Victim advocates that have been through specialized training may file via WebFile, the Fund's online claims submission system.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Policies (Sept 2025), Where a Claim Must Be Filed, p. 12
rules.source_title: Policies of the Virginia Victims Fund (revised September 2025)

params.note: All receipts, records and documents supporting each requested expense, sent with the application and for ongoing expenses.

rules.summary: Attach all receipts, records and documents that support the expenses requested, and keep sending them for ongoing expenses.
rules.quote: Applicants should attach all receipts, records and documents supporting requested expenses and continue doing so for ongoing expenses.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 2 (Returning the Application)
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

params.note: Copies of detailed, itemized billing statements from each medical provider.

rules.summary: Attach copies of detailed, itemized billing statements from the medical providers who treated crime-related injuries.
rules.quote: Attach a list of additional providers and attach copies of detailed, itemized billing statements.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), Section I (Medical Providers), application p. 3
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

params.note: Insurance documentation such as explanation of benefits (EOBs).

rules.summary: Include bills, receipts, invoices and insurance documentation with the application.
rules.quote: Please include any bills, receipts, invoices, and insurance documentation with the application.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form page, Helpful Tips
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: VVF Claim Form page (form instructions)

params.note: Proof of physical and/or emotional injury, such as health records; required once the application is deemed eligible.

rules.summary: Once the application is deemed eligible, the survivor must provide proof of physical or emotional injury, such as health records.
rules.quote: Eligible claimants must submit proof of physical and/or emotional injuries. Proof includes health records detailing a physical and/or emotional injury.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (Physical/Emotional Injuries)
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

params.note: Written explanation of the victim's physical, mental, emotional and family situation (reporting factors for crimes under the current reporting standard).

rules.summary: Include a written explanation of the victim's physical, mental, emotional and family situation with the application; the form asks for this under the reporting factors for newer crimes.
rules.quote: The victim's physical, mental, emotional and family situation (Claimants must include a written explanation of these factors with their application,)
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (The Crime)
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

params.note: Copy of any permanent protective order between the victim and offender.

rules.summary: If there is a permanent protective order between the victim and offender, attach it.
rules.quote: Is there a permanent protective order for the victim and offender? ☐ Yes ☐ No (Attach if yes.)
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), Section E (Reporting Information), application p. 2
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

params.note: Copy of the hospital charity care decision, if uninsured and treated at a hospital.

rules.summary: If the victim had no health insurance and was treated at a hospital, apply for the hospital's charity care and send a copy of the decision; VVF will not decide on health expenses without it.
rules.quote: VVF will not make a decision on reimbursing health expenses without a copy of the charity care decision.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), Section J (Insurance and Collateral Resources), application p. 3
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

params.note: Prescription receipts showing medication, prescribing doctor, date filled and amount charged.

rules.summary: For prescriptions, provide copies of receipts that show the medication, the prescribing doctor, the date filled and the amount charged.
rules.quote: The applicant must provide copies of receipts for prescriptions.
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

params.note: Medical provider verification that the victim could not work, for lost wages.

rules.summary: Lost wages are paid only when a medical provider verifies the victim could not work because of the crime-related injury.
rules.quote: Replacement of lost wages for the victim, who could not work because of the crime-related injury, as verified by a medical provider.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (Loss of Wages)
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

params.note: Copy of the law-enforcement evidence receipt plus the receipt for replacement items, when clothing or bedding was taken as evidence.

rules.summary: To be reimbursed for clothing or bedding taken as evidence, send a copy of the evidence receipt from law enforcement and the receipt for the replacement items.
rules.quote: In order to reimburse this expense, the Fund must have a copy of the evidence receipt provided to the victim by a law-enforcement agency.
rules.source_title: Policies of the Virginia Victims Fund (revised September 2025)

params.note: Dated, signed contracts and a written justification for moving expenses.

rules.summary: Moving expenses need dated, signed contracts and a written justification.
rules.quote: (Dated/signed contracts required.)
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (Moving Expenses)
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

params.note: The application itself, signed by the applicant.

rules.summary: The application is not accepted unless the applicant signs it.
rules.quote: Applications are not accepted unless this form is signed by the applicant.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), Applicant Responsibilities & Authorizations, application p. 4
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

params.agency: Office of the Attorney General of Virginia
params.enroll: An individual who is at least 18 years of age, a parent or guardian acting on behalf of a minor, a guardian acting on behalf of an incapacitated person, or an emancipated minor may apply in person at (i) sexual or domestic violence programs that have been accredited by the Virginia Sexual and Domestic Violence Program Professional Standards Committee ... or (ii) crime victim and witness assistance programs.

rules.summary: Virginia's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of the Attorney General, lets victims of sexual violence, domestic violence, stalking or child abduction use a designated address, and the office forwards their first-class mail to the actual address.
rules.quote: to protect victims of domestic violence, stalking, child abduction, or sexual violence by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims
rules.source_title: Va. Code § 2.2-515.2 (Address Confidentiality Program)

rules.summary: All Virginia Victims Fund applications and related documents, including medical records, are confidential; except where law requires otherwise, VVF discloses a victim's information only with written permission.
rules.quote: All Virginia Victims Fund (VVF) applications and related documents, including medical information and records, are highly confidential. Except as otherwise required by Virginia or federal law, VVF may only disclose a victim or applicant’s information with their written permission.
rules.pinpoint: VVF Confidentiality page, Your Claim is Confidential
rules.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Confidentiality page

params.payer: State of Vermont, paid from the Victims' Compensation Fund, for whatever the survivor's health coverage does not pay

rules.summary: The State pays for a sexual assault exam when the survivor has no health coverage or coverage does not pay the whole cost, even if the survivor gets the exam before police or a prosecutor ask for one.
rules.quote: The State shall also bear the costs of sexual assault examinations, as defined in 8 V.S.A. § 4083, administered to victims in cases of alleged sexual assault where the victim obtains such an examination prior to receiving such a request if the victim does not have health coverage or the victim's health coverage does not cover the entire cost of the examination.
rules.source_title: 32 V.S.A. § 1407, Costs to be borne by the State

rules.summary: If the survivor's health coverage leaves a co-payment, coinsurance, deductible, or other cost-sharing for the exam, the Fund pays that share directly to the provider, so the survivor does not owe it.
rules.quote: If the victim's health coverage does not cover all of the medical care provided pursuant to this section and the victim would otherwise be responsible for any co-payment, coinsurance, deductible, or other cost-sharing, the Fund shall pay the victim's share directly to the health care facility or provider.
rules.source_title: 32 V.S.A. § 1407, Costs to be borne by the State

rules.summary: Providers must bill the survivor's health plan, Medicaid, or Medicare for the exam first. If the survivor is uninsured or the plan denies the claim, the Fund pays Vermont providers 60 percent of billed charges and the provider may not bill the survivor for the balance.
rules.quote: Health care facilities and health care providers shall bill the victim's health insurance plan, Medicaid, Medicare, or another health benefit plan, as applicable, for the services described in subsection (b) of this section. If the victim does not have health coverage or if the victim's health benefit plan denies the claim, the Fund shall reimburse health care facilities and health care providers located in Vermont as defined in 18 V.S.A. § 9402 at 60 percent of the billed charges for these claims, and the health care provider or facility shall not bill any balance to the crime victim.
rules.source_title: 32 V.S.A. § 1407, Costs to be borne by the State

rules.summary: Through the CCVS Sexual Assault Program, the initial sexual assault medical exam is covered, including evidence collection, STI and HIV screening and prophylaxis, pregnancy testing, and treatment of related injuries.
rules.quote: Resources are available to pay for the initial sexual assault medical examination to include: collection of evidence STI (sexually transmitted infections) and HIV screening prophylaxis pregnancy testing treatment of related injuries
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Sexual Assault Program page, What is covered?
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Sexual Assault Program

params.payer: State of Vermont, for victims of crime committed in Vermont
params.condition: if the crime was in Vermont

rules.summary: As this section describes, the State covers the costs of certain medical care for victims of a crime committed in Vermont who have no health insurance or whose insurance does not pay for all of the care.
rules.quote: As described in this section, the State shall cover the costs of certain medical care for victims of crime committed in this State without health insurance or whose health insurance does not pay for all of the care provided.
rules.source_title: 32 V.S.A. § 1407, Costs to be borne by the State

rules.summary: An approved claim can receive up to $10,000 in total, equal to the crime-related losses not paid by other sources.
rules.quote: the Board shall authorize cash payments, not to exceed $10,000.00, to or on behalf of the applicant, equal to the unreimbursed pecuniary loss directly resulting from the injury or death of the victim.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rules.summary: Victims Compensation pays at most $100 for a one-hour individual or family counseling session, prorated for shorter sessions.
rules.quote: One-hour individual or family sessions will be paid at a maximum of $100.00 per session.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Mental Health Policy, Guidelines 1 (Fee Schedule)
rules.source_title: CCVS Victims Compensation Mental Health Policy (amended 8/12/2024)

rules.summary: The Sexual Assault Program pays at most $100 for a one-hour individual counseling session.
rules.quote: One-hour individual sessions will be paid at a maximum of $100.00 per session.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Sexual Assault Program Mental Health Policy, Guidelines & Fee Schedule
rules.source_title: CCVS Sexual Assault Program Mental Health Policy (updated 08/12/2024)

rules.summary: After a sexual assault exam, the Sexual Assault Program can pay for up to 20 sessions of mental health counseling.
rules.quote: The Sexual Assault Program can consider payment of up to 20 sessions of mental health counseling after a victim has obtained a medical sexual assault examination.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Sexual Assault Program Mental Health Policy, Introduction
rules.source_title: CCVS Sexual Assault Program Mental Health Policy (updated 08/12/2024)

rules.summary: Covered medical costs include individual or family psychological, psychiatric, or mental health counseling, and replacing eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures, or prosthetic devices taken, lost, or destroyed during the crime.
rules.quote: Medical or medically related expenses may include, but are not limited to, the costs of individual or family psychological, psychiatric, or mental health counseling and the costs of replacing or repairing eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures, or any prosthetic devices that were taken, lost, or destroyed during the commission of the crime.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rules.summary: For claims filed on or after 9/8/2025, lost wages are reimbursed up to $750 per week, for no more than 12 weeks per claim.
rules.quote: 5b) For Compensation claim filed on or after 9/8/2025: the Victims Compensation Program will reimburse lost wages not to exceed a maximum reimbursement of $750.00 per week per claim, and for not longer than 12 weeks per claim.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages, para. 5b
rules.source_title: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages (amended 9/8/2025)

rules.summary: Lost wages are paid at 85% of the victim's gross wages at the time of the loss.
rules.quote: lost wages will be paid at 85% of the victim's gross wages at the time of the loss.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages, para. 2
rules.source_title: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages (amended 9/8/2025)

rules.summary: Relocation costs such as rental trucks, movers, transportation, and up to three months of storage are capped at $1,500 in total.
rules.quote: Relocation costs could include the following: rental trucks, moving companies, transportation costs, storage fees not to exceed three months. Total relocation costs not to exceed $1,500.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Housing and Relocation, Relocation Costs
rules.source_title: CCVS Policy for Housing and Relocation

rules.summary: Emergency housing is paid at up to $100 per night, for no more than 7 nights.
rules.quote: Emergency housing will be paid at a maximum of $100.00 per night, for not more than 7 nights.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Housing and Relocation, Emergency Housing
rules.source_title: CCVS Policy for Housing and Relocation

rules.summary: The program can help with relocation when the victim's safety is at risk or the victim is displaced by the crime, generally no more than once in a 12-month period.
rules.quote: The Victims Compensation Program will generally pay relocation costs no more than once in a 12-month period.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Housing and Relocation, introduction
rules.source_title: CCVS Policy for Housing and Relocation

rules.summary: In non-homicide cases, travel to attend criminal court proceedings, Parole Board hearings, and pre-sentence investigations is capped at $2,000 per claim.
rules.quote: For all non-homicide criminal cases there is a $2,000.00 travel expense cap per claim for the eligible victim to attend criminal court proceedings, Parole Board hearings, and to participate in pre-sentence investigations.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Travel Expenses
rules.source_title: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Travel Expenses

rules.summary: Transportation for medical or mental health treatment can be paid as a medically related expense.
rules.quote: -transportation for medical/mental health treatment.
rules.source_title: Code Vt. R. 80-220-001, Victims Compensation Board rules (via Cornell LII)

rules.summary: For uninsured victims who do not qualify for hospital assistance, Medicaid, or Medicare, the Board may pay providers 60 percent of billed charges, and the provider may not bill the victim for the balance.
rules.quote: The Board may reimburse health care facilities and health care providers as defined in 18 V.S.A. § 9402 at 60 percent of the billed charges for compensation claims for uninsured crime victims who do not qualify for the hospital's patient assistance program, Medicaid, or Medicare. The health care facility or health care provider shall not bill any balance to the uninsured crime victim.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rules.summary: Pecuniary loss covers medical or medically related expenses, lost wages, and other expenses the Board finds became necessary as a direct result of the crime.
rules.quote: "Pecuniary loss" means, in the case of a victim, the amount of medical or medically related expenses, loss of wages, and any other expenses that the Board feels became necessary as a direct result of the crime.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rules.summary: Safety and security expenses are listed among the costs the program may pay.
rules.quote: Safety/security
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Eligibility page, Expenses the Victims Compensation Program may pay for
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Victims Compensation Eligibility

params.item: lost, stolen, or damaged property, except medically necessary items

rules.summary: Lost, stolen, or damaged property is not paid, except medically necessary items.
rules.quote: Expenses for lost, stolen or damaged property (except medically necessary items due to a qualifying crime)
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Eligibility page, Expenses that cannot be paid by the Compensation Program
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Victims Compensation Eligibility

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: Damages for pain and suffering are not paid.
rules.quote: Damages for pain and suffering
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Eligibility page, Expenses that cannot be paid by the Compensation Program
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Victims Compensation Eligibility

rules.summary: Attorney fees are not paid.
rules.quote: Attorney fees
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Eligibility page, Expenses that cannot be paid by the Compensation Program
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Victims Compensation Eligibility

params.extension: The Board may extend the time for good cause shown.

rules.summary: An application is denied if it is not filed within the time allowed for starting a prosecution of the crime, but the Board may extend the time for good cause.
rules.quote: (1) The application was not made within the period of time permitted for commencing prosecution of the crime. The Board may extend the time for filing for good cause shown.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rules.summary: Prosecution of sexual assault and aggravated sexual assault can begin at any time, so the prosecution period that sets the compensation filing limit does not run out for those crimes.
rules.quote: (a) Prosecutions for aggravated sexual assault, aggravated sexual assault of a child, sexual assault, sexual exploitation of a minor as defined in subsection 3258(c) of this title, human trafficking, aggravated human trafficking, murder, manslaughter, arson causing death, and kidnapping may be commenced at any time after the commission of the offense.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. § 4501, Limitation of prosecutions for certain crimes

rules.summary: Prosecution for lewd and lascivious conduct must begin within 6 years, so that is also the time limit to apply for it.
rules.quote: (b) Prosecutions for lewd and lascivious conduct, sexual abuse of a vulnerable adult under subsection 1379(a) of this title, grand larceny, robbery, burglary, embezzlement, forgery, bribery offenses, false claims, fraud under 33 V.S.A. § 141(d), and felony tax offenses shall be commenced within six years after the commission of the offense, and not after.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. § 4501, Limitation of prosecutions for certain crimes

rules.summary: For lewd and lascivious conduct against a child under 18, lewd or lascivious conduct with a child, and sexual exploitation of children, prosecution must begin within 40 years. That is also the time limit to apply.
rules.quote: (c) Prosecutions for any of the following offenses shall be commenced within 40 years after the commission of the offense, and not after: (1) lewd and lascivious conduct alleged to have been committed against a child under 18 years of age; (2) maiming; (3) lewd or lascivious conduct with a child; (4) sexual exploitation of children under chapter 64 of this title; and (5) sexual abuse of a vulnerable adult under subsection 1379(b) of this title.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. § 4501, Limitation of prosecutions for certain crimes

rules.summary: For other felonies and misdemeanors, prosecution must begin within 3 years. That is also the time limit to apply.
rules.quote: (e) Prosecutions for other felonies and for misdemeanors shall be commenced within three years after the commission of the offense, and not after.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. § 4501, Limitation of prosecutions for certain crimes

rules.summary: For Victims Compensation, a law enforcement official must have filed a report concluding that a crime was committed that caused the injury.
rules.quote: (1) a law enforcement official has filed a report concluding that a crime was committed which resulted in the injury or death of the victim
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

params.scope: the separate Sexual Assault Program

rules.summary: The separate CCVS Sexual Assault Program does not require a police report. The assault only has to be reported to a medical provider.
rules.quote: The victim does not have to report the crime to the police to be eligible , only to a medical provider .
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Sexual Assault Program page, Who is eligible?
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Sexual Assault Program

rules.summary: The program pays only losses not covered by medical, hospitalization, or disability insurance or workers' compensation.
rules.quote: (A) that is not covered by medical, hospitalization, or disability insurance or workers' compensation
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rules.summary: Insurance must be billed before the program pays.
rules.quote: Does insurance or other sources of payment have to be used? Yes. Insurance must be billed first.
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Victims Compensation FAQ

rules.summary: A claim must be denied if the victim broke a Vermont criminal law that caused or helped cause the victim's injuries.
rules.quote: (2) The victim violated a criminal law of this State that caused or contributed to the victim's injuries or death.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rules.summary: While a claim is pending, the Board rules allow an emergency advance to help a victim stay healthy or safe and avoid financial hardship. Any advance is deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: A) Emergency Advance can be made during the period of time a claim is pending approval by the full Board where such grants could help a victim maintain a reasonable level of health or safety for herself/himself or dependents and prevent financial hardship.
rules.source_title: Code Vt. R. 80-220-001, Victims Compensation Board rules (via Cornell LII)

rules.summary: Sexual assault is listed among the crimes that may qualify for compensation.
rules.quote: Robbery Sexual Assault Stalking
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Eligibility page, Types of crimes that may qualify
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Victims Compensation Eligibility

rules.summary: Injury includes bodily harm, pregnancy, or emotional harm resulting from the crime.
rules.quote: "Injury" means actual bodily harm or pregnancy, or emotional harm resulting from the crime.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

params.rule: Crime committed in Vermont (any victim), or a Vermont resident victimized in a state without an eligible compensation program

rules.summary: The crime must have happened in Vermont, or the victim is a Vermont resident and the state where it happened has no eligible compensation program.
rules.quote: (2) the crime was committed in this State; or (3) the victim is a Vermont resident, the state in which the crime occurred does not have an eligible crime Victims Compensation Program and the applicant would have been eligible for compensation under this chapter if the crime had been committed in this State;
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

params.rule: Sexual Assault Program: assault happened in Vermont

rules.summary: The Sexual Assault Program covers sexual assaults that happened in Vermont.
rules.quote: Victims of sexual assault are eligible if the crime happened in Vermont.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Sexual Assault Program page, Who is eligible?
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Sexual Assault Program

params.target:
Victims Compensation Program

Waterbury, Vermont 05676-1599

Victims Compensation Program
58 South Main Street, Suite One
Waterbury, Vermont 05676-1599

rules.quote: The application is also available and can be downloaded in other languages, as well as in a fillable PDF version if you prefer to print and mail your application to us. ONLINE Victims Compensation Application
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Application & Forms

params.note: Send any outstanding crime-related bills with the application, and send later bills as they arrive.

rules.summary: Outstanding crime-related bills should be sent in with the application.
rules.quote: If there are outstanding crime related bills, please send them with the application.
rules.pinpoint: Victims Compensation FAQ, What happens when an application is received?
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Victims Compensation FAQ

params.note: Signatures and dates in three places on the application: authorization to obtain information, repayment/subrogation agreement, and certification.
