rules.summary: The application must be signed and dated in three places (authorization, repayment agreement, certification) to be eligible; missing signatures delay a claim.
rules.quote:
You must sign and date in the three (3) places that follow to be eligible for Victims
Compensation.
rules.pinpoint: Application for Vermont Victims Compensation, page 6
rules.source_title: Application for Vermont Victims Compensation (English)

params.note: Self-employed victims claiming lost wages: prior or current tax returns, 1099s, Schedule C, W-2s, or other proof of income.

rules.summary: For self-employed victims, lost wages are figured from net income shown on tax returns, 1099 forms, Schedule C, W-2s, or other proof of income.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages, item 3
rules.source_title: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages (amended 9/8/2025)

params.note: Lost wages beyond two weeks: a Physician's Report or a mental health provider statement on the disability and return-to-work date.

rules.summary: To be paid for more than two weeks of lost wages, the victim must submit a Physician's Report or a mental health provider's statement saying when they can return to work.
rules.quote:
eligible for reimbursement of more than two weeks lost wages, a victim must
submit his/her Physician's Report, or a statement from his/her mental health
provider which states the nature of the disability and indicates when the victim
will be able to return to work.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages, item 4b
rules.source_title: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages (amended 9/8/2025)

params.note: The counselor submits a current Mental Health Treatment Plan; up to four sessions can be paid before it arrives.

rules.summary: Counseling is paid only after the treatment provider submits a current Mental Health Treatment Plan.
rules.quote:
To be eligible for payment of counseling expenses, the treatment
provider must submit a current Mental Health Treatment Plan
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Victims Compensation Mental Health Policy, section 2, Treatment Plans
rules.source_title: CCVS Victims Compensation Mental Health Policy (amended 8/12/2024)

params.note: Prepaid security deposit: landlord's receipt and a signed copy of the lease.

rules.summary: A security deposit the victim already paid is reimbursed after the victim submits the landlord's receipt and a signed copy of the lease.
rules.quote:
we will
reimburse the victim for the security deposit upon the victim's
submission of a landlord's receipt and a signed copy of the lease.
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Housing and Relocation, Security Deposits
rules.source_title: CCVS Policy for Housing and Relocation

params.note: Sexual Assault Program: the Sexual Assault Billing Form, filled out and signed with the SANE nurse at the hospital, opens the claim; no separate application.

rules.summary: For the Sexual Assault Program, the signed Sexual Assault Billing Form completed at the exam serves as the application.
rules.quote: The signed Sexual Assault Billing Form serves as the application to open a claim
rules.pinpoint: CCVS Sexual Assault Program page, How to access the Program?
rules.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Sexual Assault Program

params.program_name: Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program
params.enroll: Ready to apply? Apply Now Find an Applicant Assistant Some applicants find it helpful to use an Applicant Assistant. This is not a requirement to participate in the program.

rules.summary: The Secretary of State's Safe at Home program offers an address confidentiality service and a protected records service to survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, and human trafficking. You can apply online on the program page, on your own or with help from an Applicant Assistant at a local advocacy agency.
rules.quote: Safe at Home provides an address confidentiality service and a protected records service. The program serves survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, providers of legally protected healthcare (reproductive and gender-affirming care), and patients of legally protected healthcare.
rules.pinpoint: Vermont SOS Safe at Home page, opening paragraph; statutory basis 15 V.S.A. §§ 1150 to 1160
rules.source_title: Vermont Secretary of State, Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program page

rules.summary: Every document the Victims Compensation Board reviews to decide a compensation application is confidential and cannot be disclosed without the victim's consent, except as the statute allows.
rules.quote: (a) All documents reviewed by the Victims Compensation Board for purposes of approving an application for compensation shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed without the consent of the victim except as provided in this section and subsection 7043(c) of this title.
rules.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rules.summary: A Washington hospital or emergency medical facility may not bill or charge the survivor, directly or indirectly, for an evidence-gathering sexual assault exam, whether the assault happened in or outside Washington. The state pays.
rules.quote: No costs incurred by a hospital or other emergency medical facility in Washington for the examination of the victim of a sexual assault, whether such assault occurred in or outside the state of Washington, when such examination is performed for the purposes of gathering evidence for possible prosecution, shall be billed or charged directly or indirectly to the victim of such assault.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.170 (examination costs of sexual assault victims paid by state)

params.payer: State of Washington, through the L&I Crime Victims Compensation Program

rules.summary: The exam costs are paid by the state under the crime victims compensation law.
rules.quote: Such costs shall be paid by the state pursuant to this chapter.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.170 (examination costs of sexual assault victims paid by state)

params.payer: Crime Victims Compensation Program (primary payer)

rules.summary: Exam costs must be billed to the Crime Victims Compensation Program, which is the primary payer. The survivor does not have to file an application to get this benefit and may not be billed.
rules.quote: the costs of the examination must be billed to the crime victims compensation program. We are the primary payer of this benefit. The client is not required to file an application with us to receive this benefit and may not be billed for these costs.
rules.source_title: WAC 296-30-170 (who pays for sexual assault examinations)

rules.summary: To get the exam, a patient does not have to pay, use their own insurance, report to police, or file a compensation application.
rules.quote: In order to receive an examination, patients are not required to: Pay for the examination Use their own insurance Report to police File a crime victim's application.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Sexual Assault Victims page, Information for medical providers
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Victims (L&I page)

rules.summary: The program tells survivors they should not get any bill for the exam and to contact the program if one arrives.
rules.quote: You should not receive any bill for this examination. If you receive a bill contact us.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Sexual Assault Victims page, Information for victims
rules.source_title: Sexual Assault Victims (L&I page)

params.payer: Crime Victims Compensation Program; treatment and follow-up need a compensation application

rules.summary: If the exam includes treatment or the survivor needs follow-up care, a compensation application must be filed for those services to be considered.
rules.quote: If the examination includes treatment costs or the client will require follow-up treatment, an application for benefits must be filed with us for these services to be considered for payment.
rules.source_title: WAC 296-30-170 (who pays for sexual assault examinations)

params.payer: The jail, prison, or DSHS or Department of Corrections institution, when the victim was confined there at the time of the assault (not the program)

rules.summary: If the survivor was confined in a jail, prison, or a DSHS or Department of Corrections institution at the time of the assault, the program does not pay for the exam and providers bill the institution.
rules.quote: At the time of assault, if the victim was confined in any county or city jail, federal jail or prison or in any other federal institution, or any state correctional institution maintained and operated by the Department of Social and Health Services or the Department of Corrections or was confined or living in any other institution maintained and operated by the Department of Social and Health Services or the Department of Corrections Crime Victims Compensation Program is not responsible for payment.
rules.source_title: Billing Guidelines for Sexual Assault & DV with Strangulation Examinations (F800-100-000)

rules.summary: The program lists the maximum per claim as $190,000 (non-medical benefits plus medical and mental health treatment).
rules.quote: Maximum per claim: $190,000
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, How much we may pay
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

rules.summary: All benefits other than medical benefits (wage loss, funeral and the rest) share one cap of $40,000 for a single injury or death. Medical benefits have their own separate cap, so this is not the total award limit.
rules.quote: Except for medical benefits authorized under RCW 7.68.080 , no more than forty thousand dollars shall be granted as a result of a single injury or death.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.070 (benefits, amounts, limitations)

rules.summary: Medical benefits are capped at $150,000 per injury or death.
rules.quote: The director of labor and industries shall institute a cap on medical benefits of one hundred fifty thousand dollars per injury or death.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.085 (cap on medical benefits)

rules.summary: The program groups medical and mental health treatment under one $150,000 maximum.
rules.quote: Medical/Mental Health treatment: $150,000 maximum
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, How much we may pay
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

rules.summary: Lost wage support for a temporary total disability may not exceed $15,000.
rules.quote: Benefits payable for temporary total disability that results in financial support for lost wages shall not exceed fifteen thousand dollars.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.070 (benefits, amounts, limitations)

rules.summary: Monthly wage loss payments are 60 percent of the victim's monthly wage, up to 100 percent of the state's average monthly wage.
rules.quote: sixty percent of the victim's monthly wage but no more than one hundred percent of the state's average monthly wage as defined in RCW 7.68.020
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.070 (benefits, amounts, limitations)

rules.summary: A victim who was not working at the time of the crime gets no lost wage support unless they worked at least 12 weeks in the 6 months before the crime.
rules.quote: If the victim was not gainfully employed at the time of the criminal act, no financial support for lost wages will be paid to the victim or any beneficiaries, unless the victim was gainfully employed for a total of at least twelve weeks in the six months preceding the date of the criminal act.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.070 (benefits, amounts, limitations)

params.item: lost wages when the employer keeps paying the victim's wages

rules.summary: If the employer keeps paying the victim's wages, no lost wage support is paid.
rules.quote: If a victim's employer continues to pay the victim's wages that he or she was earning at the time of the crime, the victim shall not receive any financial support for lost wages.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.070 (benefits, amounts, limitations)

rules.summary: Sexual assault victims can receive counseling, with fees set by the department, and counseling may include immediate family members other than the perpetrator.
rules.quote: Victims of sexual assault are eligible to receive appropriate counseling. Fees for such counseling shall be determined by the department. Counseling services may include, if determined appropriate by the department, counseling of members of the victim's immediate family, other than the perpetrator of the assault.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.080 (transportation, medical services, counseling)

rules.summary: Counseling for immediate family members is covered under the victim's sexual assault claim.
rules.quote: Counseling for immediate family members will be covered under the victim's sexual assault claim.
rules.source_title: WAC 296-30-080 (counseling for family members of sexual assault victims)

rules.summary: The program may pay for medical and dental treatment, medication, mental health treatment, partial wage loss replacement, and costs other insurance does not cover such as co-pays and deductibles.
rules.quote: What we may pay for Medical/Dental treatment Medication Mental health treatment Grief counseling Partial wage loss replacement Funeral expenses Expenses not covered by other insurance (such as medical co-pays and medical deductibles)
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, What are the benefits?
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

params.scope: rides to and from the nearest proper treatment when an injury is so serious you must be taken there

rules.summary: When an injury is serious enough that the victim must be taken for treatment, reasonable transportation to and from the nearest proper treatment is reimbursed as part of the claim.
rules.quote: When the injury to any victim is so serious as to require the victim being taken from the place of injury to a place of treatment, reasonable transportation costs to and from the nearest place of proper treatment to a reasonable location of the victim's choice shall be reimbursed by the department as part of the victim's total claim under RCW 7.68.070 (1).
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.080 (transportation, medical services, counseling)

params.scope: trips of more than 15 miles one way

rules.summary: The program's page says the trip must be more than 15 miles one way from home, and the first and last 15 miles are not paid.
rules.quote: The travel must be more than 15 miles one way from your home, and the first and last 15 miles of travel are not payable.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, Travel Reimbursement
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

rules.summary: The page also says no provider of the same type may be closer to home, and the claim manager must approve the trip ahead of time. It must be for treatment of the accepted condition or for an independent medical exam the claim manager asks for.
rules.quote: No other provider of the same type is available closer to your home. Travel must also be preapproved by your claim manager for one of the following: Treatment for your accepted condition. An independent medical examination requested by your claim manager.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, Travel Reimbursement
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

rules.summary: A travel reimbursement request must be made within 1 year of the trip.
rules.quote: Your request must be made within 1 year of the trip and must indicate the date, destination and reason for travel.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, How to get reimbursed
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

params.scope: clothing or footwear lost or damaged during emergency medical treatment

rules.summary: Eligible victims may also claim the loss of or damage to their clothing or footwear during emergency medical treatment.
rules.quote: Victims otherwise eligible for compensation under this chapter may also claim compensation for loss of or damage to the victim's personal clothing or footwear incurred in the course of emergency medical treatment for injuries.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.074 (loss of or damage to clothing or footwear), certified PDF

rules.summary: The program's page lists medication among the costs it may pay for.
rules.quote: What we may pay for Medical/Dental treatment Medication
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, What are the benefits?
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

params.scope: up to a 28-day supply of HIV prevention medicine (PEP) from a Washington hospital emergency department

rules.summary: The program covers up to a 28-day supply of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) drugs dispensed directly from a Washington hospital emergency department.
rules.quote: Crime Victims Compensation Programs will cover up to a 28-day supply of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) drugs for HIV when dispensed directly from a Washington State hospital emergency department for proper and necessary treatment of a crime victim.
rules.pinpoint: F800-100-000, Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) drugs for HIV
rules.source_title: Billing Guidelines for Sexual Assault & DV with Strangulation Examinations (F800-100-000)

rules.summary: Under the damaged personal property question, the program lists eyeglasses or contacts, prosthetics (including orthotics), hearing aids, and clothing or footwear as items that may be reimbursed.
rules.quote: Eligible items may include: Eye glasses/contacts. Prosthetics, including orthotics, or hearing aids Clothing/footwear.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, Will I be reimbursed for damaged personal property?
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

params.item: loss or damage of personal property (eyeglasses or contacts, prosthetics, hearing aids, and clothing or footwear are listed exceptions); identity theft losses

rules.summary: The program does not pay for identity theft or for loss or damage of personal property, with some exceptions.
rules.quote: We don't pay for the following Crime scene cleanup Identity theft Loss or damage of personal property
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, How much we may pay
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

rules.summary: The program does not pay for crime scene cleanup.
rules.quote: We don't pay for the following Crime scene cleanup Identity theft Loss or damage of personal property
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, How much we may pay
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

params.item: services covered by Medicaid (chapter 74.09 RCW or Title XIX)

rules.summary: Compensation does not pay for services covered by Medicaid.
rules.quote: Crime victims' compensation is not available to pay for services covered under chapter 74.09 RCW or Title XIX of the federal social security act.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.070 (benefits, amounts, limitations)

params.extension: good cause, decided case by case; see the next rule for the outer limit

rules.summary: The application must be received within 3 years after the crime was reported to police or the sheriff, unless the director finds good cause to allow more time.
rules.quote: An application for benefits is not received by the department within three years after the date the criminal act was reported to a local police department or sheriff's office or the date the rights of beneficiaries accrued, unless the director has determined that "good cause" exists to expand the time permitted to receive the application.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.060 (applications for benefits, time limits, reporting, eligibility bars)

rules.summary: Good cause can extend the application window to up to 5 years after the police report.
rules.quote: may extend the period of time in which an application can be received for up to five years after the date the criminal act was reported to a local police department or sheriff's office or the date the rights of beneficiaries accrued
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.060 (applications for benefits, time limits, reporting, eligibility bars)

rules.summary: For adults who were victims of crimes as children, rights accrue when the victim discovers or reasonably should have discovered the elements of the crime.
rules.quote: the rights of adult victims of childhood criminal acts shall accrue at the time the victim discovers or reasonably should have discovered the elements of the crime.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.060 (applications for benefits, time limits, reporting, eligibility bars)

rules.summary: The program says a person who was a minor at the time of the crime must apply within 2 years of their 18th birthday.
rules.quote: For minors, at the time of the crime, the application must be filed within two years of their 18th birthday.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, Do I qualify?
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

params.extension: No deadline: may file at any time. Applies only to a minor identified as a victim of sex trafficking or commercial sexual abuse of a minor; the reporting rule and the consent and felony bars also do not apply.

rules.summary: A minor identified as a victim of sex trafficking or commercial sexual abuse of a minor may apply at any time, and the application deadline, police report rule, and consent and felony bars do not apply to them.
rules.quote: A person identified under this subsection (6)(b) may file an application for benefits at any time, and the ineligibility factors of subsections (1) and (2) of this section do not apply to such a person.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.060 (applications for benefits, time limits, reporting, eligibility bars)

params.exception: or, if you could not reasonably report that soon, within 12 months of when you could

rules.summary: For a compensation claim, the crime must be reported to police or the sheriff within 12 months, or within 12 months of when it reasonably could have been reported. The exam itself does not require a report.
rules.quote: The criminal act is not reported by the victim or someone on his or her behalf to a local police department or sheriff's office within twelve months of its occurrence or, if it could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within twelve months of the time when a report could reasonably have been made.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.060 (applications for benefits, time limits, reporting, eligibility bars)

rules.summary: The report can go to local, state, federal, tribal, or military police, or to Child Protective Services when CPS has reported to local police.
rules.quote: The crime can be reported to any of the following: (1) Local law enforcement (city, county or state police agencies); (2) Federal police; (3) Indian tribal police; (4) Military police; or (5) Child protective services (CPS) when they have reported to local police.
rules.source_title: WAC 296-30-060 (who a victim reports the crime to)

rules.summary: A claimant who refuses reasonable cooperation with law enforcement is not eligible, unless the director finds cooperation may be affected by age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or language barriers, or another health or safety concern that puts the victim's well-being at risk.
rules.quote: has refused to give reasonable cooperation to state or local law enforcement agencies in their efforts to apprehend and convict the perpetrator of the criminal act which gave rise to the claim unless the director determines such cooperation may be impacted due to a victim's age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or linguistic barriers, or any other health or safety concern that jeopardizes the victim's well-being.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.060 (applications for benefits, time limits, reporting, eligibility bars)

rules.summary: Program payment is secondary to other insurance benefits, whatever any insurance contract or coverage says.
rules.quote: Payment by the department under this chapter shall be secondary to other insurance benefits, notwithstanding the provision of any contract or coverage to the contrary.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.130 (public or private insurance)

rules.summary: Victims must use their private insurance before the program will consider paying.
rules.quote: Before payment of benefits will be considered victims shall use their private insurance coverage.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.130 (public or private insurance)

rules.summary: On an allowed claim under the maximum benefit, the claimant should not pay; providers bill insurance first and then the department, and must refund the claimant if they collected while eligibility was pending.
rules.quote: If claim costs are under the maximum benefit, the claimant should not pay any expenses relating to an allowed claim. Providers must bill the claimant's public or private insurance first, and then bill the department.
rules.source_title: WAC 296-30-087 (can a victim be billed for expenses related to their claim)

rules.summary: By statute, benefits are barred when the injury resulted from the victim's consent, provocation, or incitement, or was sustained while the victim was committing a felony. Shown for information only.
rules.quote: The result of consent, provocation, or incitement by the victim, unless an injury resulting from a criminal act caused the death of the victim; (b) Sustained while the crime victim was engaged in the attempt to commit, or the commission of, a felony
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.060 (applications for benefits, time limits, reporting, eligibility bars)

rules.summary: A victim is not eligible if convicted of a violent felony or crime against persons within the 5 years before the crime (or after it) and has not fully paid all legal financial obligations. Shown for information only.
rules.quote: Has been convicted of a felony offense within five years preceding the criminal act for which the victim is applying where the felony offense is a violent offense under RCW 9.94A.030 or a crime against persons under RCW 9.94A.411 , or is convicted of such a felony offense after the criminal act for which the victim is applying; and (b) Has not completely satisfied all legal financial obligations owed.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.060 (applications for benefits, time limits, reporting, eligibility bars)

rules.summary: To qualify, the person must have a physical injury or mental health trauma from a gross misdemeanor or felony crime in Washington.
rules.quote: Sustained a physical injury or mental health trauma as a result of a gross misdemeanor or felony crime in Washington State.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Who Can File and What is Covered, Do I qualify?
rules.source_title: Who Can File and What is Covered (L&I page)

rules.summary: The statute specifically makes sexual assault victims eligible for counseling, and the application lists sexual assault as a crime type.
rules.quote: Victims of sexual assault are eligible to receive appropriate counseling.
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.080 (transportation, medical services, counseling)

params.rule: Crimes committed in Washington; or crimes against a Washington resident committed in a state with no compensation program

rules.summary: A covered criminal act is one committed or attempted in Washington, or one committed outside Washington against a Washington resident in a state with no crime victims' compensation program.
rules.quote: an act committed outside the state of Washington against a resident of the state of Washington which would be compensable had it occurred inside this state and the crime occurred in a state which does not have a crime victims' compensation program
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.020 (definitions)

params.rule: Exam costs: paid for exams at Washington facilities whether the assault happened in or outside Washington

rules.summary: For the exam alone, the no-bill rule covers exams at Washington facilities whether the assault happened in or outside Washington.
rules.quote: whether such assault occurred in or outside the state of Washington
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.170 (examination costs of sexual assault victims paid by state)

rules.summary: The completed PDF application can be emailed as an attachment to CrimeVictimsProgramM@Lni.wa.gov.
rules.quote: Upon completion, the PDF form can be emailed as an attachment to CrimeVictimsProgramM@Lni.wa.gov or faxed to 360-902-5333.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Apply for Crime Victim Benefits page, filing instructions
rules.source_title: Apply for Crime Victim Benefits (L&I page)

rules.summary: The completed application can be faxed to 360-902-5333.
rules.quote: This form may be directly faxed to 360-902-5333 or emailed to CrimeVictimsProgramM@Lni.wa.gov .
rules.pinpoint: L&I Apply for Crime Victim Benefits page, Application for Benefits (F800-042-000)
rules.source_title: Apply for Crime Victim Benefits (L&I page)

params.target: Crime Victims Compensation Program PO Box 44520 Olympia WA 98504-4520

rules.summary: A printed application can be mailed to the Crime Victims Compensation Program, PO Box 44520, Olympia WA 98504-4520 (the address printed on the form; the L&I page says printed applications can be sent by mail or fax).
rules.quote: Crime Victims Compensation Program PO Box 44520 Olympia WA 98504-4520
rules.source_title: Crime Victim's Application for Benefits, Injury Claims (F800-042-000, 07-2017)

params.note: the application, signed and dated

rules.summary: Sign and date the application; incomplete information can delay the decision.
rules.quote: Be sure to sign and date the form. Incomplete information could delay the decision on your claim.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Apply for Crime Victim Benefits page, Note under the application form
rules.source_title: Apply for Crime Victim Benefits (L&I page)

params.note: signed Authorization to Release Confidential Information (page 5 of the application)

rules.summary: The victim or legal guardian must sign the authorization to release information for it to be valid.
rules.quote: NOTE: The victim or legal guardian must sign this form to be valid
rules.pinpoint: F800-042-000, Authorization to Release Confidential Information
rules.source_title: Crime Victim's Application for Benefits, Injury Claims (F800-042-000, 07-2017)

rules.summary: The program treats the police report as supporting documentation to send in with the claim number on each page.
rules.quote: How do I send supporting documentation such as the police report and medical reports?
rules.pinpoint: L&I Apply for Crime Victim Benefits page, Questions crime victim applicants have
rules.source_title: Apply for Crime Victim Benefits (L&I page)

params.note: medical reports

rules.summary: Medical reports are supporting documentation the program expects, sent with the claim number on each page.
rules.quote: How do I send supporting documentation such as the police report and medical reports?
rules.pinpoint: L&I Apply for Crime Victim Benefits page, Questions crime victim applicants have
rules.source_title: Apply for Crime Victim Benefits (L&I page)

params.note: provider section of the application completed by the treating medical professional, if already seen

rules.summary: If the survivor has already seen a medical or other provider, that provider completes the Provider Information section of the form.
rules.quote: If you have already seen a medical or other provider, or are completing this form in a medical office or hospital, please ask the medical professional seeing you to complete the section below.
rules.source_title: Crime Victim's Application for Benefits, Injury Claims (F800-042-000, 07-2017)

params.note: insurance company, policyholder, and policy ID for every available coverage

rules.summary: List every available insurance coverage on the form, since the program pays only after insurance.
rules.quote: Please list all available coverage to include: health insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, HCA/Medicaid, Veteran, Social Security, DSHS/public assistance, workers' compensation, Indian Health, automobile insurance (victim and offender), motorcycle insurance, life insurance, home insurance, renter's insurance.
rules.source_title: Crime Victim's Application for Benefits, Injury Claims (F800-042-000, 07-2017)

params.note: guardianship documentation, if a legal guardian applies for a minor

rules.summary: A legal guardian applying for a minor sends a copy of the guardianship documentation.
rules.quote: If you are the legal guardian, please send the Crime Victims Compensation Program a copy of the guardianship documentation.
rules.pinpoint: F800-042-000, Authorization to Release Confidential Information
rules.source_title: Crime Victim's Application for Benefits, Injury Claims (F800-042-000, 07-2017)

params.note: employer name, contact, address, rate of pay, and dates worked on the form; the program may contact the employer

rules.summary: Survivors applying for wage loss fill in the employer section, and the program may contact the employer.
rules.quote: If yes and you are requesting wage replacement benefits, provide the following employer information
rules.source_title: Crime Victim's Application for Benefits, Injury Claims (F800-042-000, 07-2017)

rules.summary: The program says applicants hear about receipt within 5-7 days and, in most cases, about the outcome within 15-18 days.
rules.quote: You will hear from us within 5-7 days regarding receipt of your application and in most cases within 15-18 days regarding the outcome of your application.
rules.pinpoint: L&I Apply for Crime Victim Benefits page, after the filing instructions
rules.source_title: Apply for Crime Victim Benefits (L&I page)

params.enroll: Interested people meet with an advocate who has been designated as an Application Assistant (AA) to create or review their safety plan and threat assessment before completing and application to apply for the program.

rules.summary: The Secretary of State's Address Confidentiality Program offers survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, or trafficking a substitute address to receive first class mail. You enroll through an advocate designated as an Application Assistant.
rules.quote: The Washington Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) offers survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, or trafficking, and Criminal Justice Affiliates, Election Officials, and Protected Health Care Workers who are a target for threats or harassment, a substitute address to receive first class mail.
rules.pinpoint: WA Secretary of State ACP page, opening paragraph; enrollment through an Application Assistant per the How to Apply section and the Application Process page (WA-S25); statutory basis chapter 40.24 RCW (RCW 40.24.030, WA-S23)
rules.source_title: Washington Secretary of State: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

rules.summary: Information in crime victim claim files and records is confidential and not open to public inspection, but the law lets some people see it.
rules.quote: Information contained in the claim files and records of victims, under the provisions of this chapter, shall be deemed confidential and shall not be open to public inspection
rules.source_title: RCW 7.68.140 (confidentiality of victim claim files and records)

params.condition: if the provider bills the state SAFE Fund

rules.summary: A health care provider that asks the state SAFE Fund to pay for a sexual assault forensic exam may not bill the survivor (or the survivor's guardian) for any of the exam costs.
rules.quote: A health care provider seeking an award under this section may not seek payment for any examination costs from the victim or any guardian of the victim.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.condition: if the provider bills the state SAFE Fund

rules.summary: A provider seeking a SAFE Fund award may not bill the survivor's insurance or any other payer for exam costs unless the survivor or guardian authorizes it.
rules.quote: may not seek payment for any examination costs from insurance or another available source of payment unless the victim or any guardian of the victim authorizes the health care provider to seek payment.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.condition: if the provider bills the state SAFE Fund

rules.summary: The DOJ's SAFE Fund page says the provider may not bill the survivor or family for a sexual assault nurse examiner (SANE) exam. If you get a bill, the page says to contact the provider right away and ask them to send it to the SAFE Fund.
rules.quote: The health care provider may not bill the victim or the family of the victim for the cost of a SANE exam. Should a victim receive a bill for a SANE exam, they must contact the health care provider immediately and ask them to submit the bill to the SAFE Fund.
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Sexual Assault Forensic Exam (SAFE) Fund

params.payer: Wisconsin Department of Justice SAFE Fund (Wis. Stat. ch. 949 subch. II), paid directly to the health care provider, unless the survivor both authorizes insurance billing and cooperates with law enforcement

rules.summary: For a sexual assault that happened in Wisconsin, the Wisconsin Department of Justice pays exam costs directly to the health care provider through the Sexual Assault Forensic Examination (SAFE) Fund. Exam costs are the evidence exam plus testing, prevention and medicine for sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) and medicine to prevent HIV, given or prescribed during the exam. The fund pays only these exam costs, not other medical treatment or follow-up visits. It does not pay if the provider is allowed to bill insurance and the survivor (or a guardian) has reported to police or helped their investigation.
rules.quote: the department shall make an award under this section to a health care provider who conducts an examination to gather evidence regarding a sex offense to reimburse the health care provider only for the examination costs
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.payer: Not the SAFE Fund when the survivor (or guardian) authorizes insurance billing and also cooperates with law enforcement; otherwise the SAFE Fund pays (949.26(1))

rules.summary: The SAFE Fund does not pay when the survivor or guardian both lets the provider bill insurance and cooperates with police. If the survivor does not authorize insurance billing, the fund pays the exam costs whether or not they report; if they authorize insurance but do not cooperate with police, the fund pays what insurance does not.
rules.quote: The department may not make an award under this section if, under sub. (2) (b), the health care provider is authorized to seek payment and the victim, or any guardian of the victim, cooperates with a law enforcement agency.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: For the forensic exam, no police report is needed: the SAFE Fund may not refuse payment because the survivor does not cooperate with law enforcement or because there is no investigation or prosecution.
rules.quote: The department may not refuse to make an award under this section because the victim or the guardian of the victim does not cooperate with a law enforcement agency regarding the sex offense, or due to lack of an investigation or prosecution of the sex offense.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: The most the program can award for one injury is $40,000, and it cannot pay expenses incurred more than 4 years after the injury (child victims follow a different timing rule).
rules.quote: the department may not make an award of more than $40,000 for any one injury or death and the department may not make any award for expenses incurred after 4 years from the date of the injury or death.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.item: computer or mobile telephone held as evidence

rules.summary: A computer or mobile phone held as evidence can be replaced up to $200.
rules.quote: (cg) Reasonable replacement value of any computer or mobile telephone that is held for evidentiary purposes, but not to exceed $200.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: Clothing and bedding held as evidence can be replaced up to $300.
rules.quote: (c) Reasonable replacement value of any clothing and bedding that is held for evidentiary purposes, but not to exceed $300.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.item: other evidence property rendered unusable by crime lab testing

rules.summary: Other property held as evidence and made unusable by crime lab testing can be replaced up to $200.
rules.quote: Reasonable replacement value for property, other than clothing and bedding under par. (c), that is held for evidentiary purposes and is rendered unusable as a result of crime laboratory testing, but not to exceed $200.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.item: parent of a minor victim: own mental health treatment and work loss combined
params.applies_to: each parent of a victim under 18

rules.summary: Each parent of a minor victim can receive up to $3,000 total for the parent's own mental health treatment and lost work combined. This limit is for parents only; it does not cap the victim's own counseling.
rules.quote: (bg) The department may award each parent of a victim not more than $3,000 total for reimbursement of expenses under par. (a) related to mental health treatment and for work loss under par. (b).
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)
rules.set_aside_reason: applies_to "each parent of a victim under 18"

rules.summary: Securing and cleaning up a crime scene is covered up to $1,000.
rules.quote: (f) Reasonable and necessary costs associated with securing and cleaning up a crime scene, not to exceed $1,000.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.item: housing accessibility adaptations for a protracted disability

rules.summary: If the crime caused a protracted disability, housing accessibility changes are covered up to $5,000.
rules.quote: reasonable and necessary housing accessibility adaptations, but not to exceed $5,000.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: Funeral and burial expenses are covered up to $5,000.
rules.quote: (d) Reasonable funeral and burial expenses, not to exceed $5,000.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: Medical treatment the program can pay includes medical, hospital, psychiatric, psychological and dental care and prescription medications.
rules.quote: “Medical treatment” includes medical, surgical, psychiatric, psychological, dental, optometric, chiropractic, podiatric and hospital care; prescription medications;
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: The program pays for medical treatment caused by the crime.
rules.quote: (a) Medical treatment, subject to the limits set forth under par. (bg).
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: Outpatient psychotherapy (counseling) is an eligible mental health service. The provider must be licensed (psychiatrist, psychologist, marriage and family therapist, professional counselor, or clinical social worker) or a supervised treatment trainee, and must submit an authorization request to the program.
rules.quote: (b) Outpatient psychotherapy services.
rules.source_title: Wis. Admin. Code ch. Jus 11, Awards for Victims of Crime

rules.summary: Lost wages are covered. Up to 2 weeks can be paid without a doctor's proof of disability; longer periods need a physician's determination.
rules.quote: 4. The department may award each victim, parent of a victim, or in the case of a homicide, family member of a victim not more than 2 weeks of lost wages without requiring proof of disability from a physician.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.scope: replacing a computer or mobile phone held as evidence

rules.summary: The reasonable replacement value of a computer or phone held as evidence can be paid.
rules.quote: Reasonable replacement value of any computer or mobile telephone that is held for evidentiary purposes
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.item: personal property losses including cash; pain and suffering

rules.summary: Personal property losses, including cash, and pain and suffering are not paid. Evidence items (clothing, bedding, phones, computers, lab-damaged property) are the only property exceptions, up to their caps.
rules.quote: Personal property losses including cash and “pain and suffering” cannot be reimbursed by the Program.
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), English

params.item: property loss or damage other than evidence items

rules.summary: Property loss or damage is not covered beyond the listed evidence items, so a phone that was stolen or broken (not held as evidence) is not covered.
rules.quote: Please note: Property loss or damage is not covered other than those items described above. A victim is not eligible for Crime Victim Compensation if only property damage or loss occurred.
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Program

params.item: mileage and time off work for scheduled appointments or court appearances

rules.summary: Mileage and time off work for scheduled appointments or court dates are not paid.
rules.quote: The Program cannot reimburse for mileage or for time off of work for scheduled appointments or court appearances.
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

params.item: pain and suffering

rules.summary: Pain and suffering is not paid.
rules.quote: The Crime Victim Compensation Program does not pay for pain and suffering.
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

params.item: court appearances or evaluations by mental health providers

rules.summary: Mental health providers' court appearances or evaluations are not paid as counseling.
rules.quote: (c) Court appearances or evaluations are not eligible services.
rules.source_title: Wis. Admin. Code ch. Jus 11, Awards for Victims of Crime

params.item: costs incurred more than 4 years after the injury

rules.summary: Except in some cases, the program does not pay for costs that come more than 4 years after the injury.
rules.quote: Except as provided in par. (b), the department may not make an award of more than $40,000 for any one injury or death and the department may not make any award for expenses incurred after 4 years from the date of the injury or death.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: Apply within 1 year of the injury.
rules.quote: No order for the payment of an award may be made unless the application was made within 1 year after the date of the personal injury or death
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.extension: waiver request with written statement

rules.summary: If the application is not filed within 1 year, the program asks for a written statement explaining the delay.
rules.quote: If the application is not filed within 1 year, attach a written statement explaining the reason for the delay.
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ CVC FAQs, Applying and Eligibility
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

rules.summary: The program's page says the 1-year limit can be waived in the interest of justice. It also says adults who were victims of a crime as children may apply.
rules.quote: The applicant must file a claim within one year of the date of the crime. This time limit may be waived in the interest of justice. Adults who were the victim of a crime as a child may apply.
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ CVC Program page, What must I do to be eligible?
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Program

rules.summary: If you were a child when it happened, the program may consider paying eligible costs from up to 1 year before you apply.
rules.quote: If an applicant was a child at the time of the injury, the department may consider for payment eligible expenses that the applicant incurred not more than 1 year before he or she submitted an application for an award under this subchapter.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.exception: or, if you could not reasonably report that soon, within 5 days of when you could, and the program can waive this

rules.summary: For compensation (beyond the exam), the crime must be reported to police within 5 days, or within 5 days of when it could reasonably be reported. The department may waive this in the interest of justice.
rules.quote: the personal injury or death was the result of an incident or offense which had been reported to the police within 5 days of its occurrence or, if the incident or offense could not reasonably have been reported within such period, within 5 days of the time when a report could reasonably have been made. The department may waive the requirements under this subsection in the interest of justice.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: No compensation award may be made if the victim has not cooperated with law enforcement. The administrative rules let the department waive the prosecution-cooperation part for a compelling health or safety reason.
rules.quote: (d) Has not cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: For compensation claims, the department may waive the duty to cooperate in the prosecution if the victim shows good cause that not cooperating is due to a compelling health or safety reason. The police report itself is still expected.
rules.quote: The department may waive the provisions of this paragraph upon good cause shown by the victim that the failure to cooperate in the prosecution is due to a compelling health or safety reason.
rules.source_title: Wis. Admin. Code ch. Jus 11, Awards for Victims of Crime

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by payments from the offender, insurance (including workers' compensation and unemployment), public funds, liable third parties, and any SAFE Fund exam award.
rules.quote: Any award made under this section shall be reduced by the amount of any payment received, or to be received, as a result of the injury or death:
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: The program is the payer of last resort: insurance and public programs such as Medical Assistance, BadgerCare and Medicare must be billed first. It may pay co-pays and costs insurance denies.
rules.quote: Do I have to submit bills to my insurance? Yes, this Program is considered the last payer, by law.
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ CVC FAQs, Medical Treatment/Counseling
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

rules.summary: The statute bars an award (not just a reduction) if the victim's own conduct substantially contributed to the injury. Shown for information only.
rules.quote: (a) Engaged in conduct which substantially contributed to the infliction of the victim’s injury or death or in which the victim could have reasonably foreseen could lead to the injury or death.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: Sexual assault (s. 940.225) is a compensable crime. Child sexual assault, sexual exploitation by a therapist, trafficking, and sexual extortion are also on the list.
rules.quote: 940.225 Sexual Assault
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Compensable Crimes list (Wis. Stat. 949.03(2))
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victims Compensable Crimes

rules.summary: Injury includes pregnancy and mental or psychological trauma, not only physical harm.
rules.quote: “Personal injury” means actual bodily harm and includes pregnancy and mental or psychological trauma.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.rule: Crime must occur in Wisconsin; any person may apply

rules.summary: The crime must have happened in Wisconsin; any person may apply, so victims who live out of state are not excluded by the statute.
rules.quote: “Crime” means an act committed in this state which would constitute a crime as defined in s. 939.12 if committed by a competent adult who has no legal defense for the act.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.rule: Wisconsin residents injured out of state may apply only if that jurisdiction has no covering compensation law

rules.summary: A Wisconsin resident hurt outside the state can apply only if the place where it happened has no compensation law covering the injury.
rules.quote: If a Wisconsin resident suffers injury or death in a situation described in s. 949.03 except that the act occurred outside this state, the resident has the same rights under this subchapter as if the act had occurred in this state upon a showing that the state, territory, country or political subdivision of a country in which the act occurred does not have a compensation of victims of crimes law which covers the injury or death suffered by the person.
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

params.target: Wisconsin Crime Victim Compensation Program PO Box 7951 Madison, WI 53707-7951

rules.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Wisconsin Crime Victim Compensation Program's PO box in Madison.
rules.quote: You may mail or fax your completed paper application. Mail to: Wisconsin Crime Victim Compensation Program PO Box 7951 Madison, WI 53707-7951
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation Application page, Submit Your Completed Paper Application
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Application

rules.summary: The completed paper application can be faxed to the program instead of mailed.
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation Application page, Submit Your Completed Paper Application
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Application

params.note: Recommended by the program. Requires an account created with a personal email; the portal also shows claim status and accepts bills and receipts later.

rules.summary: Applying online is the program's recommended option; you create an account with a personal email, then apply, check status, and upload bills and receipts.
rules.quote: Option 1: Apply Online (Recommended) To apply, you must create an account with a personal email to log in and apply.
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation Application page, Option 1 (Apply Online link)
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Application

params.note: Copies of itemized crime-related medical bills; optional at filing per the FAQ, but the program requires bills to be itemized.

rules.summary: Enclose copies of itemized crime-related medical bills, and send more as they arrive; the program only accepts itemized bills.
rules.quote: Enclose itemized copies of crime-related medical bills. Send copies of other itemized crime-related medical bills as they are received. This Program requires that the bills be itemized.
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), Application Information, What To Do
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), English

params.note: Explanations of benefits (EOBs) from insurance or other payers, with the itemized bills.

rules.summary: If insurance or another source covered expenses, attach copies of the itemized bills and the explanations of benefits.
rules.quote: Please attach copies of any crime-related itemized bills and explanations of benefits.
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), Section 6: Insurance and Benefit Information
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), English

params.note: Written reason for the delay, only if the crime was reported late or the application is filed late.

rules.summary: If the crime was reported late or the application is filed late, include a short written explanation of the delay.
rules.quote: If the crime was not reported within 5 days or the application was not filed within 1 year, include a brief but detailed written reason for the delay.
rules.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), Eligibility Requirements
rules.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Application, DJ-CVC-1 (Rev. 10/2024), English

params.note: Employer verification form, paycheck stubs, or income tax returns; only for lost wage claims.

rules.summary: Lost wage claims must be backed by an employer verification form, pay stubs, or tax returns; cash pay without documentation is not covered.
rules.quote: all lost wage claims must be documented through an employer verification form, paycheck stubs or income tax returns.
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation FAQs, Compensation
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

params.note: Physician certification of disability, only for wage loss beyond two weeks.

rules.summary: Up to two weeks of lost wages need no doctor's note; longer wage loss must be certified as a disability by a physician.
rules.quote: The Program may cover up to two weeks of lost wages without a physician certifying the absence. Wage loss beyond two weeks must be documented as a disability by a physician.
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation FAQs, Compensation
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

params.note: Therapist completes the program's authorization form; an update form is needed if treatment goes past six months.

rules.summary: For counseling to be paid, the therapist fills out the program's authorization form with a diagnosis, treatment plan, and expected length of treatment.
rules.quote: The Program requires that your therapist complete an authorization form, which gives a diagnosis, treatment plan and estimated length of treatment.
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation FAQs, Medical Treatment/Counseling
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

params.note: Only to be reimbursed for costs already paid out of pocket: canceled checks or itemized bills/receipts showing payment.

rules.summary: To be paid back for costs you already paid yourself, send canceled checks or itemized bills or receipts showing the payments.
rules.quote: We may send reimbursement checks to applicants if they have paid costs out of pocket already and have documented their payments. They should send in canceled checks or itemized bills/receipts showing their payments.
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation FAQs, Medical Treatment/Counseling
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

params.note: Approved alternative payment agreement, only if the victim is on the Wisconsin Child Support Lien Docket.

rules.summary: A victim listed on the state child support lien docket must provide a copy of an alternative payment agreement approved by the county child support agency.
rules.quote: If the victim is listed on the Wisconsin Child Support Lien Docket, the victim must provide a copy of his/her alternative payment agreement that has been approved by the county child support agency
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation FAQs, Applying and Eligibility
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation FAQs

params.note: Stated as 90-120 days or longer because of high application volume.

rules.summary: The program says intake can take 90 to 120 days or longer because of the volume of applications.
rules.quote: Due to the high volume of applications received, the intake process can take anywhere from 90-120 days or longer.
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ Crime Victim Compensation Program page, How will my claim be processed?
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Program

params.program_name: Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program
params.agency: Wisconsin Department of Justice, Office of Crime Victim Services
params.enroll: Individuals intending to enroll in Safe at Home must first participate in safety planning with an Application Assistant. After creating a safety plan with a designated Application Assistant, an individual may submit an application for enrollment in Safe at Home. A completed application may be faxed to Safe at Home's secure fax at (608) 261-8660 or mailed to Safe at Home, PO BOX 7035, Madison, WI 53707. Do not use email to submit your application.

rules.summary: Safe at Home, run by the Wisconsin Department of Justice, provides a legal substitute address to people who live in Wisconsin and are victims of domestic abuse, child abuse, sexual abuse, stalking, or trafficking, or who fear for their physical safety. You must live at an address the person you fear does not know, and not share it with them. To enroll, you first make a safety plan with a designated Application Assistant.
rules.quote: Safe at Home is an address confidentiality program that provides victims of domestic abuse, child abuse, sexual abuse, stalking, trafficking, or those who simply fear for their physical safety with a legal substitute address
rules.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ, Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program page, program description; Wis. Stat. 165.68
rules.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program

rules.summary: When a compensation claim arises from sexual assault or another listed sexual offense, the personally identifiable information on the application form is not open to public records inspection or copying.
rules.quote: any personally identifiable information, as defined in s. 19.62 (5), provided on the application form is not subject to inspection or copying under s. 19.35 (1).
rules.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rules.summary: A medical facility may not collect the cost of the sexual assault forensic exam from the survivor or from the survivor's insurance.
rules.quote: No licensed medical facility may collect the costs of a forensic medical examination from the alleged victim of a violation of this article or from the alleged victim's insurance coverage, if any.
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 61-8B-16 (Payment for forensic medical examination)

params.payer: West Virginia Prosecuting Attorneys Institute, forensic medical examination fund

rules.summary: The West Virginia Prosecuting Attorneys Institute pays the facility for the forensic exam out of the forensic medical examination fund.
rules.quote: the West Virginia prosecuting attorneys institute shall pay to a licensed medical facility from the forensic medical examination fund the cost of the forensic medical examination for the alleged victim
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 61-8B-16 (Payment for forensic medical examination)

params.payer: Not the exam fund; facility may bill survivor or insurer for nonforensic procedures

rules.summary: The exam fund does not cover nonforensic care given at the same visit (such as preventive treatment, injury treatment, pregnancy and STI testing); the facility may bill the survivor or their insurer for those.
rules.quote: The costs of additional nonforensic procedures performed by the licensed medical facility, including, but not limited to, prophylactic treatment, treatment of injuries, testing for pregnancy and testing for sexually transmitted diseases, may not be paid from the fund: Provided, That nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit a licensed medical facility from seeking payment for services referred to in this subdivision from the alleged victim or his or her insurer, if any
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 61-8B-16 (Payment for forensic medical examination)

params.scope: forensic exam only; does not apply to compensation claims

rules.summary: A survivor does not have to report to police or cooperate with law enforcement to get a state-paid forensic exam.
rules.quote: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require an alleged victim of sexual assault to participate in the criminal justice system or to cooperate with law enforcement in order to be provided a forensic medical examination pursuant to the provisions of this section.
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 61-8B-16 (Payment for forensic medical examination)

params.exception: or more in some cases

rules.summary: For an injury claim, total compensation to the victim and all other claimants may not exceed $35,000.
rules.quote: Except in the case of death, or as provided in subdivision (2) of this subsection, compensation payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to that victim may not exceed $35,000 in the aggregate.
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-14 (Denial, reduction, maximum award)

rules.summary: Relocation costs are covered up to $4,500.
rules.quote: Victim relocation costs not to exceed $4,500
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

params.scope: travel to attend court proceedings for the prosecution only; medical travel has no separate cap

rules.summary: Travel to attend court proceedings in the prosecution is covered up to $5,000. This cap applies to court travel only, not to travel for medical care.
rules.quote: Reasonable travel expenses not to exceed $5,000 for a claimant to attend court proceedings conducted for the prosecution of the offender
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Reasonable charges for needed medical and psychological care, including eyeglasses, dentures and rehabilitation, are allowable expenses.
rules.quote: Reasonable charges incurred or to be incurred for reasonably needed medical care, including products, services, and accommodations related to medical and psychological care, prosthetic devices, eye glasses, dentures, rehabilitation, and other remedial treatment and care
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

params.scope: mental health counseling by a licensed counselor

rules.summary: Mental health counseling by a licensed counselor is a reimbursable expense.
rules.quote: Mental Health Counseling by a Licensed Counselor
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Fund: Eligibility, Benefits, and Applications

params.scope: travel to and from a medical facility

rules.summary: Reasonable travel to and from a medical facility is an allowable expense.
rules.quote: Reasonable travel expenses for the transportation of a victim to and from a medical facility.
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Lost income from work the victim could not do because of the injury counts as economic loss.
rules.quote: "Work loss" means loss of income from work that the injured person would have performed if he or she had not been injured
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Income lost to attend court proceedings in the prosecution also counts as work loss.
rules.quote: "Work loss" also includes loss of income from work by the claimant, the victim, or the parent or legal guardian of a minor victim who must miss work to attend court proceedings conducted for the prosecution of the offender.
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

rules.summary: Dental costs are listed with medical costs as reimbursable.
rules.quote: Medical/Dental Mental Health Counseling by a Licensed Counselor Lost Wages/Income
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Fund: Eligibility, Benefits, and Applications

params.item: damaged or stolen personal property, including money (eyeglasses and dentures excepted)

rules.summary: Damaged or stolen property, including money, is not covered.
rules.quote: No. Damaged or stolen property, including money, is NOT recoverable.
rules.source_title: Application for West Virginia Crime Victims Compensation

params.item: personal property other than medically necessary items

rules.summary: Personal property is not covered, except medically necessary items such as eyeglasses.
rules.quote: Personal property (except medically necessary items such as eyeglasses)
rules.pinpoint: Eligibility page, Types of Losses Not Covered
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Fund: Eligibility, Benefits, and Applications

rules.summary: The application must be filed within two years after the crime.
rules.quote: All applications for an award of compensation shall be filed within two years after the occurrence of the criminally injurious conduct that is the basis of the application.
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-10 (Filing of application)

rules.summary: The Fund's page says a victim who was under 18 at the time must apply before turning 20.
rules.quote: The application for an adult victim (18 years or older at the time of crime) must be filed with the Fund within two years of the crime. The application for a minor victim (under 18 year of age at the time of the crime) must be filed with the Fund before the minor’s 20th birthday.
rules.pinpoint: Eligibility page, Time Limitations for Filing Application
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Fund: Eligibility, Benefits, and Applications

params.exam_condition: done within 96 hours of the assault
params.exception: or later with good cause, and minors need neither

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 96 hours, but for a sexual offense a forensic medical exam within 96 hours meets the requirement instead. Good cause can excuse a late report or exam, and juvenile victims are exempt.
rules.quote: The commissioner may not approve an award of compensation if the criminally injurious conduct upon which the claim is based was not reported to a law-enforcement officer or agency or, in the case of sexual offense, the victim did not undergo a forensic medical examination, within 96 hours after the occurrence of the conduct, unless it is determined that good cause existed for the failure to report the conduct or undergo a forensic medical examination within the 96-hour period: Provided , That reporting to a law-enforcement officer or agency or a forensic medical examination is not required if the victim is a juvenile in order for a commissioner to approve an award of compensation
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-14 (Denial, reduction, maximum award)

params.scope: filing of a criminal charge, not just a report; exceptions for unknown offender, juvenile claimant, or adult claimant who did not block charges where law enforcement confirms a crime occurred

rules.summary: Beyond the police report, a criminal charge generally has to be filed. It is not required when the offender is unknown or the claimant was a juvenile. It is also not required for an adult claimant when no charges were filed for reasons other than the claimant's own wish and law enforcement confirms the evidence supports that a crime occurred. A conviction is not required.
rules.quote: The filing of a criminal charge shall be a prerequisite for receipt of compensation unless it is determined that no charges were filed due to the identity of the perpetrator being unknown: Provided, That no criminal charges need be filed if: (1) The claimant is an adult at the time the conduct giving rise to the claim occurred and no criminal charges were filed for reasons other than the desire of the claimant and a law-enforcement agency confirms that the available evidence supports a finding that a crime occurred; or (2) the claimant was a juvenile at the time the conduct giving rise to the claim occurred.
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-18 (Effect of no criminal charges)

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by whatever insurance or other collateral sources pay; the fund pays last.
rules.quote: The commissioner shall reduce an award of compensation or deny a claim for an award of compensation that is otherwise payable to a claimant to the extent that the economic loss upon which the claim is based is or will be recouped from other persons, including collateral sources
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-14 (Denial, reduction, maximum award)

rules.summary: An award may be reduced or denied for contributory misconduct of the claimant or victim.
rules.quote: or if the reduction or denial is determined to be reasonable because of the contributory misconduct of the claimant or of a victim through whom he or she claims
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-14 (Denial, reduction, maximum award)

rules.summary: A commissioner may deny a claim, reduce an award, or reconsider an approved claim if the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with law enforcement or the claim investigator.
rules.quote: A commissioner, upon a finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law-enforcement agencies or the claim investigator, may deny a claim, reduce an award of compensation, or reconsider a claim already approved.
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-14 (Denial, reduction, maximum award)

rules.summary: Sexual assault is listed among the crimes resulting in personal injury that the fund covers.
rules.quote: Murder Other Violent Crimes Robbery Sexual Assault Kidnapping Human Trafficking
rules.pinpoint: Eligibility page, Crimes Resulting in Personal Injury
rules.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Fund: Eligibility, Benefits, and Applications

params.rule: Crimes in West Virginia (residents and nonresidents); West Virginia residents for crimes in a state with no compensation program or outside the United States

rules.summary: The crime must occur in West Virginia, or in a state without a victim compensation program. A nonresident is eligible only if the crime happened in West Virginia, and West Virginia residents are also covered for crimes outside the United States.
rules.quote: “Criminally injurious conduct” means conduct that occurs or is attempted in this state, or in any state not having a victim compensation program, which poses a substantial threat of personal injury or death and is punishable by fine or imprisonment. “Criminally injurious conduct” also includes criminally injurious conduct committed outside of the United States against a resident of this state.
rules.pinpoint: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3(c); nonresident limit in 14-2A-3(a)(1)
rules.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

params.target: CRIME VICTIMS COMPENSATION FUND 1900 KANAWHA BLVD E ROOM W-334 CHARLESTON WV 25305-0610

rules.summary: Mail the completed, notarized application to the Crime Victims Compensation Fund in Charleston.
rules.quote: Mail your completed application to: CRIME VICTIMS COMPENSATION FUND 1900 KANAWHA BLVD E ROOM W-334 CHARLESTON WV 25305-0610
rules.source_title: Application for West Virginia Crime Victims Compensation

rules.summary: A claim can also be filed through the Legislature's online claim form.
rules.quote: Begin your Online Claim Process This online claim form takes you through 5 simple steps to file your Crime Victims claim.
rules.pinpoint: File Your Crime Victims Claim page
rules.source_title: File Your Crime Victims Claim (online claim form start page)

rules.summary: Send a copy of the police report with the application if you have one; do not hold the application waiting for it near the deadline.
rules.quote: Include all the documentation you can - if you have a copy of the police report, hospital or doctor bills, please send with the application.
rules.source_title: Application for West Virginia Crime Victims Compensation

params.note: A copy of each medical bill; insurance statements are not accepted in place of bills.

rules.summary: Submit a copy of each of the victim's medical bills. Insurance statements are not acceptable.
rules.quote: SUBMIT A COPY OF EACH OF THE VICTIM’S MEDICAL BILLS. INSURANCE STATEMENTS ARE NOT ACCEPTABLE.
rules.source_title: Application for West Virginia Crime Victims Compensation

params.note: Claimant's release signed in front of a notary public.

rules.summary: Sign the application's release page in front of a notary; skipping the notary delays the claim.
